modules.title: Relations checked on generators
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A relation between elements of an algebra which is stable under the algebra operations
need only be checked on a generating family. This file collects the instances of that
principle needed to present a large algebra by generators and relations without assuming
the target commutative, where the usual lifts through commutative algebras are
unavailable.

There are four groups of results. The first says what a generating set of an algebra gives
about a map out of it, namely that its range, and its commutation with a fixed element,
are already determined on the generators. The second generates a tensor product, both from
its two factors and along an extension of scalars. The third is polarization, by which a
linear map into a ring whose every value squares to zero has pairwise anticommuting
values. The fourth is the same principle for a direct sum, whose summands play the role of
the generators.

Nothing here has physics content, and nothing is assumed finite.

## ii. Key results

- `Algebra.range_le_of_adjoin_eq_top`, `Algebra.apply_mem_of_mem_adjoin`,
  `Algebra.commute_of_adjoin_eq_top` : the range of an algebra map, the subalgebras it
  carries a generated subalgebra into, and its commutation with an element, are
  determined on a generating set.
- `Algebra.TensorProduct.eq_top_of_tmul_one_of_one_tmul` : a tensor product is generated by
  its two factors.
- `Algebra.TensorProduct.adjoin_one_tmul_eq_top` : extension of scalars preserves
  generation.
- `LinearMap.mul_swap_of_mul_self` : polarization.
- `DirectSum.mem_of_lof` : a subalgebra containing the image of every summand contains the
  whole image.
- `DirectSum.mul_self_iff_lof` : square-zero on a direct sum is square-zero on each
  summand plus anticommutation across summands.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Algebras generated by a set
- B. Generating a tensor product
  - B.1. Generation by the two factors
  - B.2. Generation after an extension of scalars
- C. Polarization
- D. Maps out of a direct sum into a ring
  - D.1. Membership and commutation
  - D.2. Anticommutation and the square-zero condition

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Algebras generated by a set

## B. Generating a tensor product

### B.1. Generation by the two factors
### B.2. Generation after an extension of scalars

## D. Maps out of a direct sum into a ring

A linear map out of a direct sum is determined by its restrictions to the summands, so a
relation between the images of two such maps which is stable under addition in each
argument need only be checked on the summands. The lemmas below are the instances of that
principle used when the generators of an algebra are grouped into summands.
### D.2. Anticommutation and the square-zero condition

declarations.name: Algebra.range_le_of_adjoin_eq_top
declarations.doc:
If `s` generates `A` and a subalgebra `S` of `B` contains the image of `s`, then it
contains the whole range of an algebra map `A →ₐ[R] B`.
declarations.statement:
lemma range_le_of_adjoin_eq_top {s : Set A} (hs : Algebra.adjoin R s = ⊤) (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    {S : Subalgebra R B} (h : ∀ x ∈ s, φ x ∈ S) : φ.range ≤ S

declarations.name: Algebra.apply_mem_of_mem_adjoin
declarations.doc:
An algebra map carrying a generating set into a subalgebra `S` carries the generated
subalgebra into `S`. This is what extends the stability of a subalgebra under an
endomorphism from its generators to all of its elements.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_mem_of_mem_adjoin {s : Set A} (φ : A →ₐ[R] B) {S : Subalgebra R B}
    (h : ∀ x ∈ s, φ x ∈ S) {x : A} (hx : x ∈ Algebra.adjoin R s) : φ x ∈ S

declarations.name: Algebra.commute_of_adjoin_eq_top
declarations.doc:
If `s` generates `A` and `y` commutes with the image of `s` under an algebra map, then
`y` commutes with the whole image. This is what extends a commutation relation from
generators to a factor of a tensor product.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_of_adjoin_eq_top {s : Set A} (hs : Algebra.adjoin R s = ⊤) (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    {y : B} (h : ∀ x ∈ s, Commute (φ x) y) (a : A) : Commute (φ a) y

declarations.name: Algebra.TensorProduct.mem_of_tmul_one_of_one_tmul
declarations.doc:
A subalgebra of `A ⊗[R] B` containing every `a ⊗ₜ 1` and every `1 ⊗ₜ b` contains
everything, since a pure tensor is the product of the two.

declarations.name: Algebra.TensorProduct.eq_top_of_tmul_one_of_one_tmul
declarations.doc:
A subalgebra of `A ⊗[R] B` containing every `a ⊗ₜ 1` and every `1 ⊗ₜ b` is the whole
algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_top_of_tmul_one_of_one_tmul {S : Subalgebra R (A ⊗[R] B)}
    (hA : ∀ a : A, a ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : B) ∈ S) (hB : ∀ b : B, (1 : A) ⊗ₜ[R] b ∈ S) : S = ⊤

declarations.name: Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_mul_comm
declarations.doc:
A commutative right factor is central in the tensor product. Stated as an equation of
products at abstract types, so that it can be instantiated on a concrete tensor product
without unifying its multiplication instances.
declarations.statement:
lemma includeRight_mul_comm (b : B) (x : A ⊗[R] B) :
    x * includeRight (R := R) (A := A) b = includeRight (R := R) (A := A) b * x

declarations.name: Algebra.TensorProduct.mem_adjoin_one_tmul
declarations.doc:
Extension of scalars on the elements `1 ⊗ₜ a`. If `s` generates `A` over `R` then
every `1 ⊗ₜ a` lies in the `S`-subalgebra of `S ⊗[R] A` generated by `1 ⊗ₜ s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_adjoin_one_tmul (hs : Algebra.adjoin R s = ⊤) (a : A) :
    (1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R] a ∈ Algebra.adjoin S ((fun a : A => (1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R] a) '' s)

declarations.name: Algebra.TensorProduct.mem_adjoin_one_tmul_of_generates
declarations.doc: Every element of a base change lies in the subalgebra generated by the `1 ⊗ₜ s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_adjoin_one_tmul_of_generates (hs : Algebra.adjoin R s = ⊤) (x : S ⊗[R] A) :
    x ∈ Algebra.adjoin S ((fun a : A => (1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R] a) '' s)

declarations.name: Algebra.TensorProduct.adjoin_one_tmul_eq_top
declarations.doc:
Extension of scalars preserves generation. If `s` generates `A` over `R` then the
elements `1 ⊗ₜ a`, for `a ∈ s`, generate `S ⊗[R] A` over `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoin_one_tmul_eq_top (hs : Algebra.adjoin R s = ⊤) :
    Algebra.adjoin S ((fun a : A => (1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R] a) '' s)
      = (⊤ : Subalgebra S (S ⊗[R] A))

declarations.name: LinearMap.mul_swap_of_mul_self
declarations.doc:
Polarization. If every value of a linear map into a ring squares to zero, then any two
values anticommute. Applied to a space of fermionic generators, this is what makes the
single relation "every vector squares to zero" carry the anticommutation of distinct
generators, including generators of different species, which sit in the same space.
declarations.statement:
lemma LinearMap.mul_swap_of_mul_self {R M B : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M]
    [Module R M] [Ring B] [Algebra R B] (f : M →ₗ[R] B) (h : ∀ v, f v * f v = 0) (v w : M) :
    f v * f w = -(f w * f v)

declarations.name: DirectSum.mem_of_lof
declarations.doc: If a subalgebra contains the image of every summand, it contains the whole image.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lof {S : Subalgebra R B} {F : (⨁ i, M i) →ₗ[R] B}
    (h : ∀ i x, F (lof R ι M i x) ∈ S) (v : ⨁ i, M i) : F v ∈ S

declarations.name: DirectSum.commute_of_lof_left
declarations.doc:
If the image of every summand commutes with a fixed element, so does the whole
image.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_of_lof_left {F : (⨁ i, M i) →ₗ[R] B} {b : B}
    (h : ∀ i x, Commute (F (lof R ι M i x)) b) (v : ⨁ i, M i) : Commute (F v) b

declarations.name: DirectSum.commute_of_lof
declarations.doc:
Commutation extends from the summands. If the image of every summand of one direct
sum commutes with the image of every summand of another, then the two images commute
elementwise.

declarations.name: DirectSum.mul_swap_of_lof
declarations.doc: Anticommutation extends from the summands.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_swap_of_lof {F : (⨁ i, M i) →ₗ[R] B}
    (h : ∀ i j x y, F (lof R ι M i x) * F (lof R ι M j y)
      = -(F (lof R ι M j y) * F (lof R ι M i x)))
    (v w : ⨁ i, M i) : F v * F w = -(F w * F v)

declarations.name: DirectSum.mul_self_of_lof
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_self_of_lof {F : (⨁ i, M i) →ₗ[R] B}
    (hsq : ∀ i x, F (lof R ι M i x) * F (lof R ι M i x) = 0)
    (hswap : ∀ i j x y, F (lof R ι M i x) * F (lof R ι M j y)
      = -(F (lof R ι M j y) * F (lof R ι M i x)))
    (v : ⨁ i, M i) : F v * F v = 0

declarations.name: DirectSum.mul_self_iff_lof
declarations.doc:
Square-zero on a direct sum is not square-zero summand by summand. It is equivalent to
square-zero on each summand together with anticommutation between the images of any two
summands, the second condition being vacuous only when there is at most one summand.
This is the precise sense in which Fermi statistics for a family of species is more than
the Fermi statistics of the individual species.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_self_iff_lof {F : (⨁ i, M i) →ₗ[R] B} :
    (∀ v, F v * F v = 0) ↔
      ((∀ i x, F (lof R ι M i x) * F (lof R ι M i x) = 0) ∧
        ∀ i j x y, F (lof R ι M i x) * F (lof R ι M j y)
          = -(F (lof R ι M j y) * F (lof R ι M i x)))

modules.title: Representations acting by algebra maps
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A representation of a monoid on an algebra need not respect the multiplication; the ones
that do are the ones a field theory uses, and this file collects the two constructions on
them that are otherwise missing.

Section A is about `Representation.tprod` on a tensor product of two algebras. The unit and
the product of `A ⊗[k] B` are given by those of the factors, so a pair of unit-preserving
or multiplicative representations gives one on the tensor product. The lemmas are stated at
abstract types with the factor laws as hypotheses, which is what lets them be applied at a
large concrete algebra without unfolding it: neither the unit nor the product of a free
algebra presented as a quotient can be reduced cheaply.

Section B restricts a representation to a subalgebra it preserves. The invariance
hypothesis is stated pointwise, in the form the ambient invariance lemmas produce.

Section C restricts the scalars of a representation: a representation on a complex vector
space is in particular a representation on the underlying real vector space.

Section E bundles an algebra map together with equivariance for two independently supplied
pairs of representations of two monoids, the two target representations being multiplicative
on the whole target: `Representation.EquivariantAlgHom`. Nothing relates the two pairs, the
target actions are not assumed to commute, and they are not assumed unital, which over a
monoid does not follow from multiplicativity. Section F base changes such a map along an
extension of scalars, in both directions, and section G records the one affine identity an
algebra map is used for when a representation acts on generators by a shift.

## ii. Key results

- `Representation.tprod_apply_one`, `Representation.tprod_apply_one_tmul`,
  `Representation.tprod_apply_tmul_one` : the unit laws on a tensor product.
- `Representation.tprod_apply_mul` : multiplicativity on a tensor product.
- `Representation.restrictSubalgebra` : the restriction to an invariant subalgebra, with
  `Representation.inclusion_restrictSubalgebra` for two nested ones.
- `Representation.restrictScalars` : the restriction of scalars.
- `Representation.toAlgHom` : a multiplicative representation of a group as algebra maps.
- `Representation.EquivariantAlgHom` : an algebra map intertwining two pairs of
  representations, with `EquivariantAlgHom.id`, `EquivariantAlgHom.comp`,
  `EquivariantAlgHom.compEquiv`, `EquivariantAlgHom.restrictSubalgebra` and
  `EquivariantAlgHom.compFst`.
- `Representation.baseChange` : the base change of a representation, with
  `Representation.baseChange_naturality`.
- `Representation.liftEquiv_baseChange` : base change preserves equivariance, and
  `Representation.EquivariantAlgHom.liftEquivBaseChange` : equivariant maps out of a base
  change are the equivariant maps over the smaller ring.
- `AlgHom.map_add_smul_one` : an algebra map on an affine combination `x + z • 1`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Tensor products of multiplicative representations
- B. Restriction to an invariant subalgebra
- C. Restriction of scalars
- D. Multiplicative representations as algebra maps
- E. Equivariant algebra maps
- F. Base change of an equivariant algebra map
- G. Affine combinations under an algebra map

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: Representation.tprod_apply_one
declarations.doc: The tensor product of two unit-preserving representations preserves the unit.
declarations.statement:
lemma tprod_apply_one {k G A B : Type*} [CommSemiring k] [Monoid G]
    [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [Ring B] [Algebra k B]
    (ρ : Representation k G A) (σ : Representation k G B) (g : G)
    (hρ : ρ g 1 = 1) (hσ : σ g 1 = 1) : (ρ.tprod σ) g 1 = 1

declarations.name: Representation.tprod_apply_one_tmul
declarations.doc: On a pure tensor whose left entry is the unit only the right factor moves.
declarations.statement:
lemma tprod_apply_one_tmul {k G A B : Type*} [CommSemiring k]
    [Monoid G] [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [Ring B] [Algebra k B]
    (ρ : Representation k G A) (σ : Representation k G B) (g : G)
    (hρ : ρ g 1 = 1) (y : B) :
    (ρ.tprod σ) g ((1 : A) ⊗ₜ[k] y) = (1 : A) ⊗ₜ[k] σ g y

declarations.name: Representation.tprod_apply_tmul_one
declarations.doc: On a pure tensor whose right entry is the unit only the left factor moves.
declarations.statement:
lemma tprod_apply_tmul_one {k G A B : Type*} [CommSemiring k]
    [Monoid G] [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [Ring B] [Algebra k B]
    (ρ : Representation k G A) (σ : Representation k G B) (g : G) (x : A)
    (hσ : σ g 1 = 1) :
    (ρ.tprod σ) g (x ⊗ₜ[k] (1 : B)) = ρ g x ⊗ₜ[k] (1 : B)

declarations.name: Representation.tprod_apply_mul
declarations.doc:
The tensor product of two multiplicative representations on algebras is
multiplicative.
declarations.statement:
lemma tprod_apply_mul {k G A B : Type*} [CommSemiring k] [Monoid G]
    [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [Ring B] [Algebra k B]
    (ρ : Representation k G A) (σ : Representation k G B)
    (hρ : ∀ (g : G) (x y : A), ρ g (x * y) = ρ g x * ρ g y)
    (hσ : ∀ (g : G) (x y : B), σ g (x * y) = σ g x * σ g y)
    (g : G) (x y : A ⊗[k] B) :
    (ρ.tprod σ) g (x * y) = (ρ.tprod σ) g x * (ρ.tprod σ) g y

declarations.name: Representation.restrictSubalgebra
declarations.doc: The restriction of a representation to a subalgebra each group element preserves.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictSubalgebra {k A G : Type*} [CommSemiring k]
    [Monoid G] [Semiring A] [Algebra k A] (ρ : Representation k G A) (S : Subalgebra k A)
    (hS : ∀ (g : G) {x : A}, x ∈ S → ρ g x ∈ S) : Representation k G S

declarations.name: Representation.coe_restrictSubalgebra
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_restrictSubalgebra {k A G : Type*} [CommSemiring k]
    [Monoid G] [Semiring A] [Algebra k A] (ρ : Representation k G A) (S : Subalgebra k A)
    (hS : ∀ (g : G) {x : A}, x ∈ S → ρ g x ∈ S) (g : G) (x : S) :
    (ρ.restrictSubalgebra S hS g x : A) = ρ g (x : A)

declarations.name: Representation.inclusion_restrictSubalgebra
declarations.doc:
The restrictions to two nested invariant subalgebras agree along the inclusion of the
smaller into the larger.
declarations.statement:
lemma inclusion_restrictSubalgebra {k A G : Type*} [CommSemiring k]
    [Monoid G] [Semiring A] [Algebra k A] (ρ : Representation k G A) {S S' : Subalgebra k A}
    (h : S ≤ S') (hS : ∀ (g : G) {x : A}, x ∈ S → ρ g x ∈ S)
    (hS' : ∀ (g : G) {x : A}, x ∈ S' → ρ g x ∈ S') (g : G) (x : S) :
    Subalgebra.inclusion h (ρ.restrictSubalgebra S hS g x)
      = ρ.restrictSubalgebra S' hS' g (Subalgebra.inclusion h x)

declarations.name: Representation.restrictScalars
declarations.doc:
The restriction of scalars of a representation: a representation on an `S`-module is a
representation on the same space as an `R`-module, for `R` acting through `S`.
declarations.statement:
def restrictScalars (R : Type*) {S G V : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S] [Monoid G]
    [AddCommMonoid V] [Module R V] [Module S V] [LinearMap.CompatibleSMul V V R S]
    (ρ : Representation S G V) : Representation R G V

declarations.name: Representation.restrictScalars_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma restrictScalars_apply (R : Type*) {S G V : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S]
    [Monoid G] [AddCommMonoid V] [Module R V] [Module S V] [LinearMap.CompatibleSMul V V R S]
    (ρ : Representation S G V) (g : G) (x : V) : ρ.restrictScalars R g x = ρ g x

declarations.name: Representation.apply_one_of_mul
declarations.doc:
A representation of a group acting by multiplicative maps preserves the unit. The
action of `g` is surjective, its inverse being the action of `g⁻¹`, so `ρ g 1` is a left
unit on the whole algebra.
declarations.statement: lemma apply_one_of_mul (g : G) : ρ g 1 = 1

declarations.name: Representation.toAlgHom
declarations.doc:
A representation of a group acting by multiplicative maps acts by algebra
endomorphisms.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def toAlgHom (g : G) : A →ₐ[k] A

declarations.name: Representation.toAlgHom_apply
declarations.statement: lemma toAlgHom_apply (g : G) (x : A) : ρ.toAlgHom hρ g x = ρ g x

declarations.name: Representation.EquivariantAlgHom
declarations.doc:
An algebra map `A →ₐ[k] B` intertwining two pairs of representations, `ρ₁, σ₁` of the
monoid `G₁` and `ρ₂, σ₂` of the monoid `G₂`, with both target representations multiplicative
on the whole of `B`. The two pairs are independent: the actions of `G₁` and `G₂` are not
assumed to commute, and no relation between them is used. Unit preservation is not a field
and does not follow from multiplicativity over a monoid; when the acting monoid is a group
and the target is a ring it does (`Representation.apply_one_of_mul`), and the target action
is then by algebra endomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
structure EquivariantAlgHom (ρ₁ : Representation k G₁ A) (σ₁ : Representation k G₁ B)
    (ρ₂ : Representation k G₂ A) (σ₂ : Representation k G₂ B) where
  /-- The underlying algebra map. -/
  toAlgHom : A →ₐ[k] B
  /-- The map is equivariant for the first pair of representations. -/
  map_fst : ∀ (g : G₁) (x : A), toAlgHom (ρ₁ g x) = σ₁ g (toAlgHom x)
  /-- The map is equivariant for the second pair of representations. -/
  map_snd : ∀ (g : G₂) (x : A), toAlgHom (ρ₂ g x) = σ₂ g (toAlgHom x)
  /-- The first target action is multiplicative on the whole of `B`. -/
  fst_mul : ∀ (g : G₁) (b₁ b₂ : B), σ₁ g (b₁ * b₂) = σ₁ g b₁ * σ₁ g b₂
  /-- The second target action is multiplicative on the whole of `B`. -/
  snd_mul : ∀ (g : G₂) (b₁ b₂ : B), σ₂ g (b₁ * b₂) = σ₂ g b₁ * σ₂ g b₂

declarations.name: Representation.EquivariantAlgHom.id
declarations.doc: The identity map of an algebra carrying two multiplicative representations.

declarations.name: Representation.EquivariantAlgHom.id_toAlgHom
declarations.statement:
lemma id_toAlgHom (h₁ : ∀ (g : G₁) (x y : A), ρ₁ g (x * y) = ρ₁ g x * ρ₁ g y)
    (h₂ : ∀ (g : G₂) (x y : A), ρ₂ g (x * y) = ρ₂ g x * ρ₂ g y) :
    (EquivariantAlgHom.id ρ₁ ρ₂ h₁ h₂).toAlgHom = AlgHom.id k A

declarations.name: Representation.EquivariantAlgHom.comp
declarations.doc:
The precomposition with an algebra map into the source intertwining two representations
on its own source with the two source representations; the target and its two actions are
unchanged.
declarations.statement:
def comp {A' : Type*} [Semiring A'] [Algebra k A'] {ρ₁' : Representation k G₁ A'}
    {ρ₂' : Representation k G₂ A'} (f : EquivariantAlgHom ρ₁ σ₁ ρ₂ σ₂) (φ : A' →ₐ[k] A)
    (hφ₁ : ∀ (g : G₁) (x : A'), φ (ρ₁' g x) = ρ₁ g (φ x))
    (hφ₂ : ∀ (g : G₂) (x : A'), φ (ρ₂' g x) = ρ₂ g (φ x)) :
    EquivariantAlgHom ρ₁' σ₁ ρ₂' σ₂

declarations.name: Representation.EquivariantAlgHom.comp_toAlgHom
declarations.statement:
lemma comp_toAlgHom {A' : Type*} [Semiring A'] [Algebra k A'] {ρ₁' : Representation k G₁ A'}
    {ρ₂' : Representation k G₂ A'} (f : EquivariantAlgHom ρ₁ σ₁ ρ₂ σ₂) (φ : A' →ₐ[k] A)
    (hφ₁ : ∀ (g : G₁) (x : A'), φ (ρ₁' g x) = ρ₁ g (φ x))
    (hφ₂ : ∀ (g : G₂) (x : A'), φ (ρ₂' g x) = ρ₂ g (φ x)) :
    (f.comp φ hφ₁ hφ₂).toAlgHom = f.toAlgHom.comp φ

declarations.name: Representation.EquivariantAlgHom.compEquiv
declarations.doc:
Precomposition with an algebra equivalence of the sources intertwining the source
representations: equivariant maps out of equivalent sources correspond.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def compEquiv {A' : Type*} [Semiring A'] [Algebra k A']
    {ρ₁' : Representation k G₁ A'} {ρ₂' : Representation k G₂ A'} (e : A' ≃ₐ[k] A)
    (he₁ : ∀ (g : G₁) (x : A'), e (ρ₁' g x) = ρ₁ g (e x))
    (he₂ : ∀ (g : G₂) (x : A'), e (ρ₂' g x) = ρ₂ g (e x)) :
    EquivariantAlgHom ρ₁ σ₁ ρ₂ σ₂ ≃ EquivariantAlgHom ρ₁' σ₁ ρ₂' σ₂

declarations.name: Representation.EquivariantAlgHom.compEquiv_toAlgHom
declarations.statement:
lemma compEquiv_toAlgHom {A' : Type*} [Semiring A'] [Algebra k A']
    {ρ₁' : Representation k G₁ A'} {ρ₂' : Representation k G₂ A'} (e : A' ≃ₐ[k] A)
    (he₁ : ∀ (g : G₁) (x : A'), e (ρ₁' g x) = ρ₁ g (e x))
    (he₂ : ∀ (g : G₂) (x : A'), e (ρ₂' g x) = ρ₂ g (e x))
    (f : EquivariantAlgHom ρ₁ σ₁ ρ₂ σ₂) :
    (compEquiv e he₁ he₂ f).toAlgHom = f.toAlgHom.comp e.toAlgHom

declarations.name: Representation.EquivariantAlgHom.compEquiv_symm_toAlgHom
declarations.statement:
lemma compEquiv_symm_toAlgHom {A' : Type*} [Semiring A'] [Algebra k A']
    {ρ₁' : Representation k G₁ A'} {ρ₂' : Representation k G₂ A'} (e : A' ≃ₐ[k] A)
    (he₁ : ∀ (g : G₁) (x : A'), e (ρ₁' g x) = ρ₁ g (e x))
    (he₂ : ∀ (g : G₂) (x : A'), e (ρ₂' g x) = ρ₂ g (e x))
    (f : EquivariantAlgHom ρ₁' σ₁ ρ₂' σ₂) :
    ((compEquiv e he₁ he₂).symm f).toAlgHom = f.toAlgHom.comp e.symm.toAlgHom

declarations.name: Representation.EquivariantAlgHom.restrictSubalgebra
declarations.doc:
The restriction to a subalgebra of the source preserved by both source representations,
along its inclusion; the target and its two actions are unchanged.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictSubalgebra (f : EquivariantAlgHom ρ₁ σ₁ ρ₂ σ₂) (S : Subalgebra k A)
    (hS₁ : ∀ (g : G₁) {x : A}, x ∈ S → ρ₁ g x ∈ S)
    (hS₂ : ∀ (g : G₂) {x : A}, x ∈ S → ρ₂ g x ∈ S) :
    EquivariantAlgHom (ρ₁.restrictSubalgebra S hS₁) σ₁ (ρ₂.restrictSubalgebra S hS₂) σ₂

declarations.name: Representation.EquivariantAlgHom.restrictSubalgebra_toAlgHom_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma restrictSubalgebra_toAlgHom_apply (f : EquivariantAlgHom ρ₁ σ₁ ρ₂ σ₂) (S : Subalgebra k A)
    (hS₁ : ∀ (g : G₁) {x : A}, x ∈ S → ρ₁ g x ∈ S)
    (hS₂ : ∀ (g : G₂) {x : A}, x ∈ S → ρ₂ g x ∈ S) (x : S) :
    (f.restrictSubalgebra S hS₁ hS₂).toAlgHom x = f.toAlgHom x

declarations.name: Representation.EquivariantAlgHom.compFst
declarations.doc:
The precomposition of the first pair of representations with a monoid map; the algebra
map is unchanged.
declarations.statement:
def compFst {H : Type*} [Monoid H] (f : EquivariantAlgHom ρ₁ σ₁ ρ₂ σ₂) (φ : H →* G₁) :
    EquivariantAlgHom (ρ₁.comp φ) (σ₁.comp φ) ρ₂ σ₂

declarations.name: Representation.EquivariantAlgHom.compFst_toAlgHom
declarations.statement:
lemma compFst_toAlgHom {H : Type*} [Monoid H] (f : EquivariantAlgHom ρ₁ σ₁ ρ₂ σ₂) (φ : H →* G₁) :
    (f.compFst φ).toAlgHom = f.toAlgHom

declarations.name: Representation.liftEquiv_baseChange
declarations.doc:
Base change along `R → S` preserves equivariance: the `S`-algebra map out of `S ⊗[R] A`
corresponding to an equivariant `R`-algebra map `f` intertwines the base change of the
source action with the target action.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftEquiv_baseChange {R S A B G : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S] [Algebra R S]
    [Semiring A] [Algebra R A] [Semiring B] [Algebra S B] [Algebra R B] [IsScalarTower R S B]
    [Monoid G] (f : A →ₐ[R] B) (ρ : Representation R G A) (σ : Representation S G B)
    (hf : ∀ (g : G) (x : A), f (ρ g x) = σ g (f x)) (g : G) (x : S ⊗[R] A) :
    AlgHom.liftEquiv R S A B f (LinearMap.baseChange S (ρ g) x)
      = σ g (AlgHom.liftEquiv R S A B f x)

declarations.name: Representation.baseChange
declarations.doc:
The base change of a representation along `R → S`: the same action on the second factor
of `S ⊗[R] M`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def baseChange {R M G : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (S : Type*) [CommSemiring S]
    [Algebra R S] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Monoid G] (ρ : Representation R G M) :
    Representation S G (S ⊗[R] M)

declarations.name: Representation.baseChange_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma baseChange_tmul {R M G : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (S : Type*) [CommSemiring S]
    [Algebra R S] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Monoid G] (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G)
    (s : S) (x : M) : baseChange S ρ g (s ⊗ₜ[R] x) = s ⊗ₜ[R] ρ g x

declarations.name: Representation.baseChange_naturality
declarations.doc:
Base change is natural: a linear map intertwining two representations base changes to
one intertwining their base changes.
declarations.statement:
lemma baseChange_naturality {R M N G : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (S : Type*) [CommSemiring S]
    [Algebra R S] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [Monoid G]
    {ρ : Representation R G M} {σ : Representation R G N} (f : M →ₗ[R] N)
    (h : ∀ (g : G) (x : M), f (ρ g x) = σ g (f x)) (g : G) (y : S ⊗[R] M) :
    LinearMap.baseChange S f (baseChange S ρ g y)
      = baseChange S σ g (LinearMap.baseChange S f y)

declarations.name: Representation.eq_baseChange_of_tmul
declarations.doc:
A representation on a base change acting on the pure tensors through a representation on
the second factor is that representation's base change.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_baseChange_of_tmul {R S A G : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S] [Algebra R S]
    [AddCommMonoid A] [Module R A] [Monoid G] (ρ : Representation R G A)
    (ρ' : Representation S G (S ⊗[R] A))
    (h : ∀ (g : G) (s : S) (x : A), ρ' g (s ⊗ₜ[R] x) = s ⊗ₜ[R] ρ g x) (g : G) (y : S ⊗[R] A) :
    ρ' g y = LinearMap.baseChange S (ρ g) y

declarations.name: Representation.EquivariantAlgHom.liftEquivBaseChange
declarations.doc:
For a target over `S`, the equivariant `R`-algebra maps out of `A` are the equivariant
`S`-algebra maps out of the base change `S ⊗[R] A`, by `AlgHom.liftEquiv`. The two source
actions on the base change are recognised by their values on the pure tensors, and the
target keeps its `S`-actions, restricted to `R` on the left-hand side.

declarations.name: AlgHom.map_add_smul_one
declarations.doc:
An algebra map carries an affine combination `x + z • 1` to the same combination of the
image, the shift being the image of a scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma AlgHom.map_add_smul_one {k A B : Type*} [CommSemiring k] [Semiring A] [Algebra k A]
    [Semiring B] [Algebra k B] (f : A →ₐ[k] B) (x : A) (z : k) :
    f (x + z • (1 : A)) = f x + z • (1 : B)

modules.title: Linear operators that do not enlarge support
modules.doc:
A linear operator on a space of functions with support contained in the support of the argument.

## i. Overview

A linear operator on a space of functions with support contained in the support of the argument. It
acts on compactly supported functions and has a kernel. Such operators agree at a point when their
arguments agree near it.

## ii. Key results

- `compactFields` : Compactly supported admissible fields form the source space of Green operators.
- `compactSources` : The compact test-field space depends on the admissible fields rather than the
  operator.
- `compactOperator` : The restriction of the equation to compactly supported admissible fields.
- `solutionSpace` : Homogeneous admissible fields are the kernel of the field operator.
- `IsLocalFieldSpace` : Admissibility is local when a function locally agreeing with admissible
  fields is admissible.
- `FieldIntertwiner` : A local linear map that commutes with two field equations.
- `compactMap` : Restrict the local intertwiner to compact test fields.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Linear field equations and compact sources
- B. Local field equations and causal agreement
- C. Differential constraints and Green responses

## iv. References

None.

## A. Linear field equations and compact sources

- `compactFields` : Compactly supported admissible fields form the source space of Green operators.
- `compactSources` : The compact test-field space depends on the admissible fields rather than the
  operator.
- `compactOperator` : The restriction of the equation to compactly supported admissible fields.
- `solutionSpace` : Homogeneous admissible fields are the kernel of the field operator.

Lemmas: `operator_mem_compactSources`, `compactOperator_coe`, `mem_solutionSpace`.

## B. Local field equations and causal agreement

- `IsLocalFieldSpace` : Admissibility is local when a function locally agreeing with admissible
  fields is admissible.

Lemmas: `notMem_tsupport_sub_iff_eventuallyEq`, `operator_eventuallyEq`,
`operator_eq_of_eventuallyEq`.

## C. Differential constraints and Green responses

- `FieldIntertwiner` : A local linear map that commutes with two field equations.
- `compactMap` : Restrict the local intertwiner to compact test fields.

declarations.name: LocalOperator
declarations.doc:
A linear equation on admissible fields with the support locality of a differential operator.
Smoothness is supplied by the admissible field submodule in each application.
declarations.statement:
structure LocalOperator (S : Submodule 𝕜 (M → V)) where
  /-- The field differential operator on admissible fields. -/
  operator : S →ₗ[𝕜] S
  /-- A local field equation cannot create support away from the field. -/
  support_operator : ∀ u : S, tsupport (operator u : M → V) ⊆ tsupport (u : M → V)

declarations.name: compactFields
declarations.doc: Compactly supported admissible fields form the source space of Green operators.
declarations.statement: def compactFields (S : Submodule 𝕜 (M → V)) : Submodule 𝕜 S

declarations.name: LocalOperator.compactSources
declarations.doc: The compact test-field space depends on the admissible fields rather than the operator.
declarations.statement: abbrev compactSources (_P : LocalOperator S) : Submodule 𝕜 S

declarations.name: LocalOperator.operator_mem_compactSources
declarations.doc: The equation preserves compact sources by locality.
declarations.statement:
lemma operator_mem_compactSources (u : P.compactSources) :
    P.operator u.val ∈ P.compactSources

declarations.name: LocalOperator.compactOperator
declarations.doc: The restriction of the equation to compactly supported admissible fields.
declarations.statement: def compactOperator : P.compactSources →ₗ[𝕜] P.compactSources

declarations.name: LocalOperator.compactOperator_coe
declarations.statement:
lemma compactOperator_coe (u : P.compactSources) :
    (P.compactOperator u).val = P.operator u.val

declarations.name: LocalOperator.solutionSpace
declarations.doc: Homogeneous admissible fields are the kernel of the field operator.
declarations.statement: def solutionSpace : Submodule 𝕜 S

declarations.name: LocalOperator.mem_solutionSpace
declarations.statement: lemma mem_solutionSpace (u : S) : u ∈ P.solutionSpace ↔ P.operator u = 0

declarations.name: IsLocalFieldSpace
declarations.doc: Admissibility is local when a function locally agreeing with admissible fields is admissible.
declarations.statement: def IsLocalFieldSpace (S : Submodule 𝕜 (M → V)) : Prop

declarations.name: notMem_tsupport_sub_iff_eventuallyEq
declarations.doc: Vanishing support of a difference at a point is exactly equality of field germs.
declarations.statement:
lemma notMem_tsupport_sub_iff_eventuallyEq {f g : M → V} {x : M} :
    x ∉ tsupport (f - g) ↔ f =ᶠ[𝓝 x] g

declarations.name: LocalOperator.operator_eventuallyEq
declarations.doc: A local field operator preserves equality of germs.

declarations.name: LocalOperator.operator_eq_of_eventuallyEq
declarations.doc: Equality of field germs implies equality of their equations at the observation point.

declarations.name: FieldIntertwiner
declarations.doc:
A local linear map that commutes with two field equations.
The two equations may act on different field types, as for divergence of a vector wave equation.
declarations.statement:
structure FieldIntertwiner (P : LocalOperator S) (R : LocalOperator T) where
  /-- The differential constraint or transformation of fields. -/
  toLinearMap : S →ₗ[𝕜] T
  /-- Differential constraints do not enlarge support. -/
  support : ∀ u, tsupport (toLinearMap u : M → W) ⊆ tsupport (u : M → V)
  /-- Apply the constraint before or after the corresponding field equation. -/
  commutes : ∀ u, R.operator (toLinearMap u) = toLinearMap (P.operator u)

declarations.name: FieldIntertwiner.compactMap
declarations.doc: Restrict the local intertwiner to compact test fields.
declarations.statement: def compactMap : P.compactSources →ₗ[𝕜] R.compactSources

modules.title: Hölder duality in finite dimensions
modules.doc:
The dual norm of an `ℓp` coordinate norm is the `ℓq` norm of the values on the basis.

## i. Overview

A continuous linear functional on a finite-dimensional normed space is determined by its values on
a basis. When the norm is the `ℓp` norm of the coordinates in that basis, the norm of a functional
is the `ℓq` norm of its values, `q` the Hölder conjugate of `p`; for the sup norm it is the `ℓ1`
norm. So the unit ball of the dual is the closed `ℓq` ball, resp. the `ℓ1` ball, of value vectors.

## ii. Key results

- `HolderDual.coeffEquiv` : a functional is its vector of values on a basis.
- `HolderDual.dualLp_norm_eq` : Hölder duality for `1 < p < ∞`.
- `HolderDual.dualSup_norm_eq` : Hölder duality for `p = ∞`.
- `HolderDual.dualLpEquiv`, `HolderDual.dualSupEquiv` : the unit ball of the dual in coordinates.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Functionals from their values on a basis
- B. Hölder duality, `1 < p < ∞`
- C. Hölder duality, `p = ∞`

## iv. References

- W. Rudin, *Functional Analysis*, 2nd ed., McGraw-Hill, 1991.

declarations.doc: Hölder's inequality for the absolute value of a finite sum.
declarations.statement:

declarations.doc: A functional is its vector of values on the basis.

modules.title: Elementary real bounds
modules.doc:
Elementary real estimates: suprema of sums, bounds up to `1 / (n + 1)`, and weighted averages.

## i. Overview

Three elementary estimates for real numbers: suprema of sums over a codirected family, inequalities
up to `1 / (n + 1)` for every `n`, and averages that put almost all weight on one term.

## ii. Key results

- `Real.ciSup_add` : suprema add along a family in which any two indices are dominated by a third.
- `Real.le_of_forall_nat_le_add` : `a ≤ b` if `a ≤ b + 1 / (n + 1)` for every `n`.
- `Real.abs_sum_mul_sub_le` : an average with weight at least `1 - θ` on one term is within
  `2 * A * θ` of it, for terms bounded by `A`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Suprema
- B. Averages

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: Real.ciSup_add
declarations.doc: Suprema of two bounded families add when any two indices are dominated by a common one.
declarations.statement:
lemma ciSup_add {ι : Type*} [Nonempty ι] {f g : ι → ℝ} (hf : BddAbove (Set.range f))
    (hg : BddAbove (Set.range g)) (h : ∀ i j, ∃ k, f i ≤ f k ∧ g j ≤ g k) :
    ⨆ i, (f i + g i) = (⨆ i, f i) + ⨆ i, g i

declarations.name: Real.le_of_forall_nat_le_add
declarations.doc: A real number that is at most `b + 1 / (n + 1)` for every `n` is at most `b`.
declarations.statement: lemma le_of_forall_nat_le_add {a b : ℝ} (h : ∀ n : ℕ, a ≤ b + 1 / (n + 1)) : a ≤ b

declarations.name: Real.abs_sum_mul_sub_le
declarations.doc:
An average of numbers bounded by `A`, with weight at least `1 - θ` on the `i`-th number, is
within `2 * A * θ` of it.

modules.title: Bounds on iterated derivatives
modules.doc:
Norm bounds for iterated Fréchet derivatives of a composition with a continuous linear map and of
a product.

## i. Overview

Composing with a continuous linear map `L` multiplies the `n`th derivative by at most `‖L‖ⁿ`. The
`k`th derivative of a product of two smooth real functions is bounded by `2ᵏ` times the product of
bounds of the factors. These estimates control the seminorms of Schwartz functions under linear
changes of variables and under multiplication with smooth cutoffs.

## ii. Key results

- `IteratedFDerivBounds.norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_clm_le` : composition with a linear map.
- `IteratedFDerivBounds.norm_iteratedFDeriv_mul_le_two_pow` : the Leibniz bound for a product.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Composition with a linear map
- B. Products

## iv. References

None.

## A. Composition with a linear map

- `IteratedFDerivBounds.norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_clm_le` : composition with a linear map.

## B. Products

- `IteratedFDerivBounds.norm_iteratedFDeriv_mul_le_two_pow` : the Leibniz bound for a product.

declarations.name: IteratedFDerivBounds.norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_clm_le
declarations.doc:
Composing with a continuous linear map costs the operator norm to the order of the
derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_clm_le {G : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace ℝ G]
    {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [NormedSpace ℝ H] (L : G →L[ℝ] E) {f : E → H}
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f) (n : ℕ) (y : G) :
    ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (f ∘ L) y‖ ≤ ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n f (L y)‖ * ‖L‖ ^ n

declarations.name: IteratedFDerivBounds.norm_iteratedFDeriv_mul_le_two_pow
declarations.doc:
**The Leibniz bound.** If the derivatives of order up to `k` of `b` and `v` are bounded by `B`
and `S` at `x` then the `k`th derivative of `b * v` is bounded by `2 ^ k * B * S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_iteratedFDeriv_mul_le_two_pow (b v : E → ℝ) (hb : ContDiff ℝ ∞ b)
    (hv : ContDiff ℝ ∞ v) (x : E) (k : ℕ) {B S : ℝ}
    (hB : ∀ i ≤ k, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ i b x‖ ≤ B) (hS : ∀ j ≤ k, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ j v x‖ ≤ S) :
    ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ k (fun y => b y * v y) x‖ ≤ 2 ^ k * B * S

modules.title: Smoothness of parametric integrals
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

An integral of a smooth family of functions is smooth when the derivatives have an integrable bound.

## ii. Key results

- `continuous_iteratedFDeriv_partial` : The derivatives in the first variable of a jointly smooth
  function are jointly continuous.
- `norm_iteratedFDeriv_integral_le` : Uniform integrable domination bounds every derivative of a
  parametric integral.
- `contDiffOn_integral`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Smoothness of parametric integrals

## iv. References

None.

## A. Smoothness of parametric integrals

Lemmas: `contDiffOn_integral`, `norm_iteratedFDeriv_integral_le`,
`continuous_iteratedFDeriv_partial`.

declarations.name: ParametricIntegral.contDiffOn_integral
declarations.statement:
lemma contDiffOn_integral {P α : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup P] [NormedSpace ℝ P]
    [MeasurableSpace α]
    (μ : Measure α)
    {U : Set P} (hU : IsOpen U) (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ (F : Type u) [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [CompleteSpace F] (H : P → α → F),
    (∀ a, ContDiff ℝ n fun p => H p a) →
    (∀ k ≤ n, ∀ p, AEStronglyMeasurable (fun a => iteratedFDeriv ℝ k (fun q => H q a) p) μ) →
    (∀ k ≤ n, ∃ b : α → ℝ, Integrable b μ ∧
      ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, ∀ p ∈ U, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ k (fun q => H q a) p‖ ≤ b a) →
    ContDiffOn ℝ n (fun p => ∫ a, H p a ∂μ) U

modules.title: Representations by measures on a boundary
modules.doc:
Boundary representations of points by regular probability measures, and simplices.

## i. Overview

A family of real-valued tests observes points of a space `X`. A boundary representation of a
point `x` is a regular probability measure on a boundary space `B` whose averages agree with the
tests at `x`. This formulation contains no physical structure: the tests may later be observables,
the points states, and the boundary points pure states.

A point has a boundary decomposition when at least one such measure exists, and a unique boundary
decomposition when exactly one exists. The tested space is a simplex when every point has a unique
boundary decomposition.

## ii. Key results

- `Choquet.IsBoundaryRepresentation` states that a boundary measure represents a point.
- `Choquet.HasBoundaryDecomposition` states existence of a boundary representation.
- `Choquet.HasUniqueBoundaryDecomposition` states existence and uniqueness.
- `Choquet.IsSimplexRepresentation` states that every point has a unique representation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Boundary representations
- B. Simplices

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Every point is a mixture of extreme points
modules.doc:
Choquet's theorem: each point of a metrizable compact convex set is a mixture of extreme points.

## i. Overview

Let `S` be a compact convex set that is metrizable and whose points are separated by countably many
continuous linear functionals. Every point of `S` is a mixture of extreme points: it has a
representing probability measure that lives on the extreme points. This is Choquet's theorem. For
states it says that every state is a mixture of pure states.

The measure is any maximal representing measure in the Choquet order. Suppose it gave positive
weight to the points that are not extreme. Each of them is the midpoint of two different points.
Moving the weight from the midpoints out to these endpoints would give a strictly higher measure. To
make this precise, the midpoints are grouped by the distance of their endpoints, and each group is a
closed set.

## ii. Key results

- `Choquet.measurableSet_extremePoints` proves that the extreme points form a Borel set.
- `Choquet.maximal_ae_mem_extremePoints` proves that maximal representing measures live on the
  extreme points.
- `Choquet.exists_extreme_representingMeasure` proves Choquet's theorem.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The extreme points are Borel
- B. Splitting mass between endpoints
- C. The boundary theorem

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Mixtures in a convex set
modules.doc:
Mixtures of points in a convex set, convex functions, and extreme points as non-midpoints.

## i. Overview

In a convex set `S` any two points can be mixed: `t x + (1 - t) y` lies in `S` for `0 ≤ t ≤ 1`. For
states this means preparing `x` with probability `t` and `y` otherwise. A function on `S` is convex
when its value at a mixture is at most the mixture of its values.

A point of `S` is extreme when it is not a mixture of other points. For states, the extreme points
are the pure states. A point that is not extreme is the midpoint of two different points of `S`.

## ii. Key results

- `Choquet.mix` is the mixture of two points of a convex set.
- `Choquet.IsConvexFunction` states that a function on `S` lies below its chords.
- `Choquet.exists_mixHalf_eq_of_notMem_extremePoints` proves that a point that is not extreme is the
  midpoint of two different points.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Mixtures
- B. Convex functions
- C. Extreme points as non-midpoints

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Representing measures and the Choquet order
modules.doc:
Representing measures of points of a convex set, the Choquet order, and maximal measures.

## i. Overview

A probability measure on a convex set `S` represents a point `x` when `x` is its average: every
continuous linear functional takes at `x` its average value under the measure. For states, a
representing measure is a way to prepare the state as a random mixture.

A point has many representing measures, the Dirac measure at the point being the trivial one. One
measure is higher than another in the Choquet order when it gives every continuous convex function a
larger average. Higher measures push their weight further out, towards the extreme points. On a
compact set every point has a representing measure that is maximal in this order.

## ii. Key results

- `Choquet.IsRepresentingMeasure` states that a probability measure represents a point.
- `Choquet.ChoquetLE` is the Choquet order.
- `Choquet.ChoquetLE.isRepresentingMeasure` proves that a higher measure represents the same point.
- `Choquet.exists_isChoquetMaximalAt` proves that every point has a maximal representing measure.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Representing measures
- B. The Choquet order
- C. Maximal representing measures

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Separation from dominated cones
modules.doc:
Hahn–Banach separation of vectors from a convex cone dominated by a vector.

## i. Overview

A convex cone `C` in a real vector space is dominated by `u ∈ C` when every vector plus some
multiple of `u` lies in `C`, as the positive cone of an order-unit space is dominated by its unit.
The least such multiple is a sublinear gauge. Whenever some linear functional is nonnegative on `C`
and positive at `u`, the gauge is finite and Hahn–Banach turns it into separating functionals: a
vector `v` with `v + ε • u ∉ C` is sent to a negative number by a functional nonnegative on `C`.
No topology is involved.

## ii. Key results

- `IsDominatedCone` : a convex cone dominated by a vector.
- `IsDominatedCone.gauge` : the gauge of the cone relative to the dominating vector.
- `IsDominatedCone.exists_apply_neg` : separation of a vector from a dominated cone.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Dominated cones and their gauge
- B. Separation

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Dominated cones and their gauge

declarations.name: IsDominatedCone
declarations.doc: A convex cone with a dominating element `u`: every vector plus a multiple of `u` lies in it.
declarations.statement:
structure IsDominatedCone (C : Set V) (u : V) : Prop where
  zero_mem : (0 : V) ∈ C
  add_mem : ∀ a ∈ C, ∀ b ∈ C, a + b ∈ C
  smul_mem : ∀ c : ℝ, 0 ≤ c → ∀ a ∈ C, c • a ∈ C
  mem : u ∈ C
  dominates : ∀ v, ∃ t : ℝ, v + t • u ∈ C

declarations.name: IsDominatedCone.gaugeSet
declarations.doc: The multiples `t` of `u` with `t • u - w` in the cone.
declarations.statement: def gaugeSet (C : Set V) (u w : V) : Set ℝ

declarations.name: IsDominatedCone.gaugeSet_nonempty
declarations.statement: lemma gaugeSet_nonempty (hC : IsDominatedCone C u) (w : V) : (gaugeSet C u w).Nonempty

declarations.name: IsDominatedCone.bddBelow_gaugeSet
declarations.statement: lemma bddBelow_gaugeSet (w : V) : BddBelow (gaugeSet C u w)

declarations.name: IsDominatedCone.add_mem_gaugeSet
declarations.statement:
lemma add_mem_gaugeSet {w w' : V} {t t' : ℝ} (ht : t ∈ gaugeSet C u w)
    (ht' : t' ∈ gaugeSet C u w') : t + t' ∈ gaugeSet C u (w + w')

declarations.name: IsDominatedCone.gaugeSet_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeSet_smul {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (w : V) :
    gaugeSet C u (c • w) = c • gaugeSet C u w

declarations.name: IsDominatedCone.gauge
declarations.doc: The gauge of the cone with respect to `u`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gauge (C : Set V) (u w : V) : ℝ

declarations.name: IsDominatedCone.gauge_le
declarations.statement: lemma gauge_le {w : V} {t : ℝ} (ht : t ∈ gaugeSet C u w) : gauge C u w ≤ t

declarations.name: IsDominatedCone.gauge_add_le
declarations.statement: lemma gauge_add_le (w w' : V) : gauge C u (w + w') ≤ gauge C u w + gauge C u w'

declarations.name: IsDominatedCone.gauge_smul
declarations.statement: lemma gauge_smul {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (w : V) : gauge C u (c • w) = c * gauge C u w

declarations.name: IsDominatedCone.gauge_zero
declarations.statement: lemma gauge_zero : gauge C u 0 = 0

declarations.name: IsDominatedCone.exists_apply_neg
declarations.doc:
**Separation from a cone.** If `v + ε • u` is outside the cone, a linear functional that is
nonnegative on the cone is negative at `v`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_apply_neg {v : V} {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (hv : v + ε • u ∉ C) :
    ∃ Λ : V →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ, (∀ c ∈ C, 0 ≤ Λ c) ∧ Λ v < 0

modules.title: Extreme points of `ℓq` balls
modules.doc:
The extreme points of the `ℓq` ball are its unit sphere, those of the `ℓ1` ball its vertices.

## i. Overview

The closed `ℓq` ball `{a | ∑ |a i| ^ q ≤ 1}` in `ℝⁿ` is strictly convex for `1 < q < ∞`: its
extreme points are its whole unit sphere. The `ℓ1` ball is instead a polytope, the convex hull of
its `2n` vertices `± eᵢ`, and these vertices are its only extreme points.

## ii. Key results

- `LpBall.extremePoints_lpBall` : the extreme points of the `ℓq` ball are its unit sphere.
- `LpBall.l1Ball_eq_convexHull` : the `ℓ1` ball is the convex hull of its vertices.
- `LpBall.vertex_isExtreme`, `LpBall.eq_vertex_of_isExtreme` : the extreme points of the `ℓ1` ball
  are its vertices.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Extreme points of the `ℓq` ball
- B. Extreme points of the `ℓ1` ball

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Extreme points of the `ℓq` ball
## B. Extreme points of the `ℓ1` ball

    (ht1 : t < 1) : |t * x + (1 - t) * y| ^ p < t * |x| ^ p + (1 - t) * |y| ^ p

modules.title: Compactly supported distributions and cutoffs
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A compactly supported distribution is unchanged by a cutoff that equals one near its support.

## ii. Key results

- `compactDistributions` : Compactly supported native distributions, defined by annihilation outside
  a compact bound.
- `compactDistributionBound` : A chosen compact support bound for a native compact distributional
  source.
- `multiplyDistribution` : Smooth multiplication of a distribution is the transpose of native test
  multiplication.
- `compactCutoffRadius` : A positive radius containing a compact set in its open ball.
- `compactCutoffBump` : The canonical support-bound cutoff is a smooth compact bump.
- `compactCutoff` : A native compact test cutoff equal to one in a neighborhood of the compact set.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Compact distributional sources
- B. Localization of native distributions

## iv. References

None.

## A. Compact distributional sources

- `compactDistributions` : Compactly supported native distributions, defined by annihilation outside
  a compact bound.
- `compactDistributionBound` : A chosen compact support bound for a native compact distributional
  source.

Lemmas: `compactDistributionBound_vanishes`.

## B. Localization of native distributions

- `multiplyDistribution` : Smooth multiplication of a distribution is the transpose of native test
  multiplication.
- `compactCutoffRadius` : A positive radius containing a compact set in its open ball.
- `compactCutoffBump` : The canonical support-bound cutoff is a smooth compact bump.
- `compactCutoff` : A native compact test cutoff equal to one in a neighborhood of the compact set.

Lemmas: `multiplyDistribution_apply`, `multiplyDistribution_eq_self`, `compactCutoff_one_near`.

modules.title: The Duhamel integral of Fourier multiplied slices
modules.doc:
The slice of a source at each time is propagated by a Fourier multiplier.

## i. Overview

The slice of a source at each time is propagated by a Fourier multiplier. The Duhamel integral adds
the contributions of all earlier times.

## ii. Key results

- `propagatedSlice` : The spatial Fourier propagation of the slice `f(s, ·)` by a multiplier family
  `m` over the time `r`, evaluated at the position `x`.
- `duhamel` : The retarded Duhamel integral of the sources `f` for a multiplier family `m`: the
  source at the time `s` is propagated over the time `t - s` and summed over `s ≤ t`.
- `continuous_propagatedSlice` : The propagated slices are jointly continuous in the propagation
  time, the source time and the position, for every multiplier family that is jointly continuous and
  locally bounded in time.
- `duhamel_eq_integral_fourier` : The Duhamel integral is the inverse Fourier integral of the
  per-frequency Duhamel integral of the Fourier transformed slices.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Duhamel integral of Fourier multiplied slices

## iv. References

None.

## A. The Duhamel integral of Fourier multiplied slices

- `propagatedSlice` : The spatial Fourier propagation of the slice `f(s, ·)` by a multiplier family
  `m` over the time `r`, evaluated at the position `x`.
- `duhamel` : The retarded Duhamel integral of the sources `f` for a multiplier family `m`: the
  source at the time `s` is propagated over the time `t - s` and summed over `s ≤ t`.

Lemmas: `continuous_propagatedSlice`, `propagatedSlice_eq_zero_of_notMem`, `integrable_duhamel`,
`exists_timeBound`, `duhamel_eq_intervalIntegral`, `duhamel_eq_integral_fourier`.

declarations.doc:
The spatial Fourier propagation of the slice `f(s, ·)` by a multiplier family `m` over the
time `r`, evaluated at the position `x`. It is independent of the equation: the equation only
enters through the multiplier family.

declarations.name: Duhamel.continuous_propagatedSlice
declarations.doc:
The propagated slices are jointly continuous in the propagation time, the source time and the
position, for every multiplier family that is jointly continuous and locally bounded in time.

lemma continuous_propagatedSlice (m : ℝ → E → ℂ)
    (hm : Continuous fun p : ℝ × E => m p.1 p.2)
    (hb : ∀ R : ℝ, ∃ B : ℝ, ∀ r ξ, |r| ≤ R → ‖m r ξ‖ ≤ B) :

    (hs : s ∉ Prod.fst '' tsupport f) (x : E) : propagatedSlice F f m r s x = 0

declarations.name: Duhamel.duhamel
declarations.doc:
The retarded Duhamel integral of the sources `f` for a multiplier family `m`:
the source at the time `s` is propagated over the time `t - s` and summed over `s ≤ t`.
declarations.statement: def duhamel (m : ℝ → E → ℂ) (t : ℝ) (x : E) : F

declarations.doc: The integrand of the Duhamel integral is integrable.
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_duhamel (m : ℝ → E → ℂ)
    (hm : Continuous fun p : ℝ × E => m p.1 p.2)
    (hb : ∀ R : ℝ, ∃ B : ℝ, ∀ r ξ, |r| ≤ R → ‖m r ξ‖ ≤ B) (t : ℝ) (x : E) :

declarations.doc: A time strictly before the support of the source.
declarations.statement: lemma exists_timeBound : ∃ a : ℝ, ∀ s ≤ a, s ∉ Prod.fst '' tsupport f

declarations.name: Duhamel.duhamel_eq_intervalIntegral
declarations.doc: The Duhamel integral starts at any time before the support of the source.

declarations.name: Duhamel.duhamel_eq_integral_fourier
declarations.doc:
The Duhamel integral is the inverse Fourier integral of the per-frequency Duhamel integral
of the Fourier transformed slices.
declarations.statement:
lemma duhamel_eq_integral_fourier (m : ℝ → E → ℂ)
    (hm : Continuous fun p : ℝ × E => m p.1 p.2)
    (hb : ∀ R : ℝ, ∃ B : ℝ, ∀ r ξ, |r| ≤ R → ‖m r ξ‖ ≤ B) {a : ℝ}
    (ha : ∀ s ≤ a, s ∉ Prod.fst '' tsupport f) {t : ℝ} (hat : a ≤ t) (x : E) :
    duhamel F f m t x =
      ∫ ξ : E, 𝐞 (inner ℝ ξ x) • ∫ s in a..t, m (t - s) ξ • 𝓕 (slice F f s) ξ

modules.title: Exponential twists of compactly supported functions
modules.doc:
Multiplying a compactly supported function by `exp (a ℓ x)` moves it by `O (|a|)` in every
derivative.

## i. Overview

For a continuous linear functional `ℓ` the twist `x ↦ exp (a ℓ x)` is smooth. Its derivatives of
order `i` are bounded by `(|a| ‖ℓ‖)^i exp (|a| ‖ℓ‖ ‖x‖)`. The twist minus one is bounded by
`|a| ‖ℓ‖ ‖x‖ exp (|a| ‖ℓ‖ ‖x‖)`. A Leibniz estimate turns these into a bound for the derivatives
of `twist * v - v` by `|a|` times a constant and the derivative bounds of `v`.

## ii. Key results

- `ExpTwist.twist` : the function `x ↦ exp (a ℓ x)`.
- `ExpTwist.norm_iteratedFDeriv_twist_le` : the derivatives of the twist.
- `ExpTwist.norm_iteratedFDeriv_twist_mul_sub_le` : the derivatives of `twist * v - v`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The twist
- B. The Leibniz estimate

## iv. References

None.

## A. The twist

- `ExpTwist.twist` : the function `x ↦ exp (a ℓ x)`.
- `ExpTwist.norm_iteratedFDeriv_twist_le` : the derivatives of the twist.

## B. The Leibniz estimate

- `ExpTwist.norm_iteratedFDeriv_twist_mul_sub_le` : the derivatives of `twist * v - v`.

declarations.statement: lemma abs_exp_sub_one_le (y : ℝ) : |Real.exp y - 1| ≤ |y| * Real.exp |y|

declarations.name: ExpTwist.abs_twist_sub_one_le
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_twist_sub_one_le (ℓ : E →L[ℝ] ℝ) (a : ℝ) (x : E) :
    |twist ℓ a x - 1| ≤ |a| * ‖ℓ‖ * ‖x‖ * Real.exp (|a| * ‖ℓ‖ * ‖x‖)

declarations.name: ExpTwist.norm_iteratedFDeriv_twist_sub_one_le
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_iteratedFDeriv_twist_sub_one_le (ℓ : E →L[ℝ] ℝ) {a R : ℝ} (ha : |a| ≤ 1) {x : E}
    (hx : ‖x‖ ≤ R) (k i : ℕ) (hi : i ≤ k) :
    ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ i (fun y => twist ℓ a y - 1) x‖ ≤
      |a| * ((1 + R) * (1 + ‖ℓ‖) ^ (k + 1) * Real.exp (‖ℓ‖ * R))

declarations.name: ExpTwist.norm_iteratedFDeriv_twist_mul_sub_le
declarations.doc: **The twist moves a compactly supported function by `O(|a|)` in every derivative.**
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_iteratedFDeriv_twist_mul_sub_le (ℓ : E →L[ℝ] ℝ) {a R : ℝ} (hR : 0 ≤ R) (ha : |a| ≤ 1)
    (v : E → ℝ) (hv : ContDiff ℝ ∞ v) (hvs : tsupport v ⊆ Metric.closedBall 0 R) (k : ℕ) {S : ℝ}
    (hS : ∀ j ≤ k, ∀ y, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ j v y‖ ≤ S) (x : E) :
    ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ k (fun y => twist ℓ a y * v y - v y) x‖ ≤
      2 ^ k * (|a| * ((1 + R) * (1 + ‖ℓ‖) ^ (k + 1) * Real.exp (‖ℓ‖ * R))) * S

modules.title: Exponential twists on test functions
modules.doc:
Conjugating a continuous linear operator on test functions by the exponential twist moves its
values by `O (|a|)` in every derivative.

## i. Overview

The twist `x ↦ exp (a ℓ x)` multiplies a test function. The derivatives of a test function are
bounded continuous functions, and `iterDerivCLM` makes them a continuous linear map. A
distribution of finite order is bounded on a fixed compact set by finitely many of these norms.
Together with the estimates for the twist this gives the convergence
`T (M_a C M_{-a} φ) → T (C φ)` for a continuous linear `C` with values in a fixed ball.

## ii. Key results

- `ExpTwist.twistCLM` : the multiplication by the twist as a map of test functions.
- `ExpTwist.iterDerivCLM` : the `k`-th derivative as a continuous linear map to bounded functions.
- `ExpTwist.tendsto_twistCLM` : the twisted test function tends to the test function.
- `ExpTwist.exists_bound_of_tsupport_subset` : a distribution has finite order on a compact set.
- `ExpTwist.tendsto_distribution_twist` : the conjugation limit.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Test functions and their derivatives
- B. Estimates for the twist
- C. The conjugation limit

## iv. References

None.

## A. Test functions and their derivatives

- `ExpTwist.twistCLM` : the multiplication by the twist.
- `ExpTwist.iterDerivCLM` : the `k`-th derivative as a continuous linear map.

## B. Estimates for the twist

- `ExpTwist.dnorm_twistCLM_sub_le` : the derivatives of `M_a φ - φ`.
- `ExpTwist.tendsto_twistCLM` : convergence in the test function topology.
- `ExpTwist.exists_bound_of_tsupport_subset` : finite order on a compact set.

## C. The conjugation limit

- `ExpTwist.tendsto_distribution_twist` : the conjugation limit.

declarations.name: ExpTwist.twistCLM
declarations.doc: Multiplication of a test function by the twist.
declarations.statement: def twistCLM (a : ℝ) : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ) →L[ℝ] 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ)

declarations.name: ExpTwist.twistCLM_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma twistCLM_apply (a : ℝ) (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ)) (x : E) :
    twistCLM ℓ a φ x = φ x * twist ℓ a x

declarations.name: ExpTwist.iterDerivCLM
declarations.doc: The `k`-th derivative of a test function as a bounded continuous function.
declarations.statement: def iterDerivCLM (k : ℕ) : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ) →L[ℝ] (E →ᵇ (E [×k]→L[ℝ] ℝ))

declarations.name: ExpTwist.iterDerivCLM_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma iterDerivCLM_apply (k : ℕ) (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ)) (x : E) :
    iterDerivCLM E k φ x = iteratedFDeriv ℝ k φ x

declarations.name: ExpTwist.norm_iteratedFDeriv_le_iterDerivCLM
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_iteratedFDeriv_le_iterDerivCLM (k : ℕ) (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ)) (x : E) :
    ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ k φ x‖ ≤ ‖iterDerivCLM E k φ‖

declarations.name: ExpTwist.norm_iterDerivCLM_le
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_iterDerivCLM_le (k : ℕ) (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ)) {C : ℝ} (hC : 0 ≤ C)
    (h : ∀ x, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ k φ x‖ ≤ C) : ‖iterDerivCLM E k φ‖ ≤ C

declarations.name: ExpTwist.twistConst
declarations.doc: The constant in the twist estimate.
declarations.statement: def twistConst (R : ℝ) (k : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: ExpTwist.dnorm_twistCLM_sub_le
declarations.statement:
lemma dnorm_twistCLM_sub_le {a R : ℝ} (hR : 0 ≤ R) (ha : |a| ≤ 1) (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ))
    (hs : tsupport φ ⊆ Metric.closedBall 0 R) (k : ℕ) :
    ‖iterDerivCLM E k (twistCLM ℓ a φ - φ)‖ ≤
      |a| * twistConst ℓ R k * ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), ‖iterDerivCLM E j φ‖

declarations.name: ExpTwist.tendsto_twistCLM
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_twistCLM (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ)) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun a : ℝ => twistCLM ℓ a φ) (nhds 0) (nhds φ)

declarations.name: ExpTwist.exists_bound_of_tsupport_subset
declarations.doc:
**Finite order.** A distribution is bounded on test functions supported in a compact set by
finitely many sup norms of derivatives.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_bound_of_tsupport_subset (T : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (K : Compacts E) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (c : ℝ), 0 ≤ c ∧ ∀ w : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ), tsupport w ⊆ K →
      |T w| ≤ c * ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), ‖iterDerivCLM E k w‖

declarations.name: ExpTwist.dsum
declarations.doc: The sum of the sup norms of the derivatives up to the order `N`.
declarations.statement: def dsum (N : ℕ) (w : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ)) : ℝ

declarations.name: ExpTwist.dsum_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma dsum_nonneg (N : ℕ) (w : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ)) : 0 ≤ dsum E N w

declarations.name: ExpTwist.dsum_add_le
declarations.statement:
lemma dsum_add_le (N : ℕ) (v w : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ)) :
    dsum E N (v + w) ≤ dsum E N v + dsum E N w

declarations.name: ExpTwist.dsum_neg
declarations.statement: lemma dsum_neg (N : ℕ) (w : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ)) : dsum E N (-w) = dsum E N w

declarations.name: ExpTwist.dsum_twistCLM_sub_le
declarations.statement:
lemma dsum_twistCLM_sub_le {a R : ℝ} (hR : 0 ≤ R) (ha : |a| ≤ 1) (N : ℕ)
    (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ)) (hs : tsupport φ ⊆ Metric.closedBall 0 R) :
    dsum E N (twistCLM ℓ a φ - φ) ≤
      |a| * (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), twistConst ℓ R k) * dsum E N φ

declarations.name: ExpTwist.tsupport_twistCLM_subset
declarations.statement:
lemma tsupport_twistCLM_subset (a : ℝ) (g : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ)) :
    tsupport ⇑(twistCLM ℓ a g) ⊆ tsupport g

declarations.name: ExpTwist.tendsto_distribution_twist
declarations.doc:
**Conjugation by the twist.** For a continuous linear `C` with values supported in a ball and
a distribution `T`, the twisted values `T (M_a C M_{-a} φ)` converge to `T (C φ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_distribution_twist [ProperSpace E] (T : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ)
    (C : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ) →L[ℝ] 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ)) (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens E), ℝ)) {R : ℝ}
    (hR : 0 ≤ R) (hC : ∀ g, tsupport ⇑(C g) ⊆ Metric.closedBall 0 R) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun a : ℝ => T (twistCLM ℓ a (C (twistCLM ℓ (-a) φ)))) (nhds 0)
      (nhds (T (C φ)))

modules.title: Fourier multipliers on Schwartz functions
modules.doc:
Sums and commutation of Fourier multipliers and their derivatives in a parameter.

## i. Overview

Sums and commutation of Fourier multipliers and their derivatives in a parameter. Compositions with
bounded smooth functions have temperate growth.

## ii. Key results

- `continuous_multiplierFamily_apply` : The evolution of fixed Schwartz data is jointly continuous
  in time and position, for every multiplier family that is jointly continuous and locally dominated
  against the Fourier transform of the data.
- `hasTemperateGrowth_comp_of_bounded` : Composition of a smooth function with bounded derivatives
  on `[0, ∞)` with a nonnegative function of temperate growth has temperate growth.
- `functional_fourier` : A continuous linear functional commutes with the Fourier transform of a
  Schwartz function.
- `hasDerivAt_multiplierFamily` : Differentiation in time of a family of Fourier multipliers, under
  the Fourier integral.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Klein–Gordon propagation multiplier
- B. The free Klein–Gordon evolution and its group law
- C. The free Klein–Gordon evolution as a one-parameter group
- D. The homogeneous Klein–Gordon evolution of Schwartz data
- E. Finite propagation speed for the homogeneous Klein–Gordon evolution
- F. The retarded solution as a tempered distribution in space

## iv. References

None.

## A. The Klein–Gordon propagation multiplier

Lemmas: `hasTemperateGrowth_comp_of_bounded`.

## B. The free Klein–Gordon evolution and its group law

Lemmas: `fourierMultiplierCLM_add`.

## C. The free Klein–Gordon evolution as a one-parameter group

Lemmas: `multiplier_comm`.

## D. The homogeneous Klein–Gordon evolution of Schwartz data

Lemmas: `multiplier_apply_eq`, `hasDerivAt_multiplierFamily`, `lineDeriv_fourierMultiplier`,
`continuous_multiplierFamily_apply`.

## E. Finite propagation speed for the homogeneous Klein–Gordon evolution

Lemmas: `hasLineDerivAt_lineDerivOp`, `functional_fourier`, `integrable_fourier_integrand`.

## F. The retarded solution as a tempered distribution in space

Lemmas: `fourier_smul_fourierInv_of_even`.

declarations.name: FourierMultiplier.hasTemperateGrowth_comp_of_bounded
declarations.doc:
Composition of a smooth function with bounded derivatives on `[0, ∞)` with a nonnegative
function of temperate growth has temperate growth.

declarations.name: FourierMultiplier.fourierMultiplierCLM_add
declarations.statement:
lemma fourierMultiplierCLM_add {g₁ g₂ : E → ℂ} (h₁ : g₁.HasTemperateGrowth)
    (h₂ : g₂.HasTemperateGrowth) (f : 𝓢(E, F)) :
    SchwartzMap.fourierMultiplierCLM F (g₁ + g₂) f =
      SchwartzMap.fourierMultiplierCLM F g₁ f + SchwartzMap.fourierMultiplierCLM F g₂ f

declarations.name: FourierMultiplier.multiplier_comm
declarations.statement:
lemma multiplier_comm {g₁ g₂ : E → ℂ} (h₁ : g₁.HasTemperateGrowth) (h₂ : g₂.HasTemperateGrowth)
    (f : 𝓢(E, F)) :
    SchwartzMap.fourierMultiplierCLM F g₁ (SchwartzMap.fourierMultiplierCLM F g₂ f) =
      SchwartzMap.fourierMultiplierCLM F g₂ (SchwartzMap.fourierMultiplierCLM F g₁ f)

declarations.name: FourierMultiplier.multiplier_apply_eq
declarations.doc: The pointwise Fourier integral of a Fourier multiplier with temperate growth.
declarations.statement:
lemma multiplier_apply_eq {g : E → ℂ} (hg : g.HasTemperateGrowth) (a : 𝓢(E, F)) (x : E) :
    SchwartzMap.fourierMultiplierCLM F g a x =
      ∫ ξ : E, (𝐞 (inner ℝ ξ x) : ℂ) • (g ξ • 𝓕 a ξ)

declarations.name: FourierMultiplier.hasDerivAt_multiplierFamily
declarations.doc: Differentiation in time of a family of Fourier multipliers, under the Fourier integral.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_multiplierFamily (a : 𝓢(E, F)) (x : E) (gfam gfam' : ℝ → E → ℂ)
    (hg : ∀ r, (gfam r).HasTemperateGrowth) (hg' : ∀ r, (gfam' r).HasTemperateGrowth)
    (hd : ∀ ξ r, HasDerivAt (fun r' => gfam r' ξ) (gfam' r ξ) r) (τ : ℝ)
    (B : E → ℝ) (hB : MeasureTheory.Integrable B MeasureTheory.volume)
    (hb : ∀ ξ r, r ∈ Metric.ball τ 1 → ‖gfam' r ξ‖ * ‖𝓕 a ξ‖ ≤ B ξ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun r => SchwartzMap.fourierMultiplierCLM F (gfam r) a x)
      (SchwartzMap.fourierMultiplierCLM F (gfam' τ) a x) τ

declarations.name: FourierMultiplier.lineDeriv_fourierMultiplier
declarations.doc: Directional derivatives of Schwartz functions commute with Fourier multipliers.
declarations.statement:
lemma lineDeriv_fourierMultiplier {g : E → ℂ} (hg : g.HasTemperateGrowth) (m : E)
    (f : 𝓢(E, F)) :
    ∂_{m} (SchwartzMap.fourierMultiplierCLM F g f) =
      SchwartzMap.fourierMultiplierCLM F g (∂_{m} f)

declarations.name: FourierMultiplier.continuous_multiplierFamily_apply
declarations.doc:
The evolution of fixed Schwartz data is jointly continuous in time and position, for every
multiplier family that is jointly continuous and locally dominated against the Fourier transform of
the data.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_multiplierFamily_apply (a : 𝓢(E, F)) (g : ℝ → E → ℂ)
    (hg : Continuous fun p : ℝ × E => g p.1 p.2) (hgt : ∀ r, (g r).HasTemperateGrowth)
    (hb : ∀ R : ℝ, ∃ q : E → ℝ, MeasureTheory.Integrable q MeasureTheory.volume ∧
      ∀ r ξ, |r| ≤ R → ‖g r ξ‖ * ‖𝓕 a ξ‖ ≤ q ξ) :
    Continuous fun p : ℝ × E => SchwartzMap.fourierMultiplierCLM F (g p.1) a p.2

declarations.name: FourierMultiplier.hasLineDerivAt_lineDerivOp
declarations.statement:
lemma hasLineDerivAt_lineDerivOp (f : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) (m x : E) :
    HasLineDerivAt ℝ (⇑f) (∂_{m} f x) x m

declarations.name: FourierMultiplier.functional_fourier
declarations.doc: A continuous linear functional commutes with the Fourier transform of a Schwartz function.
declarations.statement:
lemma functional_fourier (ℓ : F →L[ℂ] ℂ) (g : 𝓢(E, F)) (ξ : E) :
    ℓ (𝓕 g ξ) = 𝓕 (SchwartzMap.postcompCLM (𝕜 := ℂ) (E := E) ℓ g) ξ

declarations.name: FourierMultiplier.integrable_fourier_integrand
declarations.doc: The Fourier integrand of a multiplier applied to Schwartz data is integrable.
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_fourier_integrand {g : E → ℂ} (hg : g.HasTemperateGrowth) (a : 𝓢(E, F)) (x : E) :
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ξ : E => (𝐞 (inner ℝ ξ x) : ℂ) • (g ξ • 𝓕 a ξ))
      MeasureTheory.volume

declarations.name: FourierMultiplier.fourier_smul_fourierInv_of_even
declarations.doc: An even multiplier acts the same on a function and on its transpose.
declarations.statement:
lemma fourier_smul_fourierInv_of_even {G : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace ℂ G]
    (m : E → ℂ) (hm : ∀ x, m (-x) = m x) (g : E → G) (y : E) :
    𝓕 (fun x => m x • 𝓕⁻ g x) y = 𝓕⁻ (fun x => m x • 𝓕 g x) y

modules.title: Distributions induced by smooth functions
modules.doc:
The distribution of a continuous function is additive in the function. The weak derivative of the
distribution of a smooth function is the distribution of its derivative.

## i. Overview

A locally integrable function `u` defines the distribution `φ ↦ ∫ φ • u`. Continuous functions are
locally integrable. So the map `u ↦ ofFun u` is additive on continuous functions and commutes with
finite sums. Integration by parts for compactly supported test functions shows that the weak line
derivative of `ofFun u` is `ofFun` of the line derivative of a smooth `u`. A function vanishing
outside a set induces a distribution vanishing outside it.

## ii. Key results

- `Distribution.ofFun_continuous_add` : additivity on continuous functions.
- `Distribution.ofFun_finset_sum` : finite sums.
- `Distribution.lineDerivCLM_ofFun` : the weak derivative of the distribution of a smooth function.
- `Distribution.isVanishingOn_ofFun` : vanishing outside a set.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Linearity
- B. Weak derivatives
- C. Support

## iv. References

None.

## A. Linearity

- `Distribution.ofFun_continuous_add` : additivity on continuous functions.
- `Distribution.ofFun_finset_sum` : finite sums.

## B. Weak derivatives

- `Distribution.lineDerivCLM_ofFun` : the weak derivative of the distribution of a smooth function.

## C. Support

- `Distribution.isVanishingOn_ofFun` : vanishing outside a set.

declarations.name: Distribution.ofFun_continuous_add
declarations.statement:
lemma ofFun_continuous_add {u w : E → V} (hu : Continuous u) (hw : Continuous w) :
    ofFun (⊤ : Opens E) (u + w) μ ⊤ =
      ofFun (⊤ : Opens E) u μ ⊤ +
        ofFun (⊤ : Opens E) w μ ⊤

declarations.name: Distribution.ofFun_finset_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma ofFun_finset_sum {ι : Type*} (S : Finset ι) {g : ι → E → V}
    (hg : ∀ i, Continuous (g i)) :
    ofFun (⊤ : Opens E) (∑ i ∈ S, g i) μ ⊤ =
      ∑ i ∈ S, ofFun (⊤ : Opens E) (g i) μ ⊤

declarations.name: Distribution.lineDerivCLM_ofFun
declarations.doc:
The weak derivative of the distribution induced by a smooth function is the distribution
induced by its derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma lineDerivCLM_ofFun {u : E → V} (hu : ContDiff ℝ ∞ u) (v : E) :
    lineDerivCLM (n := ⊤) (k := ⊤) v
        (ofFun (⊤ : Opens E) u μ ⊤) =
      ofFun (⊤ : Opens E) (fun x => fderiv ℝ u x v) μ ⊤

declarations.name: Distribution.isVanishingOn_ofFun
declarations.doc: A distribution induced by a function that vanishes outside a set vanishes outside it.

modules.title: Test functions are dense in the Schwartz space
modules.doc:
A Schwartz function is the limit of its cutoffs by dilated bump functions.

## i. Overview

Let `b` be a smooth compactly supported function that equals one on the unit ball. The cutoff
`b (x / R) * f x` of a Schwartz function `f` is a test function. The derivatives of the cutoff
factor are bounded uniformly in `R ≥ 1` and vanish on the ball of radius `R`. The Schwartz
seminorms of `f - b (x / R) * f` are therefore bounded by `R⁻¹` times a seminorm of `f`.

## ii. Key results

- `exists_cutoff` : a smooth compactly supported function that equals one on the unit ball.
- `exists_bound_cutoff_sub` : the cutoff approximation estimate.
- `denseRange_ofTestFunction` : test functions are dense in the Schwartz space.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The cutoff
- B. Density

## iv. References

None.

## A. The cutoff

- `exists_cutoff` : a smooth compactly supported function that equals one on the unit ball.
- `exists_bound_cutoff_sub` : the cutoff approximation estimate.

## B. Density

- `ofTestFunction` : a real test function is a Schwartz function.
- `cutoffTest` : the cutoff of a Schwartz function as a test function.
- `denseRange_ofTestFunction` : test functions are dense in the Schwartz space.

declarations.name: SchwartzMap.exists_cutoff
declarations.doc: A smooth compactly supported function that equals one on the unit ball.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_cutoff : ∃ b : V → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ∞ b ∧ HasCompactSupport b ∧
    ∀ x : V, ‖x‖ ≤ 1 → b x = 1

declarations.name: SchwartzMap.exists_bound_dilate
declarations.doc: The derivatives of the dilated cutoff minus one are bounded uniformly in the dilation.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_bound_dilate {b : V → ℝ} (hb : ContDiff ℝ ∞ b) (hs : HasCompactSupport b) (j : ℕ) :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B ∧ ∀ R : ℝ, 1 ≤ R → ∀ x : V,
      ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ j (fun y => b (R⁻¹ • y) - 1) x‖ ≤ B

declarations.name: SchwartzMap.iteratedFDeriv_dilate_eq_zero
declarations.doc: The dilated cutoff minus one vanishes with all its derivatives inside the ball of radius `R`.

declarations.name: SchwartzMap.exists_bound_cutoff_sub
declarations.doc:
**The cutoff approximation estimate.** The weighted derivatives of `(b (R⁻¹ x) - 1) f x` are
bounded by a constant times `R⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_bound_cutoff_sub {b : V → ℝ} (hb : ContDiff ℝ ∞ b) (hs : HasCompactSupport b)
    (hone : ∀ x : V, ‖x‖ ≤ 1 → b x = 1) (f : 𝓢(V, ℝ)) (k n : ℕ) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ R : ℝ, 1 ≤ R → ∀ x : V,
      ‖x‖ ^ k * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (fun y => (b (R⁻¹ • y) - 1) * f y) x‖ ≤ C / R

declarations.name: SchwartzMap.ofTestFunction
declarations.doc: A real test function is a Schwartz function.
declarations.statement: def ofTestFunction : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens V), ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] 𝓢(V, ℝ)

declarations.name: SchwartzMap.ofTestFunction_injective
declarations.statement: lemma ofTestFunction_injective : Function.Injective (ofTestFunction (V := V))

declarations.name: SchwartzMap.ofTestFunction_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma ofTestFunction_apply (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens V), ℝ)) (x : V) :
    ofTestFunction φ x = φ x

declarations.name: SchwartzMap.cutoffTest
declarations.doc: The cutoff of a Schwartz function by the dilated bump function, as a test function.
declarations.statement:
def cutoffTest {b : V → ℝ} (hb : ContDiff ℝ ∞ b) (hs : HasCompactSupport b) (f : 𝓢(V, ℝ))
    {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens V), ℝ)

declarations.name: SchwartzMap.denseRange_ofTestFunction
declarations.doc: **Test functions are dense in the Schwartz space.**
declarations.statement: lemma denseRange_ofTestFunction : DenseRange (ofTestFunction (V := V))

modules.title: Pointwise polynomial decay of Schwartz functions
modules.doc:
A Schwartz function decays faster than every power of `1 + ‖z‖`.

## i. Overview

The estimate `‖h z‖ ≤ 2ᵏ⁻¹ (p₀ h + pₖ h) (1 + ‖z‖)⁻ᵏ` follows from the binomial bound
`(1 + t)ᵏ ≤ 2ᵏ⁻¹ (1 + tᵏ)` and the two seminorms `p₀` and `pₖ`. The constant is a seminorm of
`h`. So it is uniform on bounded sets of Schwartz functions.

## ii. Key results

- `SchwartzMap.norm_le_rpow_neg_mul` : the pointwise decay with an explicit constant.
- `SchwartzMap.exists_norm_le_rpow_neg` : the decay with an unspecified constant.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Decay

## iv. References

None.

## A. Decay

- `SchwartzMap.norm_le_rpow_neg_mul` : the pointwise decay with an explicit constant.
- `SchwartzMap.exists_norm_le_rpow_neg` : the decay with an unspecified constant.

declarations.name: SchwartzMap.norm_le_rpow_neg_mul
declarations.doc: **Decay of a Schwartz function with an explicit constant.**
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_le_rpow_neg_mul (h : 𝓢(V, F)) (k : ℕ) (z : V) :
    ‖h z‖ ≤ 2 ^ (k - 1) * (SchwartzMap.seminorm 𝕜 0 0 h + SchwartzMap.seminorm 𝕜 k 0 h) *
      (1 + ‖z‖) ^ (-(k : ℝ))

declarations.name: SchwartzMap.exists_norm_le_rpow_neg
declarations.doc: A Schwartz function decays like `(1 + ‖z‖)⁻ᵏ` for every `k`. The constant is nonnegative.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_norm_le_rpow_neg (h : 𝓢(V, F)) (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ z : V, ‖h z‖ ≤ C * (1 + ‖z‖) ^ (-(k : ℝ))

modules.title: Operations on test functions
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Multiplication by a weight and composition with a linear equivalence are continuous on test
functions.

## ii. Key results

- `precompLinearEquivSupportedCLM` : Pullback between fixed-support smooth test spaces by an
  invertible linear coordinate map.
- `precompLinearEquivCLM` : Pullback by an invertible continuous linear coordinate change is
  continuous on smooth tests.
- `weightedTestBCFLinear` : Weight a compact smooth test field and retain its bounded continuous
  representative.
- `weightedTestBCF` : Arbitrary continuous weights give continuous maps from the native LF
  test-function space into the uniform norm.
- `smoothWeightTest` : Multiplication by a smooth weight is continuous in the native LF test
  topology.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Continuous linear changes of test-function coordinates
- B. Weighted test functions in the uniform norm

## iv. References

None.

## A. Continuous linear changes of test-function coordinates

- `precompLinearEquivSupportedCLM` : Pullback between fixed-support smooth test spaces by an
  invertible linear coordinate map.
- `precompLinearEquivCLM` : Pullback by an invertible continuous linear coordinate change is
  continuous on smooth tests.

Lemmas: `precompLinearEquivCLM_apply`.

## B. Weighted test functions in the uniform norm

- `weightedTestBCFLinear` : Weight a compact smooth test field and retain its bounded continuous
  representative.
- `weightedTestBCF` : Arbitrary continuous weights give continuous maps from the native LF
  test-function space into the uniform norm.
- `smoothWeightTest` : Multiplication by a smooth weight is continuous in the native LF test
  topology.

Lemmas: `weightedTestBCF_apply`, `smoothWeightTest_apply`.

declarations.name: TestFunction.precompLinearEquivSupportedCLM
declarations.doc: Pullback between fixed-support smooth test spaces by an invertible linear coordinate map.

declarations.name: TestFunction.precompLinearEquivCLM
declarations.doc: Pullback by an invertible continuous linear coordinate change is continuous on smooth tests.
declarations.statement:
def precompLinearEquivCLM (e : A ≃L[ℝ] B) :
    𝓓((⊤ : Opens B), F) →L[ℝ] 𝓓((⊤ : Opens A), F)

declarations.name: TestFunction.precompLinearEquivCLM_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma precompLinearEquivCLM_apply (e : A ≃L[ℝ] B) (f : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens B), F)) (x : A) :
    precompLinearEquivCLM e f x = f (e x)

declarations.name: TestFunction.weightedTestBCFLinear
declarations.doc: Weight a compact smooth test field and retain its bounded continuous representative.
declarations.statement:
