def weightedTestBCFLinear (w : E → ℝ) (hw : Continuous w) :
    _root_.TestFunction (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens E) V ⊤ →ₗ[ℝ] (E →ᵇ V)

declarations.name: TestFunction.weightedTestBCF
declarations.doc:
Arbitrary continuous weights give continuous maps from the native LF test-function space
into the uniform norm. No global bound on the weight is required.
declarations.statement:
def weightedTestBCF (w : E → ℝ) (hw : Continuous w) :
    _root_.TestFunction (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens E) V ⊤ →L[ℝ] (E →ᵇ V)

declarations.name: TestFunction.weightedTestBCF_apply
declarations.doc: The weighted embedding retains the pointwise weighted field.
declarations.statement:
lemma weightedTestBCF_apply (w : E → ℝ) (hw : Continuous w)
    (φ : _root_.TestFunction (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens E) V ⊤) (x : E) :
    weightedTestBCF w hw φ x = w x • φ x

declarations.name: TestFunction.smoothWeightTest
declarations.doc: Multiplication by a smooth weight is continuous in the native LF test topology.

declarations.name: TestFunction.smoothWeightTest_apply
declarations.doc: The LF-continuous weight map is pointwise scalar multiplication.
declarations.statement:
lemma smoothWeightTest_apply (w : E → ℝ) (hw : ContDiff ℝ ∞ w)
    (φ : _root_.TestFunction (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens E) V ⊤) (p : E) :
    smoothWeightTest w hw φ p = w p • φ p

modules.title: Time slices of test functions
modules.doc:
A test function on time and space has a Schwartz function as its slice at a fixed time.

## i. Overview

A test function on time and space has a Schwartz function as its slice at a fixed time. Time and
space derivatives and the time reflection commute with slicing.

## ii. Key results

- `slice` : The slice `f(s, ·)` of a spacetime test function at the time `s` is a Schwartz function.
- `timeReflect` : Reflection in time.
- `reflect` : The time-reflected test function.
- `dt` : The time derivative of a spacetime test function.
- `reflectSourceCLM` : Time reflection acts continuously on the native compact source space.
- `timeReflectionCLE` : Time reflection on time-space coordinates.
- `dx` : Spatial differentiation of a spacetime test field in the direction `m`.
- `spatialLaplacian` : The spatial Laplacian on compact spacetime test fields.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Time slices of test functions
- B. Causal support of the retarded solution
- C. The time dependence of the Fourier transformed slices
- D. Continuous seminorm bounds for Fourier sources
- E. Continuous compactly cut off advanced response
- F. The two-sided Klein–Gordon inverse on compact test fields

## iv. References

None.

## A. Time slices of test functions

- `slice` : The slice `f(s, ·)` of a spacetime test function at the time `s` is a Schwartz function.

Lemmas: `isClosedEmbedding_prodMk`, `hasCompactSupport_slice`, `contDiff_slice`, `slice_apply`,
`norm_iteratedFDeriv_slice_le`, `exists_bound_iteratedFDeriv`, `exists_radius`,
`exists_seminorm_slice_le`, `exists_fourier_bound`, `exists_fourier_decay_pow` and more.

## B. Causal support of the retarded solution

- `timeReflect` : Reflection in time.
- `reflect` : The time-reflected test function.

Lemmas: `timeReflect_apply`, `reflect_apply`, `tsupport_reflect`, `slice_add`, `slice_smul`.

## C. The time dependence of the Fourier transformed slices

- `dt` : The time derivative of a spacetime test function.

Lemmas: `dt_apply`, `hasDerivAt_time`.

## D. Continuous seminorm bounds for Fourier sources

- `reflectSourceCLM` : Time reflection acts continuously on the native compact source space.

Lemmas: `reflectSourceCLM_eq`.

## E. Continuous compactly cut off advanced response

- `timeReflectionCLE` : Time reflection on time-space coordinates.

Lemmas: `timeReflectionCLE_apply`.

## F. The two-sided Klein–Gordon inverse on compact test fields

- `dx` : Spatial differentiation of a spacetime test field in the direction `m`.
- `spatialLaplacian` : The spatial Laplacian on compact spacetime test fields.

Lemmas: `slice_dx`, `slice_spatialLaplacian`, `dt_reflect`, `dt_neg`, `dt_dt_reflect`,
`slice_reflect`, `dx_reflect`, `spatialLaplacian_reflect`.

declarations.name: TimeSlice.isClosedEmbedding_prodMk
declarations.statement: lemma isClosedEmbedding_prodMk (s : ℝ) : IsClosedEmbedding fun x : E => (s, x)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.hasCompactSupport_slice
declarations.statement: lemma hasCompactSupport_slice (s : ℝ) : HasCompactSupport fun x : E => f (s, x)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.contDiff_slice
declarations.statement: lemma contDiff_slice (s : ℝ) : ContDiff ℝ ∞ fun x : E => f (s, x)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.slice
declarations.doc: The slice `f(s, ·)` of a spacetime test function at the time `s` is a Schwartz function.
declarations.statement: def slice (s : ℝ) : 𝓢(E, F)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.slice_apply
declarations.statement: lemma slice_apply (s : ℝ) (x : E) : slice F f s x = f (s, x)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.norm_iteratedFDeriv_slice_le
declarations.doc: The derivatives of a slice are bounded by the derivatives of the spacetime function.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_iteratedFDeriv_slice_le (p : ℕ) (s : ℝ) (x : E) :
    ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ p (fun x : E => f (s, x)) x‖ ≤ ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ p f (s, x)‖

declarations.name: TimeSlice.exists_bound_iteratedFDeriv
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_bound_iteratedFDeriv (p : ℕ) :
    ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ y : ℝ × E, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ p f y‖ ≤ M

declarations.name: TimeSlice.exists_radius
declarations.statement: lemma exists_radius : ∃ R : ℝ, 0 ≤ R ∧ ∀ y ∈ tsupport f, ‖y‖ ≤ R

declarations.name: TimeSlice.exists_seminorm_slice_le
declarations.doc: The Schwartz seminorms of the slices are bounded uniformly in the time.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_seminorm_slice_le (k p : ℕ) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ s, SchwartzMap.seminorm ℂ k p (slice F f s) ≤ C

declarations.name: TimeSlice.exists_fourier_bound
declarations.doc: The Fourier transforms of the slices decay uniformly in the time.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_fourier_bound (N : ℕ) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ s (ξ : E), ‖ξ‖ ^ N * ‖𝓕 (slice F f s) ξ‖ ≤ C

declarations.name: TimeSlice.exists_fourier_decay_pow
declarations.doc:
Polynomial decay of any order of the Fourier transforms of the slices, uniformly in the
time.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_fourier_decay_pow (N : ℕ) :
    ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ s (ξ : E), ‖𝓕 (slice F f s) ξ‖ ≤ K * (1 + ‖ξ‖) ^ (-(N : ℝ))

declarations.name: TimeSlice.exists_fourier_decay
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_fourier_decay :
    ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ s (ξ : E), ‖𝓕 (slice F f s) ξ‖ ≤ K * (1 + ‖ξ‖) ^ (-((Module.finrank ℝ E + 1 : ℕ) :
      ℝ))

declarations.name: TimeSlice.fourier_slice_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma fourier_slice_apply (s : ℝ) (ξ : E) :
    𝓕 (slice F f s) ξ = ∫ x : E, 𝐞 (-inner ℝ x ξ) • f (s, x)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.continuous_fourier_slice
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_fourier_slice :
    Continuous fun p : ℝ × E => 𝓕 (slice F f p.1) p.2

declarations.name: TimeSlice.slice_eq_zero_of_notMem
declarations.statement: lemma slice_eq_zero_of_notMem {s : ℝ} (hs : s ∉ Prod.fst '' tsupport f) : slice F f s = 0

declarations.name: TimeSlice.isCompact_timeSupport
declarations.doc: The time support of a spacetime test function is compact.
declarations.statement: lemma isCompact_timeSupport : IsCompact (Prod.fst '' tsupport f)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.timeReflect
declarations.doc: Reflection in time.
declarations.statement: def timeReflect : ℝ × E ≃ₜ ℝ × E

declarations.name: TimeSlice.timeReflect_apply
declarations.statement: lemma timeReflect_apply (p : ℝ × E) : timeReflect p = (-p.1, p.2)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.reflect
declarations.doc: The time-reflected test function.
declarations.statement: def reflect : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.reflect_apply
declarations.statement: lemma reflect_apply (p : ℝ × E) : reflect F f p = f (-p.1, p.2)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.reflect_reflect
declarations.doc: Time reflection is an involution.
declarations.statement: lemma reflect_reflect : reflect F (reflect F f) = f

declarations.name: TimeSlice.tsupport_reflect
declarations.statement: lemma tsupport_reflect : tsupport (reflect F f) = timeReflect ⁻¹' tsupport f

declarations.name: TimeSlice.slice_add
declarations.statement:
lemma slice_add (g : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F)) (s : ℝ) :
    slice F (f + g) s = slice F f s + slice F g s

declarations.name: TimeSlice.slice_smul
declarations.statement: lemma slice_smul (c : ℝ) (s : ℝ) : slice F (c • f) s = c • slice F f s

declarations.name: TimeSlice.dt
declarations.doc: The time derivative of a spacetime test function.
declarations.statement: def dt : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.dt_apply
declarations.statement: lemma dt_apply (p : ℝ × E) : dt F f p = lineDeriv ℝ f p ((1 : ℝ), (0 : E))

declarations.name: TimeSlice.hasDerivAt_time
declarations.statement: lemma hasDerivAt_time (s : ℝ) (y : E) : HasDerivAt (fun r : ℝ => f (r, y)) (dt F f (s, y)) s

declarations.name: TimeSlice.reflectSourceCLM
declarations.doc: Time reflection acts continuously on the native compact source space.
declarations.statement:
def reflectSourceCLM :
    𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F) →L[ℝ] 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.reflectSourceCLM_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma reflectSourceCLM_eq (f : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F)) :
    reflectSourceCLM F f = reflect F f

declarations.name: TimeSlice.timeReflectionCLE
declarations.doc: Time reflection on time-space coordinates.
declarations.statement:
def timeReflectionCLE (E : Type u) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] :
    (ℝ × E) ≃L[ℝ] (ℝ × E)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.timeReflectionCLE_apply
declarations.statement: lemma timeReflectionCLE_apply (p : ℝ × E) : timeReflectionCLE E p = (-p.1, p.2)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.dx
declarations.doc: Spatial differentiation of a spacetime test field in the direction `m`.
declarations.statement: def dx (m : E) : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.slice_dx
declarations.statement: lemma slice_dx (m : E) (s : ℝ) : slice F (dx F f m) s = ∂_{m} (slice F f s)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.spatialLaplacian
declarations.doc: The spatial Laplacian on compact spacetime test fields.
declarations.statement: def spatialLaplacian : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.slice_spatialLaplacian
declarations.statement:
lemma slice_spatialLaplacian (s : ℝ) :
    slice F (spatialLaplacian F f) s = Δ (slice F f s)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.dt_reflect
declarations.statement: lemma dt_reflect : dt F (reflect F f) = -reflect F (dt F f)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.dt_neg
declarations.statement: lemma dt_neg : dt F (-f) = -dt F f

declarations.name: TimeSlice.dt_dt_reflect
declarations.statement: lemma dt_dt_reflect : dt F (dt F (reflect F f)) = reflect F (dt F (dt F f))

declarations.name: TimeSlice.slice_reflect
declarations.statement: lemma slice_reflect (s : ℝ) : slice F (reflect F f) s = slice F f (-s)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.dx_reflect
declarations.statement: lemma dx_reflect (m : E) : dx F (reflect F f) m = reflect F (dx F f m)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.spatialLaplacian_reflect
declarations.statement:
lemma spatialLaplacian_reflect :
    spatialLaplacian F (reflect F f) = reflect F (spatialLaplacian F f)

modules.title: The space and time Fourier transform of a test function
modules.doc:
A test function on time and space is transformed in the space variable and then in the time
variable.

## i. Overview

The spatial transform of the slices of a test function is a smooth function of the time with
compact support. It is therefore a Schwartz function of the time. Its transform in the time is the
spacetime transform in the split variables. Fourier inversion in the time recovers the spatial
transform. The Schwartz seminorms and the integral over the frequency decay faster than every
power of the wave vector.

## ii. Key results

- `TimeSlice.spaceFourier` : the spatial transform of the slices.
- `TimeSlice.timeFourier` : the transform in the time of the spatial transform.
- `TimeSlice.spaceFourier_eq_integral` : Fourier inversion in the time.
- `TimeSlice.exists_integral_norm_timeFourier_le` : decay of the integral over the frequency.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The transforms
- B. Properties of the time transform
- C. Decay in the wave vector

## iv. References

None.

## A. The transforms

- `TimeSlice.spaceFourier` : the spatial transform of the slices.
- `TimeSlice.spaceFourierSchwartz` : the spatial transform as a Schwartz function of the time.
- `TimeSlice.timeFourier` : the transform in the time of the spatial transform.
- `TimeSlice.spaceFourier_eq_integral` : Fourier inversion in the time.
- `TimeSlice.timeFourier_eq_integral` : the time transform as an integral.

## B. Properties of the time transform

- `TimeSlice.continuous_timeFourier` : joint continuity.
- `TimeSlice.timeFourier_reflect` : reflecting the source reflects the frequency.
- `TimeSlice.integrable_timeFourier` : integrability in the frequency.

## C. Decay in the wave vector

- `TimeSlice.exists_seminorm_spaceFourier_le` : decay of the Schwartz seminorms.
- `TimeSlice.exists_integral_norm_timeFourier_le` : decay of the integral over the frequency.

declarations.name: TimeSlice.spaceFourier
declarations.doc: The spatial transform of the slices of `ψ` at the frequency `ξ` as a function of the time.
declarations.statement: def spaceFourier (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) (ξ : E) (s : ℝ) : ℂ

declarations.name: TimeSlice.hasCompactSupport_spaceFourier
declarations.statement:
lemma hasCompactSupport_spaceFourier (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) (ξ : E) :
    HasCompactSupport (spaceFourier ψ ξ)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.contDiff_spaceFourier
declarations.statement:
lemma contDiff_spaceFourier (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) (ξ : E) :
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ (spaceFourier ψ ξ)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.spaceFourierSchwartz
declarations.doc: The spatial transform of a test function is a Schwartz function of the time.
declarations.statement: def spaceFourierSchwartz (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) (ξ : E) : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.timeFourier
declarations.doc: The transform in the time of the spatial transform.
declarations.statement: def timeFourier (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) (w : ℝ) (ξ : E) : ℂ

declarations.name: TimeSlice.spaceFourier_eq_integral
declarations.doc:
**Fourier inversion in the time.** The spatial transform of a slice is the inverse transform
in the time of `timeFourier`.
declarations.statement:
lemma spaceFourier_eq_integral (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) (ξ : E) (s : ℝ) :
    spaceFourier ψ ξ s = ∫ w : ℝ, (𝐞 (s * w) : ℂ) • timeFourier ψ w ξ

declarations.name: TimeSlice.timeFourier_eq_integral
declarations.doc: The transform in the time as an integral.
declarations.statement:
lemma timeFourier_eq_integral (χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) (v : ℝ) (ξ : E) :
    timeFourier χ v ξ = ∫ s : ℝ, (𝐞 (-(s * v)) : ℂ) • spaceFourier χ ξ s

declarations.name: TimeSlice.continuous_timeFourier
declarations.doc: The transformed test function is jointly continuous in the frequency and the wave vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_timeFourier (χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) :
    Continuous fun p : ℝ × E => timeFourier χ p.1 p.2

declarations.name: TimeSlice.timeFourier_reflect
declarations.doc: Reflecting the source in the time reflects the frequency.
declarations.statement:
lemma timeFourier_reflect (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) (w : ℝ) (ξ : E) :
    timeFourier (reflect ℂ ψ) w ξ = timeFourier ψ (-w) ξ

declarations.name: TimeSlice.integrable_timeFourier
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_timeFourier (χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) (ξ : E) :
    Integrable fun w : ℝ => timeFourier χ w ξ

declarations.name: TimeSlice.exists_seminorm_spaceFourier_le
declarations.doc: The Schwartz seminorms of the spatial transform of a test function decay in the frequency.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_seminorm_spaceFourier_le (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) (N k p : ℕ) :
    ∃ B : ℝ, ∀ ξ : E, SchwartzMap.seminorm ℂ k p (spaceFourierSchwartz ψ ξ) ≤
      B * (1 + ‖ξ‖) ^ (-(N : ℝ))

declarations.name: TimeSlice.exists_integral_norm_timeFourier_le
declarations.doc: The integral over the frequency of the transformed test function decays in `ξ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_integral_norm_timeFourier_le (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) (N : ℕ) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ ξ : E, ∫ w : ℝ, ‖timeFourier ψ w ξ‖ ≤ C * (1 + ‖ξ‖) ^ (-(N : ℝ))

modules.title: Smoothness and bounds of time slices
modules.doc:
The Fourier transform of the slices depends smoothly on time and space.

## i. Overview

The Fourier transform of the slices depends smoothly on time and space. The seminorms of the slices
are bounded by seminorms of the source.

## ii. Key results

- `fourierIntegrand` : The integrand of the partial Fourier transform, as a function of the
  parameter `(s, ξ)` and the position `y`.
- `supportedSource` : The native continuous inclusion of fixed-support sources into all compact test
  sources.
- `supportedDt` : Time differentiation is a continuous endomorphism of every fixed-support source
  space.
- `hasDerivAt_fourier_slice` : The time derivative of the Fourier transformed slice is the Fourier
  transformed slice of the time derivative.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The time dependence of the Fourier transformed slices
- B. Joint smoothness of the Fourier transformed slices
- C. Smoothness of the retarded solution
- D. Continuous seminorm bounds for Fourier sources
- E. Continuous source bounds for parameter derivatives

## iv. References

None.

## A. The time dependence of the Fourier transformed slices

Lemmas: `hasDerivAt_fourier_slice`, `deriv_fourier_slice`, `iteratedDeriv_fourier_slice`,
`contDiff_fourier_slice`, `exists_iteratedDeriv_fourier_slice_bound`.

## B. Joint smoothness of the Fourier transformed slices

- `fourierIntegrand` : The integrand of the partial Fourier transform, as a function of the
  parameter `(s, ξ)` and the position `y`.

Lemmas: `contDiff_fourierIntegrand`, `fourierIntegrand_eq_zero`, `contDiff_fourier_slice_joint`.

## C. Smoothness of the retarded solution

Lemmas: `contDiff_fourier_slice_joint_infty`.

## D. Continuous seminorm bounds for Fourier sources

- `supportedSource` : The native continuous inclusion of fixed-support sources into all compact test
  sources.

Lemmas: `seminorm_slice_supported_le`, `exists_fourier_supported_seminorm`,
`exists_fourier_decay_supported_seminorm`.

## E. Continuous source bounds for parameter derivatives

- `supportedDt` : Time differentiation is a continuous endomorphism of every fixed-support source
  space.

Lemmas: `supportedSource_dt`, `supportedSource_iterate_dt`,
`exists_timeDeriv_fourier_supported_seminorm`, `exists_char_timeDeriv_supported_seminorm`.

declarations.name: TimeSlice.hasDerivAt_fourier_slice
declarations.doc:
The time derivative of the Fourier transformed slice is the Fourier transformed slice of the
time derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_fourier_slice (ξ : E) (s : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun r => 𝓕 (slice F f r) ξ) (𝓕 (slice F (dt F f) s) ξ) s

declarations.name: TimeSlice.deriv_fourier_slice
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_fourier_slice (ξ : E) :
    deriv (fun r => 𝓕 (slice F f r) ξ) = fun s => 𝓕 (slice F (dt F f) s) ξ

declarations.name: TimeSlice.iteratedDeriv_fourier_slice
declarations.doc: The `k`-th time derivative of the Fourier transformed slice.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_fourier_slice (ξ : E) (k : ℕ) :
    ∀ f : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F), iteratedDeriv k (fun r => 𝓕 (slice F f r) ξ) =
      fun s => 𝓕 (slice F ((dt F)^[k] f) s) ξ

declarations.name: TimeSlice.contDiff_fourier_slice
declarations.statement:
lemma contDiff_fourier_slice (ξ : E) (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ f : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F), ContDiff ℝ n (fun r => 𝓕 (slice F f r) ξ)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.exists_iteratedDeriv_fourier_slice_bound
declarations.doc: All time derivatives of the Fourier transformed slice decay rapidly, uniformly in time.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_iteratedDeriv_fourier_slice_bound (k N : ℕ) :
    ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ (ξ : E) (s : ℝ), ‖iteratedDeriv k (fun r => 𝓕 (slice F f r) ξ) s‖ ≤
      K * (1 + ‖ξ‖) ^ (-(N : ℝ))

declarations.name: TimeSlice.fourierIntegrand
declarations.doc:
The integrand of the partial Fourier transform, as a function of the parameter `(s, ξ)` and the
position `y`.
declarations.statement: def fourierIntegrand (z : (ℝ × E) × E) : F

declarations.name: TimeSlice.contDiff_fourierIntegrand
declarations.statement: lemma contDiff_fourierIntegrand : ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fourierIntegrand F f)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.fourierIntegrand_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma fourierIntegrand_eq_zero {R : ℝ} (hR : ∀ y ∈ tsupport f, ‖y‖ ≤ R) {y : E} (hy : R < ‖y‖)
    (q : ℝ × E) : fourierIntegrand F f ((q), y) = 0

declarations.name: TimeSlice.contDiff_fourier_slice_joint
declarations.doc:
The partial Fourier transform of a spacetime test function is jointly smooth in the time and
the frequency.
declarations.statement:
lemma contDiff_fourier_slice_joint (n : ℕ) :
    ContDiff ℝ n (fun p : ℝ × E => 𝓕 (slice F f p.1) p.2)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.contDiff_fourier_slice_joint_infty
declarations.statement:
lemma contDiff_fourier_slice_joint_infty :
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun p : ℝ × E => 𝓕 (slice F f p.1) p.2)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.supportedSource
declarations.doc: The native continuous inclusion of fixed-support sources into all compact test sources.
declarations.statement:
def supportedSource (K : Compacts (ℝ × E)) :
    ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K →L[ℝ] 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.seminorm_slice_supported_le
declarations.doc: Every slice seminorm is controlled by a native spacetime source seminorm.
declarations.statement:
lemma seminorm_slice_supported_le (K : Compacts (ℝ × E)) {R : ℝ} (hR0 : 0 ≤ R)
    (hR : ∀ p ∈ K, ‖p‖ ≤ R) (f : ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K)
    (k j : ℕ) (s : ℝ) :
    SchwartzMap.seminorm ℂ k j (slice F (supportedSource F K f) s) ≤
      R ^ k * ContDiffMapSupportedIn.seminorm ℝ (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K j f

declarations.name: TimeSlice.exists_fourier_supported_seminorm
declarations.doc: Fourier moments of all fixed-support sources are controlled by one continuous seminorm.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_fourier_supported_seminorm (K : Compacts (ℝ × E)) (N : ℕ) :
    ∃ q : Seminorm ℝ (ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K), Continuous q ∧
      ∀ (f : ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K) (s : ℝ) (ξ : E),
        ‖ξ‖ ^ N * ‖𝓕 (slice F (supportedSource F K f) s) ξ‖ ≤ q f

declarations.name: TimeSlice.exists_fourier_decay_supported_seminorm
declarations.doc: A continuous source seminorm controls arbitrary polynomial Fourier decay uniformly in time.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_fourier_decay_supported_seminorm (K : Compacts (ℝ × E)) (N : ℕ) :
    ∃ q : Seminorm ℝ (ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K), Continuous q ∧
      ∀ (f : ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K) (s : ℝ) (ξ : E),
        ‖𝓕 (slice F (supportedSource F K f) s) ξ‖ ≤ q f * (1 + ‖ξ‖) ^ (-(N : ℝ))

declarations.name: TimeSlice.supportedDt
declarations.doc: Time differentiation is a continuous endomorphism of every fixed-support source space.
declarations.statement:
def supportedDt (K : Compacts (ℝ × E)) :
    ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K →L[ℝ] ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K

declarations.name: TimeSlice.supportedSource_dt
declarations.statement:
lemma supportedSource_dt (K : Compacts (ℝ × E)) (f : ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K) :
    supportedSource F K (supportedDt F K f) = dt F (supportedSource F K f)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.supportedSource_iterate_dt
declarations.statement:
lemma supportedSource_iterate_dt (K : Compacts (ℝ × E)) (j : ℕ)
    (f : ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K) :
    supportedSource F K ((supportedDt F K)^[j] f) = (dt F)^[j] (supportedSource F K f)

declarations.name: TimeSlice.exists_timeDeriv_fourier_supported_seminorm
declarations.doc: Time derivatives of Fourier slices are bounded by continuous source seminorms.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_timeDeriv_fourier_supported_seminorm (K : Compacts (ℝ × E)) (j N : ℕ) :
    ∃ q : Seminorm ℝ (ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K), Continuous q ∧
      ∀ (f : ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K) (s : ℝ) (ξ : E),
        ‖iteratedDeriv j (fun r => 𝓕 (slice F (supportedSource F K f) r) ξ) s‖ ≤
          q f * (1 + ‖ξ‖) ^ (-(N : ℝ))

declarations.name: TimeSlice.exists_char_timeDeriv_supported_seminorm
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_char_timeDeriv_supported_seminorm (K : Compacts (ℝ × E)) (i j N : ℕ) :
    ∃ q : Seminorm ℝ (ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K), Continuous q ∧
      ∀ (f : ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K) (s : ℝ) (ξ : E),
        (2 * π * ‖ξ‖) ^ i *
          ‖iteratedDeriv j (fun r => 𝓕 (slice F (supportedSource F K f) r) ξ) s‖ ≤
            q f * (1 + ‖ξ‖) ^ (-(N : ℝ))

modules.title: Translation of test functions
modules.doc:
Translation is continuous on the space of test functions.

## i. Overview

Composition with a translation `x ↦ x + b` maps a smooth function with support in a compact set
`K` to a smooth function with support in the translated set. It does not change the norms of the
derivatives. So it is continuous between the spaces of test functions with fixed support. It is
then continuous on all test functions.

## ii. Key results

- `TestFunction.precompTranslationSupportedCLM` : the pullback between fixed-support spaces.
- `TestFunction.precompTranslationCLM` : the pullback is continuous on test functions.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The pullback along a translation

## iv. References

None.

## A. The pullback along a translation

- `TestFunction.precompTranslationSupportedCLM` : the pullback between fixed-support spaces.
- `TestFunction.precompTranslationCLM` : the pullback is continuous on test functions.

declarations.name: TestFunction.precompTranslationSupportedCLM
declarations.doc: The pullback along a translation between fixed-support smooth test spaces.

declarations.name: TestFunction.precompTranslationCLM
declarations.doc: The pullback along a translation is continuous on test functions.
declarations.statement: def precompTranslationCLM (b : A) : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens A), F) →L[ℝ] 𝓓((⊤ : Opens A), F)

declarations.name: TestFunction.precompTranslationCLM_apply
declarations.doc: The pullback along a translation evaluates the function at the translated point.
declarations.statement:
lemma precompTranslationCLM_apply (b : A) (f : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens A), F)) (x : A) :
    precompTranslationCLM b f x = f (x + b)

modules.title: Derivations and representations on the exterior algebra
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Mathlib's `ExteriorAlgebra` carries the universal property `ExteriorAlgebra.lift` and the
functorial map `ExteriorAlgebra.map`, but neither the derivation extending a linear
endomorphism of the generators nor the representation extending a representation on them.
This file provides both, as the exterior counterparts of the symmetric-algebra
constructions in `PhyslibAlpha.Mathematics.SymmetricAlgebra`.

A linear endomorphism `d` of `M` extends uniquely to an *even* derivation of the exterior
algebra — the Leibniz rule with no Koszul signs — because the generator map
`ι x ↦ (ι x, ι (d x))` into the trivial square-zero extension squares to zero: degree-one
elements of an exterior algebra anticommute. A representation of a monoid `G` on `M`
extends to one on the exterior algebra by functoriality of `ExteriorAlgebra.map`, and every
element of `G` then acts by an algebra homomorphism.

## ii. Key results

- `ExteriorAlgebra.derivationOfLinear` : the even derivation extending a linear
  endomorphism of the generators.
- `ExteriorAlgebra.derivationOfLinear_mul` : the Leibniz rule.
- `ExteriorAlgebra.derivationOfLinear_comm_apply` : derivations extending commuting
  endomorphisms commute.
- `ExteriorAlgebra.algHom_derivationOfLinear` : an algebra map determined by an
  intertwining linear map carries one derivation to the other.
- `Representation.exteriorAlgebra` : the representation extending one on the generators.
- `Representation.exteriorAlgebra_apply_mul` : each element acts multiplicatively.
- `ExteriorAlgebra.exteriorAlgebra_derivationOfLinear` : covariance of the derivation
  under the representation.
- `ExteriorAlgebra.mapEquiv` : transport of the algebra along a linear equivalence of the
  generators.
- `ExteriorAlgebra.algHom_exteriorAlgebra` : an algebra map determined by an intertwining
  linear map carries one representation to the other.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The derivation extending a linear endomorphism
- B. The representation extending a representation on the generators
- C. Transport along a linear equivalence

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The derivation extending a linear endomorphism
## B. The representation extending a representation on the generators

## C. Transport along a linear equivalence

Mathlib's `ExteriorAlgebra.congr` goes through `CliffordAlgebra.equivOfIsometry`, whose
quadratic-form layer the elaborator cannot see through cheaply once the underlying module is
a large direct sum. The version below is built from `ExteriorAlgebra.map` instead.

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.derivationGen
declarations.doc:
The generator map of the derivation extending `d`, into the trivial square-zero
extension of the exterior algebra: `ι x ↦ (ι x, ι (d x))`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivationGen :
    M →ₗ[R] TrivSqZeroExt (ExteriorAlgebra R M) (ExteriorAlgebra R M)

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.derivationGen_fst
declarations.statement: lemma derivationGen_fst (x : M) : (derivationGen d x).fst = ι R x

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.derivationGen_snd
declarations.statement: lemma derivationGen_snd (x : M) : (derivationGen d x).snd = ι R (d x)

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.derivationGen_mul_self
declarations.doc:
The generator map squares to zero: degree-one elements of the exterior algebra
anticommute, which is exactly the square-zero condition on the pair.
declarations.statement: lemma derivationGen_mul_self (x : M) : derivationGen d x * derivationGen d x = 0

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.derivationHom
declarations.doc:
The lift of the derivation extending `d` to the trivial square-zero extension of the
exterior algebra: the algebra homomorphism `x ↦ (x, derivationOfLinear d x)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivationHom :
    ExteriorAlgebra R M →ₐ[R]
      TrivSqZeroExt (ExteriorAlgebra R M) (ExteriorAlgebra R M)

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.derivationHom_ι
declarations.statement: lemma derivationHom_ι (x : M) : derivationHom d (ι R x) = derivationGen d x

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.derivationHom_fst
declarations.doc: The first component of the square-zero lift is the identity.
declarations.statement: lemma derivationHom_fst (x : ExteriorAlgebra R M) : (derivationHom d x).fst = x

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.derivationOfLinear
declarations.doc:
The even derivation of the exterior algebra extending a linear endomorphism `d` of
`M`: the map obeying the Leibniz rule, with no Koszul signs, whose value on a generator
`ι x` is `ι (d x)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def derivationOfLinear : ExteriorAlgebra R M →ₗ[R] ExteriorAlgebra R M

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.derivationOfLinear_ι
declarations.statement: lemma derivationOfLinear_ι (x : M) : derivationOfLinear d (ι R x) = ι R (d x)

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.derivationOfLinear_one
declarations.statement: lemma derivationOfLinear_one : derivationOfLinear d (1 : ExteriorAlgebra R M) = 0

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.derivationOfLinear_algebraMap
declarations.statement:
lemma derivationOfLinear_algebraMap (r : R) :
    derivationOfLinear d (algebraMap R (ExteriorAlgebra R M) r) = 0

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.derivationOfLinear_mul
declarations.doc:
The Leibniz rule for the derivation extending `d`, with no Koszul signs: the derivation
is even even though the generators are odd.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivationOfLinear_mul (x y : ExteriorAlgebra R M) :
    derivationOfLinear d (x * y)
      = derivationOfLinear d x * y + x * derivationOfLinear d y

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.derivationOfLinear_comm_apply
declarations.doc: Derivations extending commuting endomorphisms commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivationOfLinear_comm_apply {d₁ d₂ : M →ₗ[R] M} (h : d₁ ∘ₗ d₂ = d₂ ∘ₗ d₁)
    (x : ExteriorAlgebra R M) :
    derivationOfLinear d₁ (derivationOfLinear d₂ x)
      = derivationOfLinear d₂ (derivationOfLinear d₁ x)

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.algHom_derivationOfLinear
declarations.doc:
An algebra map carries one derivation to the other when the linear map it is
determined by on the generators intertwines the two endomorphisms. The hypotheses are
stated pointwise so that the lemma can be applied without rewriting inside a large
algebra.

declarations.name: Representation.exteriorAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The representation on the exterior algebra extending a representation on the
generators, by functoriality of `ExteriorAlgebra.map`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def exteriorAlgebra (ρ : Representation R G M) :
    Representation R G (ExteriorAlgebra R M)

declarations.name: Representation.exteriorAlgebra_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma exteriorAlgebra_apply (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G)
    (x : ExteriorAlgebra R M) :
    ρ.exteriorAlgebra g x = ExteriorAlgebra.map (ρ g) x

declarations.name: Representation.exteriorAlgebra_ι
declarations.statement:
lemma exteriorAlgebra_ι (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G) (x : M) :
    ρ.exteriorAlgebra g (ExteriorAlgebra.ι R x) = ExteriorAlgebra.ι R (ρ g x)

declarations.name: Representation.exteriorAlgebra_apply_one
declarations.statement:
lemma exteriorAlgebra_apply_one (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G) :
    ρ.exteriorAlgebra g (1 : ExteriorAlgebra R M) = 1

declarations.name: Representation.exteriorAlgebra_apply_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma exteriorAlgebra_apply_mul (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G)
    (x y : ExteriorAlgebra R M) :
    ρ.exteriorAlgebra g (x * y) = ρ.exteriorAlgebra g x * ρ.exteriorAlgebra g y

declarations.name: Representation.exteriorAlgebra_algebraMap
declarations.statement:
lemma exteriorAlgebra_algebraMap (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G) (r : R) :
    ρ.exteriorAlgebra g (algebraMap R (ExteriorAlgebra R M) r)
      = algebraMap R (ExteriorAlgebra R M) r

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.exteriorAlgebra_derivationOfLinear
declarations.doc:
Covariance of the derivation under the representation. If the representation
carries each endomorphism of a family into a combination of the others on the generators,
then it carries the derivation extending one into the same combination of the derivations
extending the others on the whole exterior algebra. This is the shape the statement that
the total derivative is a Lorentz vector takes; it is proved by induction rather than by
algebra-map extensionality, a derivation not being an algebra map.
declarations.statement:
lemma exteriorAlgebra_derivationOfLinear {G κ : Type*} [Monoid G] [Fintype κ]
    (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G) (d : κ → M →ₗ[R] M) (μ : κ) (c : κ → R)
    (h : ∀ x, ρ g (d μ x) = ∑ a, c a • d a (ρ g x)) (y : ExteriorAlgebra R M) :
    ρ.exteriorAlgebra g (derivationOfLinear (d μ) y)
      = ∑ a, c a • derivationOfLinear (d a) (ρ.exteriorAlgebra g y)

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.algHom_exteriorAlgebra
declarations.doc:
An algebra map carries one representation to the other when the linear map it is
determined by on the generators intertwines the two representations on them. Unlike the
derivation statement this is pure extensionality of algebra maps, each group element
acting by one; the hypotheses are stated pointwise so that the lemma can be applied
without rewriting inside a large algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma algHom_exteriorAlgebra {N G : Type*} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Monoid G]
    (F : ExteriorAlgebra R M →ₐ[R] ExteriorAlgebra R N) {f : M →ₗ[R] N}
    (hF : ∀ x, F (ι R x) = ι R (f x))
    {ρ : Representation R G M} {σ : Representation R G N} (g : G)
    (h : ∀ x, f (ρ g x) = σ g (f x)) (y : ExteriorAlgebra R M) :
    F (ρ.exteriorAlgebra g y) = σ.exteriorAlgebra g (F y)

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.mapEquiv
declarations.doc:
Transport of an exterior algebra along a linear equivalence, built from
`ExteriorAlgebra.map` so that no `CliffordAlgebra` isometry has to be unfolded.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def mapEquiv {R M N : Type*} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (e : M ≃ₗ[R] N) :
    ExteriorAlgebra R M ≃ₐ[R] ExteriorAlgebra R N

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.mapEquiv_apply_ι
declarations.statement:
lemma mapEquiv_apply_ι {R M N : Type*} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (e : M ≃ₗ[R] N) (x : M) :
    mapEquiv e (ExteriorAlgebra.ι R x) = ExteriorAlgebra.ι R (e x)

modules.title: Scalar matrices
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Lemmas on the scalar matrices `Matrix.scalar n x` of a commutative `*`-ring: they commute
with the conjugate transpose, with entrywise maps fixing zero and with scalar actions; they
are fixed by conjugation with a unitary scalar; and a self-adjoint element gives a scalar
matrix real-linearly. A `1 × 1` matrix is the scalar matrix of its entry.

## ii. Key results

- `Matrix.star_scalar`, `Matrix.map_scalar`, `Matrix.scalar_smul` : compatibilities.
- `Matrix.scalar_eq_conj` : conjugation by a unitary scalar fixes a scalar matrix.
- `Matrix.scalarSelfAdjoint` : self-adjoint elements as scalar matrices.
- `Matrix.eq_scalar_fin_one` : a `1 × 1` matrix is scalar.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Scalar matrices

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: Matrix.star_scalar
declarations.doc: The conjugate transpose of a scalar matrix is the scalar matrix of the star.
declarations.statement: lemma star_scalar [StarRing R] (x : R) : star (scalar n x) = scalar n (star x)

declarations.name: Matrix.map_scalar
declarations.doc: An entrywise map fixing zero sends a scalar matrix to a scalar matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_scalar {S : Type*} [CommRing S] (f : R → S) (hf : f 0 = 0) (x : R) :
    (scalar n x).map f = scalar n (f x)

declarations.name: Matrix.scalar_smul
declarations.doc: A scalar action passes into a scalar matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma scalar_smul {M : Type*} [Monoid M] [DistribMulAction M R] (c : M) (x : R) :
    scalar n (c • x) = c • scalar n x

declarations.name: Matrix.scalar_eq_conj
declarations.doc: Conjugation by a unitary scalar fixes a scalar matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma scalar_eq_conj [StarRing R] {u : R} (hu : u * star u = 1) (x : R) :
    scalar n x = scalar n u * scalar n x * star (scalar n u)

declarations.name: Matrix.scalarSelfAdjoint
declarations.doc: A self-adjoint element as a scalar matrix, real-linearly.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def scalarSelfAdjoint [StarRing R] [Algebra ℝ R] [StarModule ℝ R] :
    ↥(selfAdjoint R) →ₗ[ℝ] Matrix n n R

declarations.name: Matrix.scalarSelfAdjoint_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma scalarSelfAdjoint_apply [StarRing R] [Algebra ℝ R] [StarModule ℝ R]
    (a : ↥(selfAdjoint R)) : (scalarSelfAdjoint (n := n)) a = scalar n a.1

declarations.name: Matrix.eq_scalar_fin_one
declarations.doc: A `1 × 1` matrix is the scalar matrix of its entry.
declarations.statement: lemma eq_scalar_fin_one (A : Matrix (Fin 1) (Fin 1) R) : A = scalar (Fin 1) (A 0 0)

modules.title: Peeling the first slot off a sum over tuples
modules.doc:
Sums over tuples of indices, split into the first slot and the remaining ones.

## i. Overview

A monomial in several slots contributes one factor per slot, and summing such monomials over
all tuples of indices is the basic operation of a component expansion. Both lemmas here peel
the first slot off such a sum, turning a sum over `Fin (n + 1) → ι` into a double sum over `ι`
and `Fin n → ι` along `Fin.consEquiv`. `sum_pi_succ_prod_smul` does this for a sum weighted by
one scalar per slot, and `sum_filter_weight_succ` for a sum restricted to the tuples of a
prescribed total weight, where the first slot takes its own weight and the rest make up the
remainder. They are the induction steps of the component expansions which the weight
decompositions run on.

## ii. Key results

- `Physlib.Fin.sum_pi_succ_prod_smul` : a sum over tuples, weighted by one scalar factor per
  slot, split into the first slot and the rest.
- `Physlib.Fin.sum_filter_weight_succ` : the same split for a sum over the tuples of a
  prescribed total weight.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Splitting off the first slot

## iv. References

The `Fin.consEquiv` along which the splitting is done is Mathlib's.

sections.text: ## A. Splitting off the first slot

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.sum_pi_succ_prod_smul
declarations.doc:
A sum over tuples of indices, weighted by one scalar factor per slot, split into the
first slot and the remaining ones.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_pi_succ_prod_smul {R M ι : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
    [Fintype ι] {n : ℕ} (c : Fin (n + 1) → ι → R) (X : (Fin (n + 1) → ι) → M) :
    ∑ q : Fin (n + 1) → ι, (∏ i, c i (q i)) • X q =
      ∑ b : ι, ∑ p : Fin n → ι, (c 0 b * ∏ i, c i.succ (p i)) • X (Fin.cons b p)

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.sum_filter_weight_succ
declarations.doc:
Peeling the first slot off a sum over the tuples of a prescribed total weight: the first
slot takes its own weight `w b` and the remaining slots make up the rest. Each slot draws its
letter from the same alphabet `ι`, `w` gives a letter its weight and the weights of the slots
add; `f s` is the factor contributed by slot `s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_filter_weight_succ {R ι : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [Fintype ι] {n : ℕ} (w : ι → ℤ)
    (f : Fin (n + 1) → ι → R) (m : ℤ) :
    ∑ q ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun q : Fin (n + 1) → ι => (∑ s, w (q s)) = m), ∏ s, f s (q s)
      = ∑ b : ι, f 0 b
          * ∑ q ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun q : Fin n → ι => (∑ s, w (q s)) = m - w b),
              ∏ s, f s.succ (q s)

modules.title: Fourier integrals and their derivatives
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Derivative bounds for the Fourier character and the Laplacian of an inverse Fourier integral.

## ii. Key results

- `laplacian_fourierInvIntegral` : The Laplacian of the inverse Fourier integral of `h` is the
  integral of `-(2π)² ‖ξ‖² h`.
- `char_pow_mul_decay_le` : Polynomial factors from spatial derivatives are absorbed by additional
  Fourier decay.
- `fourierInvIntegral_eq_fourier` : The inverse Fourier integral is the Fourier integral of the
  reflected function.
- `norm_iteratedFDeriv_timeShift_le` : The derivatives of a time translate are bounded by those of
  the function.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Laplacian of an inverse Fourier integral
- B. Derivative bounds for the Fourier character and for time translates
- C. Smoothness of the retarded solution

## iv. References

None.

## A. The Laplacian of an inverse Fourier integral

Lemmas: `fourierInvIntegral_eq_fourier`, `laplacian_fourierInvIntegral`.

## B. Derivative bounds for the Fourier character and for time translates

Lemmas: `iteratedDeriv_fourierChar`, `norm_iteratedFDeriv_fourierChar`, `contDiff_fourierChar_real`,
`norm_iteratedFDeriv_char_le`, `norm_iteratedFDeriv_timeShift_le`, `char_pow_mul_decay_le`.

## C. Smoothness of the retarded solution

Lemmas: `contDiff_char_pair`.

declarations.name: FourierIntegral.fourierInvIntegral_eq_fourier
declarations.doc: The inverse Fourier integral is the Fourier integral of the reflected function.
declarations.statement:
lemma fourierInvIntegral_eq_fourier (h : E → F) (x : E) :
    ∫ ξ : E, (𝐞 (inner ℝ ξ x) : ℂ) • h ξ = 𝓕 (fun v => h (-v)) x

declarations.name: FourierIntegral.laplacian_fourierInvIntegral
declarations.doc: The Laplacian of the inverse Fourier integral of `h` is the integral of `-(2π)² ‖ξ‖² h`.
declarations.statement:
lemma laplacian_fourierInvIntegral {h : E → F} (hm : AEStronglyMeasurable h volume)
    (hi : ∀ n : ℕ, n ≤ 2 → Integrable (fun ξ : E => ‖ξ‖ ^ n * ‖h ξ‖)) (x : E) :
    Δ (fun y : E => ∫ ξ : E, (𝐞 (inner ℝ ξ y) : ℂ) • h ξ) x =
      ∫ ξ : E, (-((2 * π) ^ 2 * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) • ((𝐞 (inner ℝ ξ x) : ℂ) • h ξ)

declarations.name: FourierIntegral.iteratedDeriv_fourierChar
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_fourierChar (i : ℕ) :
    iteratedDeriv i (fun r : ℝ => (𝐞 r : ℂ)) = fun r => (2 * π * Complex.I) ^ i * (𝐞 r : ℂ)

declarations.name: FourierIntegral.norm_iteratedFDeriv_fourierChar
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_iteratedFDeriv_fourierChar (i : ℕ) (r : ℝ) :
    ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ i (fun r : ℝ => (𝐞 r : ℂ)) r‖ = (2 * π) ^ i

declarations.name: FourierIntegral.contDiff_fourierChar_real
declarations.statement: lemma contDiff_fourierChar_real : ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun r : ℝ => (𝐞 r : ℂ))

declarations.name: FourierIntegral.norm_iteratedFDeriv_char_le
declarations.doc: The derivatives of `(t, x) ↦ 𝐞 ⟪ξ, x⟫` are bounded by `(2π‖ξ‖)ⁱ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_iteratedFDeriv_char_le (ξ : E) (i : ℕ) (q : ℝ × E) :
    ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ i (fun q : ℝ × E => (𝐞 (inner ℝ ξ q.2) : ℂ)) q‖ ≤ (2 * π * ‖ξ‖) ^ i

declarations.name: FourierIntegral.norm_iteratedFDeriv_timeShift_le
declarations.doc: The derivatives of a time translate are bounded by those of the function.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_iteratedFDeriv_timeShift_le (g : ℝ → F) (hg : ContDiff ℝ ∞ g) (r : ℝ) (j : ℕ)
    (q : ℝ × E) :
    ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ j (fun q : ℝ × E => g (q.1 - r)) q‖ ≤ ‖iteratedDeriv j g (q.1 - r)‖

declarations.name: FourierIntegral.char_pow_mul_decay_le
declarations.doc: Polynomial factors from spatial derivatives are absorbed by additional Fourier decay.
declarations.statement:
lemma char_pow_mul_decay_le {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] (ξ : E) (i N : ℕ) :
    (2 * π * ‖ξ‖) ^ i * (1 + ‖ξ‖) ^ (-((i + N : ℕ) : ℝ)) ≤
      (2 * π) ^ i * (1 + ‖ξ‖) ^ (-(N : ℝ))

declarations.name: FourierIntegral.contDiff_char_pair
declarations.statement:
lemma contDiff_char_pair : ContDiff ℝ ∞ fun w : (ℝ × E) × (ℝ × E) =>
    (𝐞 (inner ℝ w.2.2 w.1.2) : ℂ)

modules.title: Fourier inversion for Schwartz functions on the line
modules.doc:
A Schwartz function on the line is the integral of its transform against the exponential.

## i. Overview

Mathlib states Fourier inversion for the Fourier multiplier on the Schwartz space. This file
unfolds it to the pointwise integral with the character `𝐞 (y * ξ)`. The integrand is integrable
because the transform is.

## ii. Key results

- `SchwartzMap.integral_char_smul_fourier` : the pointwise inversion formula.
- `SchwartzMap.integral_char_mul_fourier` : the same with the product in place of the scalar action.
- `SchwartzMap.integrable_char_mul_fourier` : the integrand is integrable.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Pointwise inversion

## iv. References

None.

## A. Pointwise inversion

- `SchwartzMap.integral_char_smul_fourier` : the pointwise inversion formula.
- `SchwartzMap.integral_char_mul_fourier` : the same with the product.
- `SchwartzMap.integrable_char_mul_fourier` : the integrand is integrable.

declarations.name: SchwartzMap.integral_char_smul_fourier
declarations.doc: **Fourier inversion on the line.**
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_char_smul_fourier (g : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) (y : ℝ) :
    ∫ ξ : ℝ, (𝐞 (y * ξ) : ℂ) • 𝓕 g ξ = g y

declarations.name: SchwartzMap.integral_char_mul_fourier
declarations.doc: Fourier inversion on the line with the product in place of the scalar action.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_char_mul_fourier (g : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) (y : ℝ) :
    ∫ ξ : ℝ, (𝐞 (y * ξ) : ℂ) * 𝓕 g ξ = g y

declarations.name: SchwartzMap.integrable_char_mul_fourier
declarations.doc: The integrand of Fourier inversion is integrable.
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_char_mul_fourier (g : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) (y : ℝ) :
    Integrable fun ξ : ℝ => (𝐞 (y * ξ) : ℂ) * 𝓕 g ξ

modules.title: The Fourier transform under a linear change of variables
modules.doc:
Composition with the inverse transpose of a linear equivalence turns into evaluation of the
transform at the image point.

## i. Overview

For a linear equivalence `L` of a finite dimensional inner product space the map `A = (L⁻¹)ᵀ` is
again a linear equivalence. The Fourier transform of `f ∘ A` at `ξ` is `|det L|` times the
transform of `f` at `L ξ`. The proof moves the integral along `A` with the Haar measure scaling
and uses `⟨A⁻¹ y, ξ⟩ = ⟨y, L ξ⟩`.

## ii. Key results

- `Fourier.invTranspose` : the inverse transpose of a linear equivalence.
- `Fourier.fourier_comp_invTranspose` : the transform of `f ∘ (L⁻¹)ᵀ`.
- `Fourier.fourier_comp_isometry` : the transform commutes with linear isometries.
- `Fourier.fourier_comp_add_right` : the transform of a translate.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The inverse transpose
- B. The transform
- C. Isometries
- D. Translations

## iv. References

None.

## A. The inverse transpose

- `Fourier.det_adjoint` : the determinant of the adjoint.
- `Fourier.invTranspose` : the inverse transpose of a linear equivalence.

## B. The transform

- `Fourier.fourier_comp_invTranspose` : the transform of `f ∘ (L⁻¹)ᵀ`.

## C. Isometries

- `Fourier.fourier_eq_complex` : the transform of a complex valued function.
- `Fourier.fourier_comp_isometry` : the transform commutes with linear isometries.

## D. Translations

- `Fourier.fourier_comp_add_right` : the transform of a translate.

declarations.name: Fourier.det_adjoint
declarations.doc: The determinant of the adjoint.
declarations.statement: lemma det_adjoint (f : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) : LinearMap.det (LinearMap.adjoint f) = LinearMap.det f

declarations.name: Fourier.invTranspose
declarations.doc: The inverse transpose of a linear equivalence for the inner product.
declarations.statement: def invTranspose (L : V ≃L[ℝ] V) : V ≃L[ℝ] V

declarations.name: Fourier.invTranspose_symm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma invTranspose_symm_apply (L : V ≃L[ℝ] V) (x : V) :
    (invTranspose L).symm x = LinearMap.adjoint L.toLinearMap x

declarations.name: Fourier.inner_invTranspose_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_invTranspose_symm (L : V ≃L[ℝ] V) (x y : V) :
    inner ℝ ((invTranspose L).symm x) y = inner ℝ x (L y)

declarations.name: Fourier.abs_det_invTranspose
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_det_invTranspose (L : V ≃L[ℝ] V) :
    |LinearMap.det (invTranspose L : V →ₗ[ℝ] V)| = |LinearMap.det (L : V →ₗ[ℝ] V)|⁻¹

declarations.name: Fourier.fourier_comp_invTranspose
declarations.doc:
**Fourier transform and a linear change of variables.** Composition with the inverse
transpose of `L` turns into evaluation at `L ξ` and the factor `|det L|`.
declarations.statement:
lemma fourier_comp_invTranspose (L : V ≃L[ℝ] V) (f : V → E) (ξ : V) :
    𝓕 (f ∘ invTranspose L) ξ = |LinearMap.det (L : V →ₗ[ℝ] V)| • 𝓕 f (L ξ)

declarations.name: Fourier.fourier_eq_complex
declarations.doc: The Fourier transform of a complex valued function is the explicit integral.
declarations.statement:
lemma fourier_eq_complex {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V]
    [MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V] [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] (f : V → ℂ) (ξ : V) :
    𝓕 f ξ = ∫ x, (𝐞 (-inner ℝ x ξ) : ℂ) • f x

declarations.name: Fourier.fourier_comp_isometry
declarations.doc: The Fourier transform commutes with linear isometries.
declarations.statement:
lemma fourier_comp_isometry (A : V ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] W) (f : W → ℂ) (ξ : V) :
    𝓕 (f ∘ A) ξ = 𝓕 f (A ξ)

declarations.name: Fourier.fourier_comp_add_right
declarations.doc: The Fourier transform turns translation into a phase.
declarations.statement:
lemma fourier_comp_add_right (f : V → ℂ) (q ζ : V) :
    𝓕 (fun v => f (v + q)) ζ = 𝐞 (inner ℝ q ζ) • 𝓕 f ζ

modules.title: The marginal of a Schwartz function on a Euclidean product
modules.doc:
The integral of a Schwartz function over the second factor is continuous and integrable. Its
Fourier transform is the restriction of the transform to the first factor.

## i. Overview

A Schwartz function on `WithLp 2 (E × F)` decays faster than every power in the second variable,
uniformly in the first. The marginal over `F` is therefore a continuous integrable function on
`E`. Its Fourier transform at `ξ` is the transform of the original function at `(ξ, 0)`.

## ii. Key results

- `EuclideanProd.fourier_marginal` : the transform of the marginal is the restriction of the
  transform.
- `EuclideanProd.continuous_marginal` : the marginal of a Schwartz function is continuous.
- `EuclideanProd.integrable_marginal` : the marginal of a Schwartz function is integrable.
- `EuclideanProd.fourier_eq_integral_integral` : the transform is the iterated transform.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The transform of the marginal
- B. The marginal of a Schwartz function
- C. The iterated transform

## iv. References

None.

## A. The transform of the marginal

- `EuclideanProd.fourier_marginal` : the transform of the marginal is the restriction of the
  transform.

## B. The marginal of a Schwartz function

- `EuclideanProd.exists_bound_marginal` : a Schwartz function decays in the extra variables.
- `EuclideanProd.continuous_marginal` : the marginal of a Schwartz function is continuous.
- `EuclideanProd.integrable_marginal` : the marginal of a Schwartz function is integrable.

## C. The iterated transform

- `EuclideanProd.fourier_eq_integral_integral` : the transform is the iterated transform.

declarations.name: EuclideanProd.fourier_marginal
declarations.doc:
**The transform of the marginal.** The Fourier transform of the integral over `F` is the
restriction of the transform to the frequencies `(ξ, 0)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma fourier_marginal {φ : WithLp 2 (E × F) → ℂ} (hφ : Integrable φ) (ξ : E) :
    ∫ x : E, (𝐞 (-inner ℝ x ξ) : ℂ) • ∫ y : F, φ (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y)) =
      ∫ z, (𝐞 (-inner ℝ z (WithLp.toLp 2 (ξ, (0 : F)))) : ℂ) • φ z

declarations.name: EuclideanProd.exists_bound_marginal
declarations.doc: A Schwartz function decays in the extra variables, uniformly in the others.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_bound_marginal (h : 𝓢(WithLp 2 (E × F), ℂ)) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (x : E) (y : F), ‖h (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y))‖ ≤
      C * (1 + ‖y‖) ^ (-((Module.finrank ℝ F + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ))

declarations.name: EuclideanProd.continuous_marginal
declarations.doc: The marginal of a Schwartz function is continuous.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_marginal (h : 𝓢(WithLp 2 (E × F), ℂ)) :
    Continuous fun x : E => ∫ y : F, h (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y))

declarations.name: EuclideanProd.integrable_marginal
declarations.doc: The marginal of a Schwartz function is integrable.
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_marginal (h : 𝓢(WithLp 2 (E × F), ℂ)) :
    Integrable fun x : E => ∫ y : F, h (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y))

declarations.name: EuclideanProd.fourier_eq_integral_integral
declarations.doc:
**The iterated form of the Fourier transform.** The transform on the Euclidean product is the
transform in the first variable of the transform in the second.
declarations.statement:
lemma fourier_eq_integral_integral (g : 𝓢(WithLp 2 (E × F), ℂ)) (ζ : E) (ξ : F) :
    𝓕 g (WithLp.toLp 2 (ζ, ξ)) = ∫ x : E, 𝐞 (-(inner ℝ x ζ)) •
      ∫ y : F, 𝐞 (-(inner ℝ y ξ)) • g (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y))

modules.title: The integral of a Fourier transform is bounded by Schwartz seminorms
modules.doc:
The `L¹` norm of the Fourier transform of a Schwartz function is bounded by finitely many
Schwartz seminorms of the function.

## i. Overview

The Fourier transform is continuous on Schwartz space. A weighted supremum of the transform is
therefore bounded by finitely many seminorms of the function. The weight `(1 + ‖ξ‖)^n` with
`n` above the dimension makes the transform integrable. The constants do not depend on the
function.

## ii. Key results

- `exists_integral_norm_fourier_le` : the bound of `∫ ‖𝓕 g‖` by seminorms of `g`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The bound

## iv. References

None.

## A. The bound

- `exists_integral_norm_fourier_le` : the bound of `∫ ‖𝓕 g‖` by seminorms of `g`.

declarations.name: SchwartzMap.exists_integral_norm_fourier_le
declarations.doc:
**The `L¹` norm of a Fourier transform.** The integral of `‖𝓕 g‖` is bounded by a constant
times a finite supremum of Schwartz seminorms of `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_integral_norm_fourier_le :
    ∃ (S : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) (C : ℝ), 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ g : 𝓢(E, F),
      ∫ ξ : E, ‖𝓕 g ξ‖ ≤ C * (S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℂ E F)) g

modules.title: Simplices
modules.doc:
Simplices as convex hulls of affinely independent points, and the standard simplex.

## i. Overview

A simplex is the convex hull of finitely many affinely independent points, its extreme points. Every
point of a simplex is a mixture of the extreme points with unique weights, its barycentric
coordinates. The model is the standard simplex of probability vectors in `ι → ℝ`, whose extreme
points are the standard basis vectors. Being a simplex is invariant under affine equivalences.

## ii. Key results

- `IsSimplex` states that a convex set is generated by finitely many affinely independent extreme
  points.
- `IsSimplex.eq_of_affineCombination_eq` proves that the weights are unique.
- `affineIndependent_of_convexCombination_eq` proves that unique weights give affine independence.
- `stdSimplexSet` is the standard simplex in `ι → ℝ`.
- `extremePoints_stdSimplexSet` proves that its extreme points are the standard basis vectors.
- `isSimplex_of_affineEquiv_stdSimplexSet` proves that a set affinely equivalent to a standard
  simplex is a simplex.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Simplices
- B. The standard simplex
- C. Affine equivalences

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: IsSimplex
declarations.doc: A set generated by finitely many affinely independent extreme points.
declarations.statement:
structure IsSimplex (K : Set E) : Prop where
  /-- There are finitely many extreme points. -/
  finite : (K.extremePoints ℝ).Finite
  /-- The set is the convex hull of its extreme points. -/
  generates : K = convexHull ℝ (K.extremePoints ℝ)
  /-- The extreme points are affinely independent. -/
  affineIndependent : AffineIndependent ℝ (Subtype.val : ↥(K.extremePoints ℝ) → E)

declarations.name: IsSimplex.eq_of_affineCombination_eq
declarations.doc:
Two convex combinations of the extreme points of a simplex giving the same point have the
same weights.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsSimplex.eq_of_affineCombination_eq {K : Set E} (hK : IsSimplex K)
    (s₁ s₂ : Finset ↥(K.extremePoints ℝ)) (w₁ w₂ : ↥(K.extremePoints ℝ) → ℝ)
    (hw₁ : ∑ i ∈ s₁, w₁ i = 1) (hw₂ : ∑ i ∈ s₂, w₂ i = 1)
    (heq : s₁.affineCombination ℝ Subtype.val w₁ = s₂.affineCombination ℝ Subtype.val w₂) :
    Set.indicator (↑s₁) w₁ = Set.indicator (↑s₂) w₂

declarations.name: isSimplex_of_extremePoints_eq_pair
declarations.doc: A set generated by two distinct extreme points is a simplex.
declarations.statement:
lemma isSimplex_of_extremePoints_eq_pair {K : Set E} {p q : E} (hpq : p ≠ q)
    (hK : K = convexHull ℝ {p, q}) (hext : K.extremePoints ℝ = {p, q}) : IsSimplex K

declarations.name: IsSimplex.card_le_finrank_add_one_of_mapsTo
declarations.doc: A simplex has at most `finrank + 1` extreme points.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsSimplex.card_le_finrank_add_one_of_mapsTo {K : Set E} [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    (hK : IsSimplex K) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {p : ι → E} (hp : Function.Injective p)
    (hpK : ∀ i, p i ∈ K.extremePoints ℝ) :
    Fintype.card ι ≤ Module.finrank ℝ E + 1

declarations.name: sum_max_neg_zero_eq
declarations.doc: Splitting weights summing to zero into positive and negative parts gives equal sums.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_max_neg_zero_eq {ι : Type*} {s : Finset ι} {w : ι → ℝ} (hw : ∑ i ∈ s, w i = 0) :
    ∑ i ∈ s, max (-w i) 0 = ∑ i ∈ s, max (w i) 0

declarations.name: sum_max_smul_eq
affineIndependent_of_convexCombination_eq
declarations.doc: A family is affinely independent when its convex combinations have unique weights.
declarations.statement:
lemma affineIndependent_of_convexCombination_eq {ι : Type*} {p : ι → E}
    (h : ∀ (s : Finset ι) (w₁ w₂ : ι → ℝ), (∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ w₁ i) → (∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ w₂ i) →
      ∑ i ∈ s, w₁ i = 1 → ∑ i ∈ s, w₂ i = 1 → ∑ i ∈ s, w₁ i • p i = ∑ i ∈ s, w₂ i • p i →
      ∀ i ∈ s, w₁ i = w₂ i) : AffineIndependent ℝ p

declarations.name: stdSimplexSet
declarations.doc: The standard simplex in `ι → ℝ`: the vectors with nonnegative coordinates summing to `1`.
declarations.statement: def stdSimplexSet : Set (ι → ℝ)

declarations.name: convex_stdSimplexSet
declarations.statement: lemma convex_stdSimplexSet : Convex ℝ (stdSimplexSet ι)

declarations.name: le_one_of_mem_stdSimplexSet
declarations.statement: lemma le_one_of_mem_stdSimplexSet {f : ι → ℝ} (hf : f ∈ stdSimplexSet ι) (i : ι) : f i ≤ 1

declarations.name: single_mem_stdSimplexSet
declarations.statement: lemma single_mem_stdSimplexSet (i : ι) : Pi.single i (1 : ℝ) ∈ stdSimplexSet ι

declarations.name: eq_single_of_mem_stdSimplexSet
declarations.doc: A point of the standard simplex with coordinate `1` at `i` is the `i`-th basis vector.

declarations.name: convexHull_range_single
declarations.statement:
lemma convexHull_range_single :
    convexHull ℝ (Set.range fun i : ι => Pi.single i (1 : ℝ)) = stdSimplexSet ι

declarations.name: extremePoints_stdSimplexSet
declarations.doc: The extreme points of the standard simplex are the standard basis vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma extremePoints_stdSimplexSet :
    (stdSimplexSet ι).extremePoints ℝ = Set.range fun i : ι => Pi.single i (1 : ℝ)

declarations.name: affineIndependent_pi_single
declarations.statement: lemma affineIndependent_pi_single : AffineIndependent ℝ fun i : ι => Pi.single i (1 : ℝ)

declarations.name: isSimplex_stdSimplexSet
declarations.statement: lemma isSimplex_stdSimplexSet : IsSimplex (stdSimplexSet ι)

declarations.name: AffineEquiv.image_extremePoints
declarations.doc: An affine equivalence maps extreme points to extreme points.

declarations.doc: The image of a simplex under an affine equivalence is a simplex.
declarations.statement: lemma IsSimplex.map {K : Set E} (hK : IsSimplex K) (e : E ≃ᵃ[ℝ] F) : IsSimplex (e '' K)

declarations.doc: A set affinely equivalent to a standard simplex is a simplex.

declarations.doc: The unit interval is a simplex.

modules.title: Fourier transform of the sphere measure
modules.doc:
Archimedes' formula computes the exact sine multiplier of the sphere measure.

## i. Overview

Archimedes' formula computes the exact sine multiplier of the sphere measure.

## ii. Key results

* `integral_exp_symm`.
* `sphere_fourier_axis`: The Fourier transform of the sphere measure along an axis.
* `sphere_fourier`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Fourier transform of the sphere measure

## iv. References

* Bär, [Green-hyperbolic operators on globally hyperbolic
  spacetimes](https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.0738).

## A. Fourier transform of the sphere measure

declarations.name: Sphere3.integral_exp_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_exp_symm (a R : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    ∫ z in (-R)..R, Complex.exp (Complex.I * (a * z)) = 2 * Real.sin (a * R) / a

declarations.name: Sphere3.sphere_fourier_axis
declarations.doc: The Fourier transform of the sphere measure along an axis.
declarations.statement:
lemma sphere_fourier_axis (i : Fin 3) {a R : ℝ} (ha : a ≠ 0) (hR : 0 < R) :
    ∫ n : Sph, Complex.exp (Complex.I * (a * (R * n.1 i))) ∂sphereMeasure =
      (4 * Real.pi * Real.sin (a * R) / (a * R) : ℝ)

declarations.name: Sphere3.sphere_fourier
declarations.statement:
lemma sphere_fourier (k : Space 3) (hk : k ≠ 0) {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) :
    ∫ n : Sph, Complex.exp (Complex.I * ((R * inner ℝ k n.1 : ℝ) : ℂ)) ∂sphereMeasure =
      (4 * Real.pi * Real.sin (R * ‖k‖) / (R * ‖k‖) : ℝ)

modules.title: Polar coordinates on balls of space
modules.doc:
Integrals over balls of `Space 3` reduce to integrals over the unit sphere and the radius.

## i. Overview

The coordinate slice `Space 3 ≃ ℝ × Space 2` preserves volume. This gives integrals over a ball of
functions of one coordinate as one-dimensional integrals against the disc area `π (R² - z²)`.
Polar coordinates write the ball integral as an integral over the unit sphere and over the radius.
The unit sphere carries the surface measure of total mass `4 π`. The same holds for general
integrands. Integrability of `1 / |x|` times a continuous function and of radial exponentials is
included.

## ii. Key results

* `slice_measurePreserving`: the slice map preserves volume.
* `integral_ball_coord`: a ball integral of a function of one coordinate.
* `ball_integral_polar`, `ball_integral_polar_general`: polar coordinates on a ball.
* `integrable_inv_norm_mul`: integrability of the singular Green density.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Volume preservation of coordinate maps
- B. Integrals over a ball of a function of one coordinate
- C. Polar coordinates on the ball
- D. Polar coordinates for general integrands

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Volume preservation of coordinate maps
## B. Integrals over a ball of a function of one coordinate
## C. Polar coordinates on the ball
## D. Polar coordinates for general integrands

declarations.statement:

declarations.name: Sphere3.volume_ball_two
declarations.statement:
lemma volume_ball_two (ρ : ℝ) (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) :
    volume (Metric.ball (0 : Space 2) ρ) = ENNReal.ofReal (Real.pi * ρ ^ 2)

declarations.name: Sphere3.integral_ball_coord_aux
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_ball_coord_aux {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    (i : Fin 3) (h : ℝ → F) {R : ℝ} :
    ∫ x in Metric.ball (0 : Space 3) R, h (x i) =
      ∫ p : ℝ × Space 2, (Metric.ball (0 : Space 3) R).indicator (fun x => h (x i))
        ((Space.slice i).symm p)

declarations.name: Sphere3.indicator_slice_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma indicator_slice_apply {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F]
    (i : Fin 3) (h : ℝ → F) {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) (z : ℝ) (y : Space 2) :
    (Metric.ball (0 : Space 3) R).indicator (fun x => h (x i)) ((Space.slice i).symm (z, y)) =
      {y' : Space 2 | z ^ 2 + ‖y'‖ ^ 2 < R ^ 2}.indicator (fun _ => h z) y

declarations.name: Sphere3.slab_section_volume

lemma slab_section_volume (R z : ℝ) :
    volume {y : Space 2 | z ^ 2 + ‖y‖ ^ 2 < R ^ 2} =
      ENNReal.ofReal (Real.pi * (R ^ 2 - z ^ 2))

declarations.name: Sphere3.integral_ball_coord
declarations.doc:
A ball integral of a function of one coordinate reduces to a one-dimensional integral against
the disc area.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_ball_coord {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [CompleteSpace F]
    (i : Fin 3) {h : ℝ → F} (hh : Continuous h) {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) :
    ∫ x in Metric.ball (0 : Space 3) R, h (x i) =
      ∫ z in Set.Ioo (-R) R, (Real.pi * (R ^ 2 - z ^ 2)) • h z

declarations.name: Sphere3.Sph
declarations.doc: The unit sphere of `Space 3` with its surface measure.
declarations.statement: abbrev Sph

declarations.name: Sphere3.sphereMeasure
declarations.doc: The surface measure on the unit sphere, normalized so that the total mass is `4 π`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev sphereMeasure : Measure Sph

declarations.name: Sphere3.integrable_ball_indicator_coord
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_ball_indicator_coord {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F]
    (i : Fin 3) {h : ℝ → F} (hh : Continuous h) (R : ℝ) :
    Integrable ((Metric.ball (0 : Space 3) R).indicator (fun x => h (x i))) volume

declarations.name: Sphere3.ball_integral_polar
declarations.statement:
lemma ball_integral_polar {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    (i : Fin 3) {h : ℝ → F} (hh : Continuous h) {R : ℝ} :
    ∫ x in Metric.ball (0 : Space 3) R, h (x i) =
      ∫ n : Sph, ∫ r in Set.Ioo 0 R, r ^ 2 • h (r * (n.1 i)) ∂volume ∂sphereMeasure

declarations.name: Sphere3.integrable_ball_indicator
declarations.doc: A continuous function has an integrable restriction to a ball.
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_ball_indicator {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F]
    {g : Space 3 → F} (hg : Continuous g) (R : ℝ) :
    Integrable ((Metric.ball (0 : Space 3) R).indicator g) volume

declarations.name: Sphere3.integrable_inv_norm_mul
declarations.doc: `‖z‖⁻¹` times a continuous function is integrable on a ball of `Space 3`.
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_inv_norm_mul {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    {k : Space 3 → F} (hk : Continuous k) (R : ℝ) :
    Integrable ((Metric.ball (0 : Space 3) R).indicator (fun z => (‖z‖⁻¹ : ℝ) • k z)) volume

declarations.name: Sphere3.ball_integral_polar_general
declarations.doc: Polar coordinates on a ball for a general continuous integrand.
declarations.statement:
lemma ball_integral_polar_general {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    {g : Space 3 → F} {R : ℝ}
    (hg : Integrable ((Metric.ball (0 : Space 3) R).indicator g) volume) :
    ∫ y in Metric.ball (0 : Space 3) R, g y =
      ∫ n : Sph, ∫ r in Set.Ioo 0 R, r ^ 2 • g (r • n.1) ∂volume ∂sphereMeasure

declarations.name: Sphere3.setIntegral_ball_translate
declarations.doc: Translation of a ball integral to the origin.
declarations.statement:
lemma setIntegral_ball_translate {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    (G : Space 3 → F) (x : Space 3) (R : ℝ) :
    ∫ y in Metric.ball x R, G y = ∫ z in Metric.ball (0 : Space 3) R, G (x + z)

modules.title: Spherical profiles and invariant sphere integrals
modules.doc:
The invariant sphere measure has mass `4 π` and admits directional integration formulas.

## i. Overview

Differentiating the ball integral in the radius gives Archimedes' projection of the sphere onto an
axis. This is the sphere transform for axis directions. Rotation invariance of the sphere measure
extends it to every direction.

## ii. Key results

* `sphereProfile_eq`: Archimedes' projection of the sphere onto an axis.
* `sphereEquiv_measurePreserving`: the sphere measure is invariant under linear isometries.
* `sphereMeasure_univ`: the total mass is `4 π`.
* `sphereIntegral_dir`: Archimedes' formula for a function of one direction.
* `integral_sphere_neg`: invariance of the sphere measure under the antipodal map.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The radial profile of the sphere average
- B. Archimedes' projection
- C. Rotation invariance and general directions
- D. Functions of one direction

## iv. References

* None.

    (i : Fin 3) {h : ℝ → F} (hh : Continuous h) {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) :
    ∫ x in Metric.ball (0 : Space 3) R, h (x i) =
      ∫ r in Set.Ioo 0 R, r ^ 2 • sphereProfile i h r

lemma continuous_sphereProfile {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]

    Continuous (sphereProfile i h)

declarations.doc: The closed-form side: the integral of `π (R² - z²) h(z)`, as a function of `R`.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: Sphere3.sphereIntegral_dir
declarations.doc:
**Archimedes in an arbitrary direction.** The sphere integral of a function of the inner product
with a fixed vector `z ≠ 0` is a one-dimensional integral over `[-‖z‖, ‖z‖]`.

      (2 * Real.pi / ‖z‖) • ∫ s in (-‖z‖)..‖z‖, h s
