modules.title: Subalgebras generated by homogeneous submodules
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Let `f : B →ₐ[R] B[X]` be an algebra map into the polynomials over a possibly
noncommutative algebra `B`. The degree-`w` part of a subalgebra `A` is the submodule
`A.homogeneousSubmodule f w` of elements `x ∈ A` with `f x = monomial w x`. Nothing
requires `f` to be a grading of `B`: the pieces need not span `B`, and `f x` need not
determine `x`.

Suppose that `A` is generated by a family of submodules `D n`, and that `f` is the monomial
`X ^ deg n` on `D n`. Then the degree-`w` part of `A` is spanned by the products
`D n₁ * ⋯ * D nₖ`, in every order of the factors, whose degrees add up to `w`
(`homogeneousSubmodule_eq_productsOfDegree`). The empty product is `1`, so degree zero
contains the scalars. This is a spanning statement. It gives no unique decomposition, and
it assumes neither that the generators commute nor that their products are nonzero.

Everything else is read off from it.

- Removing the leftmost factor of each product: the degree-`w` part, for `w` positive, is
  spanned by the products `D k * A_(w - deg k)` (`homogeneousSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul`). This
  needs no positivity. When some `deg k` vanishes, the right-hand side contains the term
  `D k * A_w` of the same degree, so the equality holds without giving a decreasing
  recursion.
- If every generator has positive degree, degree zero is exactly the scalar submodule `1`
  (`homogeneousSubmodule_zero_eq_one`), the image of `R` in `B`, which need not be a copy
  of `R`.
- If moreover `n < deg n`, the degree-`i` part is spanned by the generators of degree `i`
  and the products of two parts of smaller positive degree
  (`homogeneousSubmodule_eq_sup_iSup_mul`). The bound makes the index ranges finite.
- A property of degrees holding at zero and at every generator degree, and closed under
  addition, holds at every degree with a nonzero part (`homogeneousSubmodule_eq_bot`).
  This only proves vanishing: a degree with the property may still have zero part.

## ii. Key results

- `Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule` : the degree-`w` part of a subalgebra.
- `Submodule.productsOfDegree` : the span of the products of generators of total degree `w`.
- `Subalgebra.coeff_mem_homogeneousSubmodule` : the coefficients of `f x` are homogeneous.
- `Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_productsOfDegree` : spanning by products.
- `Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul` : removing the leftmost generator.
- `Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_zero_eq_one` : degree zero is the scalars.
- `Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_sup_iSup_mul` : the binary recursion.
- `Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_bot` : unreachable degrees vanish.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The homogeneous submodules of a subalgebra
- B. Products of generators of a given total degree
- C. Subalgebras generated by homogeneous submodules
  - C.1. Generators and coefficients
  - C.2. Spanning by products of generators
  - C.3. Removing the leftmost generator
  - C.4. Degree zero and the binary recursion
  - C.5. Unreachable degrees

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The homogeneous submodules of a subalgebra
## B. Products of generators of a given total degree

## C. Subalgebras generated by homogeneous submodules

Throughout, `A` is generated by the submodules `D n` (`hA`), and `f` is the monomial
`X ^ deg n` on `D n` (`hD`).
### C.2. Spanning by products of generators
### C.4. Degree zero and the binary recursion

declarations.name: Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule
declarations.doc: The degree-`w` part of `A` for `f`: the elements `x ∈ A` with `f x = monomial w x`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def homogeneousSubmodule (A : Subalgebra R B) (f : B →ₐ[R] Polynomial B)
    (w : ℕ) : Submodule R B

declarations.name: Subalgebra.mem_homogeneousSubmodule_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_homogeneousSubmodule_iff {w : ℕ} {x : B} :
    x ∈ A.homogeneousSubmodule f w ↔ x ∈ A ∧ f x = Polynomial.monomial w x

declarations.name: Subalgebra.one_le_homogeneousSubmodule_zero
declarations.doc: The scalars have degree zero.
declarations.statement: lemma one_le_homogeneousSubmodule_zero : (1 : Submodule R B) ≤ A.homogeneousSubmodule f 0

declarations.name: Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_mul_le
declarations.doc: Degrees add under multiplication.
declarations.statement:
lemma homogeneousSubmodule_mul_le (m n : ℕ) :
    A.homogeneousSubmodule f m * A.homogeneousSubmodule f n
      ≤ A.homogeneousSubmodule f (m + n)

declarations.name: Submodule.productsOfDegree
declarations.doc:
The span of the products `D n₁ * ⋯ * D nₖ` whose degrees `deg n₁ + ⋯ + deg nₖ` add up
to `w`. Every order of the factors occurs separately, and the empty product is `1`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def productsOfDegree (D : ℕ → Submodule R B) (deg : ℕ → ℕ) (w : ℕ) :
    Submodule R B

declarations.name: Submodule.list_prod_le_productsOfDegree
declarations.statement:
lemma list_prod_le_productsOfDegree (l : List ℕ) :
    (l.map D).prod ≤ productsOfDegree D deg (l.map deg).sum

declarations.name: Submodule.productsOfDegree_mul_le
declarations.doc: Concatenating products adds their degrees.
declarations.statement:
lemma productsOfDegree_mul_le (a b : ℕ) :
    productsOfDegree D deg a * productsOfDegree D deg b ≤ productsOfDegree D deg (a + b)

declarations.name: Subalgebra.le_homogeneousSubmodule
declarations.doc: A generator in `D n` has degree `deg n`.
declarations.statement: lemma le_homogeneousSubmodule (n : ℕ) : D n ≤ A.homogeneousSubmodule f (deg n)

declarations.name: Subalgebra.list_prod_le_homogeneousSubmodule
declarations.doc: A product of generators has the sum of their degrees.
declarations.statement:
lemma list_prod_le_homogeneousSubmodule (l : List ℕ) :
    (l.map D).prod ≤ A.homogeneousSubmodule f (l.map deg).sum

declarations.name: Subalgebra.productsOfDegree_le_homogeneousSubmodule
declarations.doc: The products of generators of total degree `w` lie in the degree-`w` part of `A`.
declarations.statement:
lemma productsOfDegree_le_homogeneousSubmodule (w : ℕ) :
    productsOfDegree D deg w ≤ A.homogeneousSubmodule f w

declarations.name: Subalgebra.coeff_mem_productsOfDegree
declarations.doc:
Every coefficient of `f x`, for `x ∈ A`, is a sum of products of generators: the one
induction over the generation of `A`.
declarations.statement:
lemma coeff_mem_productsOfDegree {x : B} (hx : x ∈ A) (m : ℕ) :
    (f x).coeff m ∈ productsOfDegree D deg m

declarations.name: Subalgebra.coeff_mem_homogeneousSubmodule
declarations.doc: The coefficient of `X ^ m` in `f x`, for `x ∈ A`, lies in the degree-`m` part of `A`.
declarations.statement:
lemma coeff_mem_homogeneousSubmodule {x : B} (hx : x ∈ A) (m : ℕ) :
    (f x).coeff m ∈ A.homogeneousSubmodule f m

declarations.name: Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_productsOfDegree
declarations.doc:
The degree-`w` part of `A` is spanned by the products of generators, in every order,
whose degrees add up to `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma homogeneousSubmodule_eq_productsOfDegree (w : ℕ) :
    A.homogeneousSubmodule f w = productsOfDegree D deg w

declarations.name: Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul
declarations.doc:
For positive `w`, the degree-`w` part of `A` is spanned by the products of a generator
`D k` of degree at most `w` with the part of the remaining degree. The bound `n ≤ deg n`
only makes the range of `k` finite.
declarations.statement:
lemma homogeneousSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul (hle : ∀ n, n ≤ deg n) {w : ℕ} (hw : 0 < w) :
    A.homogeneousSubmodule f w
      = ⨆ k ∈ (Finset.range (w + 1)).filter (fun k => deg k ≤ w),
          D k * A.homogeneousSubmodule f (w - deg k)

declarations.name: Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_zero_eq_one
declarations.doc: If every generator has positive degree, degree zero is the scalar submodule.
declarations.statement:
lemma homogeneousSubmodule_zero_eq_one (hpos : ∀ n, 0 < deg n) :
    A.homogeneousSubmodule f 0 = 1

declarations.name: Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_sup_iSup_mul
declarations.doc:
If `n < deg n` for every `n`, the degree-`i` part of `A`, for positive `i`, is spanned
by the generators of degree `i` and the products of two parts of positive degrees adding
up to `i`. It follows from removing the leftmost generator: a generator of degree `i`
leaves degree zero, which is the scalars.
declarations.statement:
lemma homogeneousSubmodule_eq_sup_iSup_mul (hlt : ∀ n, n < deg n) (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    A.homogeneousSubmodule f i
      = (⨆ k ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun k : Fin i => deg k = i), D k)
        ⊔ (⨆ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : Fin i × Fin i => (p.1 : ℕ) + (p.2 : ℕ) = i),
            A.homogeneousSubmodule f p.1 * A.homogeneousSubmodule f p.2)

declarations.name: Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
If a set of degrees contains `0` and every `deg n` and is closed under addition, a
degree outside it has zero part. This proves vanishing only: a degree in the set may
still have zero part.
declarations.statement:
lemma homogeneousSubmodule_eq_bot (P : ℕ → Prop) (h0 : P 0) (hP : ∀ n, P (deg n))
    (hadd : ∀ a b, P a → P b → P (a + b)) {w : ℕ} (hw : ¬ P w) :
    A.homogeneousSubmodule f w = ⊥

modules.title: Reducing invariants modulo a stable submodule
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Let `σ : G → B →ₗ[R] B` be a family of linear maps, indexed by an arbitrary type. No group or
representation law is assumed. An element `x` is invariant when `σ g x = x` for every `g`, and
a submodule is stable when every `σ g` carries it into itself.

The relation `ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W` says: for every stable submodule `S`, every invariant
of `V ⊔ S` lies in `W ⊔ S`. It is transitive, antitone in the source, monotone in the target
and, for stable sources and a stable target, closed under joins of the source. Since an element
of a join lies in a join over finitely many summands, the index type need not be finite:
`ReducesInvariantsTo.iSup_of_biSup`, and with it `ReducesInvariantsTo.iSup`. A classification
of the invariants of a family can therefore be applied one family at a time, the other families
being kept in the stable remainder `S`. A submodule on which one map of the family acts by a
scalar other than `1` reduces to `⊥`: `reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_apply_eq_smul`.

Such a reduction is usually proved in the quotient `B ⧸ S`. If every invariant of the image of
`V` in `B ⧸ S` lies in the image of `W`, then every invariant of `V ⊔ S` lies in `W ⊔ S`, and
when `W` is pointwise fixed the remainder in `S` is itself invariant:
`IsStableUnder.exists_add_of_quotient`. The quotient hypothesis is not implied by a
classification of the invariants of `V` alone, since the invariants of `B ⧸ S` are the classes
`x` with `σ g x - x ∈ S`. For a pointwise-fixed `W ≤ V` a reduction describes the invariants
of `V ⊔ S` exactly, as the elements of `W` plus an invariant element of `S`:
`ReducesInvariantsTo.mem_sup_and_forall_eq_self_iff`.

`InvariantReductionToSpan σ V` packages a reduction of `V` to the span of one fixed vector,
the form in which the classification theorems are applied.

For a finite family moved by matrices, `σ g (T l) = ∑ a, M g a l • T a`, the quotient
hypothesis reduces to a finite problem about coefficient vectors: the law holds again for the
classes of the members in `B ⧸ S`, so an invariant there is the combination of a coefficient
vector fixed by every `M g`, and any classification of the fixed coefficient vectors gives a
reduction, `reducesInvariantsTo_of_mulVec_eq`.

## ii. Key results

- `ReducesInvariantsTo.iSup_of_biSup` : a reduction of every join over a finite set of indices is a
  reduction of the join over the whole index type, which may be infinite: an element of the join
  lies in the join over finitely many of the summands
- `ReducesInvariantsTo.iSup` : reductions of stable submodules to a common stable target combine
  over any index type, finite or not: `biSup` combines them over every finite set of indices, and
  `iSup_of_biSup` passes to the whole join
- `reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_apply_eq_smul` : a submodule on which one map of the family acts by a
  scalar `μ ≠ 1` reduces to `⊥`
- `ReducesInvariantsTo.mem_sup_and_forall_eq_self_iff`
- `IsStableUnder.exists_add_of_quotient` : quotient to remainder: when every invariant of the image
  of `V` in `B ⧸ S` lies in the image of a pointwise-fixed `W`, an invariant of `V ⊔ S` is an
  element of `W` plus an invariant element of `S`
- `reducesInvariantsTo_of_mulVec_eq` : a family moved by matrices whose conjugate transposes are
  among them reduces to the combinations of any submodule `E` of coefficient vectors containing
  every vector fixed by all the matrices

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Stable and fixed submodules
- B. Reducing invariants
- C. Reduction through a quotient
- D. Reduction to the span of one vector
- E. Families moved by matrices

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## B. Reducing invariants

To reduce `V₁ ⊔ V₂` to `W`, the summand `V₂` is first moved into the remainder, which needs `V₂`
stable; the result lies in `W ⊔ (V₂ ⊔ S)`, and reducing `V₂` from there needs `W` stable.

## C. Reduction through a quotient

For a `σ`-stable `S`, the maps `S.mapQ S (σ g) _` act on `B ⧸ S`. The hypotheses below classify
invariants of that action on the image of the source, which is where a classification valid in
every module is applied.
## D. Reduction to the span of one vector

## E. Families moved by matrices

A finite family `T : ι → B` is moved by matrices when `σ g (T l) = ∑ a, M g a l • T a`, the
summed index in the row slot. For a stable `S` the classes of the members in `B ⧸ S` obey the
same law (`Submodule.mapQ_mkQ_eq_sum_smul`), and that law is all that
`Fintype.exists_mulVec_eq_of_conjTranspose_mem` needs: an invariant of the image of the span in
`B ⧸ S` is the combination of a coefficient vector fixed by every `M g`. A description of the
fixed coefficient vectors, a submodule `E` containing them all, therefore reduces the span to
the combinations of `E`. What is classified is coefficient vectors, which do not depend on `S`;
no classification of invariants of `B` is assumed to descend to `B ⧸ S`.

declarations.name: IsStableUnder
declarations.doc: A submodule carried into itself by every map of the family `σ`.

declarations.name: IsFixedBy
declarations.doc: A submodule fixed pointwise by every map of the family `σ`.
declarations.statement: def IsFixedBy (σ : G → B →ₗ[R] B) (V : Submodule R B) : Prop

declarations.name: isStableUnder_iff_map
declarations.doc: Stability as an inclusion of images.
declarations.statement:
lemma isStableUnder_iff_map {V : Submodule R B} :
    IsStableUnder σ V ↔ ∀ g, Submodule.map (σ g) V ≤ V

declarations.name: IsFixedBy.isStableUnder
declarations.doc: A pointwise-fixed submodule is stable.
declarations.statement: lemma IsFixedBy.isStableUnder {V : Submodule R B} (hV : IsFixedBy σ V) : IsStableUnder σ V

declarations.name: IsFixedBy.sup

declarations.name: isStableUnder_bot

declarations.statement: lemma isStableUnder_bot : IsStableUnder σ (⊥ : Submodule R B)

declarations.name: IsStableUnder.sup

declarations.statement:
lemma IsStableUnder.sup {V V' : Submodule R B} (hV : IsStableUnder σ V)

An indexed join of stable submodules is stable. The index is a `Sort`, so this covers
the bounded join `⨆ i ∈ s, V i`.

declarations.name: isFixedBy_iSup
declarations.doc: An indexed join of pointwise-fixed submodules is pointwise fixed.

declarations.name: isFixedBy_span_range

declarations.name: isStableUnder_span_range
declarations.doc: The span of a family is stable when each map sends each member into the span.

declarations.name: isStableUnder_span_range_of_sum
declarations.doc:
The span of a finite family is stable when each map sends each member to a combination
of the family.

declarations.name: IsStableUnder.mul
declarations.doc:
A product of two stable submodules of an algebra is stable under maps respecting
multiplication.
declarations.statement:

    {σ : G → A →ₗ[R] A} (hσ : ∀ g (a b : A), σ g (a * b) = σ g a * σ g b)
    {V V' : Submodule R A} (hV : IsStableUnder σ V) (hV' : IsStableUnder σ V') :
    IsStableUnder σ (V * V')

declarations.name: ReducesInvariantsTo
declarations.doc: Every invariant of `V ⊔ S`, for `S` a `σ`-stable submodule, lies in `W ⊔ S`.
declarations.statement: def ReducesInvariantsTo (σ : G → B →ₗ[R] B) (V W : Submodule R B) : Prop

declarations.name: reducesInvariantsTo_of_le
declarations.doc: A submodule reduces to any submodule containing it.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_of_le {V W : Submodule R B} (hVW : V ≤ W) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W

declarations.name: ReducesInvariantsTo.mono_left
declarations.doc: A reduction restricts to a smaller source.
declarations.statement:
lemma ReducesInvariantsTo.mono_left {V V' W : Submodule R B} (hP : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V' W)
    (hV : V ≤ V') : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W

declarations.name: ReducesInvariantsTo.mono_right
declarations.doc: A reduction extends to a larger target.
declarations.statement:
lemma ReducesInvariantsTo.mono_right {V W W' : Submodule R B}
    (hP : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W') (hW : W' ≤ W) : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W

declarations.name: ReducesInvariantsTo.trans
declarations.doc: Successive reductions compose.
declarations.statement:
lemma ReducesInvariantsTo.trans {V W W' : Submodule R B} (hP : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W)
    (hQ : ReducesInvariantsTo σ W W') : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W'

declarations.name: ReducesInvariantsTo.sup
declarations.doc:
Reductions of `V` and of a stable `V'` to a common stable target combine to a reduction of
`V ⊔ V'`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ReducesInvariantsTo.sup {V V' W : Submodule R B} (hP : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W)
    (hQ : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V' W) (hV' : IsStableUnder σ V') (hW : IsStableUnder σ W) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo σ (V ⊔ V') W

declarations.name: ReducesInvariantsTo.biSup
declarations.doc: Reductions of stable submodules to a common stable target combine over a finite set.
declarations.statement:
lemma ReducesInvariantsTo.biSup {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {V : ι → Submodule R B}
    {W : Submodule R B} (hP : ∀ i, ReducesInvariantsTo σ (V i) W)
    (hV : ∀ i, IsStableUnder σ (V i)) (hW : IsStableUnder σ W) (s : Finset ι) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo σ (⨆ i ∈ s, V i) W

declarations.name: ReducesInvariantsTo.iSup_of_biSup
declarations.doc:
A reduction of every join over a finite set of indices is a reduction of the join over the
whole index type, which may be infinite: an element of the join lies in the join over finitely
many of the summands. No stability is assumed of the summands or of the target; the remainder
is stable, as in every reduction.

declarations.name: ReducesInvariantsTo.iSup
declarations.doc:
Reductions of stable submodules to a common stable target combine over any index type,
finite or not: `biSup` combines them over every finite set of indices, and
`iSup_of_biSup` passes to the whole join.

declarations.name: ReducesInvariantsTo.comp
declarations.doc:
A reduction for the subfamily `σ ∘ ι` is a reduction for `σ`: an invariant of `σ` is an
invariant of the subfamily, and a `σ`-stable submodule is stable under the subfamily.
declarations.statement:
lemma ReducesInvariantsTo.comp {G' : Type*} (ι : G' → G) {V W : Submodule R B}
    (hP : ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g' => σ (ι g')) V W) : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W

declarations.name: reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_apply_eq_smul
declarations.doc:
A submodule on which one map of the family acts by a scalar `μ ≠ 1` reduces to `⊥`. An
invariant `v + s` of `V ⊔ S` has `(μ - 1) • v = s - σ g s`, which lies in `S`, and so does
`v`. Of the stability of `S` only stability under `σ g` is used.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_apply_eq_smul (g : G) {μ : K} (hμ : μ ≠ 1)
    {V : Submodule K B} (hV : ∀ v ∈ V, σ g v = μ • v) : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V ⊥

declarations.name: IsStableUnder.mem_sup_of_quotient
declarations.doc:
An invariant of `V ⊔ S` lies in `W ⊔ S` when every invariant of the image of `V` in
`B ⧸ S` lies in the image of `W`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsStableUnder.mem_sup_of_quotient (hS : IsStableUnder σ S)
    (hclass : ∀ x ∈ V.map S.mkQ, (∀ g, S.mapQ S (σ g) (hS g) x = x) → x ∈ W.map S.mkQ)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ V ⊔ S) (hinv : ∀ g, σ g x = x) : x ∈ W ⊔ S

declarations.name: reducesInvariantsTo_of_quotient
declarations.doc:
`V` reduces to `W` when, for every stable `S`, every invariant of the image of `V` in
`B ⧸ S` lies in the image of `W`.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_of_quotient
    (hclass : ∀ S : Submodule R B, ∀ hS : IsStableUnder σ S, ∀ x ∈ V.map S.mkQ,
      (∀ g, S.mapQ S (σ g) (hS g) x = x) → x ∈ W.map S.mkQ) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W

declarations.name: IsFixedBy.exists_add_of_mem_sup
declarations.doc:
An invariant of `W ⊔ S`, for `W` pointwise fixed, is an element of `W` plus an invariant
element of `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsFixedBy.exists_add_of_mem_sup (hW : IsFixedBy σ W) {x : B} (hx : x ∈ W ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g, σ g x = x) : ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ y ∈ S, x = w + y ∧ ∀ g, σ g y = y

declarations.name: ReducesInvariantsTo.mem_sup_and_forall_eq_self_iff
declarations.doc:
A reduction of `V` to a pointwise-fixed `W ≤ V` describes the invariants of `V ⊔ S`, for
`S` stable, exactly: they are the elements of `W` plus an invariant element of `S`. This is
the form in which a classification is stated.
declarations.statement:
lemma ReducesInvariantsTo.mem_sup_and_forall_eq_self_iff (hP : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W)
    (hWV : W ≤ V) (hW : IsFixedBy σ W) (hS : IsStableUnder σ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ V ⊔ S ∧ ∀ g, σ g x = x) ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g, σ g y = y) ∧ x - y ∈ W

declarations.name: IsStableUnder.exists_add_of_quotient
declarations.doc:
Quotient to remainder: when every invariant of the image of `V` in `B ⧸ S` lies in the
image of a pointwise-fixed `W`, an invariant of `V ⊔ S` is an element of `W` plus an
invariant element of `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsStableUnder.exists_add_of_quotient (hS : IsStableUnder σ S) (hW : IsFixedBy σ W)
    (hclass : ∀ x ∈ V.map S.mkQ, (∀ g, S.mapQ S (σ g) (hS g) x = x) → x ∈ W.map S.mkQ)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ V ⊔ S) (hinv : ∀ g, σ g x = x) :
    ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ y ∈ S, x = w + y ∧ ∀ g, σ g y = y

declarations.name: IsStableUnder.exists_smul_add_of_quotient
declarations.doc:
Quotient to remainder for a single fixed vector `v`: when every invariant of the image of
`V` in `B ⧸ S` is a multiple of the class of `v`, an invariant of `V ⊔ S` is a multiple of
`v` plus an invariant element of `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsStableUnder.exists_smul_add_of_quotient (hS : IsStableUnder σ S) {v : B}
    (hv : ∀ g, σ g v = v)
    (hclass : ∀ x ∈ V.map S.mkQ, (∀ g, S.mapQ S (σ g) (hS g) x = x) → ∃ c : R, x = c • S.mkQ v)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ V ⊔ S) (hinv : ∀ g, σ g x = x) :
    ∃ c : R, ∃ y ∈ S, x = c • v + y ∧ ∀ g, σ g y = y

declarations.name: InvariantReductionToSpan
declarations.doc:
A stable submodule `V` together with a fixed vector such that, for every stable `S`, every
invariant of `V ⊔ S` is a multiple of that vector plus an element of `S`. The vector need not
be nonzero or lie in `V`.
declarations.statement:
structure InvariantReductionToSpan (σ : G → B →ₗ[R] B) (V : Submodule R B) where
  /-- The vector whose span receives the invariants of `V`. -/
  spanningVector : B
  /-- The submodule is stable. -/
  stable : IsStableUnder σ V
  /-- The spanning vector is invariant. -/
  spanningVector_fixed : ∀ g, σ g spanningVector = spanningVector
  /-- An invariant of `V ⊔ S`, for `S` stable, is a multiple of the spanning vector plus an
    element of `S`. -/
  reduce : ∀ S : Submodule R B, IsStableUnder σ S → ∀ x ∈ V ⊔ S, (∀ g, σ g x = x) →
    ∃ c : R, ∃ y ∈ S, x = c • spanningVector + y

declarations.name: InvariantReductionToSpan.reducesInvariantsTo
declarations.doc: The submodule reduces to the span of the spanning vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo (r : InvariantReductionToSpan σ V) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo σ V (R ∙ r.spanningVector)

declarations.name: InvariantReductionToSpan.reducesInvariantsTo_iSup
declarations.doc:
A family of reductions to spans, over any index type, reduces the join of the submodules to
the span of the spanning vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_iSup {κ : Type*} {V : κ → Submodule R B}
    (r : ∀ k, InvariantReductionToSpan σ (V k)) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo σ (⨆ k, V k)
      (Submodule.span R (Set.range fun k => (r k).spanningVector))

declarations.name: InvariantReductionToSpan.ofReducesInvariantsTo
declarations.doc: The reduction of a stable submodule to the span of a fixed vector.
declarations.statement:
def ofReducesInvariantsTo (hV : IsStableUnder σ V) (v : B) (hv : ∀ g, σ g v = v)
    (h : ReducesInvariantsTo σ V (R ∙ v)) : InvariantReductionToSpan σ V

declarations.name: InvariantReductionToSpan.ofFixed
declarations.doc: The span of a fixed vector reduces to itself.
declarations.statement:
def ofFixed (b : B) (hb : ∀ g, σ g b = b) :
    InvariantReductionToSpan σ (R ∙ b)

declarations.name: InvariantReductionToSpan.ofFixedFamily
declarations.doc:
The span of a nonempty family whose members all equal one fixed vector reduces to the
span of that vector.

declarations.name: Submodule.mapQ_mkQ_eq_sum_smul
declarations.doc:
A map moving each member of a family by a matrix moves their classes modulo a submodule
that it preserves by the same matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma Submodule.mapQ_mkQ_eq_sum_smul {R B ι : Type*} [Ring R] [AddCommGroup B] [Module R B]
    [Fintype ι] (S : Submodule R B) {f : B →ₗ[R] B} (hS : ∀ y ∈ S, f y ∈ S) {T : ι → B}
    {M : Matrix ι ι R} {l : ι} (hf : f (T l) = ∑ a, M a l • T a) :
    S.mapQ S f hS (S.mkQ (T l)) = ∑ a, M a l • S.mkQ (T a)

declarations.name: reducesInvariantsTo_of_mulVec_eq
declarations.doc:
A family moved by matrices whose conjugate transposes are among them reduces to the
combinations of any submodule `E` of coefficient vectors containing every vector fixed by
all the matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_of_mulVec_eq (T : ι → B) (M : G → Matrix ι ι ℂ)
    (hT : ∀ g l, σ g (T l) = ∑ a, M g a l • T a) (hM : ∀ g, ∃ g', M g' = (M g)ᴴ)
    (E : Submodule ℂ (ι → ℂ)) (hE : ∀ c, (∀ g, M g *ᵥ c = c) → c ∈ E) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo σ (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range T))
      (E.map (Fintype.linearCombination ℂ T))

declarations.name: reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_mulVec_eq
declarations.doc:
The form of `reducesInvariantsTo_of_mulVec_eq` when no nonzero coefficient vector is
fixed: the span reduces to `⊥`.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_mulVec_eq (T : ι → B) (M : G → Matrix ι ι ℂ)
    (hT : ∀ g l, σ g (T l) = ∑ a, M g a l • T a) (hM : ∀ g, ∃ g', M g' = (M g)ᴴ)
    (hE : ∀ c, (∀ g, M g *ᵥ c = c) → c = 0) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo σ (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range T)) ⊥

declarations.name: reducesInvariantsTo_span_singleton_of_mulVec_eq
declarations.doc:
The form of `reducesInvariantsTo_of_mulVec_eq` when every fixed coefficient vector is a
multiple of `e`: the span reduces to the span of the combination with coefficients `e`.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_span_singleton_of_mulVec_eq (T : ι → B) (M : G → Matrix ι ι ℂ)
    (hT : ∀ g l, σ g (T l) = ∑ a, M g a l • T a) (hM : ∀ g, ∃ g', M g' = (M g)ᴴ)
    (e : ι → ℂ) (hE : ∀ c, (∀ g, M g *ᵥ c = c) → ∃ z : ℂ, c = z • e) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo σ (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range T)) (ℂ ∙ ∑ i, e i • T i)

modules.title: Ladder systems
modules.doc:
Ladder systems of creation and annihilation operators, their `gl(d)` action and number operators.

## i. Overview

A `LadderSystem K V d` packages `d` pairs of creation and annihilation endomorphisms of a
`K`-vector space `V` satisfying the canonical commutation relations. The definition abstracts the
algebraic structure shared by bosonic systems independently of a particular representation. The
bilinears `E i j := acᵢaⱼ` satisfy the `gl(d)` commutation relations and define a `gl(d)`-module
structure on `V` via `toGlHom`.

- `Basic.lean` : this file -- the structure itself, the `gl(d)`-module structure it generates, and
    the number operator.
- `Vacuum.lean` : a vacuum state, the creation-operator words built over it, and the excitation-
    number sector they span, bundled as a `gl(d)` Lie submodule.
- `OccupationBasis.lean` : the occupation-number states form a basis of each fixed-
    excitation-number sector, with an explicit dimension formula.
- `SymmetricPower.lean` : that sector is linearly isomorphic to `Sym^n(K^d)`.

The harmonic-oscillator instance is defined in
`QuantumMechanics/HarmonicOscillator/LadderOperators.lean`.

## ii. Key results

Definitions:
- `LadderSystem.E` : the `gl(d)` bilinears `E i j := acᵢaⱼ`.
- `LadderSystem.toGlHom` : the `gl(d)`-representation on `V` generated by a ladder system.
- `LadderSystem.N` : the number operator for mode `i`, `Nᵢ ≔ Eᵢᵢ`.

Theorems:
- `LadderSystem.lie_E` : `E` satisfies the defining relations of `gl(d)`.
- `LadderSystem.lie_N_a`, `LadderSystem.lie_N_ac` : `[Nᵢ, aⱼ] = -δᵢⱼaᵢ` and
    `[Nᵢ, acⱼ] = δᵢⱼacᵢ`.
- `LadderSystem.lie_N_N` : the number operators commute among themselves, `[Nᵢ, Nⱼ] = 0`.
- `LadderSystem.lie_totalN_E` : the *total* number operator `∑ᵢNᵢ` is central in `gl(d)` --
    it commutes with every generator `E i j`, not just the diagonal ones. This is what makes an
    isotropic Hamiltonian (a function of `∑ᵢNᵢ` alone) compatible with the full `gl(d)`-module
    structure on `vacuumSpan`, not just individually with each `Nᵢ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The `LadderSystem` structure
- B. The `gl(d)`-module structure
- C. The number operator
  - C.1. Commutation relations
  - C.2. The total number operator

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.doc:
A `K`-linear map agreeing with the bracket on basis pairs agrees with the bracket
everywhere.
declarations.statement:
theorem LinearMap.lie_apply_eq_of_lie_basis_eq (b : Basis ι K L) (f : L →ₗ[K] L')

declarations.doc:
Same, from a spanning set rather than a basis (`LinearMap.ext_on` in place of `Basis.ext`) —

declarations.name: LadderSystem
declarations.doc:
A system of `d` independent ladder pairs on a `K`-vector space `V`: annihilation operators
`a i` and creation operators `ac i` (`i : Fin d`), satisfying the canonical commutation relations.
A physical system exhibits its own concrete operators as one instance of this (e.g.
`QuantumMechanics/HarmonicOscillator/LadderOperators.lean`'s `toLadderSystem`, via
`ContinuousLinearMap.toLinearMap`) and inherits every result in `LadderSystem/` for free.
declarations.statement:
structure LadderSystem (K V : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (d : ℕ) where
  /-- The `d` annihilation operators. -/
  a : Fin d → Module.End K V
  /-- The `d` creation operators, `a⁺`. -/
  ac : Fin d → Module.End K V
  /-- `[a i, ac j] = δᵢⱼ`. -/
  comm_a_ac : ∀ i j, (⁅a i, ac j⁆ : Module.End K V) = if i = j then 1 else 0
  /-- `[a i, a j] = 0`. -/
  comm_a_a : ∀ i j, (⁅a i, a j⁆ : Module.End K V) = 0
  /-- `[ac i, ac j] = 0`. -/
  comm_ac_ac : ∀ i j, (⁅ac i, ac j⁆ : Module.End K V) = 0

declarations.name: LadderSystem.assoc_leibniz
declarations.statement:
lemma assoc_leibniz (x y z : Module.End K V) :
    (⁅x, y * z⁆ : Module.End K V) = ⁅x, y⁆ * z + y * ⁅x, z⁆

declarations.name: LadderSystem.assoc_leibniz'
declarations.statement:
lemma assoc_leibniz' (x y z : Module.End K V) :
    (⁅x * y, z⁆ : Module.End K V) = x * ⁅y, z⁆ + ⁅x, z⁆ * y

declarations.name: LadderSystem.E
declarations.doc: The `gl(d)` bilinears `E i j := ac i · a j`.
declarations.statement: def E (i j : Fin d) : Module.End K V

declarations.name: LadderSystem.lie_E
declarations.doc:
`E` satisfies the defining relations of `gl(d)`:
`[E i j, E k l] = δⱼₖ E i l - δₗᵢ E k j`.
declarations.statement:
theorem lie_E (i j k l : Fin d) :
    (⁅L.E i j, L.E k l⁆ : Module.End K V)
      = (δ[j,k] : K) • L.E i l - (δ[l,i] : K) • L.E k j

declarations.name: LadderSystem.lie_single
declarations.doc: The matrix units satisfy the same relations, at the level of `gl(d)` itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma lie_single (i j k l : Fin d) :
    (⁅Matrix.single i j (1 : K), Matrix.single k l (1 : K)⁆ : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) K)
      = (δ[j,k] : K) • Matrix.single i l 1 - (δ[l,i] : K) • Matrix.single k j 1

declarations.name: LadderSystem.toGlHomLinear
declarations.doc: The `K`-linear map sending matrix unit `Matrix.single i j 1` to `E i j`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toGlHomLinear (L : LadderSystem K V d) :
    Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) K →ₗ[K] Module.End K V

declarations.name: LadderSystem.toGlHomLinear_stdBasis
declarations.statement:
lemma toGlHomLinear_stdBasis (L : LadderSystem K V d) (i j : Fin d) :
    L.toGlHomLinear (Matrix.stdBasis K (Fin d) (Fin d) (i, j)) = L.E i j

declarations.name: LadderSystem.toGlHomLinear_single
declarations.statement:
lemma toGlHomLinear_single (L : LadderSystem K V d) (i j : Fin d) :
    L.toGlHomLinear (Matrix.single i j (1 : K)) = L.E i j

declarations.name: LadderSystem.toGlHomLinear_lie
declarations.doc: `toGlHomLinear` respects brackets.
declarations.statement:
lemma toGlHomLinear_lie (L : LadderSystem K V d) (x y : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) K) :
    L.toGlHomLinear ⁅x, y⁆ = ⁅L.toGlHomLinear x, L.toGlHomLinear y⁆

declarations.name: LadderSystem.toGlHom
declarations.doc: The `gl(d)`-representation on `V` generated by a ladder system, bundled as a `LieHom`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toGlHom (L : LadderSystem K V d) :
    Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) K →ₗ⁅K⁆ Module.End K V

declarations.name: LadderSystem.toLieRingModule
declarations.doc:
`V` as a `gl(d)`-module, the `LieRingModule` instance (not global -- depends on `L`; use via
`haveI := L.toLieRingModule`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toLieRingModule (L : LadderSystem K V d) :
    LieRingModule (Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) K) V

declarations.name: LadderSystem.toLieModule
declarations.doc: The companion `LieModule` instance.
declarations.statement:
lemma toLieModule (L : LadderSystem K V d) :
    @LieModule K (Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) K) V _ _ _ _ _ L.toLieRingModule

declarations.name: LadderSystem.N
declarations.doc: The number operator for mode `i`, `Nᵢ ≔ Eᵢᵢ = acᵢaᵢ`.
declarations.statement: def N (i : Fin d) : Module.End K V

declarations.name: LadderSystem.lie_N_a
declarations.doc: `[Nᵢ, aⱼ] = -δᵢⱼaᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lie_N_a (i j : Fin d) :
    (⁅L.N i, L.a j⁆ : Module.End K V) = (-δ[i,j] : K) • L.a i

declarations.name: LadderSystem.lie_N_ac
declarations.doc: `[Nᵢ, acⱼ] = δᵢⱼacᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lie_N_ac (i j : Fin d) :
    (⁅L.N i, L.ac j⁆ : Module.End K V) = (δ[i,j] : K) • L.ac i

declarations.name: LadderSystem.lie_N_N
declarations.doc: `[Nᵢ, Nⱼ] = 0`: the number operators commute among themselves.
declarations.statement: lemma lie_N_N (i j : Fin d) : (⁅L.N i, L.N j⁆ : Module.End K V) = 0

declarations.name: LadderSystem.totalN
declarations.doc: The total number operator, `∑ᵢNᵢ` -- the total excitation count across every mode.
declarations.statement: def totalN (L : LadderSystem K V d) : Module.End K V

declarations.name: LadderSystem.lie_totalN_E
declarations.doc:
The total number operator is central in `gl(d)`: it commutes with every generator
`E i j`, not just the diagonal ones (contrast `lie_N_N`, which only says the diagonal `Nᵢ`
commute *among themselves*). Consequently any operator built from `L.totalN` alone --
in particular an *isotropic* Hamiltonian -- preserves `vacuumSpan` sector-by-sector for the same
reason `vacuumSpanLieSubmodule` does: it is `L.toGlHomLinear` applied to a central element of
`gl(d)` (the identity matrix), so it acts diagonally on the whole `gl(d)`-module structure.
declarations.statement: theorem lie_totalN_E (j k : Fin d) : (⁅L.totalN, L.E j k⁆ : Module.End K V) = 0

modules.title: Irreducibility of the excitation-number sector
modules.doc:
The excitation-number sector `vacuumSpan L Ω n` of a ladder system is `gl(d)`-irreducible.

## i. Overview

`LadderSystem.vacuumSpan L Ω n` is `gl(d)`-irreducible: the only submodules of `vacuumSpan L Ω n`
invariant under every `E i j` are `⊥` and `vacuumSpan L Ω n` itself. Completeness in an ambient
Hilbert space is a separate analytic question. The proof uses linear algebra over a field of
characteristic zero.

## ii. Key results

- `LadderSystem.vacuumSpan_eq_of_ne_bot` : a nonzero `E i j`-invariant submodule of
    `vacuumSpan L Ω n` is all of `vacuumSpan L Ω n`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Moving a quantum between modes
- B. Extracting a single basis vector from an invariant submodule
- C. Connectivity: one basis vector reaches every other
- D. Irreducibility

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Moving a quantum between modes
## B. Extracting a single basis vector from an invariant submodule
## C. Connectivity: one basis vector reaches every other

declarations.name: LadderSystem.moveOneTo
declarations.doc:
`α` with one quantum moved from color `j` to color `i`. Only meaningful for `i ≠ j`; the
degenerate `i = j` case is handled separately by `N_word`.
declarations.statement: def moveOneTo (α : Fin d → ℕ) (i j : Fin d) : Fin d → ℕ

declarations.name: LadderSystem.countWord_moveOneTo_perm
declarations.statement:
lemma countWord_moveOneTo_perm {i j : Fin d} (hij : i ≠ j) {α : Fin d → ℕ} :
    List.Perm (i :: (countWord d α).erase j) (countWord d (moveOneTo α i j))

declarations.name: LadderSystem.E_word_countWord
declarations.doc:
The transfer formula: `E i j` moves one quantum from color `j` to color `i`, scaled by
`j`'s occupation number.
declarations.statement:
lemma E_word_countWord {Ω : V} (P : L.HasVacuum Ω) {i j : Fin d} (hij : i ≠ j)
    {α : Fin d → ℕ} :
    L.E i j (L.word (countWord d α) Ω) =
      (α j : K) • L.word (countWord d (moveOneTo α i j)) Ω

declarations.name: LadderSystem.mapsTo_aeval
declarations.doc: A submodule invariant under an endomorphism `M` is invariant under any polynomial in `M`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mapsTo_aeval {W : Submodule K V} {M : Module.End K V} (hW : ∀ w ∈ W, M w ∈ W)
    (p : Polynomial K) : ∀ w ∈ W, (Polynomial.aeval M p) w ∈ W

declarations.name: LadderSystem.exists_word_countWord_mem_of_ne_bot
declarations.doc:
A nonzero `E i j`-invariant submodule of `vacuumSpan L Ω n` contains an occupation-number
basis vector. A Lagrange-interpolation polynomial in the diagonal separator
`∑ᵢ(n+1)^i • Nᵢ` projects a nonzero element onto one of its basis components.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_word_countWord_mem_of_ne_bot {Ω : V} (P : L.HasVacuum Ω) (n : ℕ)
    {W : Submodule K V} (hWle : W ≤ vacuumSpan L Ω n)
    (hWE : ∀ i j, ∀ w ∈ W, L.E i j w ∈ W) (hWbot : W ≠ ⊥) :
    ∃ α : CountFun d n, L.word (countWord d α.1) Ω ∈ W

declarations.name: LadderSystem.sum_eq_length_countWord
declarations.doc: The total occupation number matches the length of the canonical word representing it.
declarations.statement: lemma sum_eq_length_countWord (α : Fin d → ℕ) : (∑ c, α c) = (countWord d α).length

declarations.name: LadderSystem.sum_moveOneTo
declarations.doc: Moving one quantum between two modes preserves the total occupation number.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_moveOneTo {i j : Fin d} (hij : i ≠ j) {α : Fin d → ℕ} (hj : α j ≠ 0) :
    (∑ c, moveOneTo α i j c) = ∑ c, α c

declarations.name: LadderSystem.moveOneTo_self
declarations.doc: `moveOneTo` at the color it moves quanta *into* just increments that color's count.
declarations.statement: lemma moveOneTo_self (α : Fin d → ℕ) (i j : Fin d) : moveOneTo α i j i = α i + 1

declarations.name: LadderSystem.moveOneTo_moveOneTo
declarations.doc: Moving a quantum from `j` to `i` and then immediately back from `i` to `j` is the identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma moveOneTo_moveOneTo {i j : Fin d} (hij : i ≠ j) {α : Fin d → ℕ} (hj : α j ≠ 0) :
    moveOneTo (moveOneTo α i j) j i = α

declarations.name: LadderSystem.word_countWord_moveOneTo_mem
declarations.doc:
The atomic move: if `W` is `E i j`-invariant and contains the word for `β`, and mode `k`
is occupied, `W` also contains the word obtained by moving one quantum from `k` to any other
mode `l`.

declarations.name: LadderSystem.word_countWord_hub_mem_of_mem
declarations.doc:
Every occupation-number word reaches the mode-`0` hub word, given `W`
is `E i j`-invariant and contains it. Proved by strong induction on the mass sitting outside
mode `0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma word_countWord_hub_mem_of_mem {hd : 0 < d} {Ω : V} (P : L.HasVacuum Ω)
    {W : Submodule K V} (hWE : ∀ i j, ∀ w ∈ W, L.E i j w ∈ W) :
    ∀ m : ℕ, ∀ α : Fin d → ℕ, (∑ c, α c) - α (⟨0, hd⟩ : Fin d) = m →
      L.word (countWord d α) Ω ∈ W →
      L.word (countWord d (fun c => if c = (⟨0, hd⟩ : Fin d) then (∑ c, α c) else 0)) Ω ∈ W

declarations.name: LadderSystem.word_countWord_mem_of_hub_mem
declarations.doc:
The hub word reaches every occupation-number word, given `W` is `E i j`-invariant and
contains it. Proved by strong induction on the mass sitting outside mode `0` in the target.
declarations.statement:
lemma word_countWord_mem_of_hub_mem {hd : 0 < d} {Ω : V} (P : L.HasVacuum Ω)
    {W : Submodule K V} (hWE : ∀ i j, ∀ w ∈ W, L.E i j w ∈ W) :
    ∀ m : ℕ, ∀ α : Fin d → ℕ, (∑ c, α c) - α (⟨0, hd⟩ : Fin d) = m →
      L.word (countWord d (fun c => if c = (⟨0, hd⟩ : Fin d) then (∑ c, α c) else 0)) Ω ∈ W →
      L.word (countWord d α) Ω ∈ W

declarations.name: LadderSystem.word_countWord_mem_of_mem
declarations.doc:
Connectivity: any two occupation-number words of the same total excitation number reach
each other, given `W` is `E i j`-invariant and contains one of them.
declarations.statement:
lemma word_countWord_mem_of_mem {hd : 0 < d} {Ω : V} (P : L.HasVacuum Ω)
    {W : Submodule K V} (hWE : ∀ i j, ∀ w ∈ W, L.E i j w ∈ W) {α α' : Fin d → ℕ}
    (hsum : (∑ c, α c) = ∑ c, α' c) (hmem : L.word (countWord d α) Ω ∈ W) :
    L.word (countWord d α') Ω ∈ W

declarations.name: LadderSystem.vacuumSpan_eq_of_ne_bot
declarations.doc:
`vacuumSpan L Ω n` is `gl(d)`-irreducible. The only submodules of `vacuumSpan L Ω n`
invariant under every `E i j` are `⊥` and `vacuumSpan L Ω n` itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem vacuumSpan_eq_of_ne_bot {hd : 0 < d} {Ω : V} (P : L.HasVacuum Ω) (n : ℕ)
    {W : Submodule K V} (hWle : W ≤ vacuumSpan L Ω n)
    (hWE : ∀ i j, ∀ w ∈ W, L.E i j w ∈ W) (hWbot : W ≠ ⊥) :
    W = vacuumSpan L Ω n

modules.title: The occupation-number basis
modules.doc:
The occupation-number states form a basis of `vacuumSpan L Ω n`, of dimension `(d+n-1).choose n`.

## i. Overview

The occupation-number states `word (countWord d α) Ω`, indexed by degree-`n` count functions
`α : CountFun d n`, form a basis of `vacuumSpan L Ω n`. For linear independence, each state is
viewed as a nonzero eigenvector of the diagonal operator
`M := ∑ᵢ (n+1)^i • Nᵢ`, at the pairwise-distinct eigenvalue `countEncode n α` (a positional
encoding of `α`), so Mathlib's general "eigenvectors at distinct eigenvalues are independent" fact
applies. It follows that `vacuumSpan` is finite-dimensional and has dimension
`(d+n-1).choose n`, the degeneracy of the `n`-th level of a `d`-dimensional bosonic oscillator.

## ii. Key results

Definitions:
- `CountFun d n` : a degree-`n` count function on `d` colors.
- `LadderSystem.vacuumBasis` : the occupation-number basis of `vacuumSpan L Ω n`.

Theorems:
- `LadderSystem.linearIndependent_word_countFun` : the occupation-number states are linearly
    independent.
- `LadderSystem.finrank_vacuumSpan_eq_choose` : `vacuumSpan L Ω n` has dimension
    `(d+n-1).choose n`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Count functions
- B. Exact annihilation
- C. The occupation-number basis
  - C.1. A positional encoding of count functions
  - C.2. Linear independence
  - C.3. The basis and its dimension

## iv. References

* None.

### C.3. The basis and its dimension

declarations.name: CountFun
declarations.doc: A degree-`n` count function on `d` colors.
declarations.statement: abbrev CountFun (d n : ℕ)

declarations.name: countFunEquivSym
declarations.doc: Degree-`n` count functions on `d` colors biject with `Sym (Fin d) n`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def countFunEquivSym (d n : ℕ) : CountFun d n ≃ Sym (Fin d) n

declarations.name: instFintypeCountFun
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance instFintypeCountFun {d n : ℕ} : Fintype (CountFun d n)

declarations.name: card_countFun
declarations.doc: There are exactly `(d + n - 1).choose n` degree-`n` count functions on `d` colors.
declarations.statement: lemma card_countFun (d n : ℕ) : Fintype.card (CountFun d n) = (d + n - 1).choose n

declarations.name: LadderSystem.pow_a_comm_ac
declarations.doc: Annihilation and creation operators of different colors commute at any power.
declarations.statement:
lemma pow_a_comm_ac {i c : Fin d} (hic : i ≠ c) (k : ℕ) (y : V) :
    ((L.a i) ^ k) (L.ac c y) = L.ac c (((L.a i) ^ k) y)

declarations.name: LadderSystem.word_peel_eq_count
declarations.doc:
Exact annihilation: applying `a i` exactly `count i` times removes every `i`, scaled by the
factorial.
declarations.statement:
lemma word_peel_eq_count (L : LadderSystem K V d) (i : Fin d) {x : V} (hx : L.a i x = 0) :
    ∀ v : List (Fin d),
      ((L.a i) ^ (v.count i)) (L.word v x) = (v.count i).factorial • L.word (v.filter (· != i)) x

declarations.name: LadderSystem.annMono
declarations.doc:
The joint annihilation monomial for a list of colors `cs` and exponents `α`:
`∏_{c ∈ cs} (a c)^{α c}`.
declarations.statement: def annMono (cs : List (Fin d)) (α : Fin d → ℕ) : Module.End K V

declarations.name: LadderSystem.annMono_nil
declarations.statement: lemma annMono_nil (α : Fin d → ℕ) : L.annMono [] α = 1

declarations.name: LadderSystem.annMono_cons
declarations.statement:
lemma annMono_cons (c : Fin d) (cs : List (Fin d)) (α : Fin d → ℕ) :
    L.annMono (c :: cs) α = (L.a c) ^ (α c) * L.annMono cs α

declarations.name: LadderSystem.annMono_eq_count
declarations.doc: Exact annihilation of every color in the list produces the product of factorials.
declarations.statement:
lemma annMono_eq_count (L : LadderSystem K V d) {x : V} (hx : ∀ i, L.a i x = 0) :
    ∀ (cs : List (Fin d)), cs.Nodup → ∀ (α : Fin d → ℕ) (v : List (Fin d)),
      (∀ c ∈ cs, v.count c = α c) →
      (L.annMono cs α) (L.word v x)
        = ((cs.map (fun c => (α c).factorial)).prod) •
            L.word (v.filter (fun y => !cs.contains y)) x
  | [], _, _, _, _ => by simp
  | c :: cs', hnodup, α, v, hmatch => by
    obtain ⟨hcnotmem, hnodup'⟩

declarations.name: countWord_filter_finRange
declarations.doc: `countWord α` contains only colors from `List.finRange d`, i.e. everything.
declarations.statement:
lemma countWord_filter_finRange {d : ℕ} (α : Fin d → ℕ) :
    (LadderSystem.countWord d α).filter (fun y => !(List.finRange d).contains y) = []

declarations.name: encode_injOn_aux
declarations.doc: A base-`b` positional encoding is injective on tuples with digits `< b`.
declarations.statement:
lemma encode_injOn_aux : ∀ (d b : ℕ), 0 < b → ∀ γ γ' : Fin d → ℕ,
    (∀ c, γ c < b) → (∀ c, γ' c < b) →
    (∑ i : Fin d, γ i * b ^ (i : ℕ)) = (∑ i : Fin d, γ' i * b ^ (i : ℕ)) → γ = γ'

declarations.name: countEncode
declarations.doc:
The base-`(n+1)` positional encoding of a degree-`n` count function; injective on such
functions.
declarations.statement: def countEncode (n : ℕ) {d : ℕ} (γ : Fin d → ℕ) : ℕ

declarations.name: countEncode_injOn
LadderSystem.word_countWord_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
Every occupation-number state is nonzero: peeling every color's annihilation operator down to
the vacuum leaves a nonzero factorial multiple of `Ω`.
declarations.statement:
lemma word_countWord_ne_zero {Ω : V} (hΩ : L.HasVacuum Ω) (α : Fin d → ℕ) :
    L.word (countWord d α) Ω ≠ 0

declarations.name: LadderSystem.hasEigenvector_word_countWord
declarations.doc:
The occupation-number states are the eigenvectors, at pairwise-distinct eigenvalues, of the
single diagonal operator `M := ∑ᵢ (n+1)^i • Nᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasEigenvector_word_countWord {Ω : V} (hΩ : L.HasVacuum Ω) (n : ℕ) (α : CountFun d n) :
    Module.End.HasEigenvector (∑ i : Fin d, ((n + 1 : K)) ^ (i : ℕ) • L.N i)
      (countEncode n α.1 : K) (L.word (countWord d α.1) Ω)

declarations.name: LadderSystem.linearIndependent_word_countFun
declarations.doc:
The occupation-number family is linearly independent because its elements are eigenvectors at
pairwise-distinct eigenvalues (`Module.End.eigenvectors_linearIndependent'`).
declarations.statement:
theorem linearIndependent_word_countFun {Ω : V} (P : L.HasVacuum Ω) (n : ℕ) :
    LinearIndependent K (fun α : CountFun d n => L.word (countWord d α.1) Ω)

declarations.name: LadderSystem.span_word_countFun_eq_vacuumSpan
declarations.doc: The occupation-number family spans `vacuumSpan L Ω n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma span_word_countFun_eq_vacuumSpan (Ω : V) (n : ℕ) :
    Submodule.span K (Set.range fun α : CountFun d n => L.word (countWord d α.1) Ω)
      = L.vacuumSpan Ω n

declarations.name: LadderSystem.vacuumBasis
declarations.doc: A basis of `vacuumSpan L Ω n` indexed by degree-`n` occupation-count functions.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def vacuumBasis {Ω : V} (P : L.HasVacuum Ω) (n : ℕ) :
    Basis (CountFun d n) K (L.vacuumSpan Ω n)

declarations.name: LadderSystem.vacuumBasis_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma vacuumBasis_apply {Ω : V} (P : L.HasVacuum Ω) (n : ℕ) (α : CountFun d n) :
    (vacuumBasis L P n α : V) = L.word (countWord d α.1) Ω

declarations.name: LadderSystem.finrank_vacuumSpan_eq_choose
declarations.doc:
The dimension of `vacuumSpan L Ω n` is `(d+n-1).choose n`, the degeneracy of the `n`-th level
of a `d`-mode bosonic system.
declarations.statement:
theorem finrank_vacuumSpan_eq_choose {Ω : V} (P : L.HasVacuum Ω) (n : ℕ) :
    Module.finrank K (L.vacuumSpan Ω n) = (d + n - 1).choose n

declarations.name: LadderSystem.finiteDimensional_vacuumSpan
declarations.statement:
lemma finiteDimensional_vacuumSpan {Ω : V} (P : L.HasVacuum Ω) (n : ℕ) :
    FiniteDimensional K (L.vacuumSpan Ω n)

declarations.name: LadderSystem.vacuumSpan_ne_bot
declarations.statement:
lemma vacuumSpan_ne_bot {Ω : V} (P : L.HasVacuum Ω) (hd : 0 < d) (n : ℕ) :
    L.vacuumSpan Ω n ≠ ⊥

modules.title: The excitation sector is the symmetric power
modules.doc:
The excitation-number sector `vacuumSpan L Ω n` is linearly isomorphic to `Sym^n(K^d)`.

## i. Overview

`vacuumSpan L Ω n` is linearly isomorphic to the `n`-th symmetric power of `K^d` -- concretely, to
the free `K`-vector space on `Sym (Fin d) n` (Mathlib's own type of size-`n` multisets on `Fin d`,
the standard combinatorial model of `Sym^n(K^d)`'s natural basis once a basis `e_1,…,e_d` of `K^d`
is fixed: a multiset `{i_1,…,i_n}` names the basis vector `e_{i_1} ⊙ ⋯ ⊙ e_{i_n}`). The
isomorphism sends this basis to the occupation-number states, i.e. it is exactly
`OccupationBasis.lean`'s `vacuumBasis` reindexed along `countFunEquivSym`.

## ii. Key results

- `LadderSystem.vacuumSpanSymEquiv` : `(Sym (Fin d) n →₀ K) ≃ₗ[K] vacuumSpan L Ω n`.
- `LadderSystem.vacuumSpanSymEquiv_single` : the basis vector of a multiset is sent to the
  occupation-number state of its count function.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The isomorphism with the symmetric power
- B. The image of the basis vectors

## iv. References

* None.

## B. The image of the basis vectors

declarations.name: LadderSystem.vacuumSpanSymEquiv
declarations.doc:
`vacuumSpan L Ω n` is linearly isomorphic to `Sym^n(K^d)` (realized as the free `K`-module
on `Sym (Fin d) n`), matching the natural monomial-type basis on one side to the occupation-number
basis on the other.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def vacuumSpanSymEquiv {Ω : V} (P : L.HasVacuum Ω) (n : ℕ) :
    (Sym (Fin d) n →₀ K) ≃ₗ[K] L.vacuumSpan Ω n

declarations.name: LadderSystem.vacuumSpanSymEquiv_single
declarations.doc:
The isomorphism sends the basis vector for multiset `s` to the occupation-number state with
that multiset's count function.
declarations.statement:
lemma vacuumSpanSymEquiv_single {Ω : V} (P : L.HasVacuum Ω) (n : ℕ) (s : Sym (Fin d) n) :
    (L.vacuumSpanSymEquiv P n (Finsupp.single s 1) : V)
      = L.word (countWord d ((countFunEquivSym d n).symm s).1) Ω

modules.title: Vacuum states and creation-operator words
modules.doc:
Vacuum states of a ladder system, creation-operator words, and the `n`-particle sector.

## i. Overview

A vacuum `Ω` of a `LadderSystem` is a nonzero vector killed by every annihilation operator. This
file develops creation-operator words `acᵢ₁acᵢ₂⋯acᵢₙΩ` and the excitation-number sector they span,
`vacuumSpan`. This sector is bundled as a `gl(d)` Lie submodule. Its occupation-number basis is
constructed in `OccupationBasis.lean`, and its irreducibility is proved in `Irreducibility.lean`.

## ii. Key results

Definitions:
- `LadderSystem.HasVacuum` : `Ω` is nonzero and killed by every `a i`.
- `LadderSystem.word` : a word of creation operators applied to a vector.
- `LadderSystem.vacuumSpan` : the span of all length-`n` words over a vacuum -- the
    `n`-particle sector.
- `LadderSystem.vacuumSpanLieSubmodule` : `vacuumSpan`, bundled as a `gl(d)` Lie submodule.

Theorems:
- `LadderSystem.word_perm` : a word depends only on the multiset of colors it represents.
- `LadderSystem.word_peel` : `aᵢ` applied to a word removes one occurrence of color `i`, scaled
    by its count.
- `LadderSystem.E_word`, `LadderSystem.N_word` : how `E i j`/`N i` act on a word.
- `LadderSystem.E_mem_vacuumSpan` : `vacuumSpan` is closed under every `gl(d)` generator `E i j`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Vacuum states
- B. Words
- C. The excitation-number sector
  - C.1. `gl(d)`-invariance

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: LadderSystem.HasVacuum
declarations.doc: A vacuum: a nonzero vector killed by every annihilation operator.
declarations.statement:
structure HasVacuum (Ω : V) : Prop where
  /-- A vacuum is nonzero. -/
  ne_zero : Ω ≠ 0
  /-- A vacuum is killed by every annihilation operator. -/
  ann : ∀ i, L.a i Ω = 0

declarations.name: LadderSystem.word
declarations.doc: A word of creation operators applied to a fixed vector.
declarations.statement: def word (L : LadderSystem K V d) (v : List (Fin d)) (x : V) : V

declarations.name: LadderSystem.word_cons
declarations.statement:
lemma word_cons (L : LadderSystem K V d) (i : Fin d) (v : List (Fin d)) (x : V) :
    L.word (i :: v) x = L.ac i (L.word v x)

declarations.name: LadderSystem.word_perm
declarations.doc: A word depends only on the multiset of colors it represents, not their order.
declarations.statement:
lemma word_perm (L : LadderSystem K V d) {v v' : List (Fin d)} (h : v.Perm v') (x : V) :
    L.word v x = L.word v' x

declarations.name: LadderSystem.word_peel
declarations.doc: Peeling: `a i` applied to a word removes one occurrence of color `i`, scaled by its count.
declarations.statement:
lemma word_peel (L : LadderSystem K V d) (i : Fin d) {x : V} (hx : L.a i x = 0) :
    ∀ v : List (Fin d), L.a i (L.word v x) = (v.count i) • L.word (v.erase i) x

declarations.name: LadderSystem.E_word
declarations.doc:
How `E i j` acts on a word: removes one occurrence of `j`, adds one of `i`, scaled by `j`'s
count.
declarations.statement:
lemma E_word (L : LadderSystem K V d) {x : V} (hx : ∀ i, L.a i x = 0) (i j : Fin d)
    (v : List (Fin d)) :
    (L.E i j) (L.word v x) = (v.count j) • L.word (i :: v.erase j) x

declarations.name: LadderSystem.N_word
declarations.doc: Words are eigenvectors of the number operator, with eigenvalue their own color count.
declarations.statement:
lemma N_word (L : LadderSystem K V d) {x : V} (hx : ∀ i, L.a i x = 0) (i : Fin d)
    (v : List (Fin d)) : (L.N i) (L.word v x) = (v.count i) • L.word v x

declarations.name: LadderSystem.countWord
declarations.doc:
The canonical word representing a count function `α`: `α c` copies of color `c`, in
increasing order.
declarations.statement: def countWord (d : ℕ) (α : Fin d → ℕ) : List (Fin d)

declarations.name: LadderSystem.count_countWord
declarations.doc: `countWord α` has exactly `α i` copies of color `i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma count_countWord {d : ℕ} (α : Fin d → ℕ) (i : Fin d) :
    (countWord d α).count i = α i

declarations.name: LadderSystem.sum_count_eq_length
declarations.doc: A word's length is the sum of its per-color counts.
declarations.statement: lemma sum_count_eq_length {d : ℕ} : ∀ v : List (Fin d), (∑ c : Fin d, v.count c) = v.length

declarations.name: LadderSystem.vacuumSpan
declarations.doc:
The `n`-th excitation-number sector generated by a vacuum: the span of all length-`n`
creation words.
declarations.statement: def vacuumSpan (L : LadderSystem K V d) (Ω : V) (n : ℕ) : Submodule K V

declarations.name: LadderSystem.exists_ofFn_eq_of_length_eq
declarations.statement:

declarations.statement:

declarations.doc:
`E`-invariance of a submodule extends to full `gl(d)`-invariance, by linearity off the
matrix-unit basis.

declarations.name: LadderSystem.E_mem_vacuumSpan
declarations.doc:
`vacuumSpan` is closed under every `gl(d)` generator `E i j`. Unconditional: no
`FiniteDimensional`/spanning hypothesis on the ambient `V` is used or needed.
declarations.statement:
lemma E_mem_vacuumSpan (L : LadderSystem K V d) {Ω : V} (P : L.HasVacuum Ω) (n : ℕ)

modules.title: Contracting the Levi-Civita symbol against a matrix
modules.doc:
The symbol is a tensor density of weight one.

## i. Overview

Contracting the Levi-Civita symbol against the rows of a matrix `M` picked out by an index
family `a` gives `det M` times the symbol of `a`. This is the statement that `ε` transforms as
a tensor density of weight one, and it is what makes an `ε` contraction invariant under a
determinant-one group.

Both sides are the determinant of the matrix of those rows: on the left by expanding it along
the Leibniz formula, on the right by the product rule, the row selection being the matrix of
Kronecker deltas of `a`. The bridge to an arbitrary commutative ring is `cast_leviCivitaSymbol`,
which carries the integer determinant of the delta matrix along the ring map from `ℤ`.

## ii. Key results

- `cast_leviCivitaSymbol` : the symbol as a determinant over any commutative ring.
- `sum_leviCivitaSymbol_mul_prod` : contracted against the rows of `M` selected by `a`, the
  symbol gives `det M` times the symbol of `a`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Contraction against a matrix

## iv. References

* https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levi-Civita_symbol. [ref: wiki_levi_civita_symbol]

sections.text:
## A. Contraction against a matrix

Contracting the symbol against the rows of a matrix `M` picked out by `a` gives `det M` times
the symbol of `a`. Both sides are the determinant of the matrix of those rows: on the left by
expanding it along the Leibniz formula, on the right by the product rule, the row selection
being the matrix of Kronecker deltas of `a`.

declarations.name: cast_leviCivitaSymbol
declarations.doc:
The symbol as a determinant over any commutative ring, the integer determinant carried
along the ring map from `ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma cast_leviCivitaSymbol (g : ι → ι) :
    ((leviCivitaSymbol g : ℤ) : R)
      = (Matrix.of fun i j : ι => if g i = j then (1 : R) else 0).det

declarations.name: sum_leviCivitaSymbol_mul_prod
declarations.doc:
Contracted against the rows of `M` selected by `a`, the symbol gives `det M` times the
symbol of `a`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_leviCivitaSymbol_mul_prod (M : Matrix ι ι R) (a : ι → ι) :
    ∑ g : ι → ι, ((leviCivitaSymbol g : ℤ) : R) * ∏ i, M (a i) (g i)
      = M.det * ((leviCivitaSymbol a : ℤ) : R)

modules.title: Finite linear combinations under a linear map
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A family `T : ι → B` of vectors of an `R`-module spans Mathlib's
`Submodule.span R (Set.range T)`. The index type is arbitrary and may be empty. When it is
finite, the elements of the span are exactly the combinations `∑ i, c i • T i`, for
coefficients `c : ι → R` that need not be unique (`Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun`).
The one fact added here is that a linear map carries this span to the span of the images of
the family (`Submodule.map_span_range`).

Two bookkeeping identities about these combinations: contracting
against coefficients moved by a matrix regroups as the same combination of the matrix-moved
components, and a linear map given on the family by a matrix moves a combination by that matrix
acting on the coefficients.

Over `ℂ`, when linear maps on `B` move combinations by moving their coefficients, a combination
fixed by all the maps is the combination of fixed coefficients, provided the coefficient maps
have their adjoints among themselves: `Fintype.exists_invariant_coeff_of_adjoint_mem`. When the
coefficient maps are matrices, the condition is that the conjugate transpose of each matrix is
again one of them: `Fintype.exists_mulVec_eq_of_conjTranspose_mem`.

Spans are bounded through their members: the range of a linear map is the span of the images
of a basis, and a product of submodules lying in spans of families lies in any submodule
containing the products of their members.

## ii. Key results

- `Submodule.map_span_range` : the image of the span of a family is the span of the images
- `Fintype.exists_invariant_coeff_of_adjoint_mem` : a vector of the span of `T` fixed by every `φ g`
  is the combination of coefficients fixed by every `A g`, where `φ g` moves combinations by moving
  their coefficients with `A g`
- `Fintype.exists_mulVec_eq_of_conjTranspose_mem`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The image of the span of a family
- B. Combinations moved by linear maps
- C. Fixed vectors of the span
- D. Spans bounded through their members

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The image of the span of a family
## B. Combinations moved by linear maps
## C. Fixed vectors of the span
## D. Spans bounded through their members

declarations.name: Submodule.map_span_range
declarations.doc: The image of the span of a family is the span of the images.
declarations.statement:
lemma Submodule.map_span_range {R B B' : Type*} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid B] [Module R B]
    [AddCommMonoid B'] [Module R B'] {ι : Sort*} (f : B →ₗ[R] B') (T : ι → B) :
    (Submodule.span R (Set.range T)).map f = Submodule.span R (Set.range fun i => f (T i))

declarations.name: Fintype.sum_sum_mul_smul
declarations.doc:
Contracting the components against coefficients moved by a matrix is the original
combination of the matrix-moved components.
declarations.statement:
lemma Fintype.sum_sum_mul_smul (M : ι → κ → R) (c : κ → R) (T : ι → B) :
    ∑ a, (∑ d, c d * M a d) • T a = ∑ d, c d • ∑ a, M a d • T a

declarations.name: LinearMap.map_sum_smul_of_forall_eq
declarations.doc:
A linear map that moves each component of a family by a matrix moves a combination of the
components by that matrix acting on the coefficients, with the free index first.
declarations.statement:
lemma LinearMap.map_sum_smul_of_forall_eq (φ : B →ₗ[R] B') (T : ι → B) (T' : κ → B')
    (M : κ → ι → R) (hT : ∀ l, φ (T l) = ∑ a, M a l • T' a) (c : ι → R) :
    φ (∑ l, c l • T l) = ∑ a, (∑ l, c l * M a l) • T' a

declarations.name: LinearMap.map_sum_smul_eq_sum_mulVec_smul
declarations.doc:
The matrix form of `LinearMap.map_sum_smul_of_forall_eq`: a linear map moving `T l` to
`∑ a, M a l • T' a` moves the combination with coefficients `c` to the combination with
coefficients `M *ᵥ c`.
declarations.statement:
lemma LinearMap.map_sum_smul_eq_sum_mulVec_smul (φ : B →ₗ[R] B') (T : ι → B) (T' : κ → B')
    (M : Matrix κ ι R) (hT : ∀ l, φ (T l) = ∑ a, M a l • T' a) (c : ι → R) :
    φ (∑ l, c l • T l) = ∑ a, (M *ᵥ c) a • T' a

declarations.name: Fintype.exists_invariant_coeff_of_adjoint_mem
declarations.doc:
A vector of the span of `T` fixed by every `φ g` is the combination of coefficients fixed
by every `A g`, where `φ g` moves combinations by moving their coefficients with `A g`. The
one condition on `A` is that for every `g` some `g'` acts as the adjoint of `g` for the
standard inner product on coefficients; neither the `φ g` nor the `A g` need form a
representation, and `B` carries no inner product. The components may be dependent, so the
coefficients need not be unique: the proof takes the part of any coefficients orthogonal to
those contracting to `0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma Fintype.exists_invariant_coeff_of_adjoint_mem {ι G B : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    [AddCommGroup B] [Module ℂ B] (T : ι → B) (φ : G → B →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (A : G → (ι → ℂ) →ₗ[ℂ] (ι → ℂ))
    (hφ : ∀ (g : G) (c : ι → ℂ), φ g (∑ i, c i • T i) = ∑ i, A g c i • T i)
    (hA : ∀ g : G, ∃ g' : G, ∀ u v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι,
      ⟪u, WithLp.toLp 2 (A g v.ofLp)⟫_ℂ = ⟪WithLp.toLp 2 (A g' u.ofLp), v⟫_ℂ)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range T)) (hinv : ∀ g, φ g x = x) :
    ∃ c : ι → ℂ, x = ∑ i, c i • T i ∧ ∀ g, A g c = c

declarations.name: Fintype.exists_mulVec_eq_of_conjTranspose_mem
declarations.doc:
The matrix form of `Fintype.exists_invariant_coeff_of_adjoint_mem`: when each `φ g` moves
the family by a matrix `M g`, and the conjugate transpose of each `M g` is some `M g'`, a
vector of the span fixed by every `φ g` is the combination of a coefficient vector fixed by
every `M g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma Fintype.exists_mulVec_eq_of_conjTranspose_mem {ι G B : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    [AddCommGroup B] [Module ℂ B] (T : ι → B) (φ : G → B →ₗ[ℂ] B) (M : G → Matrix ι ι ℂ)
    (hT : ∀ g l, φ g (T l) = ∑ a, M g a l • T a) (hM : ∀ g, ∃ g', M g' = (M g)ᴴ)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range T)) (hinv : ∀ g, φ g x = x) :
    ∃ c : ι → ℂ, x = ∑ i, c i • T i ∧ ∀ g, M g *ᵥ c = c

declarations.name: LinearMap.range_eq_span_range_basis
declarations.doc: The range of a linear map is the span of the images of a basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma LinearMap.range_eq_span_range_basis {ι R M N : Type*} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M]
    [Module R M] [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (f : M →ₗ[R] N) :
    LinearMap.range f = Submodule.span R (Set.range fun i => f (b i))

declarations.name: Submodule.mul_le_of_le_span_range
declarations.doc:
A product of two submodules, each inside the span of a family, lies in any submodule
containing the products of the members of the two families.
declarations.statement:
lemma Submodule.mul_le_of_le_span_range {ι κ R A : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [Semiring A]
    [Algebra R A] {V V' X : Submodule R A} {a : ι → A} {b : κ → A}
    (hV : V ≤ Submodule.span R (Set.range a)) (hV' : V' ≤ Submodule.span R (Set.range b))
    (hX : ∀ i j, a i * b j ∈ X) : V * V' ≤ X

declarations.name: Submodule.mul_mul_le_of_le_span_range
declarations.doc: The three-factor form of `Submodule.mul_le_of_le_span_range`.
declarations.statement:
lemma Submodule.mul_mul_le_of_le_span_range {ι κ ν R A : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [Semiring A]
    [Algebra R A] {V V' V'' X : Submodule R A} {a : ι → A} {b : κ → A} {c : ν → A}
    (hV : V ≤ Submodule.span R (Set.range a)) (hV' : V' ≤ Submodule.span R (Set.range b))
    (hV'' : V'' ≤ Submodule.span R (Set.range c)) (hX : ∀ i j k, a i * (b j * c k) ∈ X) :
    V * (V' * V'') ≤ X

modules.title: Bounded measurable functions
modules.doc:
The vector lattice of bounded measurable functions, staircase approximation and integrability.

## i. Overview

The bounded measurable functions on a space `Ω` are the observables of a classical system with
outcomes in `Ω`. They form a vector lattice under the pointwise operations. The least upper bound of
a sequence bounded above is its pointwise supremum. Every bounded measurable function is uniformly
approximated from below by a staircase, a finite combination of indicator functions, and it is
integrable against every finite measure.

## ii. Key results

- `BoundedMeasurable Ω` is the space of bounded measurable real functions on `Ω`.
- `BoundedMeasurable.isLUB_range_iff` proves that least upper bounds of sequences are pointwise.
- `BoundedMeasurable.abs_sub_staircase_le` proves that the staircase approximation is uniform.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The vector space
- B. The lattice order
- C. Least upper bounds of sequences
- D. Indicators and staircases
- E. Integrability

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Integration over the Euclidean product
modules.doc:
The Euclidean product `WithLp 2 (E × F)` carries the product of the Lebesgue measures.

## i. Overview

The `L²` product of two finite dimensional inner product spaces is measure preservingly equivalent
to the plain product. Integrals over it are iterated integrals. The norm of a point dominates the
norm of each coordinate.

## ii. Key results

- `EuclideanProd.integral_withLp_prod` : integration over the Euclidean product.
- `EuclideanProd.integrable_withLp_prod` : integrability over the Euclidean product.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Integration
- B. Norms

## iv. References

None.

## A. Integration

- `EuclideanProd.integral_withLp_prod` : integration over the Euclidean product.
- `EuclideanProd.integrable_withLp_prod` : integrability over the Euclidean product.

## B. Norms

- `EuclideanProd.norm_le_norm_toLp_right` : the second coordinate is dominated by the norm.
- `EuclideanProd.norm_toLp_zero` : the norm of a point with vanishing second coordinate.

declarations.name: EuclideanProd.integral_withLp_prod
declarations.doc: Integration over the Euclidean product is iterated integration.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_withLp_prod {G : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace ℝ G]
    (φ : WithLp 2 (E × F) → G) :
    ∫ z, φ z = ∫ p : E × F, φ (WithLp.toLp 2 p)

declarations.name: EuclideanProd.integrable_withLp_prod
declarations.doc: Integrability over the Euclidean product is integrability over the product.
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_withLp_prod {G : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup G] {φ : WithLp 2 (E × F) → G}
    (hφ : Integrable φ) : Integrable (fun p : E × F => φ (WithLp.toLp 2 p))

declarations.name: EuclideanProd.norm_le_norm_toLp_right
declarations.doc: The second coordinate is dominated by the norm of the point.
declarations.statement: lemma norm_le_norm_toLp_right (x : E) (y : F) : ‖y‖ ≤ ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y)‖

declarations.name: EuclideanProd.norm_toLp_zero
declarations.doc: The norm of a point with vanishing second coordinate.
declarations.statement: lemma norm_toLp_zero (ξ : E) : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (ξ, (0 : F))‖ = ‖ξ‖

modules.title: Lifting, averaging and conditioning probability measures
modules.doc:
Lifting, averaging, conditioning and replacing parts of probability measures.

## i. Overview

This file collects operations on probability measures used in Choquet's theorem. A probability
measure on the compact range of a continuous map is the image of a probability measure on its
source. The images of one measure under two maps can be averaged. A measure can be conditioned on an
event of positive probability. Finally, the part of a measure on an event can be handed to another
measure.

## ii. Key results

- `ProbabilityMeasure.exists_map_eq_of_continuous_of_compl_range_null` proves that a probability
  measure on the range of a continuous map lifts to its source.
- `ProbabilityMeasure.averageMap` is the average of two images of a measure.
- `ProbabilityMeasure.condition` conditions a measure on an event.
- `ProbabilityMeasure.replacePart` replaces the part of a measure on an event.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Lifting through a compact continuous map
- B. Averaging two pushforwards
- C. Conditioning and replacing part of a measure

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Lifting through a compact continuous map
## C. Conditioning and replacing part of a measure

declarations.doc:
A probability measure charging only the range of a continuous map from a compact space lifts

domain, which extends and is represented by a measure.

    (mu : ProbabilityMeasure Y) (hmu : (mu : Measure Y) (Set.range q)ᶜ = 0) :
    ∃ nu : ProbabilityMeasure X, nu.map q = mu

declarations.name: ProbabilityMeasure.integral_averageMap
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_averageMap {rho : ProbabilityMeasure A} {f g : A → B}
    (hf : AEMeasurable f rho) (hg : AEMeasurable g rho) {u : B → ℝ}
    (hu : Integrable u (rho.map f))
    (hv : Integrable u (rho.map g)) :
    ∫ x, u x ∂(averageMap rho f g hf hg : Measure B) =
      ((1 : ℝ) / 2) * (∫ x, u (f x) ∂(rho : Measure A)) +
        ((1 : ℝ) / 2) * (∫ x, u (g x) ∂(rho : Measure A))

modules.title: Monotonicity of finite product measures
modules.doc:
Finite product measures `MeasureTheory.Measure.pi` are monotone in each of their factors.

## i. Overview

Mathlib constructs the finite product `Measure.pi μ` of a family of measures `μ i`, but does
not (yet) record that it is monotone in the family. This file proves that if `μ i ≤ ν i` for
every `i`, then `Measure.pi μ ≤ Measure.pi ν`. No `SigmaFinite` assumption is needed, since the
proof goes through the outer measure `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.pi` from which `Measure.pi` is
built.

## ii. Key results

- `MeasureTheory.Measure.pi_mono` : the finite product of measures is monotone in the family.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Monotonicity of the product measure

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.doc:

if `μ i ≤ ν i` for every `i`, then `Measure.pi μ ≤ Measure.pi ν`.

modules.title: Positive functionals are integrals
modules.doc:
A positive functional given on part of `C(X, ℝ)` is integration against a probability measure.

## i. Overview

On a compact space `X`, a positive linear functional on continuous functions is integration against
a measure. This is the Riesz–Markov–Kakutani theorem. Often the functional is only known on some
continuous functions, for example on observables seen as functions on the pure states.

Here the functional `φ` is given through a linear map `T : V → C(X, ℝ)` whose range contains the
constant `1`. Suppose `φ v ≥ 0` whenever `T v ≥ 0`, and `φ` equals `1` at a preimage of `1`. Then
`φ` is integration of `T` against a regular probability measure. The M. Riesz extension theorem
first extends `φ` positively to all continuous functions.

## ii. Key results

- `ContinuousMap.instPosSMulMono` proves that scaling by a nonnegative number preserves the order of
  continuous functions.
- `exists_positive_extension` proves that `φ` extends to a positive functional on `C(X, ℝ)`.
- `exists_regular_probabilityMeasure_integral_eq` proves that `φ` is an integral.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Scaling continuous functions preserves their order
- B. Positive functionals are integrals

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: The integral of a radial function over the plane
modules.doc:
Integrating a radial function over two extra variables gives the tail integral of its profile.

## i. Overview

For a radial function with profile `Φ` the integral over the plane at distance `ρ` is
`∫ Φ (√(ρ² + |y|²)) dy`. In polar coordinates this is `2π ∫ s Φ (√(ρ² + s²)) ds`. The substitution
`u = √(ρ² + s²)` turns it into `2π ∫_{u > ρ} u Φ (u) du`. The tail integral has the derivative
`-ρ Φ (ρ)`.

## ii. Key results

- `RadialPlane.integral_plane_radial` : the integral of a radial function over the plane.
- `RadialPlane.hasDerivAt_tail` : the derivative of the tail integral.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The plane integral
- B. The tail integral

## iv. References

None.

## A. The plane integral

- `RadialPlane.integral_plane_radial` : the integral of a radial function over the plane.

## B. The tail integral

- `RadialPlane.hasDerivAt_tail` : the derivative of the tail integral.

declarations.name: RadialPlane.RadialDecay
declarations.doc: The decay of the profile used in the radial estimates.
declarations.statement: def RadialDecay (Φ : ℝ → ℂ) : Prop

declarations.name: RadialPlane.radial_bound
declarations.doc: A bound for the profile times the radius.
declarations.statement:
lemma radial_bound {Φ : ℝ → ℂ} {C : ℝ} (hC : ∀ u : ℝ, 0 ≤ u → ‖Φ u‖ ≤ C * (1 + u) ^ (-(3 : ℝ)))
    {x u : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hxu : x ≤ u) : ‖x • Φ u‖ ≤ |C| * (1 + ‖x‖) ^ (-(2 : ℝ))

declarations.name: RadialPlane.integral_plane_radial
declarations.doc: **The integral of a radial function over the plane.**
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_plane_radial {Φ : ℝ → ℂ} (hΦ : RadialDecay Φ) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) :
    ∫ y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), Φ (Real.sqrt (ρ ^ 2 + ‖y‖ ^ 2)) =
      (2 * Real.pi : ℝ) • ∫ u in Ioi ρ, u • Φ u

modules.title: Regular measures
modules.doc:
Inner regularity and regularity pass to smaller measures, continuous images and subsets.

## i. Overview

A measure is regular when the measure of a set is approximated by compact sets from inside and by
open sets from outside. For finite measures on a Hausdorff space the inner approximation is enough.
Inner regularity passes to smaller measures, along continuous maps and to measurable subsets, and so
regularity does too.

## ii. Key results

- `MeasureTheory.Measure.InnerRegular.of_le` proves that a measure below a finite inner regular
  measure is inner regular.
- `MeasureTheory.Measure.Regular.of_innerRegular` proves that a finite inner regular measure is
  regular.
- `MeasureTheory.Measure.Regular.map_of_continuous` proves that regularity passes along continuous
  maps.
- `MeasureTheory.Measure.InnerRegular.comap_subtype` proves that inner regularity passes to
  measurable subsets.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Measures below inner regular measures
- B. Regularity from inner regularity

## iv. References

* None.
