declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.diagEnd
declarations.doc: The diagonal action `A ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ B` of two endomorphisms on `M ⊗ N`.
declarations.statement: def diagEnd (A : Module.End K M) (B : Module.End K N) : Module.End K (M ⊗[K] N)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.diagEnd_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma diagEnd_tmul (A : Module.End K M) (B : Module.End K N) (x : M) (y : N) :
    diagEnd A B (x ⊗ₜ y) = A x ⊗ₜ y + x ⊗ₜ B y

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.lie_diagEnd
declarations.doc: The diagonal action respects commutators.
declarations.statement:
lemma lie_diagEnd (A A' : Module.End K M) (B B' : Module.End K N) :
    ⁅diagEnd A B, diagEnd A' B'⁆ = diagEnd ⁅A, A'⁆ ⁅B, B'⁆

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.diagEnd_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma diagEnd_smul (c : K) (A : Module.End K M) (B : Module.End K N) :
    diagEnd (c • A) (c • B) = c • diagEnd A B

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.diagEnd_add
declarations.doc: The diagonal action is additive in both endomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
lemma diagEnd_add (A A' : Module.End K M) (B B' : Module.End K N) :
    diagEnd (A + A') (B + B') = diagEnd A B + diagEnd A' B'

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.diagEnd_sub
declarations.doc: The diagonal action respects differences.
declarations.statement:
lemma diagEnd_sub (A A' : Module.End K M) (B B' : Module.End K N) :
    diagEnd (A - A') (B - B') = diagEnd A B - diagEnd A' B'

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.StandardSl2Module.vNat
declarations.doc:
The coordinate vector `v_i` of `StandardSl2Module K n`, indexed by a natural number;
it is zero for `i > n`.
declarations.statement: def StandardSl2Module.vNat (n i : ℕ) : StandardSl2Module K n

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.StandardSl2Module.vNat_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma vNat_apply (i : ℕ) (k : Fin (n + 1)) :
    vNat (K := K) n i k = if (k : ℕ) = i then 1 else 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.StandardSl2Module.vNat_eq_v
declarations.statement: lemma vNat_eq_v {i : ℕ} (hi : i ≤ n) : vNat (K := K) n i = v ⟨i, by omega⟩

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.StandardSl2Module.vNat_of_lt
declarations.statement: lemma vNat_of_lt {i : ℕ} (hi : n < i) : vNat (K := K) n i = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρH_vNat
declarations.statement:
lemma ρH_vNat (i : ℕ) :
    (ρH : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) (vNat n i) = ((n : K) - 2 * i) • vNat n i

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρF_vNat
declarations.statement:
lemma ρF_vNat (i : ℕ) :
    (ρF : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) (vNat n i) = vNat n (i + 1)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρE_vNat_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma ρE_vNat_zero :
    (ρE : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) (vNat n 0) = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρE_vNat_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma ρE_vNat_succ [CharZero K] (i : ℕ) :
    (ρE : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) (vNat n (i + 1)) =
      (((i : K) + 1) * ((n : K) - i)) • vNat n i

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorE
declarations.doc: The diagonal raising operator on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)`.
declarations.statement: def tensorE (m n : ℕ) : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorF
declarations.doc: The diagonal lowering operator on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)`.
declarations.statement: def tensorF (m n : ℕ) : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorH
declarations.doc: The diagonal weight operator on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)`.
declarations.statement: def tensorH (m n : ℕ) : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorCoord
declarations.doc: The coefficient of `v_i ⊗ v_j` in an element of `V(m) ⊗ V(n)`.
declarations.statement:
def tensorCoord (m n : ℕ) (i : Fin (m + 1)) (j : Fin (n + 1)) :
    StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n →ₗ[K] K

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorCoord_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorCoord_tmul (i : Fin (m + 1)) (j : Fin (n + 1)) (x : StandardSl2Module K m)
    (y : StandardSl2Module K n) : tensorCoord m n i j (x ⊗ₜ y) = x i * y j

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorH_tmul_vNat
declarations.doc: The diagonal weight operator on a product of coordinate vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorH_tmul_vNat (a b : ℕ) :
    tensorH (K := K) m n (vNat m a ⊗ₜ vNat n b) =
      ((m : K) + n - 2 * (a + b)) • (vNat m a ⊗ₜ vNat n b)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.isSl2Triple_tensor
declarations.doc: The diagonal operators on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` form an `sl₂` triple when `m + n > 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isSl2Triple_tensor [CharZero K] (hmn : 0 < m + n) :
    IsSl2Triple (tensorH (K := K) m n) (tensorE m n) (tensorF m n)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoeff
declarations.doc:
The coefficient of `v_a ⊗ v_{k-a}` in the highest-weight vector of weight `m + n - 2k`
of `V(m) ⊗ V(n)`: `(-1)^a (k choose a) (n-k+a)! (m-a)!`.
declarations.statement: def cgCoeff (m n k a : ℕ) : K

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoeff_rec
declarations.doc: The two-term recursion of the coefficients that makes the raising operator vanish.
declarations.statement:
lemma cgCoeff_rec {j a : ℕ} (hjm : j + 1 ≤ m) (hjn : j + 1 ≤ n) (ha : a ≤ j) :
    cgCoeff (K := K) m n (j + 1) (a + 1) * (((a : K) + 1) * ((m : K) - a)) +
      cgCoeff m n (j + 1) a * ((((j - a : ℕ) : K) + 1) * ((n : K) - ((j - a : ℕ) : K))) = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.hwVec
declarations.doc: The highest-weight vector of weight `m + n - 2k` in `V(m) ⊗ V(n)`.
declarations.statement: def hwVec (m n k : ℕ) : StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorH_hwVec
declarations.doc: `hwVec m n k` has weight `m + n - 2k`.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorH_hwVec (k : ℕ) :
    tensorH (K := K) m n (hwVec m n k) = ((m : K) + n - 2 * k) • hwVec m n k

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorE_hwVec
declarations.doc: `hwVec m n k` is killed by the diagonal raising operator when `k ≤ min m n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorE_hwVec [CharZero K] {k : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) :
    tensorE (K := K) m n (hwVec m n k) = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.hwVec_ne_zero
declarations.doc: `hwVec m n k` is nonzero for `k ≤ n`: its `v_0 ⊗ v_k` coefficient is `(n-k)! m!`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hwVec_ne_zero [CharZero K] {k : ℕ} (hkn : k ≤ n) :
    hwVec (K := K) m n k ≠ 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.hwVec_hasPrimitiveVectorWith
declarations.doc: `hwVec m n k` is a primitive vector of weight `m + n - 2k` for the diagonal action.
declarations.statement:
lemma hwVec_hasPrimitiveVectorWith [CharZero K] {k : ℕ} (hmn : 0 < m + n) (hkm : k ≤ m)
    (hkn : k ≤ n) :
    (isSl2Triple_tensor (K := K) hmn).HasPrimitiveVectorWith (hwVec (K := K) m n k)
      ((m + n - 2 * k : ℕ) : K)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorF_pow_hwVec_ne_zero
declarations.doc: The first `m + n - 2k + 1` members of the lowering string of `hwVec m n k` are nonzero.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorF_pow_hwVec_ne_zero [CharZero K] {k l : ℕ} (hmn : 0 < m + n) (hkm : k ≤ m)
    (hkn : k ≤ n) (hl : l ≤ m + n - 2 * k) :
    (tensorF (K := K) m n ^ l) (hwVec m n k) ≠ 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorF_pow_hwVec_eq_zero
declarations.doc: The lowering string of `hwVec m n k` ends after `m + n - 2k + 1` steps.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorF_pow_hwVec_eq_zero [CharZero K] {k : ℕ} (hmn : 0 < m + n) (hkm : k ≤ m)
    (hkn : k ≤ n) :
    (tensorF (K := K) m n ^ (m + n - 2 * k + 1)) (hwVec m n k) = 0

modules.title: Intertwiners out of a tensor product of standard sl₂ modules
modules.doc:
Linear maps `V(m) ⊗ V(n) → V(p)` compatible with the diagonal `sl₂` action.

## i. Overview

A tensor intertwiner is a linear map `φ : V(m) ⊗ V(n) → V(p)` that carries the diagonal raising,
lowering and weight operators of `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` to those of `V(p)`. Composing with the inverse of
the Clebsch–Gordan isomorphism `cgEquiv : V(m) ⊗ V(n) ≃ ⨁_j V(m + n - 2j)` gives, on each summand,
an intertwiner `V(m + n - 2j) → V(p)`. By Schur's lemma these vanish unless `m + n - 2j = p`, and
the summand with `m + n - 2j = p` contributes a scalar multiple of the identity. Hence:

- if `p` is not of the form `m + n - 2j` with `j ≤ min m n`, every tensor intertwiner is zero;
- if `p = m + n - 2j`, every tensor intertwiner is a scalar multiple of the projection `cgProj`
  onto the summand `V(m + n - 2j)`, and this projection is not zero.

In physics notation (`m = 2j₁`, `n = 2j₂`, `p = 2J`) the condition is the triangle rule
`|j₁ - j₂| ≤ J ≤ j₁ + j₂` together with `j₁ + j₂ - J ∈ ℕ`.

## ii. Key results

- `IsTensorIntertwiner` is the predicate for tensor intertwiners.
- `cgProj` is the projection onto a summand of the Clebsch–Gordan decomposition, and
  `cgProj_isTensorIntertwiner` shows that it is a tensor intertwiner.
- `IsTensorIntertwiner.eq_zero_of_forall_ne` is the selection rule.
- `IsTensorIntertwiner.exists_eq_smul_cgProj` shows that a tensor intertwiner onto
  `V(m + n - 2j)` is a multiple of `cgProj`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Tensor intertwiners
  - A.1. Definition and closure properties
  - A.2. The Clebsch–Gordan projections
  - A.3. Restriction to the summands
  - A.4. Selection rule and uniqueness

## iv. References

- Mathlib, `Mathlib.Algebra.Lie.Sl2`.

## A. Tensor intertwiners

### A.1. Definition and closure properties

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsTensorIntertwiner
declarations.doc:
A linear map `V(m) ⊗ V(n) → V(p)` is a tensor intertwiner if it carries the diagonal raising,
lowering and weight operators on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` to those on `V(p)`.
declarations.statement:
structure IsTensorIntertwiner
    (φ : StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n →ₗ[K] StandardSl2Module K p) : Prop where
  comm_E : φ ∘ₗ tensorE m n = ρE ∘ₗ φ
  comm_F : φ ∘ₗ tensorF m n = ρF ∘ₗ φ
  comm_H : φ ∘ₗ tensorH m n = ρH ∘ₗ φ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsTensorIntertwiner.smul
declarations.doc: Scalar multiples of tensor intertwiners are tensor intertwiners.
declarations.statement: lemma smul (hφ : IsTensorIntertwiner φ) (c : K) : IsTensorIntertwiner (c • φ)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsTensorIntertwiner.add
declarations.doc: Sums of tensor intertwiners are tensor intertwiners.
declarations.statement:
lemma add (hφ : IsTensorIntertwiner φ) (hψ : IsTensorIntertwiner ψ) :
    IsTensorIntertwiner (φ + ψ)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.component_sumEnd
declarations.doc: The component of a direct sum commutes with a summand-wise endomorphism.
declarations.statement:
lemma component_sumEnd (A : ∀ j, Module.End K (CGSummand K m n j)) (j : Fin (min m n + 1))
    (y : CGSum K m n) :
    DirectSum.component K _ (CGSummand K m n) j (sumEnd A y) =
      A j (DirectSum.component K _ (CGSummand K m n) j y)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgProj
declarations.doc:
The projection of `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` onto the summand `V(m + n - 2j)` of the Clebsch–Gordan
decomposition.

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgProj_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma cgProj_apply (hmn : 0 < m + n) (j : Fin (min m n + 1))
    (x : StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n) :
    cgProj hmn j x = DirectSum.component K _ (CGSummand K m n) j (cgEquiv hmn x)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgProj_isTensorIntertwiner
declarations.doc: The projections are tensor intertwiners.
declarations.statement:
lemma cgProj_isTensorIntertwiner (hmn : 0 < m + n) (j : Fin (min m n + 1)) :
    IsTensorIntertwiner (cgProj (K := K) hmn j)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgProj_cgEquiv_symm_lof
declarations.doc:
The projection sends the preimage of the highest-weight vector of the `j`-th summand to that
vector; in particular it is not zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma cgProj_cgEquiv_symm_lof (hmn : 0 < m + n) (j : Fin (min m n + 1))
    (z : CGSummand K m n j) :
    cgProj hmn j ((cgEquiv hmn).symm (DirectSum.lof K _ (CGSummand K m n) j z)) = z

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgProj_ne_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma cgProj_ne_zero (hmn : 0 < m + n) (j : Fin (min m n + 1)) :
    cgProj (K := K) hmn j ≠ 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgEquiv_symm_sumEnd_E
declarations.statement:
lemma cgEquiv_symm_sumEnd_E (y : CGSum K m n) :
    (cgEquiv hmn).symm (sumEnd (fun _ => ρE) y) = tensorE m n ((cgEquiv hmn).symm y)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgEquiv_symm_sumEnd_F
declarations.statement:
lemma cgEquiv_symm_sumEnd_F (y : CGSum K m n) :
    (cgEquiv hmn).symm (sumEnd (fun _ => ρF) y) = tensorF m n ((cgEquiv hmn).symm y)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgEquiv_symm_sumEnd_H
declarations.statement:
lemma cgEquiv_symm_sumEnd_H (y : CGSum K m n) :
    (cgEquiv hmn).symm (sumEnd (fun _ => ρH) y) = tensorH m n ((cgEquiv hmn).symm y)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgRestrict
declarations.doc:
The restriction of a linear map on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` to the `j`-th summand of the
Clebsch–Gordan decomposition.
declarations.statement:
def cgRestrict
    (φ : StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n →ₗ[K] StandardSl2Module K p)
    (j : Fin (min m n + 1)) : CGSummand K m n j →ₗ[K] StandardSl2Module K p

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsTensorIntertwiner.cgRestrict_isIntertwiner
declarations.doc: The restriction of a tensor intertwiner to a summand is an intertwiner.
declarations.statement:
lemma cgRestrict_isIntertwiner (hφ : IsTensorIntertwiner φ) (j : Fin (min m n + 1)) :
    IsIntertwiner (cgRestrict hmn φ j)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsTensorIntertwiner.eq_of_cgRestrict_eq
declarations.doc: A linear map on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` is determined by its restrictions to the summands.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_of_cgRestrict_eq (hmn : 0 < m + n) {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module K M]
    {α β : StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n →ₗ[K] M}
    (h : ∀ j, α ∘ₗ (cgEquiv hmn).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ DirectSum.lof K _ (CGSummand K m n) j =
      β ∘ₗ (cgEquiv hmn).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ DirectSum.lof K _ (CGSummand K m n) j) :
    α = β

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsTensorIntertwiner.eq_zero_of_forall_ne
declarations.doc:
**Selection rule.** If `p` is not of the form `m + n - 2j` with `j ≤ min m n`, every tensor
intertwiner `V(m) ⊗ V(n) → V(p)` is zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_zero_of_forall_ne (hmn : 0 < m + n)
    {φ : StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n →ₗ[K] StandardSl2Module K p}
    (hφ : IsTensorIntertwiner φ) (hp : ∀ j : Fin (min m n + 1), m + n - 2 * (j : ℕ) ≠ p) :
    φ = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsTensorIntertwiner.exists_eq_smul_cgProj
declarations.doc:
Every tensor intertwiner onto the summand `V(m + n - 2j)` is a scalar multiple of the
projection `cgProj`.

modules.title: Weight spaces for sl₂ modules
modules.doc:
Restates the rank-one weight-space results using endomorphism eigenspaces.

## i. Overview

The eigenspaces of the Cartan operator are weight spaces. The raising and lowering
operators map them to neighboring weights. In a finite-dimensional irreducible module the
weights in a primitive string occur with multiplicity one, and the highest weight is unique.

## ii. Key results

- `weightSpace` defines the Cartan eigenspace.
- `e_mapsTo_weightSpace` and `f_mapsTo_weightSpace` shift weights by two.
- `weightSpace_finrank_le_one` and `weightSpace_highest_unique` express multiplicity one
  and uniqueness of the highest weight.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Weight spaces

## iv. References

- Mathlib, `Mathlib.Algebra.Lie.Sl2`.

## A. Weight spaces

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.weightSpace
declarations.doc: The eigenspace of the Cartan operator `h` with eigenvalue `n`.
declarations.statement: def weightSpace (_t : IsSl2Triple h e f) (n : K) : Submodule K M

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.e_mapsTo_weightSpace
declarations.doc: The raising operator maps weight `n` into weight `n + 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma e_mapsTo_weightSpace (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) (n : K) :
    ∀ v ∈ weightSpace (M := M) t n, LieModule.toEnd K L M e v ∈ weightSpace t (n + 2)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.f_mapsTo_weightSpace
declarations.doc: `f` lowers the weight by `2`. Dual to `e_mapsTo_weightSpace`.
declarations.statement:
lemma f_mapsTo_weightSpace (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) (n : K) :
    ∀ v ∈ weightSpace (M := M) t n, LieModule.toEnd K L M f v ∈ weightSpace t (n - 2)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.repr_apply_diag
declarations.doc: If a basis diagonalises `T`, then `T` multiplies the `i`-th coordinate by `μ i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma repr_apply_diag {ι : Type*} (b : Module.Basis ι K M) (T : Module.End K M)
    (μ : ι → K) (hT : ∀ j, T (b j) = μ j • b j) (i : ι) (w : M) :
    b.repr (T w) i = μ i * b.repr w i

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.string_coord_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A weight vector has vanishing string coordinates at every other weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma string_coord_eq_zero {n : K} {w : M} (hw : w ∈ weightSpace (M := M) t n)
    (i : Fin (N + 1)) (hi : (N : K) - 2 * (i : ℕ) ≠ n) : (stringBasis P).repr w i = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.weightSpace_eq_bot_of_ne
declarations.doc: The weight space is trivial at a value that is not a weight of the string.
declarations.statement:
lemma weightSpace_eq_bot_of_ne {n : K} (hn : ∀ i : Fin (N + 1), (N : K) - 2 * (i : ℕ) ≠ n) :
    weightSpace (M := M) t n = ⊥

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.weightSpace_finrank_le_one_of_eq
declarations.doc: The weight space of a weight of the string has dimension at most one.
declarations.statement:
lemma weightSpace_finrank_le_one_of_eq {n : K} (i₀ : Fin (N + 1))
    (hi₀ : (N : K) - 2 * (i₀ : ℕ) = n) : Module.finrank K (weightSpace (M := M) t n) ≤ 1

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.weightSpace_finrank_le_one
declarations.doc:
Every Cartan weight space of a finite-dimensional irreducible `sl₂` module has
dimension at most one. The lowering-string basis has pairwise distinct weights.
declarations.statement:
lemma weightSpace_finrank_le_one [IsAlgClosed K] [CharZero K] [FiniteDimensional K M]
    (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) [LieModule.IsIrreducible K ↥(t.toLieSubalgebra (R := K)) M]
    (n : K) : Module.finrank K (weightSpace (M := M) t n) ≤ 1

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.lie_e_eq_zero_of_top_weight
declarations.doc: A vector at a weight with empty weight space two steps above is killed by `e`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lie_e_eq_zero_of_top_weight {n : K} {v : M} (t : IsSl2Triple h e f)
    (hv : v ∈ weightSpace (M := M) t n) (hn : weightSpace (M := M) t (n + 2) = ⊥) :
    ⁅e, v⁆ = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.finrank_of_top_weight
declarations.doc: A top weight `p` of a finite-dimensional irreducible module fixes the dimension.
declarations.statement:
lemma finrank_of_top_weight [CharZero K] [FiniteDimensional K M]
    (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) [LieModule.IsIrreducible K ↥(t.toLieSubalgebra (R := K)) M]
    {p : ℕ} (hp : weightSpace (M := M) t (p : K) ≠ ⊥)
    (hp' : weightSpace (M := M) t ((p : K) + 2) = ⊥) : Module.finrank K M = p + 1

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.weightSpace_highest_unique
declarations.doc:
A nonzero weight space with no weight space two steps above it determines the
highest weight of a finite-dimensional irreducible module.
declarations.statement:
lemma weightSpace_highest_unique [CharZero K] [FiniteDimensional K M]
    (t : IsSl2Triple h e f) [LieModule.IsIrreducible K ↥(t.toLieSubalgebra (R := K)) M]
    {m n : ℕ} (hm : weightSpace (M := M) t (m : K) ≠ ⊥)
    (hm' : weightSpace (M := M) t ((m : K) + 2) = ⊥)
    (hn : weightSpace (M := M) t (n : K) ≠ ⊥)
    (hn' : weightSpace (M := M) t ((n : K) + 2) = ⊥) : m = n

modules.title: Generalised Laguerre polynomials
modules.doc:
The generalised Laguerre polynomials `L_N^(α)` for natural `N` and `α`, their differential
equation, their moments against `x^q e^(-x)` and the four weighted integrals of `L_N^(α)²` that
give the radial expectation values of the hydrogen atom.

## i. Overview

We define `L_N^(α)(x) = Σ_{i ≤ N} (-1)^i C(N + α, N - i) x^i / i!` as an explicit polynomial and
check the Laguerre equation `x L'' + (α + 1 - x) L' + N L = 0` coefficientwise.

The moments `Σ_i c_i (q + i)!` of the coefficients reduce, by the Chu–Vandermonde identity for
the generalised binomial coefficient `Ring.choose`, to `q! · C(N + α - q - 1, N)`. With Euler's
integral `∫₀^∞ x^q e^(-x) dx = q!` this evaluates

`∫₀^∞ x^e e^(-x) L_N^(α)(x)² dx`

for `e = α + 1, α, α - 1, α - 2`: the terms with large `i` vanish because the upper argument of
the binomial coefficient is a natural number below `N`, and the remaining ones are
`C(-1, N) = (-1)^N` and `C(-2, N) = (-1)^N (N + 1)`.

## ii. Key results

- `laguerre`: the polynomial `L_N^(α)`.
- `laguerre_ode`: the Laguerre differential equation.
- `sum_laguerreCoeff_mul_factorial`: the moment identity.
- `integral_laguerre_sq_alpha`: `∫ x^α e^(-x) L² = (N + α)!/N!`.
- `integral_laguerre_sq_alpha_add_one`: `∫ x^(α+1) e^(-x) L² = (N + α)!/N! · (2N + α + 1)`.
- `integral_laguerre_sq_alpha_sub_one`, `integral_laguerre_sq_alpha_sub_two`: the weights
  `x^(α-1)` and `x^(α-2)`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Definition and differential equation
- B. Moments
- C. Integrals

## iv. References

- NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, chapter 18, https://dlmf.nist.gov/18.
- H. A. Bethe and E. E. Salpeter, *Quantum Mechanics of One- and Two-Electron Atoms*, Springer
  (1957).

## A. Definition and differential equation

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.laguerreCoeff
declarations.doc: The coefficient `(-1)^i C(N + α, N - i) / i!` of `x^i` in `L_N^(α)`.
declarations.statement: def laguerreCoeff (N α i : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.laguerre
declarations.doc: The generalised Laguerre polynomial `L_N^(α)(x) = Σ_i (-1)^i C(N + α, N - i) x^i / i!`.
declarations.statement: def laguerre (N α : ℕ) : ℝ[X]

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.eval_laguerre
declarations.statement:
lemma eval_laguerre (x : ℝ) :
    (laguerre N α).eval x = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), laguerreCoeff N α i * x ^ i

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.eval_laguerre_zero
declarations.statement: lemma eval_laguerre_zero : (laguerre N α).eval 0 = ((N + α).choose N : ℝ)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.eval_derivative_laguerre
declarations.statement:
lemma eval_derivative_laguerre (x : ℝ) :
    (derivative (laguerre N α)).eval x =
      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), laguerreCoeff N α i * ((i : ℝ) * x ^ (i - 1))

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.eval_derivative_derivative_laguerre
declarations.statement:
lemma eval_derivative_derivative_laguerre (x : ℝ) :
    (derivative (derivative (laguerre N α))).eval x =
      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N + 1),
        laguerreCoeff N α i * ((i : ℝ) * ((i - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * x ^ (i - 1 - 1))

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.laguerreCoeff_succ_mul
declarations.doc: The two-term recursion of the coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma laguerreCoeff_succ_mul {i : ℕ} (hi : i < N) :
    laguerreCoeff N α (i + 1) * (((i : ℝ) + 1) * ((i : ℝ) + 1 + α)) =
      -((N : ℝ) - i) * laguerreCoeff N α i

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.laguerre_ode
declarations.doc: **Laguerre's differential equation** `x L'' + (α + 1 - x) L' + N L = 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma laguerre_ode (x : ℝ) :
    x * (derivative (derivative (laguerre N α))).eval x +
      ((α : ℝ) + 1 - x) * (derivative (laguerre N α)).eval x +
        (N : ℝ) * (laguerre N α).eval x = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.sum_choose_mul_choose_neg
declarations.doc:
`Σ_i (-1)^i C(N + α, N - i) C(q + i, i) = C(N + α - q - 1, N)`, the Chu–Vandermonde identity
with a negative upper index.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_choose_mul_choose_neg (q : ℕ) :
    ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), (-1 : ℤ) ^ i * ((N + α).choose (N - i) : ℤ) * ((q + i).choose i) =
      Ring.choose ((N + α : ℤ) - q - 1) N

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.sum_laguerreCoeff_mul_factorial
declarations.doc:
**Moments.** `Σ_i c_i (q + i)! = q! C(N + α - q - 1, N)`, the integral of `x^q e^(-x) L_N^(α)`
with the integer binomial coefficient `Ring.choose`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_laguerreCoeff_mul_factorial (q : ℕ) :
    ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), laguerreCoeff N α i * ((q + i).factorial : ℝ) =
      (q.factorial : ℝ) * ((Ring.choose ((N + α : ℤ) - q - 1) N : ℤ) : ℝ)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.ringChoose_natCast_of_lt
declarations.statement: lemma ringChoose_natCast_of_lt {t : ℕ} (h : t < N) : Ring.choose (t : ℤ) N = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.ringChoose_neg_one
declarations.statement: lemma ringChoose_neg_one : Ring.choose (-1 : ℤ) N = (-1) ^ N

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.ringChoose_neg_two
declarations.statement: lemma ringChoose_neg_two : Ring.choose (-2 : ℤ) N = (-1) ^ N * (N + 1)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.integrableOn_pow_mul_exp_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma integrableOn_pow_mul_exp_neg (q : ℕ) :
    IntegrableOn (fun x : ℝ => x ^ q * Real.exp (-x)) (Ioi 0)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.integral_pow_mul_exp_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_pow_mul_exp_neg (q : ℕ) :
    ∫ x in Ioi (0 : ℝ), x ^ q * Real.exp (-x) = q.factorial

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.integral_pow_mul_exp_neg_mul_laguerre_sq
declarations.doc: `∫₀^∞ x^e e^(-x) L(x)² dx = Σ_j c_j Σ_i c_i (e + j + i)!`.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_pow_mul_exp_neg_mul_laguerre_sq (e : ℕ) :
    ∫ x in Ioi (0 : ℝ), x ^ e * Real.exp (-x) * ((laguerre N α).eval x) ^ 2 =
      ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), laguerreCoeff N α j *
        ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), laguerreCoeff N α i * ((e + j + i).factorial : ℝ)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.integral_pow_mul_exp_neg_mul_laguerre_sq_eq
declarations.doc: The integrals through the moments.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_pow_mul_exp_neg_mul_laguerre_sq_eq (e : ℕ) :
    ∫ x in Ioi (0 : ℝ), x ^ e * Real.exp (-x) * ((laguerre N α).eval x) ^ 2 =
      ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), laguerreCoeff N α j * (((e + j).factorial : ℝ) *
        ((Ring.choose ((N + α : ℤ) - (e + j : ℕ) - 1) N : ℤ) : ℝ))

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.neg_one_pow_mul_self
declarations.statement: lemma neg_one_pow_mul_self (n : ℕ) : (-1 : ℝ) ^ n * (-1) ^ n = 1

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.integral_laguerre_sq_alpha
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_laguerre_sq_alpha :
    ∫ x in Ioi (0 : ℝ), x ^ α * Real.exp (-x) * ((laguerre N α).eval x) ^ 2 =
      ((N + α).factorial : ℝ) / N.factorial

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.integral_laguerre_sq_alpha_add_one
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_laguerre_sq_alpha_add_one :
    ∫ x in Ioi (0 : ℝ), x ^ (α + 1) * Real.exp (-x) * ((laguerre N α).eval x) ^ 2 =
      ((N + α).factorial : ℝ) / N.factorial * (2 * N + α + 1)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.integral_laguerre_sq_alpha_sub_one
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_laguerre_sq_alpha_sub_one (hα : 1 ≤ α) :
    ∫ x in Ioi (0 : ℝ), x ^ (α - 1) * Real.exp (-x) * ((laguerre N α).eval x) ^ 2 =
      ((N + α).factorial : ℝ) / (N.factorial * α)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.integral_laguerre_sq_alpha_sub_two
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_laguerre_sq_alpha_sub_two (hα : 2 ≤ α) :
    ∫ x in Ioi (0 : ℝ), x ^ (α - 2) * Real.exp (-x) * ((laguerre N α).eval x) ^ 2 =
      ((N + α).factorial : ℝ) * (2 * N + α + 1) /
        (N.factorial * (((α : ℝ) - 1) * α * (α + 1)))

modules.title: The sine propagation function `t ↦ sin (ω t) / ω`
modules.doc:
The function `sincPropagator t ω = sin (ω t) / ω` solves `u'' + ω² u = 0` with `u 0 = 0` and
`u' 0 = 1`.

## i. Overview

The function `sincPropagator t ω = sin (ω t) / ω` solves `u'' + ω² u = 0` with `u 0 = 0` and
`u' 0 = 1`. It is the time dependence of every free wave with frequency `ω`.
Writing it as `t * sinc (ω t)` removes the case `ω = 0`, where it equals `t`.
Together with the cosine it forms the one-parameter group of the harmonic oscillator.
The group law is proved in `Exponential.lean` from the exponential of the generator.

## ii. Key results

- `sincPropagator` : The function `sin (ω t) / ω`, with the value `t` at `ω = 0`.
- `sincPropagator_zero_left`
- `sincPropagator_zero_right`
- `sincPropagator_eq_sin_div`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The sine propagation function `t ↦ sin (ω t) / ω`
- B. Equivalent forms of the sine propagation function

## iv. References

None.

## A. The sine propagation function `t ↦ sin (ω t) / ω`

- `sincPropagator` : The function `sin (ω t) / ω`, with the value `t` at `ω = 0`.

Lemmas: `sincPropagator_zero_left`, `sincPropagator_zero_right`, `sincPropagator_eq_sin_div`,
`sincPropagator_neg_left`, `abs_sincPropagator_le`, `hasDerivAt_sincPropagator`,
`hasDerivAt_cos_mul`, `continuous_sincPropagator`.

## B. Equivalent forms of the sine propagation function

Lemmas: `sinc_abs`, `sincPropagator_eq_mul_sincSqrt`.

declarations.name: Real.sincPropagator
declarations.doc: The function `sin (ω t) / ω`, with the value `t` at `ω = 0`.
declarations.statement: def sincPropagator (t ω : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: Real.sincPropagator_zero_left
declarations.statement: lemma sincPropagator_zero_left (ω : ℝ) : sincPropagator 0 ω = 0

declarations.name: Real.sincPropagator_zero_right
declarations.statement: lemma sincPropagator_zero_right (t : ℝ) : sincPropagator t 0 = t

declarations.name: Real.sincPropagator_eq_sin_div
declarations.statement:
lemma sincPropagator_eq_sin_div {ω : ℝ} (hω : ω ≠ 0) (t : ℝ) :
    sincPropagator t ω = sin (ω * t) / ω

declarations.name: Real.sincPropagator_neg_left
declarations.statement: lemma sincPropagator_neg_left (t ω : ℝ) : sincPropagator (-t) ω = - sincPropagator t ω

declarations.name: Real.abs_sincPropagator_le
declarations.statement: lemma abs_sincPropagator_le (t ω : ℝ) : |sincPropagator t ω| ≤ |t|

declarations.name: Real.hasDerivAt_sincPropagator
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_sincPropagator (ω t : ℝ) : HasDerivAt (fun s => sincPropagator s ω) (cos (ω * t))
    t

declarations.name: Real.hasDerivAt_cos_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_cos_mul (ω t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun s => cos (ω * s)) (-ω ^ 2 * sincPropagator t ω) t

declarations.name: Real.continuous_sincPropagator
declarations.statement: lemma continuous_sincPropagator : Continuous fun p : ℝ × ℝ => sincPropagator p.1 p.2

declarations.name: Real.sinc_abs
declarations.statement: lemma sinc_abs (x : ℝ) : sinc |x| = sinc x

declarations.name: Real.sincPropagator_eq_mul_sincSqrt
declarations.statement:
lemma sincPropagator_eq_mul_sincSqrt (t ω : ℝ) :
    sincPropagator t ω = t * sincSqrt (t ^ 2 * ω ^ 2)

modules.title: The Bessel function `J₀` and the massive sine propagation function on the line
modules.doc:
The sine propagation function with mass is the cosine transform of the Bessel kernel on the
interval `[-r, r]`.

## i. Overview

The Bessel function `J₀` is defined by its power series. The kernel `½ J₀ (m √(r² - u²))` on the
interval `[-r, r]` has the cosine transform `sin (r √(k² + m²)) / √(k² + m²)`. This is the retarded
Green function of the Klein–Gordon equation in one space dimension. The proof expands both sides in
power series in `m²`. The moments of `(1 - s²)ⁿ` are computed by a recurrence. The derivative of
the series in `y = z²` is expressed by the Bessel function `J₁`.

## ii. Key results

- `moment_eq` : the moments of `(1 - s²)ⁿ`.
- `besselSq` : `J₀ (√y)` as a power series in `y`.
- `integral_besselSq_cos` : the cosine transform of the Bessel kernel.
- `besselJ1` : the Bessel function `J₁`.
- `mul_besselSqDeriv_eq_besselJ1` : the tail of the Green function in terms of `J₁`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Moments
- B. The Bessel series
- C. The cosine transform
- D. The derivative and `J₁`

## iv. References

None.

## A. Moments

- `moment_eq` : the moments of `(1 - s²)ⁿ`.
- `moment_scaled` : the moments of `(r² - u²)ⁿ` on `[-r, r]`.

## B. The Bessel series

- `besselSq` : `J₀ (√y)` as a power series in `y`.
- `continuousOn_besselSq` : the Bessel series is continuous on bounded sets.

## C. The cosine transform

- `hasSum_integral_besselSq_cos` : the cosine transform as a double series.
- `hasSum_integral_besselSq_cos_series` : the cosine transform as a series in `k² + M`.
- `integral_besselSq_cos` : the cosine transform of the Bessel kernel.

## D. The derivative and `J₁`

- `besselSqDeriv` : the derivative of the Bessel series.
- `hasDerivAt_besselSq` : the derivative of the Bessel series.
- `besselJ1` : the Bessel function `J₁`.
- `besselSqDeriv_sq` : the derivative at `z²` in terms of `J₁`.
- `mul_besselSqDeriv_eq_besselJ1` : the tail of the Green function in terms of `J₁`.

declarations.name: Real.momentFormula
declarations.doc: The closed form of the moments of `(1 - s²)ⁿ`.
declarations.statement: def momentFormula (n j : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: Real.momentFormula_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma momentFormula_succ (n j : ℕ) :
    momentFormula (n + 1) j = momentFormula n j - momentFormula n (j + 1)

declarations.name: Real.moment_eq
declarations.doc: The moments of `(1 - s²)ⁿ` on `[-1, 1]`.
declarations.statement:
lemma moment_eq (n j : ℕ) :
    ∫ s in (-1 : ℝ)..1, (1 - s ^ 2) ^ n * s ^ (2 * j) = momentFormula n j

declarations.name: Real.besselSq
declarations.doc: `J₀ (√y)` as a power series in `y`: `∑ (-y / 4)ⁿ / (n !)²`.
declarations.statement: def besselSq (y : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: Real.summable_pow_div_factorial_sq
declarations.statement: lemma summable_pow_div_factorial_sq (a : ℝ) : Summable fun n : ℕ => a ^ n / (n ! : ℝ) ^ 2

declarations.name: Real.summable_even_pow_div_factorial
declarations.statement:
lemma summable_even_pow_div_factorial (x : ℝ) :
    Summable fun j : ℕ => x ^ (2 * j) / ((2 * j) ! : ℝ)

declarations.name: Real.hasSum_besselSq
declarations.statement: lemma hasSum_besselSq (y : ℝ) : HasSum (fun n : ℕ => (-y / 4) ^ n / (n ! : ℝ) ^ 2) (besselSq y)

declarations.name: Real.moment_scaled
declarations.doc: The moments of `(r² - u²)ⁿ` on `[-r, r]`.
declarations.statement:
lemma moment_scaled {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (n j : ℕ) :
    ∫ u in (-r)..r, (r ^ 2 - u ^ 2) ^ n * u ^ (2 * j) =
      r ^ (2 * n + 2 * j + 1) * momentFormula n j

declarations.name: Real.hasSum_integral_besselSq_cos
declarations.doc: The cosine transform of the Bessel kernel as a double series.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasSum_integral_besselSq_cos {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (k M : ℝ) :
    HasSum (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => (-M / 4) ^ p.1 / (p.1 ! : ℝ) ^ 2 *
      ((-1) ^ p.2 * k ^ (2 * p.2) / ((2 * p.2) ! : ℝ)) *
        (r ^ (2 * p.1 + 2 * p.2 + 1) * momentFormula p.1 p.2))
      (∫ u in (-r)..r, besselSq (M * (r ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) * Real.cos (k * u))

declarations.name: Real.coeff_eq
declarations.doc: The coefficient of the double series, simplified.

declarations.name: Real.hasSum_integral_besselSq_cos_series
declarations.doc: **The cosine transform of the Bessel kernel as a series in the frequency squared.**
declarations.statement:
lemma hasSum_integral_besselSq_cos_series {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (k M : ℝ) :
    HasSum (fun N : ℕ => 2 * ((-1) ^ N * (k ^ 2 + M) ^ N * r ^ (2 * N + 1) /
      ((2 * N + 1) ! : ℝ)))
      (∫ u in (-r)..r, besselSq (M * (r ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) * Real.cos (k * u))

declarations.name: Real.hasSum_sincPropagator_series
declarations.doc: The sine propagation function as a power series in the frequency squared.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasSum_sincPropagator_series (r a : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ a) :
    HasSum (fun N : ℕ => (-1) ^ N * a ^ N * r ^ (2 * N + 1) / ((2 * N + 1) ! : ℝ))
      (Real.sincPropagator r (Real.sqrt a))

declarations.name: Real.integral_besselSq_cos
declarations.doc:
**The cosine transform of the Bessel kernel.** For `r ≥ 0` and `k² + M ≥ 0`
`∫_{-r}^{r} J₀ (√M √(r² - u²)) cos (k u) du = 2 sin (r √(k² + M)) / √(k² + M)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_besselSq_cos {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (k M : ℝ) (h : 0 ≤ k ^ 2 + M) :
    ∫ u in (-r)..r, besselSq (M * (r ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) * Real.cos (k * u) =
      2 * Real.sincPropagator r (Real.sqrt (k ^ 2 + M))

declarations.name: Real.continuousOn_besselSq
declarations.doc: The Bessel series is continuous on bounded sets.
declarations.statement: lemma continuousOn_besselSq (R : ℝ) : ContinuousOn besselSq (Set.Icc (-R) R)

declarations.name: Real.besselSqDeriv
declarations.doc: The termwise derivative of the Bessel series.
declarations.statement: def besselSqDeriv (y : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: Real.summable_besselSqDeriv_bound
declarations.statement:
lemma summable_besselSqDeriv_bound (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ a) :
    Summable fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) * (1 / 4) * a ^ (n - 1) / (n ! : ℝ) ^ 2

declarations.name: Real.hasDerivAt_besselSq
declarations.doc: **The derivative of the Bessel series.**
declarations.statement: lemma hasDerivAt_besselSq (y : ℝ) : HasDerivAt besselSq (besselSqDeriv y) y

declarations.name: Real.continuous_besselSqDeriv
declarations.statement: lemma continuous_besselSqDeriv : Continuous besselSqDeriv

declarations.name: Real.besselJ1
declarations.doc: The Bessel function `J₁` by its power series.
declarations.statement: def besselJ1 (z : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: Real.summable_besselSqDeriv
declarations.statement:
lemma summable_besselSqDeriv (y : ℝ) :
    Summable fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) * (-1 / 4) * (-y / 4) ^ (n - 1) / (n ! : ℝ) ^ 2

declarations.name: Real.besselSqDeriv_sq
declarations.doc: The derivative of the Bessel series is `-J₁ (z) / (2 z)` at `y = z²`.
declarations.statement: lemma besselSqDeriv_sq {z : ℝ} (hz : z ≠ 0) : besselSqDeriv (z ^ 2) = -besselJ1 z / (2 * z)

declarations.name: Real.continuous_besselSq
declarations.statement: lemma continuous_besselSq : Continuous besselSq

declarations.name: Real.besselSq_zero
declarations.statement: lemma besselSq_zero : besselSq 0 = 1

declarations.name: Real.mul_besselSqDeriv_eq_besselJ1
declarations.doc:
**The Bessel tail in terms of `J₁`.** For `|u| < τ` the derivative of the Bessel series at
`m² (τ² - u²)` is `J₁ (m √(τ² - u²)) / √(τ² - u²)` up to the factor `-1 / (2 m)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_besselSqDeriv_eq_besselJ1 {m τ u : ℝ} (hm : m ≠ 0) (hu : |u| < τ) (c : ℝ) :
    2 * m ^ 2 * (c * besselSqDeriv (m ^ 2 * (τ ^ 2 - u ^ 2))) =
      -(m * (c * (besselJ1 (m * Real.sqrt (τ ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) / Real.sqrt (τ ^ 2 - u ^ 2))))

modules.title: The Laplace transform of the sine propagation function
modules.doc:
The transform of `t ↦ sin (ω t) / ω` over the positive half line is `1 / (ω² - z²)`.

## i. Overview

The retarded Green function of the oscillator is the sine propagation function on the positive
half line. Its Fourier transform in time exists for frequencies in the upper half plane. It
equals `1 / (ω² - z²)`. The value at `ω = 0` is the transform of the identity function.

## ii. Key results

- `integral_exp_mul_sincPropagator` : the transform for a nonzero frequency.
- `integral_exp_mul_sincPropagator_zero` : the transform for zero frequency.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The transform

## iv. References

None.

## A. The transform

- `integral_exp_mul_sincPropagator` : the transform for a nonzero frequency.

declarations.name: Real.integral_exp_mul_sincPropagator
declarations.doc: The Laplace transform of the sine propagation function for a nonzero frequency.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_exp_mul_sincPropagator {ω : ℝ} (hω : ω ≠ 0) {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) :
    ∫ t in Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ), Complex.exp (I * z * t) * (t.sincPropagator ω : ℂ) =
      1 / ((ω : ℂ) ^ 2 - z ^ 2)

declarations.name: Real.integral_exp_mul_sincPropagator_zero
declarations.doc: The Laplace transform of the sine propagation function at zero frequency.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_exp_mul_sincPropagator_zero {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) :
    ∫ t in Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ), Complex.exp (I * z * t) * (t.sincPropagator 0 : ℂ) =
      1 / ((0 : ℂ) ^ 2 - z ^ 2)

declarations.name: Real.integral_exp_mul_sincPropagator_all
declarations.doc: The Laplace transform of the sine propagation function for every frequency.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_exp_mul_sincPropagator_all (ω : ℝ) {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) :
    ∫ t in Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ), Complex.exp (I * z * t) * (t.sincPropagator ω : ℂ) =
      1 / ((ω : ℂ) ^ 2 - z ^ 2)

modules.title: The harmonic oscillator
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The matrix exponential of the generator and the Duhamel formula for the oscillator with a source.

## ii. Key results

- `generator` : The generator `[[0, 1], [-ω², 0]]` of the free evolution of Cauchy data at frequency
  `ω`.
- `evolutionMatrix` : The evolution matrix of the Cauchy data at frequency `ω` over the time `t`.
- `duhamelOsc` : The retarded solution of `u'' + ω² u = G` with zero data at the time `a`.
- `duhamelOscCos` : The derivative of `duhamelOsc`: the same integral with the cosine kernel.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The exponential of the Klein–Gordon generator
- B. Duhamel's formula for the harmonic oscillator

## iv. References

None.

## A. The exponential of the Klein–Gordon generator

- `generator` : The generator `[[0, 1], [-ω², 0]]` of the free evolution of Cauchy data at frequency
  `ω`.
- `evolutionMatrix` : The evolution matrix of the Cauchy data at frequency `ω` over the time `t`.

Lemmas: `generator_sq`, `generator_pow_even`, `generator_pow_odd`, `hasSum_sincPropagator`,
`hasSum_exp_generator`, `evolutionMatrix_eq`, `exp_generator`, `evolutionMatrix_add`,
`sincPropagator_add`, `cos_mul_add`.

## B. Duhamel's formula for the harmonic oscillator

- `duhamelOsc` : The retarded solution of `u'' + ω² u = G` with zero data at the time `a`.
- `duhamelOscCos` : The derivative of `duhamelOsc`: the same integral with the cosine kernel.

Lemmas: `sincPropagator_sub_split`, `cos_sub_split`, `cos_sq_add_sq_mul`,
`continuous_sincPropagator_smul`, `continuous_cos_smul`, `duhamelOsc_eq`, `duhamelOscCos_eq`,
`hasDerivAt_cosIntegral`, `hasDerivAt_sinIntegral`, `hasDerivAt_duhamelOsc` and more.

declarations.name: SincPropagator.generator
declarations.doc: The generator `[[0, 1], [-ω², 0]]` of the free evolution of Cauchy data at frequency `ω`.
declarations.statement: def generator (ω : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ

declarations.name: SincPropagator.generator_sq
declarations.statement:
lemma generator_sq (ω : ℝ) : generator ω ^ 2 = (-((ω ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ)) • (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2)
    ℂ)

declarations.name: SincPropagator.generator_pow_even
declarations.statement:
lemma generator_pow_even (ω : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    generator ω ^ (2 * n) = (-((ω ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ)) ^ n • (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)

declarations.name: SincPropagator.generator_pow_odd
declarations.statement:
lemma generator_pow_odd (ω : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    generator ω ^ (2 * n + 1) = (-((ω ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ)) ^ n • generator ω

declarations.name: SincPropagator.hasSum_sincPropagator
declarations.doc: The series of `sincPropagator`, as a convergent sum.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasSum_sincPropagator (t ω : ℝ) :
    HasSum (fun n : ℕ => (-1) ^ n * t ^ (2 * n + 1) * ω ^ (2 * n) / (2 * n + 1)!)
      (sincPropagator t ω)

declarations.name: SincPropagator.hasSum_exp_generator
declarations.statement:
lemma hasSum_exp_generator (t ω : ℝ) :
    HasSum (fun n : ℕ => ((n ! : ℂ)⁻¹) • ((t : ℂ) • generator ω) ^ n)
      (((cos (ω * t) : ℝ) : ℂ) • (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) +
        ((sincPropagator t ω : ℝ) : ℂ) • generator ω)

declarations.name: SincPropagator.evolutionMatrix
declarations.doc: The evolution matrix of the Cauchy data at frequency `ω` over the time `t`.
declarations.statement: def evolutionMatrix (t ω : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ

declarations.name: SincPropagator.evolutionMatrix_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma evolutionMatrix_eq (t ω : ℝ) :
    evolutionMatrix t ω = ((cos (ω * t) : ℝ) : ℂ) • (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) +
      ((sincPropagator t ω : ℝ) : ℂ) • generator ω

declarations.name: SincPropagator.exp_generator
declarations.doc: The exponential of the generator is the evolution matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma exp_generator (t ω : ℝ) :
    exp ((t : ℂ) • generator ω) = evolutionMatrix t ω

declarations.name: SincPropagator.evolutionMatrix_add
declarations.doc:
The group law of the evolution matrix, from `exp (A + B) = exp A * exp B` for commuting
`A` and `B`.
declarations.statement:
lemma evolutionMatrix_add (s t ω : ℝ) :
    evolutionMatrix (s + t) ω = evolutionMatrix s ω * evolutionMatrix t ω

declarations.name: Real.sincPropagator_add
declarations.doc: The addition law of `sincPropagator`, read off from the entry `(0, 1)` of the group law.
declarations.statement:
lemma sincPropagator_add (s t ω : ℝ) :
    sincPropagator (s + t) ω =
      cos (ω * s) * sincPropagator t ω + sincPropagator s ω * cos (ω * t)

declarations.name: Real.cos_mul_add
declarations.doc: The addition law of the cosine, read off from the entry `(0, 0)` of the group law.
declarations.statement:
lemma cos_mul_add (s t ω : ℝ) :
    cos (ω * (s + t)) =
      cos (ω * s) * cos (ω * t) - ω ^ 2 * sincPropagator s ω * sincPropagator t ω

declarations.name: Real.duhamelOsc
declarations.doc: The retarded solution of `u'' + ω² u = G` with zero data at the time `a`.
declarations.statement: def duhamelOsc (ω a : ℝ) (G : ℝ → V) (t : ℝ) : V

declarations.name: Real.duhamelOscCos
declarations.doc: The derivative of `duhamelOsc`: the same integral with the cosine kernel.
declarations.statement: def duhamelOscCos (ω a : ℝ) (G : ℝ → V) (t : ℝ) : V

declarations.name: Real.sincPropagator_sub_split
declarations.statement:
lemma sincPropagator_sub_split (ω t s : ℝ) :
    sincPropagator (t - s) ω =
      sincPropagator t ω * cos (ω * s) - cos (ω * t) * sincPropagator s ω

declarations.name: Real.cos_sub_split
declarations.statement:
lemma cos_sub_split (ω t s : ℝ) :
    cos (ω * (t - s)) =
      cos (ω * t) * cos (ω * s) + ω ^ 2 * sincPropagator t ω * sincPropagator s ω

declarations.name: Real.cos_sq_add_sq_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma cos_sq_add_sq_mul (ω t : ℝ) :
    cos (ω * t) ^ 2 + ω ^ 2 * sincPropagator t ω ^ 2 = 1

declarations.name: Real.continuous_sincPropagator_smul
declarations.statement: lemma continuous_sincPropagator_smul : Continuous fun s => sincPropagator s ω • G s

declarations.name: Real.continuous_cos_smul
declarations.statement: lemma continuous_cos_smul : Continuous fun s => cos (ω * s) • G s

declarations.name: Real.duhamelOsc_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma duhamelOsc_eq (t : ℝ) :
    duhamelOsc ω a G t =
      sincPropagator t ω • (∫ s in a..t, cos (ω * s) • G s) -
        cos (ω * t) • (∫ s in a..t, sincPropagator s ω • G s)

declarations.name: Real.duhamelOscCos_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma duhamelOscCos_eq (t : ℝ) :
    duhamelOscCos ω a G t =
      cos (ω * t) • (∫ s in a..t, cos (ω * s) • G s) +
        (ω ^ 2 * sincPropagator t ω) • (∫ s in a..t, sincPropagator s ω • G s)

declarations.name: Real.hasDerivAt_cosIntegral
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_cosIntegral (t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun u => ∫ s in a..u, cos (ω * s) • G s) (cos (ω * t) • G t) t

declarations.name: Real.hasDerivAt_sinIntegral
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_sinIntegral (t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun u => ∫ s in a..u, sincPropagator s ω • G s) (sincPropagator t ω • G t) t

declarations.name: Real.hasDerivAt_duhamelOsc
declarations.doc: The derivative of the retarded oscillator solution is the cosine Duhamel integral.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_duhamelOsc (t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (duhamelOsc ω a G) (duhamelOscCos ω a G t) t

declarations.name: Real.hasDerivAt_duhamelOscCos
declarations.doc: The second derivative: the force minus `ω²` times the solution.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_duhamelOscCos (t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (duhamelOscCos ω a G) (G t - ω ^ 2 • duhamelOsc ω a G t) t

declarations.name: Real.duhamelOsc_operator
declarations.doc: The oscillator Green kernel recovers a twice differentiable field up to its initial data.
declarations.statement:
lemma duhamelOsc_operator {g g' g'' : ℝ → V}
    (hg : ∀ s, HasDerivAt g (g' s) s) (hg' : ∀ s, HasDerivAt g' (g'' s) s)
    (hg'' : Continuous g'') (ω a t : ℝ) :
    duhamelOsc ω a (fun s => g'' s + ω ^ 2 • g s) t =
      g t - (cos (ω * (t - a)) • g a + sincPropagator (t - a) ω • g' a)

declarations.name: Real.duhamelOsc_operator_of_initial_zero
declarations.doc: The retarded oscillator Green operator is a left inverse on fields with zero initial data.
declarations.statement:
lemma duhamelOsc_operator_of_initial_zero {g g' g'' : ℝ → V}
    (hg : ∀ s, HasDerivAt g (g' s) s) (hg' : ∀ s, HasDerivAt g' (g'' s) s)
    (hg'' : Continuous g'') (ω a t : ℝ) (hga : g a = 0) (hg'a : g' a = 0) :
    duhamelOsc ω a (fun s => g'' s + ω ^ 2 • g s) t = g t

modules.title: Resolvent estimates for the sine propagation function
modules.doc:
The damped time integral of the sine propagation function is a resolvent in the frequency.

## i. Overview

The Laplace transform of the sine propagation function is `1 / (ω² - z²)`. Fourier inversion turns
the damped time integral against a Schwartz function into an integral over the frequency. The
resolvent `1 / (A - (b + i ε)²)` is bounded by `2 / ε²` for `A ≥ 0`. It is bounded by `2 / δ`
when `A` stays at distance `δ` from `b²`.

## ii. Key results

- `Real.integral_damped_sincPropagator` : the damped time integral as a frequency integral.
- `Real.norm_resolvent_le_two_div` : the bound `2 / ε²` for every nonnegative `A`.
- `Real.norm_resolvent_le` : the bound `2 / δ` away from the shell.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Bounds of the resolvent
- B. The damped time integral

## iv. References

None.

## A. Bounds of the resolvent

- `Real.half_sq_le_norm_den` : the denominator is at least `ε² / 2`.
- `Real.norm_resolvent_le_two_div` : the bound `2 / ε²` for every nonnegative `A`.
- `Real.norm_resolvent_le` : the bound `2 / δ` away from the shell.

## B. The damped time integral

- `Real.integral_damped_sincPropagator` : the damped time integral as a frequency integral.

declarations.name: Real.half_sq_le_norm_den
declarations.doc: The denominator of the resolvent is bounded away from zero by `ε² / 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma half_sq_le_norm_den {A : ℝ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (b : ℝ) :
    ε ^ 2 / 2 ≤ ‖(A : ℂ) - (b + ε * Complex.I) ^ 2‖

declarations.name: Real.norm_resolvent_le_two_div
declarations.doc: The resolvent is bounded by `2 / ε²` for every frequency.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_resolvent_le_two_div {A : ℝ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (b : ℝ) :
    ‖(1 : ℂ) / ((A : ℂ) - (b + ε * Complex.I) ^ 2)‖ ≤ 2 / ε ^ 2

declarations.name: Real.norm_resolvent_le
declarations.doc: The resolvent stays bounded away from the mass shell.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_resolvent_le {A w ε δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ) (hε0 : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1)
    (hεδ : ε ≤ δ / 2) (h : δ ≤ |A - (2 * Real.pi * w) ^ 2|) :
    ‖(1 : ℂ) / ((A : ℂ) - (2 * Real.pi * w + ε * Complex.I) ^ 2)‖ ≤ 2 / δ

declarations.name: Real.integral_damped_sincPropagator
declarations.doc:
**Damped time integral.** The Fourier inversion and the Laplace transform of the sine
propagation function turn the damped time integral into an integral over the frequency.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_damped_sincPropagator {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (w₀ : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) :
    ∫ s in Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ), (Real.exp (-(ε * s)) : ℂ) * ((s.sincPropagator w₀ : ℂ) * g s) =
      ∫ w : ℝ, 𝓕 g w * (1 / ((w₀ : ℂ) ^ 2 - (2 * Real.pi * w + ε * Complex.I) ^ 2))

modules.title: `cos √y` and `sinc √y` as entire functions
modules.doc:
The functions `cos √y` and `sinc √y` are even in `√y`.

## i. Overview

The functions `cos √y` and `sinc √y` are even in `√y`. They are therefore power series in `y` with
infinite radius, and smooth on all of `ℝ` although `√` is not differentiable at `0`.
This file defines them by their series and proves that they are smooth.
It then proves that every derivative is bounded by `2⁻ʲ` on `[0, ∞)`.

## ii. Key results

- `sqrtCoeff` : coefficients `(-1)ⁿ / (2n + k)!`
- `cosSqrt` : `cos √y` as an entire function of `y`.
- `sincSqrt` : `sinc √y` as an entire function of `y`.
- `abs_iteratedDeriv_le` : All derivatives of `cos √y` and `sinc √y` are bounded by `2⁻ʲ` on
  `[0, ∞)`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. `cos √y` and `sinc √y` as entire functions

## iv. References

None.

## A. `cos √y` and `sinc √y` as entire functions

- `sqrtCoeff` : coefficients `(-1)ⁿ / (2n + k)!`
- `cosSqrt` : `cos √y` as an entire function of `y`.
- `sincSqrt` : `sinc √y` as an entire function of `y`.

Lemmas: `radius_sqrtCoeff`, `cosSqrt_eq_sum`, `sincSqrt_eq_sum`, `analyticOnNhd_sqrtSum`,
`contDiff_cosSqrt`, `contDiff_sincSqrt`, `sqrt_pow_two_mul`, `cosSqrt_of_nonneg`,
`sincSqrt_of_nonneg`, `analyticOnNhd_cosSqrt` and more.

declarations.statement: def sqrtCoeff (k n : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.statement:

    HasDerivAt cosSqrt (-(1 / 2) * sincSqrt y) y

declarations.statement: lemma deriv_cosSqrt : deriv cosSqrt = fun y => -(1 / 2) * sincSqrt y

    cosSqrt y = sincSqrt y + 2 * y * deriv sincSqrt y

lemma hasDerivAt_integral_scale {G : ℝ → ℝ} (hG : ContDiff ℝ 1 G) (k : ℕ) (y : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun y => ∫ u in (0:ℝ)..1, u ^ k * G (u ^ 2 * y))
      (∫ u in (0:ℝ)..1, u ^ (k + 2) * deriv G (u ^ 2 * y)) y

    cosSqrt y = sincSqrt y + 2 * y * deriv sincSqrt y

declarations.name: Real.sincSqrt_eq_integral
declarations.doc: `sinc √y` is the mean of `cos √(u² y)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sincSqrt_eq_integral (y : ℝ) :
    sincSqrt y = ∫ u in (0:ℝ)..1, cosSqrt (u ^ 2 * y)

declarations.name: Real.iteratedDeriv_succ_cosSqrt
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_succ_cosSqrt (j : ℕ) :
    iteratedDeriv (j + 1) cosSqrt = fun y => -(1 / 2) * iteratedDeriv j sincSqrt y

declarations.name: Real.contDiff_iteratedDeriv_cosSqrt
declarations.statement: lemma contDiff_iteratedDeriv_cosSqrt (j : ℕ) : ContDiff ℝ 1 (iteratedDeriv j cosSqrt)

declarations.name: Real.iteratedDeriv_sincSqrt
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_sincSqrt (j : ℕ) :
    iteratedDeriv j sincSqrt = fun y => ∫ u in (0:ℝ)..1, u ^ (2 * j) * iteratedDeriv j cosSqrt (u ^
      2 * y)

declarations.name: Real.abs_iteratedDeriv_le
declarations.doc: All derivatives of `cos √y` and `sinc √y` are bounded by `2⁻ʲ` on `[0, ∞)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_iteratedDeriv_le (j : ℕ) {y : ℝ} (hy : 0 ≤ y) :
    |iteratedDeriv j cosSqrt y| ≤ (1 / 2) ^ j ∧ |iteratedDeriv j sincSqrt y| ≤ (1 / 2) ^ j

modules.title: Walsh characters
modules.doc:
The Walsh characters on `Fin n → Fin 2` and the orthonormal basis of rescaled Walsh vectors.

## i. Overview

For `x z : Fin n → Fin 2` the Walsh character `walsh x z = ∏ i, (-1) ^ (x i * z i)` is the
additive character `z ↦ (-1) ^ (x ⬝ z)` of `(ZMod 2)ⁿ`. The orthogonality relation
`sum_walsh_mul_walsh` is the explicit form of the orthogonality of characters of a finite
abelian group, which Mathlib states as `AddChar.wInner_cWeight_eq_boole`. We work with the
explicit `Fin 2`-indexed form because `Fin n → Fin 2` is what indexes the computational basis
of `n` qubits. The matrix `Matrix.of walsh`, with entries `(-1) ^ (x ⬝ z)`, is the Sylvester
Hadamard matrix of order `2 ^ n` in the sense of Mathlib's `Matrix.IsHadamard`.

Rescaling by `(√(2 ^ n))⁻¹`, the vectors `z ↦ (√(2 ^ n))⁻¹ * walsh x z` form an orthonormal
basis `walshBasis n` of `EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n → Fin 2)`, and Parseval's identity for this
basis is `sum_norm_sq_sum_mul_inv_sqrt_mul_walsh`.

## ii. Key results

- `walshSign` : the sign `(-1) ^ (j * k)` on `Fin 2`.
- `walsh` : the Walsh character on `Fin n → Fin 2`.
- `sum_walsh_mul_walsh` : orthogonality of the Walsh characters.
- `walshBasis` : the orthonormal basis of rescaled Walsh vectors.
- `sum_norm_sq_sum_mul_inv_sqrt_mul_walsh` : Parseval's identity for the rescaled Walsh vectors.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Signs on `Fin 2`
- B. Walsh characters
- C. The Walsh basis
  - C.1. Rescaled Walsh vectors
  - C.2. The orthonormal basis
  - C.3. Parseval's identity

## iv. References

- M. F. Pusey, J. Barrett and T. Rudolph, *On the reality of the quantum state*,
  Nature Phys. 8, 475–478 (2012), arXiv:1111.3328. [ref: Pusey:2011de]

sections.text:
## C. The Walsh basis

### C.1. Rescaled Walsh vectors

declarations.name: walshSign
declarations.doc: The sign `(-1) ^ (j * k)` for `j k : Fin 2`, as a complex number.
declarations.statement: def walshSign (j k : Fin 2) : ℂ

declarations.name: walshSign_zero_left
declarations.doc: The sign `walshSign 0 k` is `1`.
declarations.statement: lemma walshSign_zero_left (k : Fin 2) : walshSign 0 k = 1

declarations.name: walshSign_zero_right
declarations.doc: The sign `walshSign j 0` is `1`.
declarations.statement: lemma walshSign_zero_right (j : Fin 2) : walshSign j 0 = 1

declarations.statement: lemma walshSign_one_one : walshSign 1 1 = -1

declarations.doc: The sign `(-1) ^ (j * k)` is symmetric in `j` and `k`.
declarations.statement: lemma walshSign_comm (j k : Fin 2) : walshSign j k = walshSign k j

declarations.name: walshSign_mul_self
declarations.doc: A sign squares to one.
declarations.statement: lemma walshSign_mul_self (j k : Fin 2) : walshSign j k * walshSign j k = 1

declarations.name: conj_walshSign
declarations.doc: A sign equals its complex conjugate.
declarations.statement: lemma conj_walshSign (j k : Fin 2) : starRingEnd ℂ (walshSign j k) = walshSign j k

declarations.name: norm_walshSign
declarations.doc: A sign has unit norm.
declarations.statement: lemma norm_walshSign (j k : Fin 2) : ‖walshSign j k‖ = 1

declarations.name: sum_walshSign_mul_walshSign
declarations.doc: Orthogonality of the signs on `Fin 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_walshSign_mul_walshSign (a b : Fin 2) :
    ∑ k, walshSign a k * walshSign b k = if a = b then 2 else 0

declarations.name: walsh
declarations.doc: The Walsh character `∏ i, (-1) ^ (x i * z i)` on `Fin n → Fin 2`.
declarations.statement: def walsh (x z : Fin n → Fin 2) : ℂ

declarations.name: walsh_eq
declarations.doc: The Walsh character is the product of the signs of the components.
declarations.statement: lemma walsh_eq (x z : Fin n → Fin 2) : walsh x z = ∏ i, walshSign (x i) (z i)

declarations.name: walsh_comm
declarations.doc: The Walsh character `walsh x z` is symmetric in `x` and `z`.
declarations.statement: lemma walsh_comm (x z : Fin n → Fin 2) : walsh x z = walsh z x

declarations.name: walsh_mul_self
declarations.doc: A Walsh character squares to one.
declarations.statement: lemma walsh_mul_self (x z : Fin n → Fin 2) : walsh x z * walsh x z = 1

declarations.name: conj_walsh
declarations.doc: A Walsh character equals its complex conjugate.
declarations.statement: lemma conj_walsh (x z : Fin n → Fin 2) : starRingEnd ℂ (walsh x z) = walsh x z

declarations.name: norm_walsh
declarations.doc: A Walsh character has unit norm.
declarations.statement: lemma norm_walsh (x z : Fin n → Fin 2) : ‖walsh x z‖ = 1

declarations.name: sum_walsh_mul_walsh
declarations.doc: Orthogonality of the Walsh characters.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_walsh_mul_walsh (x y : Fin n → Fin 2) :
    ∑ z, walsh x z * walsh y z = if x = y then 2 ^ n else 0

declarations.name: walshVec
declarations.doc:
The rescaled Walsh vector `z ↦ (√(2 ^ n))⁻¹ * walsh x z` in
`EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n → Fin 2)`.
declarations.statement: def walshVec (x : Fin n → Fin 2) : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n → Fin 2)

declarations.name: walshVec_apply
declarations.doc: The component `z` of `walshVec x` is `(√(2 ^ n))⁻¹ * walsh x z`.
declarations.statement:
lemma walshVec_apply (x z : Fin n → Fin 2) :
    walshVec x z = (Real.sqrt (2 ^ n))⁻¹ * walsh x z

declarations.name: orthonormal_walshVec
declarations.doc: The rescaled Walsh vectors are orthonormal.
declarations.statement: lemma orthonormal_walshVec : Orthonormal ℂ (walshVec (n := n))

declarations.name: walshBasis
declarations.doc:
The orthonormal basis of `EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n → Fin 2)` formed by the rescaled Walsh
vectors `walshVec x`.
declarations.statement:
def walshBasis (n : ℕ) :
    OrthonormalBasis (Fin n → Fin 2) ℂ (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n → Fin 2))

declarations.name: coe_walshBasis
declarations.doc: The vectors of `walshBasis n` are the rescaled Walsh vectors.
declarations.statement: lemma coe_walshBasis (n : ℕ) : ⇑(walshBasis n) = walshVec

declarations.name: sum_norm_sq_sum_mul_inv_sqrt_mul_walsh
declarations.doc:
Parseval's identity for the rescaled Walsh vectors. The vector
`x ↦ ∑ z, β z * (√(2 ^ n))⁻¹ * walsh x z` has the same squared norm as `β`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_norm_sq_sum_mul_inv_sqrt_mul_walsh (n : ℕ) (β : (Fin n → Fin 2) → ℂ) :
    ∑ x : Fin n → Fin 2, ‖∑ z, β z * ((Real.sqrt (2 ^ n))⁻¹ * walsh x z)‖ ^ 2 =
      ∑ z, ‖β z‖ ^ 2

modules.title: Restricting a polynomial-valued algebra map to a subalgebra
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A grading of an algebra `A` is often recorded by an algebra map `f : A →ₐ[R] A[X]`, the
weight-`n` part being the eigenspace on which `f` is the monomial `X ^ n`. A subalgebra `S`
of `A` inherits such a grading exactly when `f` carries `S` into the polynomials with
coefficients in `S`, and this file supplies the two steps that gives.

Section A reduces the closure condition to the generators: since `f` is an algebra map and
the polynomials with coefficients in `S` form a subalgebra of `A[X]`, it is enough that
each generator lands there. Section B turns the closure condition into an algebra map
`S →ₐ[R] S[X]`, through the injection of `S[X]` into `A[X]`, and records that an eigenvalue
equation in `S` is the ambient one.

Nothing here is about any particular algebra. It is stated for an arbitrary `S` so that it
can be used at concrete algebras, where unfolding instances to check the corresponding
statement directly would be expensive.

## ii. Key results

- `Subalgebra.mem_range_mapAlgHom_of_adjoin` : the closure condition follows from the
  generators.
- `Subalgebra.polyRestrict` : the restricted map `S →ₐ[R] S[X]`.
- `Subalgebra.polyRestrict_eq_monomial_iff` : an eigenvalue equation in `S` is the ambient
  one.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Closure from the generators
- B. The restricted map

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Linear minorants of sublinear functionals
modules.doc:
A sublinear functional has a linear minorant attaining it at any given point (Hahn–Banach).

## i. Overview

A sublinear functional is the largest of the linear functionals below it. At every point the
Hahn–Banach theorem gives a linear functional below it that agrees with it there.

## ii. Key results

- `exists_linearMap_le_eq_of_sublinear` proves that a linear functional below a sublinear functional
  can be chosen to agree with it at a given point.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Linear minorants

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.statement: lemma map_zero_of_sublinear : N 0 = 0

declarations.doc: A sublinear functional dominates the multiples of its value at a point.
declarations.statement: lemma smul_le_of_sublinear (c : ℝ) (x : V) : c * N x ≤ N (c • x)

modules.title: Functoriality of the symmetric algebra
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Mathlib's `SymmetricAlgebra` carries the universal property `SymmetricAlgebra.lift` but no
functorial API. This file provides it: the algebra homomorphism induced by a linear map, the
algebra equivalence induced by a linear equivalence, generation by the degree-one elements,
and the decomposition of the symmetric algebra of a direct sum as a tensor product — the
bosonic analogue of `CliffordAlgebra.prodEquiv`, with the ordinary rather than the graded
tensor product because everything commutes.

## ii. Key results

- `SymmetricAlgebra.map` : the algebra homomorphism induced by a linear map.
- `SymmetricAlgebra.congr` : the algebra equivalence induced by a linear equivalence.
- `SymmetricAlgebra.adjoin_range_ι` : the symmetric algebra is generated by `ι`.
- `SymmetricAlgebra.prodEquiv` : the symmetric algebra of a direct sum is the tensor
  product of the symmetric algebras.
- `SymmetricAlgebra.derivationOfLinear` : the derivation extending a linear endomorphism.
- `SymmetricAlgebra.algHom_derivationOfLinear` : an algebra map determined by an
  intertwining linear map carries one derivation to the other.
- `Representation.symmetricAlgebra` : the representation extending one on the generators.
- `SymmetricAlgebra.symmetricAlgebra_derivationOfLinear` : covariance of the derivation
  under the representation.
- `SymmetricAlgebra.algHom_symmetricAlgebra` : an algebra map determined by an intertwining
  linear map carries one representation to the other.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Functoriality of the symmetric algebra
- B. Generation by the degree-one elements
- C. The symmetric algebra of a direct sum
- D. The derivation extending a linear endomorphism
- E. The representation extending a representation on the generators

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Functoriality of the symmetric algebra

Stated over a commutative semiring and additive commutative monoids: the local field
algebra of a gauge field datum carries its bosonic factor on that instance path, and
identifying it with the one a `CommRing`/`AddCommGroup` statement produces is blocked by
the unexposed `TensorAlgebra.symRingCon`.
## B. Generation by the degree-one elements

## C. The symmetric algebra of a direct sum

The symmetric algebra of `M × N` is the tensor product of the symmetric algebras of the
summands. Unlike the exterior-algebra analogue this is the *ordinary* tensor product: the
generators of the two factors commute, as bosonic generators must.

## D. The derivation extending a linear endomorphism

A linear endomorphism `d` of `M` extends uniquely to a derivation of the symmetric algebra:
the map obeying the Leibniz rule whose value on a generator `ι x` is `ι (d x)`. It is built
by lifting the generator map `ι x ↦ (ι x, ι (d x))` to an algebra homomorphism into the
trivial square-zero extension and taking the second component.
## E. The representation extending a representation on the generators

    (map f).comp (map g) = map (f ∘ₗ g)

declarations.doc:
The algebra equivalence between symmetric algebras induced by a linear equivalence of
the underlying modules.
