declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.adjoin_range_ι
declarations.doc:
The symmetric algebra is generated, as an `R`-algebra, by the degree-one elements.
Only a commutative semiring of scalars and a module are needed, so that the statement
applies to a module whose additive structure is not presented as a group, such as a
direct sum.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoin_range_ι :
    Algebra.adjoin R (Set.range (ι R M)) = (⊤ : Subalgebra R (SymmetricAlgebra R M))

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.prodToTensor
declarations.doc:
The forward half of `prodEquiv`: a generator `(m, n)` is sent to
`ι m ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ ι n`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def prodToTensor :
    SymmetricAlgebra R (M × N) →ₐ[R] SymmetricAlgebra R M ⊗[R] SymmetricAlgebra R N

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.prodToTensor_ι
declarations.statement:
lemma prodToTensor_ι (x : M × N) :
    prodToTensor (ι R (M × N) x)
      = ι R M x.1 ⊗ₜ[R] 1 + (1 : SymmetricAlgebra R M) ⊗ₜ[R] ι R N x.2

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.tensorToProd
declarations.doc:
The backward half of `prodEquiv`: the two inclusions of the factors, multiplied
together.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorToProd :
    SymmetricAlgebra R M ⊗[R] SymmetricAlgebra R N →ₐ[R] SymmetricAlgebra R (M × N)

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.tensorToProd_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorToProd_tmul (a : SymmetricAlgebra R M) (b : SymmetricAlgebra R N) :
    tensorToProd (a ⊗ₜ[R] b) = map (LinearMap.inl R M N) a * map (LinearMap.inr R M N) b

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.prodEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The symmetric algebra of a direct sum is the tensor product of the symmetric
algebras.** Two bosonic fields taken together are one field valued in the direct sum of
their target spaces; their generators commute, so the ordinary tensor product suffices —
no grading is needed, in contrast to the exterior-algebra analogue.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def prodEquiv :
    SymmetricAlgebra R (M × N) ≃ₐ[R] SymmetricAlgebra R M ⊗[R] SymmetricAlgebra R N

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.prodEquiv_ι
declarations.statement:
lemma prodEquiv_ι (x : M × N) :
    prodEquiv (ι R (M × N) x)
      = ι R M x.1 ⊗ₜ[R] 1 + (1 : SymmetricAlgebra R M) ⊗ₜ[R] ι R N x.2

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.derivationHom
declarations.doc:
The lift of the derivation extending `d` to the trivial square-zero extension of the
symmetric algebra: the algebra homomorphism `x ↦ (x, derivationOfLinear d x)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivationHom :
    SymmetricAlgebra R M →ₐ[R]
      TrivSqZeroExt (SymmetricAlgebra R M) (SymmetricAlgebra R M)

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.derivationHom_ι
declarations.statement:
lemma derivationHom_ι (x : M) :
    derivationHom d (ι R M x) = (ι R M x, ι R M (d x))

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.derivationHom_fst
declarations.doc: The first component of the square-zero lift is the identity.
declarations.statement: lemma derivationHom_fst (x : SymmetricAlgebra R M) : (derivationHom d x).fst = x

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.derivationOfLinear
declarations.doc:
**The derivation of the symmetric algebra extending a linear endomorphism** `d` of `M`:
the map obeying the Leibniz rule whose value on a generator `ι x` is `ι (d x)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def derivationOfLinear : SymmetricAlgebra R M →ₗ[R] SymmetricAlgebra R M

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.derivationOfLinear_ι
declarations.statement:
lemma derivationOfLinear_ι (x : M) :
    derivationOfLinear d (ι R M x) = ι R M (d x)

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.derivationOfLinear_one
declarations.statement: lemma derivationOfLinear_one : derivationOfLinear d (1 : SymmetricAlgebra R M) = 0

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.derivationOfLinear_algebraMap
declarations.statement:
lemma derivationOfLinear_algebraMap (r : R) :
    derivationOfLinear d (algebraMap R (SymmetricAlgebra R M) r) = 0

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.derivationOfLinear_mul
declarations.doc: The Leibniz rule for the derivation extending `d`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivationOfLinear_mul (x y : SymmetricAlgebra R M) :
    derivationOfLinear d (x * y)
      = derivationOfLinear d x * y + x * derivationOfLinear d y

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.derivationOfLinear_comm_apply
declarations.doc: Derivations extending commuting endomorphisms commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivationOfLinear_comm_apply {d₁ d₂ : M →ₗ[R] M} (h : d₁ ∘ₗ d₂ = d₂ ∘ₗ d₁)
    (x : SymmetricAlgebra R M) :
    derivationOfLinear d₁ (derivationOfLinear d₂ x)
      = derivationOfLinear d₂ (derivationOfLinear d₁ x)

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.algHom_derivationOfLinear
declarations.doc:
An algebra map carries one derivation to the other when the linear map it is
determined by on the generators intertwines the two endomorphisms. The hypotheses are
stated pointwise so that the lemma can be applied without rewriting inside a large
algebra.

declarations.name: Representation.symmetricAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The representation on the symmetric algebra extending a representation on the
generators: the substitution homomorphism determined by the action on the generators.
It is built from `SymmetricAlgebra.lift` rather than from `SymmetricAlgebra.map`, so that
it is available over a commutative semiring and an additive commutative monoid — the
generality the generator spaces of a multi-species field theory, which are direct sums,
are elaborated at.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def symmetricAlgebra (ρ : Representation R G M) :
    Representation R G (SymmetricAlgebra R M)

declarations.name: Representation.symmetricAlgebraAlgHom
declarations.doc: The action of a group element, as an algebra homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def symmetricAlgebraAlgHom (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G) :
    SymmetricAlgebra R M →ₐ[R] SymmetricAlgebra R M

declarations.name: Representation.symmetricAlgebra_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetricAlgebra_apply (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G)
    (x : SymmetricAlgebra R M) :
    ρ.symmetricAlgebra g x = ρ.symmetricAlgebraAlgHom g x

declarations.name: Representation.symmetricAlgebra_ι
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetricAlgebra_ι (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G) (x : M) :
    ρ.symmetricAlgebra g (SymmetricAlgebra.ι R M x)
      = SymmetricAlgebra.ι R M (ρ g x)

declarations.name: Representation.symmetricAlgebra_apply_one
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetricAlgebra_apply_one (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G) :
    ρ.symmetricAlgebra g (1 : SymmetricAlgebra R M) = 1

declarations.name: Representation.symmetricAlgebra_apply_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetricAlgebra_apply_mul (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G)
    (x y : SymmetricAlgebra R M) :
    ρ.symmetricAlgebra g (x * y)
      = ρ.symmetricAlgebra g x * ρ.symmetricAlgebra g y

declarations.name: Representation.symmetricAlgebra_algebraMap
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetricAlgebra_algebraMap (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G) (r : R) :
    ρ.symmetricAlgebra g (algebraMap R (SymmetricAlgebra R M) r)
      = algebraMap R (SymmetricAlgebra R M) r

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.symmetricAlgebra_derivationOfLinear
declarations.doc:
Covariance of the derivation under the representation. If the representation
carries each endomorphism of a family into a combination of the others on the generators,
then it carries the derivation extending one into the same combination of the derivations
extending the others on the whole exterior algebra. This is the shape the statement that
the total derivative is a Lorentz vector takes; it is proved by induction rather than by
algebra-map extensionality, a derivation not being an algebra map.
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetricAlgebra_derivationOfLinear {G κ : Type*} [Monoid G] [Fintype κ]
    (ρ : Representation R G M) (g : G) (d : κ → M →ₗ[R] M) (μ : κ) (c : κ → R)
    (h : ∀ x, ρ g (d μ x) = ∑ a, c a • d a (ρ g x)) (y : SymmetricAlgebra R M) :
    ρ.symmetricAlgebra g (derivationOfLinear (d μ) y)
      = ∑ a, c a • derivationOfLinear (d a) (ρ.symmetricAlgebra g y)

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.algHom_symmetricAlgebra
declarations.doc:
An algebra map carries one representation to the other when the linear map it is
determined by on the generators intertwines the two representations on them. Unlike the
derivation statement this is pure extensionality of algebra maps, each group element
acting by one; the hypotheses are stated pointwise so that the lemma can be applied
without rewriting inside a large algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma algHom_symmetricAlgebra {N G : Type*} [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [Monoid G]
    (F : SymmetricAlgebra R M →ₐ[R] SymmetricAlgebra R N) {f : M →ₗ[R] N}
    (hF : ∀ x, F (ι R M x) = ι R N (f x))
    {ρ : Representation R G M} {σ : Representation R G N} (g : G)
    (h : ∀ x, f (ρ g x) = σ g (f x)) (y : SymmetricAlgebra R M) :
    F (ρ.symmetricAlgebra g y) = σ.symmetricAlgebra g (F y)

modules.title: Bochner's theorem on discrete abelian groups
modules.doc:
A function `φ` on a discrete abelian group `G` is positive definite, `∑ᵢ ∑ⱼ cᵢ conj(cⱼ) φ(gᵢ - gⱼ) ≥
0` for every finite family, if and only if it is the Fourier–Stieltjes transform `φ(g) = ∫ χ(g)
dμ(χ)` of a finite inner regular positive measure `μ` on the Pontryagin dual of `G`.

## i. Overview

A function `φ` on a discrete abelian group `G` is positive definite,
`∑ᵢ ∑ⱼ cᵢ conj(cⱼ) φ(gᵢ - gⱼ) ≥ 0` for every finite family, if and only if it is the
Fourier–Stieltjes transform `φ(g) = ∫ χ(g) dμ(χ)` of a finite inner regular positive measure `μ`
on the Pontryagin dual of `G`. Every function on a discrete group is continuous, so no
continuity hypothesis appears.

The representing measure is the one of Bochner's theorem on locally compact abelian groups,
`TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.exists_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_of_continuousAt`, whose
continuity hypothesis is automatic on a discrete group.

For `G = ℤ` this recovers Herglotz's theorem, proved separately by Fejér means in
`TauCeti.Analysis.Bochner.Herglotz`.

## ii. Key results

* `TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_exists_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq`: **Bochner's theorem**
  for discrete abelian groups.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* W. Rudin, *Fourier Analysis on Groups*, Interscience (1962), §1.4.
* G. B. Folland, *A Course in Abstract Harmonic Analysis*, 2nd ed., CRC Press (2016), §3.3
  and §4.2.

declarations.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_exists_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq
declarations.doc:
**Bochner's theorem on a discrete abelian group.** A function on a discrete abelian group is
positive definite if and only if it is the Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a finite inner regular
measure on the Pontryagin dual.
declarations.statement:
lemma isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_exists_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq (φ : G → ℂ) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub φ ↔
      ∃ μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)),
        μ.toMeasure.InnerRegular ∧ μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform = φ

modules.title: Bochner's theorem on locally compact abelian groups
modules.doc:
A positive-definite function `φ` on a locally compact abelian group `G` that is continuous at `0` is
the Fourier–Stieltjes transform `φ(g) = ∫ χ(g) dμ(χ)` of a finite inner regular positive measure `μ`
on the Pontryagin dual of `G`.

## i. Overview

A positive-definite function `φ` on a locally compact abelian group `G` that is continuous at `0`
is the Fourier–Stieltjes transform `φ(g) = ∫ χ(g) dμ(χ)` of a finite inner regular positive
measure `μ` on the Pontryagin dual of `G`.

The representing measure is unique among finite inner regular measures, and conversely the
transform of every such measure is continuous and positive definite. Thus this is a full Bochner
characterization without any countability assumption. When the dual is Polish, every finite Borel
measure is regular, giving the corresponding characterization by arbitrary finite measures. The
dual is Polish when `G` is second countable.

The measure comes from the GNS construction. The function `φ` is a matrix coefficient
`φ(g) = ⟪v, U(-g) v⟫` of the unitary translation representation `U` on its GNS Hilbert space,
which is strongly continuous because `φ` is continuous at `0`. The cyclic spectral theorem for
strongly continuous unitary representations,
`ContRepresentation.exists_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_inner`, writes such a matrix coefficient
as a Fourier–Stieltjes transform.

The existence theorem assumes no second countability of `G`, and the GNS space need not be
separable: the integrated form behind the spectral theorem is defined through the inner
regularity of the Haar measure.

## ii. Key results

* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.exists_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_of_continuousAt`: a
  positive-definite function, continuous at `0`, on a locally compact abelian group is the
  Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a finite inner regular measure on the dual group.
* The countability-free Bochner characterization: continuous positive-definite functions are
  precisely the transforms of unique finite inner regular measures.
* `TauCeti.continuous_and_isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_existsUnique_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq`:
  the full Bochner characterization by unique finite measures on a locally compact abelian
  group with Polish dual.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* G. B. Folland, *A Course in Abstract Harmonic Analysis*, 2nd ed., CRC Press (2016),
  Theorem 4.18.

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.exists_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_of_continuousAt
declarations.doc:
**Bochner's theorem on a locally compact abelian group**, existence half.
A positive-definite function that is continuous at `0` is the Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a
finite inner regular measure on the Pontryagin dual.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsPositiveDefiniteSub.exists_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_of_continuousAt {φ : G → ℂ}
    (hφ : IsPositiveDefiniteSub φ) (hφ₀ : ContinuousAt φ 0) :
    ∃ μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)),
      μ.toMeasure.InnerRegular ∧ μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform = φ

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.existsUnique_innerRegular_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_of_continuousAt
declarations.doc:
**Unique inner regular form of Bochner's theorem.** A positive-definite function continuous at
`0` has a unique finite inner regular representing measure on the Pontryagin dual. No countability
or metrizability assumption is needed.
declarations.statement:
lemma
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub.existsUnique_innerRegular_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_of_continuousAt
    {φ : G → ℂ} (hφ : IsPositiveDefiniteSub φ) (hφ₀ : ContinuousAt φ 0) :
    ∃! μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)),
      μ.toMeasure.InnerRegular ∧ μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform = φ

declarations.name: TauCeti.continuous_and_isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_existsUnique_innerRegular_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq
declarations.doc:
**Bochner's characterization without countability assumptions.** A function on a locally
compact abelian group is continuous and positive definite if and only if it is the
Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a unique finite inner regular measure on the Pontryagin dual.
declarations.statement:
lemma
    continuous_and_isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_existsUnique_innerRegular_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq
    (φ : G → ℂ) :
    (Continuous φ ∧ IsPositiveDefiniteSub φ) ↔
      ∃! μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)),
        μ.toMeasure.InnerRegular ∧ μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform = φ

declarations.name: TauCeti.continuous_and_isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_existsUnique_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq
declarations.doc:
**Bochner's characterization on a locally compact abelian group with Polish dual.** A
function is continuous and positive definite if and only if it is the Fourier–Stieltjes
transform of a unique finite positive Borel measure on the dual group. The dual is Polish when
the group is second countable.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_and_isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_existsUnique_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq
    [PolishSpace (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))] (φ : G → ℂ) :
    (Continuous φ ∧ IsPositiveDefiniteSub φ) ↔
      ∃! μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)),
        μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform = φ

modules.title: Positive functionals on commutative C⋆-algebras are measures on the character space
modules.doc:
Let `A` be a unital commutative C⋆-algebra, with character space `Δ = characterSpace ℂ A`.

## i. Overview

Let `A` be a unital commutative C⋆-algebra, with character space `Δ = characterSpace ℂ A`. A
linear functional `f : A → ℂ` that is nonnegative on every `star a * a` is integration against a
finite inner regular positive measure on `Δ`:

`f a = ∫ ω, ω a ∂μ`.

The Gelfand transform identifies `A` with `C(Δ, ℂ)`, and under this identification
`star a * a` runs through the nonnegative functions, so `f` becomes a positive linear functional
on `C(Δ, ℝ)`. The compact space `Δ` then carries its Riesz–Markov–Kakutani measure.

This is the commutative case of the passage from positive functionals to spectral data; it turns
a cyclic commuting family of operators, such as a unitary representation of an abelian group,
into a measure on the joint spectrum.

## ii. Key results

* `LinearMap.exists_isFiniteMeasure_integral_characterSpace_eq`: a functional nonnegative on
  `star a * a` is integration against a finite inner regular measure on the character space.
* `WeakDual.CharacterSpace.integral_apply_star_mul_self`: integrating `ω ↦ ω (star a * a)`
  gives the squared `L²` norm of `ω ↦ ω a`, so a measure representing a functional `f` computes
  `f (star a * a)`.
* `StarSubalgebra.exists_isFiniteMeasure_integral_characterSpace_eq_inner`: for a closed
  commutative star algebra of operators on a Hilbert space, each positive vector functional
  `a ↦ ⟪ξ, a ξ⟫` is integration against a finite inner regular measure on the character space.
* `StarSubalgebra.integral_norm_sq_eq_norm_apply_sq`: a measure representing such a functional
  computes `‖a ξ‖²` as the squared `L²` norm of `ω ↦ ω a`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* W. Rudin, *Functional Analysis*, 2nd ed., McGraw–Hill (1991), Theorem 11.18 and §12.
* G. J. Murphy, *C⋆-Algebras and Operator Theory*, Academic Press (1990), §2.1.

declarations.name: LinearMap.exists_isFiniteMeasure_integral_characterSpace_eq
declarations.doc:
**Positive functionals on a commutative C⋆-algebra are measures on its character space.**
A linear functional on a unital commutative C⋆-algebra that is nonnegative on every
`star a * a` is integration against a finite inner regular positive measure `μ` on the
character space: `f a = ∫ ω, ω a ∂μ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma LinearMap.exists_isFiniteMeasure_integral_characterSpace_eq (f : A →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ)
    (hf : ∀ a, 0 ≤ f (star a * a)) :
    ∃ μ : Measure (characterSpace ℂ A), IsFiniteMeasure μ ∧ μ.InnerRegular ∧
      ∀ a, f a = ∫ ω, ω a ∂μ

declarations.name: WeakDual.CharacterSpace.integral_apply_star_mul_self
declarations.doc:
For a measure `μ` on the character space of a unital C⋆-algebra, integrating
`ω ↦ ω (star a * a) = |ω a|²` gives the squared `L²` norm of `ω ↦ ω a`. Hence if `μ` represents a
functional `f`, as in `LinearMap.exists_isFiniteMeasure_integral_characterSpace_eq`, then
`f (star a * a) = ∫ |ω a|² dμ(ω)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma WeakDual.CharacterSpace.integral_apply_star_mul_self {E : Type*} [CStarAlgebra E]
    [MeasurableSpace (characterSpace ℂ E)] (μ : Measure (characterSpace ℂ E)) (a : E) :
    ∫ ω, ω (star a * a) ∂μ = ((∫ ω, ‖ω a‖ ^ 2 ∂μ : ℝ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: StarSubalgebra.integral_norm_sq_eq_norm_apply_sq
declarations.doc:
For a closed star algebra `B` of operators, if a measure `μ` on the character space
represents the positive vector functional of `ξ`, then `∫ |ω a|² dμ(ω) = ‖a ξ‖²` for every
`a ∈ B`.

declarations.name: StarSubalgebra.exists_isFiniteMeasure_integral_characterSpace_eq_inner
declarations.doc:
**Positive vector functionals are measures on the character space.** For a closed
commutative star algebra `B` of operators on a complex Hilbert space and a vector `ξ`, the
positive vector functional `a ↦ ⟪ξ, a ξ⟫` is integration against a finite inner regular positive
measure on the character space of `B`.
declarations.statement:
lemma StarSubalgebra.exists_isFiniteMeasure_integral_characterSpace_eq_inner (ξ : H) :
    ∃ μ : Measure (characterSpace ℂ B), IsFiniteMeasure μ ∧ μ.InnerRegular ∧
      ∀ a : B, ⟪ξ, (a : H →L[ℂ] H) ξ⟫_ℂ = ∫ ω, ω a ∂μ

modules.title: Characters from unitary multipliers
modules.doc:
A unitary representation need not be continuous in the norm of a C⋆-algebra.

## i. Overview

A unitary representation need not be continuous in the norm of a C⋆-algebra. Nevertheless,
a character of a subalgebra detects a continuous circle-valued character whenever it is nonzero
on an operator whose translates are norm continuous and belong to the subalgebra. The resulting
character describes every translate that belongs to the subalgebra, so it is independent of
the operator used to detect it.

This is the character-identification step in the spectral representation of a strongly
continuous unitary representation, applied to a nonzero integrated operator.

## ii. Key results

This file proves the statement described in the overview.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* G. B. Folland, *A Course in Abstract Harmonic Analysis*, second edition, §4.4.

declarations.name: MonoidHom.existsUnique_pontryaginDual_of_unitary_translate
declarations.doc:
A character nonzero on a commuting operator with norm-continuous unitary translates
induces a unique continuous circle-valued character. It describes every translate in the subalgebra,
not just the translates of the witnessing operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.MonoidHom.existsUnique_pontryaginDual_of_unitary_translate
    (ρ : G →* B) (hρ : ∀ g, ρ g ∈ unitary B)
    (A : StarSubalgebra ℂ B) [CompleteSpace A]
    (a : A) (hcomm : ∀ g, Commute (ρ g) (a : B))
    (hmem : ∀ g, ρ g * (a : B) ∈ A)
    (hcont : Continuous fun g => ρ g * (a : B))
    (ω : characterSpace ℂ A) (ha : ω a ≠ 0) :
    ∃! χ : PontryaginDual G,
      ∀ (g : G) (b : A) (hb : ρ g * (b : B) ∈ A),
        ω ⟨ρ g * (b : B), hb⟩ = (χ g : ℂ) * ω b

modules.title: Continuity of the Fourier–Stieltjes transform on a Pontryagin dual
modules.doc:
The Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a tight finite positive measure on the Pontryagin dual is
continuous on the original locally compact group.

## i. Overview

The Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a tight finite positive measure on the Pontryagin dual is
continuous on the original locally compact group. Together with its positive-definiteness,
this supplies the measure-to-function direction of Bochner representation on locally compact
abelian groups for regular measures. A compact set carries almost all of the measure; character
evaluation is uniformly continuous there near each fixed group element, while the complement
contributes at most its small mass.

This is the standard compact truncation argument for Fourier–Stieltjes transforms; see
G. B. Folland, *A Course in Abstract Harmonic Analysis*, Chapter 4.

## ii. Key results

This file proves the statement described in the overview.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* Standard material; the statements and proofs are original to this formalization.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.continuous_pontryaginMeasureTransform
declarations.doc:
The transform of a tight finite measure on the Pontryagin dual is continuous. Tightness is
automatic for finite Radon measures and is the regularity needed when the dual is not metrizable.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.continuous_pontryaginMeasureTransform
    (μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)))
    (hμ : IsTightMeasureSet {μ.toMeasure}) :
    Continuous μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform

modules.title: Evaluation of Pontryagin characters
modules.doc:
Evaluation at a fixed monoid element is continuous on the Pontryagin dual.

## i. Overview

Evaluation at a fixed monoid element is continuous on the Pontryagin dual. Its complex-valued
form is integrable against every finite measure. These lemmas supply the integrands for
Fourier–Stieltjes transforms, and apply to arbitrary monoids with a topology.

## ii. Key results

This file proves the statement described in the overview.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* Standard material; the statements and proofs are original to this formalization.

declarations.name: TauCeti.PontryaginDual.continuous_coe_eval_const
declarations.doc: Complex-valued evaluation of a Pontryagin character at a fixed monoid element is continuous.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_coe_eval_const (g : G) :
    Continuous (fun χ : _root_.PontryaginDual G => (χ g : ℂ))

declarations.name: TauCeti.PontryaginDual.integrable_coe_eval
declarations.doc: Complex-valued evaluation of a Pontryagin character is integrable against a finite measure.
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_coe_eval
    {μ : Measure (_root_.PontryaginDual G)} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (g : G) :
    Integrable (fun χ : _root_.PontryaginDual G => (χ g : ℂ)) μ

modules.title: Fourier–Stieltjes transform of measures on a Pontryagin dual
modules.doc:
Integrating character evaluations against a finite positive measure on the Pontryagin dual defines a
complex-valued function on the original additive group.

## i. Overview

Integrating character evaluations against a finite positive measure on the Pontryagin dual
defines a complex-valued function on the original additive group. The transform records the
measure's mass at the identity and respects addition, scaling, and point masses.

## ii. Key results

This file proves the statement described in the overview.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* Standard material; the statements and proofs are original to this formalization.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform
declarations.doc:
The Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a finite measure on the Pontryagin dual of an
additive group.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform
    (μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) (g : G) : ℂ

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_apply
declarations.doc: The transform evaluated at a group element is the integral of character evaluations.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_apply
    (μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) (g : G) :
    μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform g =
      ∫ χ, (χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) : ℂ) ∂μ.toMeasure

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_zero
declarations.doc: At the identity, the transform records the total mass of the measure.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_zero
    (μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) :
    μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform 0 = (μ.toMeasure.real Set.univ : ℂ)

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_zero_measure
declarations.doc: The transform of the zero measure vanishes.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_zero_measure :
    (0 : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))).pontryaginMeasureTransform = 0

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_smul
declarations.doc: The transform commutes with nonnegative scalar multiplication of finite measures.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_smul
    (c : NNReal) (μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) :
    (c • μ).pontryaginMeasureTransform = c • μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_add
declarations.doc: The transform commutes with addition of finite measures.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_add
    (μ ν : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) :
    (μ + ν).pontryaginMeasureTransform =
      μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform + ν.pontryaginMeasureTransform

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_dirac
declarations.doc: The transform of a point mass is its character.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_dirac
    (χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) (g : G) :
    FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform
      (⟨Measure.dirac χ, inferInstance⟩ : FiniteMeasure
        (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) g =
      (χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) : ℂ)

modules.title: Matrix coefficients of strongly continuous unitary representations
modules.doc:
Let `π` be a strongly continuous unitary representation of a locally compact abelian group `G` on a
complex Hilbert space `H`, and let `ξ ∈ H`.

## i. Overview

Let `π` be a strongly continuous unitary representation of a locally compact abelian group `G`
on a complex Hilbert space `H`, and let `ξ ∈ H`. The
diagonal matrix coefficient `g ↦ ⟪ξ, π(g) ξ⟫` is the Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a finite
inner regular positive measure on the Pontryagin dual of `G`. This is the cyclic form of the
Stone–Naimark–Ambrose–Godement spectral theorem.

The operators `π(g)` are only strongly continuous, so the spectral measure is built from the
integrated operators `π(f)`, `f ∈ L¹(G)`, taken with respect to a Haar measure. They generate a
unital commutative C⋆-algebra `A`, and the vector functional `a ↦ ⟪ξ, a ξ⟫` is integration
against a finite measure `ν` on the character space of `A`. A character `ω` that does not vanish
on every integrated operator determines a continuous group character `χ_ω` with
`ω(π(g) π(f)) = χ_ω(g) ω(π(f))`; this assignment is continuous on the open set of such
characters, and the image of `ν` under it is the required measure. The characters annihilating
every integrated operator do not contribute: since `π(f) ξ` approximates `ξ`, the identity
`∫ |ω(π(f)) - 1|² dν = ‖π(f) ξ - ξ‖²` forces their measure to be zero.
Compact approximation inside the open set of non-annihilating characters then proves that the
pushforward measure is inner regular.

No second countability of `G` and no separability of `H` is needed: the integrated form is defined
for the Haar measure through its inner regularity for compact sets.

## ii. Key results

* `ContRepresentation.exists_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_inner`: a diagonal matrix coefficient
  of a strongly continuous unitary representation of a locally compact abelian group is the
  Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a finite inner regular measure on the dual group.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* G. B. Folland, *A Course in Abstract Harmonic Analysis*, 2nd ed., CRC Press (2016), §§3.2,
  4.4 and Theorem 4.44.

declarations.name: ContRepresentation.exists_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_inner
declarations.doc:
**Spectral theorem for strongly continuous unitary representations**, cyclic form. For a
strongly continuous unitary representation `π` of a locally compact abelian group `G` on a
Hilbert space `H` and a vector `ξ`, the matrix coefficient `g ↦ ⟪ξ, π(g) ξ⟫` is the
Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a finite inner regular measure on the Pontryagin dual of `G`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ContRepresentation.exists_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_inner
    (π : ContRepresentation ℂ (Multiplicative G) H)
    (hcont : ∀ v, Continuous fun g : G ↦ π (.ofAdd g) v)
    (hπ : ContRepresentation.IsUnitary π) (ξ : H) :
    ∃ μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)),
      μ.toMeasure.InnerRegular ∧ ∀ g, μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform g = ⟪ξ, π (.ofAdd g) ξ⟫_ℂ

modules.title: Uniqueness of Fourier--Stieltjes measures on a Pontryagin dual
modules.doc:
On a Polish Pontryagin dual, a finite measure is determined by the integrals of the evaluation
characters.

## i. Overview

On a Polish Pontryagin dual, a finite measure is determined by the integrals of the evaluation
characters.  Equivalently, the Fourier--Stieltjes transform of a finite measure on the dual is
injective.  On the dual of an arbitrary locally compact abelian group, where the dual need be
neither metrizable nor second countable, the same holds for finite inner regular measures.  These
are the uniqueness halves of Bochner's theorem for locally compact abelian groups.

The proof packages finite linear combinations of evaluation characters as a star subalgebra of
bounded continuous functions.  Evaluation characters separate points of the dual simply because
two continuous homomorphisms that agree at every group element are equal.  Mathlib's extension
theorem for finite measures on Polish spaces, or its inner regular counterpart
`TauCeti.MeasureTheory.ext_of_forall_mem_subalgebra_integral_eq_of_innerRegular` on locally
compact Hausdorff spaces, then promotes equality of the character integrals to equality of the
measures.

The construction of `evalMonoidHom`, `evalAlgHom` and `evalPoly`, together with the proofs that
`evalPoly` is closed under `star` and separates points, is adapted from Jakob Stiefel's
`charMonoidHom`, `charAlgHom`, `charPoly`, `star_mem_range_charAlgHom` and
`separatesPoints_charPoly` in `Mathlib.Analysis.Fourier.BoundedContinuousFunctionChar`, which
treats characters of the form `v ↦ e (L v w)` on a real vector space.

## ii. Key results

* `PontryaginDual.evalBoundedContinuous`: evaluation at a group element, bundled as a
  bounded continuous function on the dual.
* `PontryaginDual.evalPoly`: the star subalgebra of finite linear combinations of
  evaluation characters.
* `MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.ext_of_forall_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq`: finite measures on a
  Polish dual with the same Fourier--Stieltjes transform are equal.
* `MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.ext_of_forall_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_of_innerRegular`:
  finite inner regular measures on the dual of a locally compact abelian group with the same
  Fourier--Stieltjes transform are equal.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* W. Rudin, *Fourier Analysis on Groups*, Chapter 1.
* J. Stiefel, `Mathlib.Analysis.Fourier.BoundedContinuousFunctionChar`, Mathlib.

declarations.name: PontryaginDual.evalBoundedContinuous
declarations.doc:
Evaluation at `g`, as a bounded continuous complex-valued function on the Pontryagin dual.
Its values lie on the unit circle, so its norm is bounded by one.
declarations.statement:
def evalBoundedContinuous (g : G) :
    _root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G) →ᵇ ℂ

declarations.name: PontryaginDual.evalBoundedContinuous_apply
declarations.doc: Evaluation of `evalBoundedContinuous` at a character.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalBoundedContinuous_apply (g : G)
    (χ : _root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) :
    evalBoundedContinuous g χ = (χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) : ℂ)

declarations.name: PontryaginDual.evalBoundedContinuous_zero
declarations.doc: Evaluation at zero is the constant function one.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalBoundedContinuous_zero :
    evalBoundedContinuous (0 : G) = 1

declarations.name: PontryaginDual.evalBoundedContinuous_add
declarations.doc: Evaluation turns addition in the original group into pointwise multiplication.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalBoundedContinuous_add (g h : G) :
    evalBoundedContinuous (g + h) =
      evalBoundedContinuous g * evalBoundedContinuous h

declarations.name: PontryaginDual.evalBoundedContinuous_neg
declarations.doc: Evaluation at the negative of a group element is the pointwise star of evaluation there.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalBoundedContinuous_neg (g : G) :
    evalBoundedContinuous (-g) = star (evalBoundedContinuous g)

declarations.name: PontryaginDual.evalMonoidHom
declarations.doc: Evaluation as a monoid homomorphism from the multiplicative copy of the original group.
declarations.statement:
def evalMonoidHom : Multiplicative G →*
    (_root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G) →ᵇ ℂ)

declarations.name: PontryaginDual.evalMonoidHom_apply
declarations.doc: Evaluation of `evalMonoidHom` at a character.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalMonoidHom_apply (g : Multiplicative G)
    (χ : _root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) :
    evalMonoidHom g χ = (χ g : ℂ)

declarations.name: PontryaginDual.evalAlgHom
declarations.doc:
The algebra homomorphism sending a formal finite linear combination of group elements to the
corresponding finite linear combination of evaluation characters.
declarations.statement:
def evalAlgHom : AddMonoidAlgebra ℂ G →ₐ[ℂ]
    (_root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G) →ᵇ ℂ)

declarations.name: PontryaginDual.evalAlgHom_apply
declarations.doc: Evaluation of `evalAlgHom` is the corresponding finite linear combination of characters.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalAlgHom_apply (a : AddMonoidAlgebra ℂ G)
    (χ : _root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) :
    evalAlgHom a χ = a.coeff.sum fun g c => c * (χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) : ℂ)

declarations.name: PontryaginDual.star_mem_range_evalAlgHom
declarations.doc: The range of `evalAlgHom` is closed under pointwise complex conjugation.

declarations.name: PontryaginDual.evalPoly
declarations.doc: The star subalgebra of bounded continuous functions generated by evaluation characters.
declarations.statement:
def evalPoly : StarSubalgebra ℂ
    (_root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G) →ᵇ ℂ)

declarations.name: PontryaginDual.evalPoly_toSubalgebra
declarations.doc: The underlying subalgebra of `evalPoly` is the range of `evalAlgHom`.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalPoly_toSubalgebra :
    (evalPoly (G := G)).toSubalgebra = evalAlgHom.range

declarations.name: PontryaginDual.mem_evalPoly
declarations.doc:
Membership in `evalPoly` means being a finite linear combination of evaluation
characters.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_evalPoly (f : _root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G) →ᵇ ℂ) :
    f ∈ evalPoly ↔
      ∃ a : AddMonoidAlgebra ℂ G,
        f = a.coeff.sum fun g c => c • evalBoundedContinuous g

declarations.name: PontryaginDual.evalBoundedContinuous_mem_evalPoly
declarations.doc: Every evaluation character belongs to `evalPoly`.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalBoundedContinuous_mem_evalPoly (g : G) :
    evalBoundedContinuous g ∈ evalPoly

declarations.name: PontryaginDual.separatesPoints_evalPoly
declarations.doc: The evaluation-character algebra separates points of the Pontryagin dual.
declarations.statement:
lemma separatesPoints_evalPoly :
    ((evalPoly : StarSubalgebra ℂ
      (_root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G) →ᵇ ℂ)).map
        (BoundedContinuousFunction.toContinuousMapStarₐ ℂ)).SeparatesPoints

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.integral_eq_of_forall_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq
declarations.doc:
Two finite measures on the dual with the same Fourier--Stieltjes transform integrate every
finite linear combination of evaluation characters equally.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.integral_eq_of_forall_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq
    {P Q : FiniteMeasure (_root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))}
    (h : ∀ g, P.pontryaginMeasureTransform g = Q.pontryaginMeasureTransform g)
    {f : _root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G) →ᵇ ℂ} (hf : f ∈ _root_.PontryaginDual.evalPoly) :
    ∫ χ, f χ ∂P = ∫ χ, f χ ∂Q

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.ext_of_forall_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq
declarations.doc:
**Uniqueness of Fourier--Stieltjes measures on a Polish Pontryagin dual.** Two finite measures
on the dual are equal when their transforms agree on every element of the original group.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.ext_of_forall_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq
    {P Q : FiniteMeasure (_root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))}
    (h : ∀ g, P.pontryaginMeasureTransform g = Q.pontryaginMeasureTransform g) :
    P = Q

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_injective
declarations.doc:
The Fourier--Stieltjes transform is injective on finite measures on a Polish Pontryagin
dual.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_injective :
    Function.Injective
      (fun P : FiniteMeasure (_root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) =>
        P.pontryaginMeasureTransform)

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.ext_of_forall_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_of_innerRegular
declarations.doc:
**Uniqueness of inner regular Fourier--Stieltjes measures.** On the Pontryagin dual of a
locally compact abelian group, two finite inner regular measures are equal when their transforms
agree on every element of the group. No countability or metrizability is assumed.
declarations.statement:
lemma
    _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.ext_of_forall_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq_of_innerRegular
    {P Q : FiniteMeasure (_root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))}
    [P.toMeasure.InnerRegular] [Q.toMeasure.InnerRegular]
    (h : ∀ g, P.pontryaginMeasureTransform g = Q.pontryaginMeasureTransform g) :
    P = Q

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_injOn_innerRegular
declarations.doc:
The Fourier--Stieltjes transform is injective on finite inner regular measures on the
Pontryagin dual of a locally compact abelian group.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.pontryaginMeasureTransform_injOn_innerRegular :
    Set.InjOn
      (fun P : FiniteMeasure (_root_.PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) =>
        P.pontryaginMeasureTransform)
      {P | P.toMeasure.InnerRegular}

modules.title: Spans of orthonormal subfamilies
modules.doc:
For a finite-index orthonormal basis and a set of indices, `spanIndices` is the subspace spanned by
the corresponding basis vectors.

## i. Overview

For a finite-index orthonormal basis and a set of indices, `spanIndices` is the
subspace spanned by the corresponding basis vectors.

## ii. Key results

* `OrthonormalBasis.spanIndices_eq_span`: the explicit span characterization.
* `OrthonormalBasis.spanIndices_mono`: monotonicity under index-set inclusion.
* `OrthonormalBasis.mem_spanIndices_of_mem`: selected basis vectors belong to the span.
* `OrthonormalBasis.mem_spanIndices_iff`: membership means coordinates vanish
  outside the selected indices.
* `OrthonormalBasis.finrank_spanIndices`: the dimension of a selected finite span.
* `OrthonormalBasis.finrank_spanIndices_set`: dimension as set cardinality.
* `OrthonormalBasis.orthogonal_spanIndices`: orthogonal complement by index complement.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

Source: Adapted from `ForTauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/BasisSpan.lean` in the
[AIQ-Kitware DKPS formalization](https://github.com/AIQ-Kitware/aiq-dkps-formalization)
(Kitware, Inc.; Apache-2.0). The selected-span construction originates in the
Courant--Fischer development.

declarations.name: OrthonormalBasis.spanIndices
declarations.doc:
The subspace spanned by the orthonormal basis vectors `b i` for indices
`i ∈ s`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spanIndices (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 E) (s : Set ι) :
    Submodule 𝕜 E

declarations.name: OrthonormalBasis.spanIndices_eq_span
declarations.doc:
The selected subspace is the span of its basis vectors.
Use this identity to apply `Submodule.span`'s induction or universal property.
declarations.statement:
lemma spanIndices_eq_span (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 E) (s : Set ι) :
    b.spanIndices s = Submodule.span 𝕜 (b '' s)

declarations.name: OrthonormalBasis.spanIndices_mono
declarations.doc: Selecting more indices spans more.
declarations.statement:
lemma spanIndices_mono (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 E) {s t : Set ι} (h : s ⊆ t) :
    b.spanIndices s ≤ b.spanIndices t

declarations.name: OrthonormalBasis.mem_spanIndices_of_mem
declarations.doc: A selected basis vector lies in the span of its index set.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_spanIndices_of_mem (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 E) {s : Set ι} {i : ι}
    (hi : i ∈ s) : b i ∈ b.spanIndices s

declarations.name: OrthonormalBasis.repr_eq_zero_of_mem_spanIndices
declarations.doc:
A vector in the span of a selected subfamily has zero coordinate at any
index outside the selection.
declarations.statement:
lemma repr_eq_zero_of_mem_spanIndices (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 E)
    {s : Set ι} {x : E} (hx : x ∈ b.spanIndices s) {i : ι} (hi : i ∉ s) :
    b.repr x i = 0

declarations.name: OrthonormalBasis.mem_spanIndices_iff
declarations.doc:
Membership in the span of a selected subfamily is exactly the vanishing of
the coordinates outside the selection.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_spanIndices_iff (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 E)
    {s : Set ι} {x : E} :
    x ∈ b.spanIndices s ↔ ∀ i ∉ s, b.repr x i = 0

declarations.name: OrthonormalBasis.finrank_spanIndices
declarations.doc:
The span of a selected subfamily has dimension the number of selected
indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma finrank_spanIndices (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 E) (s : Finset ι) :
    finrank 𝕜 (b.spanIndices ↑s) = s.card

declarations.name: OrthonormalBasis.finrank_spanIndices_set
declarations.doc:
The span of a selected set of basis vectors has dimension equal to the
number of selected indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma finrank_spanIndices_set (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 E) (s : Set ι) :
    finrank 𝕜 (b.spanIndices s) = s.ncard

declarations.name: OrthonormalBasis.orthogonal_spanIndices
declarations.doc:
The orthogonal complement of the span of a selected subfamily is the span
of the complementary subfamily.
declarations.statement:
lemma orthogonal_spanIndices (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 E) (s : Set ι) :
    (b.spanIndices s)ᗮ = b.spanIndices sᶜ

modules.title: Courant–Fischer min–max theorem and Weyl's inequality
modules.doc:
For a finite-dimensional inner-product space over `ℝ` or `ℂ`, the min–max theorem characterizes the
decreasingly sorted eigenvalues of a symmetric endomorphism through its Rayleigh form.

## i. Overview

For a finite-dimensional inner-product space over `ℝ` or `ℂ`, the min–max theorem
characterizes the decreasingly sorted eigenvalues of a symmetric endomorphism
through its Rayleigh form.  The same argument gives monotonicity under quadratic-
form domination and Weyl's perturbation bound.

## ii. Key results

* `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.re_inner_apply_self_eq_sum_eigenvalues_mul_sq`:
  diagonal expansion of the Rayleigh form in an eigenbasis.
* `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.exists_unit_vector_re_inner_le_eigenvalue` and
  `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.exists_submodule_forall_unit_eigenvalue_le_re_inner`:
  the two min–max directions.
* `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues_eq_iSup_iInf_re_inner`:
  the Courant–Fischer equality.
* `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalue_mono`:
  monotonicity of sorted eigenvalues under quadratic-form order.
* `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.abs_eigenvalue_sub_eigenvalue_le` and
  `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.abs_eigenvalue_sub_eigenvalue_le_norm`:
  Weyl's perturbation inequality.
* `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalue_compression_le` and
  `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalue_le_eigenvalue_compression`:
  Cauchy interlacing for an operator on a subspace with the same quadratic form, such as the
  compression `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.compression`.
* `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalue_ascending_le_ritz`: the Hylleraas–Undheim–MacDonald
  bound, the `k`-th lowest Ritz value bounds the `k`-th lowest eigenvalue from above.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development
  - A.1. The quadratic form in the eigenbasis
  - A.2. Discrete Courant–Fischer directional bounds
  - A.3. The Courant–Fischer min-max equality
  - A.4. Sorted-eigenvalue uniqueness and Loewner monotonicity
  - A.5. Weyl's inequality
  - A.6. Courant–Fischer on subspaces of larger dimension
  - A.7. Cauchy interlacing and Rayleigh–Ritz bounds
  - A.8. The orthogonal compression

## iv. References

* R. A. Horn and C. R. Johnson, *Matrix Analysis*, 2nd ed.,
  Theorems 4.2.6 and 4.3.1.
* R. Bhatia, *Matrix Analysis*, Corollary III.2.6.
* E. A. Hylleraas and B. Undheim, *Numerische Berechnung der 2S-Terme von Ortho- und
  Par-Helium*, Z. Phys. 65 (1930) 759–772, pp. 763–764. [ref: hylleraas_undheim_1930]
* J. K. L. MacDonald, *Successive Approximations by the Rayleigh-Ritz Variation Method*,
  Phys. Rev. 43 (1933) 830–833, rule (1) and Corollary 1.1. [ref: macdonald_1933]

Provenance: Ported and adapted from
[`ForTauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/CourantFischer.lean`](https://github.com/AIQ-Kitware/aiq-dkps-formalization/blob/main/ForTauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/CourantFischer.lean)
in Kitware's DKPS formalization (Apache-2.0).  The original proof development
was by Claude Fable 5, with polishing by Claude Opus 4.8 and oversight by
Jon Crall.

### A.4. Sorted-eigenvalue uniqueness and Loewner monotonicity

Courant–Fischer consequences needed by the Ky Fan / unitarily-invariant-norm
development: an antitone list diagonalizing a symmetric operator in *some*
orthonormal basis is *the* sorted eigenvalue list, and the sorted eigenvalues
are monotone in the quadratic form (Loewner order).
### A.6. Courant–Fischer on subspaces of larger dimension
### A.7. Cauchy interlacing and Rayleigh–Ritz bounds

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.re_inner_apply_self_eq_sum_of_eigenbasis
declarations.doc:
Diagonalization of the quadratic form in any orthonormal eigenbasis: if
`S (w i) = μ i • w i` for all `i`, then
`re ⟪S x, x⟫ = ∑ i, μ i * ‖w.repr x i‖ ^ 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma re_inner_apply_self_eq_sum_of_eigenbasis
    (hS : S.IsSymmetric) (w : OrthonormalBasis (Fin n) 𝕜 E) {μ : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hw : ∀ i, S (w i) = (μ i : 𝕜) • w i) (x : E) :
    RCLike.re ⟪S x, x⟫_𝕜 = ∑ i : Fin n, μ i * ‖w.repr x i‖ ^ 2

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.le_re_inner_of_eigenbasis
declarations.doc:
On the span of the eigenvectors selected by `s`, the quadratic form is
bounded below by any lower bound on the selected values (general-eigenbasis
version of `le_re_inner_apply_self_of_mem_spanIndices`).

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.re_inner_le_of_eigenbasis
declarations.doc: Dual of `le_re_inner_of_eigenbasis`.

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.re_inner_apply_self_eq_sum_eigenvalues_mul_sq
declarations.doc:
The quadratic form `re ⟪T x, x⟫` of a symmetric operator `T` expressed in
its eigenbasis: it is the eigenvalue-weighted sum of the squared norms of the
coordinates of `x`.  This is the diagonalization of the quadratic form.  (For
symmetric `T` the inner product `⟪T x, x⟫` is real, so no information is lost
by taking the real part.)
declarations.statement:
lemma re_inner_apply_self_eq_sum_eigenvalues_mul_sq
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) (x : E) :
    RCLike.re ⟪T x, x⟫_𝕜
      = ∑ i : Fin n, hT.eigenvalues hn i * ‖(hT.eigenvectorBasis hn).repr x i‖ ^ 2

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.re_inner_apply_self_le_of_mem_spanIndices
declarations.doc:
On the span of a selected subfamily of the eigenbasis, the quadratic form
is bounded by any bound on the selected eigenvalues: if
`x ∈ b.spanIndices s` (so its coordinates vanish off `s`) and every selected
eigenvalue satisfies `λᵢ ≤ c`, then `re ⟪T x, x⟫ ≤ c ‖x‖²`.
declarations.statement:
lemma re_inner_apply_self_le_of_mem_spanIndices
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) {s : Set (Fin n)} {c : ℝ}
    (hc : ∀ i ∈ s, hT.eigenvalues hn i ≤ c)
    {x : E} (hx : x ∈ (hT.eigenvectorBasis hn).spanIndices s) :
    RCLike.re ⟪T x, x⟫_𝕜 ≤ c * ‖x‖ ^ 2

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.le_re_inner_apply_self_of_mem_spanIndices
declarations.doc:
Dual of `re_inner_apply_self_le_of_mem_spanIndices`: if
`x ∈ b.spanIndices s` and every selected eigenvalue satisfies `c ≤ λᵢ`, then
`c ‖x‖² ≤ re ⟪T x, x⟫`.
declarations.statement:
lemma le_re_inner_apply_self_of_mem_spanIndices
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) {s : Set (Fin n)} {c : ℝ}
    (hc : ∀ i ∈ s, c ≤ hT.eigenvalues hn i)
    {x : E} (hx : x ∈ (hT.eigenvectorBasis hn).spanIndices s) :
    c * ‖x‖ ^ 2 ≤ RCLike.re ⟪T x, x⟫_𝕜

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.exists_unit_vector_re_inner_le_eigenvalue
declarations.doc:
**Courant–Fischer, upper direction.** On any subspace `V` of dimension
`k + 1` there is a unit vector `x` with `re ⟪T x, x⟫ ≤ λₖ(T)`, where `λ` is the
decreasing enumeration `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues` of the eigenvalues
of the symmetric operator `T`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_unit_vector_re_inner_le_eigenvalue
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) (k : Fin n)
    (V : Submodule 𝕜 E) (hV : finrank 𝕜 V = (k : ℕ) + 1) :
    ∃ x ∈ V, ‖x‖ = 1 ∧ RCLike.re ⟪T x, x⟫_𝕜 ≤ hT.eigenvalues hn k

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.exists_submodule_forall_unit_eigenvalue_le_re_inner
declarations.doc:
**Courant–Fischer, lower direction.** There is a subspace `V` of dimension
`k + 1` on which every unit vector `x` satisfies `λₖ(T) ≤ re ⟪T x, x⟫`, where
`λ` is the decreasing enumeration `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues` of the
eigenvalues of the symmetric operator `T`.

Witness: `V = span {bᵢ : i ≤ k}`; on it the quadratic form is bounded below by
`λₖ` since all involved eigenvalues are `≥ λₖ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_submodule_forall_unit_eigenvalue_le_re_inner
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) (k : Fin n) :
    ∃ V : Submodule 𝕜 E, finrank 𝕜 V = (k : ℕ) + 1 ∧
      ∀ x ∈ V, ‖x‖ = 1 → hT.eigenvalues hn k ≤ RCLike.re ⟪T x, x⟫_𝕜

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues_eq_iSup_iInf_re_inner
declarations.doc:
**Courant–Fischer min-max equality.** The `k`-th (decreasingly sorted)
eigenvalue of a symmetric operator on a finite-dimensional inner product space
over `𝕜 = ℝ, ℂ` is the supremum, over the subspaces `V` of dimension `k + 1`,
of the infimum of the Rayleigh quotient `re ⟪T x, x⟫` over the unit vectors of
`V`.

Horn & Johnson, *Matrix Analysis* 2nd ed., Theorem 4.2.6.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenvalues_eq_iSup_iInf_re_inner
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) (k : Fin n) :
    hT.eigenvalues hn k =
      ⨆ V : {V : Submodule 𝕜 E // finrank 𝕜 V = (k : ℕ) + 1},
        ⨅ x : {x : E // x ∈ (V : Submodule 𝕜 E) ∧ ‖x‖ = 1},
          RCLike.re ⟪T (x : E), (x : E)⟫_𝕜

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues_eq_of_eigenbasis
declarations.doc:
**Sorted-eigenvalue uniqueness.**  If an orthonormal basis `w`
diagonalizes the symmetric operator `S` with an *antitone* value list `μ`,
then `μ` is the sorted eigenvalue list: `hS.eigenvalues hn = μ`.
(Courant–Fischer: both lists satisfy the same minimax characterization.)
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenvalues_eq_of_eigenbasis
    (hS : S.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) (w : OrthonormalBasis (Fin n) 𝕜 E)
    {μ : Fin n → ℝ} (hμ : Antitone μ) (hw : ∀ i, S (w i) = (μ i : 𝕜) • w i) :
    hS.eigenvalues hn = μ

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalue_mono
declarations.doc:
**Loewner monotonicity of the sorted eigenvalues.**  If the quadratic form
of `T` is dominated by that of `S`, then so is every sorted eigenvalue.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenvalue_mono
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hS : S.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n)
    (h : ∀ x, RCLike.re ⟪T x, x⟫_𝕜 ≤ RCLike.re ⟪S x, x⟫_𝕜) (k : Fin n) :
    hT.eigenvalues hn k ≤ hS.eigenvalues hn k

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.map_mem_spanIndices
declarations.doc:
The span of a selected subfamily of the eigenbasis of a symmetric operator
is invariant under the operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_mem_spanIndices (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n)
    (s : Set (Fin n)) {x : E}
    (hx : x ∈ (hT.eigenvectorBasis hn).spanIndices s) :
    T x ∈ (hT.eigenvectorBasis hn).spanIndices s

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.abs_eigenvalue_sub_eigenvalue_le
declarations.doc:
**Weyl's inequality** for symmetric operators on a finite-dimensional inner
product space over `𝕜 = ℝ, ℂ`: the `k`-th (decreasingly sorted) eigenvalues of
`T` and `S` differ by at most the operator norm of `T − S`.

At `LinearMap` level there is no operator norm, so the bound is supplied as the
pointwise hypothesis `∀ x, ‖(T − S) x‖ ≤ ε * ‖x‖`; see
`LinearMap.IsSymmetric.abs_eigenvalue_sub_eigenvalue_le_norm` for the continuous-linear-map
operator-norm form.

Horn & Johnson, *Matrix Analysis* 2nd ed., Theorem 4.3.1; Bhatia,
*Matrix Analysis*, Corollary III.2.6.
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_eigenvalue_sub_eigenvalue_le
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hS : S.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n)
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : ∀ x : E, ‖(T - S) x‖ ≤ ε * ‖x‖) (k : Fin n) :
    |hT.eigenvalues hn k - hS.eigenvalues hn k| ≤ ε

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.abs_eigenvalue_sub_eigenvalue_le_norm
declarations.doc:
**Weyl's inequality**, operator-norm form, for symmetric (equivalently,
self-adjoint) continuous linear maps on a finite-dimensional inner product
space: the `k`-th sorted eigenvalues of `T` and `S` differ by at most
`‖T − S‖`.  The symmetry hypotheses are stated on the underlying linear maps
so that the signature does not require the adjoint star structure (whose
instance needs `CompleteSpace E`, which `FiniteDimensional` deliberately does
not register as an instance).

The bound is expressed directly in the norm of a continuous linear map.
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_eigenvalue_sub_eigenvalue_le_norm
    {T S : E →L[𝕜] E}
    (hT : LinearMap.IsSymmetric (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] E))
    (hS : LinearMap.IsSymmetric (S : E →ₗ[𝕜] E))
    (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) (k : Fin n) :
    |hT.eigenvalues hn k - hS.eigenvalues hn k| ≤ ‖T - S‖

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.abs_eigenvalues_sub_le_opNorm
declarations.doc:
Weyl's inequality for linear maps, using the operator norm of the
corresponding continuous linear map.  Unlike the preceding theorem, the symmetry
hypotheses and eigenvalue enumeration are directly attached to `LinearMap`s.
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_eigenvalues_sub_le_opNorm
    {T S : E →ₗ[𝕜] E} (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hS : S.IsSymmetric)
    (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) (k : Fin n) :
    |hT.eigenvalues hn k - hS.eigenvalues hn k|
      ≤ ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (T - S)‖

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues_congr
declarations.doc:
Sorted eigenvalues are congruent along an operator equality (the eigenvalue
enumeration depends only on the operator, not on the symmetry proof).
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenvalues_congr {S₁ S₂ : E →ₗ[𝕜] E} (h : S₁ = S₂)
    (hS₁ : S₁.IsSymmetric) (hS₂ : S₂.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) :
    hS₁.eigenvalues hn = hS₂.eigenvalues hn

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues_cast
declarations.doc:
The eigenvalue enumeration does not depend on which witness of the dimension indexes
it: two witnesses `finrank 𝕜 E = m` and `finrank 𝕜 E = n` enumerate the same eigenvalues,
read across the induced `Fin m ≃ Fin n`.

Both spellings occur in practice.  A matrix over `Fin n` has
`Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues₀` indexed by `Fin (Fintype.card (Fin n))`, while the
operator theory it is transported to indexes by `Fin n`; `Fintype.card (Fin n) = n` is a
theorem and not definitional, so the two index types are genuinely different.

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.exists_unit_vector_re_inner_le_eigenvalue_of_le
declarations.doc:
**Courant–Fischer, upper direction, for large subspaces.** On any subspace `W` of dimension
at least `k + 1` there is a unit vector `x` with `re ⟪T x, x⟫ ≤ λₖ(T)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_unit_vector_re_inner_le_eigenvalue_of_le
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n) (k : Fin n)
    (W : Submodule 𝕜 E) (hW : (k : ℕ) + 1 ≤ finrank 𝕜 W) :
    ∃ x ∈ W, ‖x‖ = 1 ∧ RCLike.re ⟪T x, x⟫_𝕜 ≤ hT.eigenvalues hn k

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalue_compression_le
declarations.doc:
**Upper Cauchy interlacing.** If the quadratic form of the symmetric operator `A` on `V`
agrees with that of `T`, then `μₖ(A) ≤ λₖ(T)` for every `k < m`.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenvalue_compression_le
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n)
    (hA : A.IsSymmetric) (hm : finrank 𝕜 V = m)
    (hcomp : ∀ y : V, RCLike.re ⟪A y, y⟫_𝕜 = RCLike.re ⟪T y, y⟫_𝕜)
    (k : Fin m) (hk : (k : ℕ) < n) :
    hA.eigenvalues hm k ≤ hT.eigenvalues hn ⟨k, hk⟩

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalue_le_eigenvalue_compression
declarations.doc:
**Lower Cauchy interlacing.** If the quadratic form of the symmetric operator `A` on `V`
agrees with that of `T`, then `λ_{k + (n - m)}(T) ≤ μₖ(A)` for every `k < m`.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenvalue_le_eigenvalue_compression
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n)
    (hA : A.IsSymmetric) (hm : finrank 𝕜 V = m)
    (hcomp : ∀ y : V, RCLike.re ⟪A y, y⟫_𝕜 = RCLike.re ⟪T y, y⟫_𝕜)
    (k : Fin m) (hmn : m ≤ n) :
    hT.eigenvalues hn ⟨k + (n - m), by omega⟩ ≤ hA.eigenvalues hm k

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalue_ascending_le_ritz
declarations.doc:
**Hylleraas–Undheim–MacDonald.** In ascending order, the `k`-th lowest Ritz value is an upper
bound for the `k`-th lowest exact eigenvalue: `λ↑ₖ(T) ≤ μ↑ₖ(S)` for every `k < m`.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenvalue_ascending_le_ritz
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n)
    (hA : A.IsSymmetric) (hm : finrank 𝕜 V = m)
    (hcomp : ∀ y : V, RCLike.re ⟪A y, y⟫_𝕜 = RCLike.re ⟪T y, y⟫_𝕜)
    (hmn : m ≤ n) (k : ℕ) (hk : k < m) :
    hT.eigenvalues hn ⟨n - 1 - k, by omega⟩ ≤ hA.eigenvalues hm ⟨m - 1 - k, by omega⟩

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalue_min_le_ritz_min
declarations.doc:
**Variational ground-state bound.** The lowest Ritz value bounds the lowest exact eigenvalue
from above.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenvalue_min_le_ritz_min
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n)
    (hA : A.IsSymmetric) (hm : finrank 𝕜 V = m)
    (hcomp : ∀ y : V, RCLike.re ⟪A y, y⟫_𝕜 = RCLike.re ⟪T y, y⟫_𝕜)
    (hmn : m ≤ n) (hm0 : 0 < m) :
    hT.eigenvalues hn ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩ ≤ hA.eigenvalues hm ⟨m - 1, by omega⟩

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.compression
declarations.doc: The compression `P_V ∘ T ∘ ι_V` of `T` to the subspace `V` (the Ritz operator).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def compression (_hT : T.IsSymmetric) (V : Submodule 𝕜 E) : V →ₗ[𝕜] V

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.inner_compression_left
declarations.doc: The compression has the inner products of `T` against vectors of `V`.
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_compression_left (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (V : Submodule 𝕜 E) (y z : V) :
    ⟪hT.compression V y, z⟫_𝕜 = ⟪T y, z⟫_𝕜

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.compression_isSymmetric
declarations.doc: The compression of a symmetric operator is symmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma compression_isSymmetric (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (V : Submodule 𝕜 E) :
    (hT.compression V).IsSymmetric

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.re_inner_compression
declarations.doc:
The compression has the quadratic form of `T` on `V`, as required by the interlacing
lemmas.
declarations.statement:
lemma re_inner_compression (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (V : Submodule 𝕜 E) (y : V) :
    RCLike.re ⟪hT.compression V y, y⟫_𝕜 = RCLike.re ⟪T y, y⟫_𝕜

modules.title: Comparing linear combinations by their Gram kernels
modules.doc:
Two families with the same pairwise inner products give linear combinations of the same norm when
supplied with the same finitely supported coefficients.

## i. Overview

Two families with the same pairwise inner products give linear combinations of the same norm
when supplied with the same finitely supported coefficients. This comparison applies in
seminormed inner product spaces and is useful for comparing realizations of a positive-definite
kernel before constructing an isometry between their closed spans.

## ii. Key results

This file proves the statement described in the overview.

## iii. Table of contents
