declarations.name: Finsupp.norm_linearCombination_eq_of_inner_eq
declarations.doc:
Families with equal pairwise inner products give linear combinations of equal norm
for the same finitely supported coefficients.

modules.title: Analytic bounds for positive-semidefinite matrices
modules.doc:
This file supplements the foundational API in `TauCeti.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.PosSemidef` with scalar
Cauchy--Schwarz and vanishing bounds for `RCLike`-valued positive-semidefinite matrices, together
with the resulting estimate for *Hankel* matrices: a sequence bounded above whose Hankel matrix `(m,
n) ↦ a (m + n)` is positive semidefinite cannot increase at the first step.

## i. Overview

This file supplements the foundational API in `TauCeti.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.PosSemidef` with
scalar Cauchy--Schwarz and vanishing bounds for `RCLike`-valued positive-semidefinite matrices,
together with the resulting estimate for *Hankel* matrices: a sequence bounded above whose Hankel
matrix `(m, n) ↦ a (m + n)` is positive semidefinite cannot increase at the first step.

The results apply in particular to positive-definite kernels, represented directly as matrices,
but do not depend on Tau Ceti's positive-definite-function theory.

They supply the matrix prerequisites for Part C of the `OneParameterSemigroups` roadmap, including
the positive-definite-function/kernel correspondence and the GNS/Kolmogorov decomposition. No
Mathlib code is vendored.

## ii. Key results

* `Matrix.PosSemidef.normSq_le`: scalar Cauchy--Schwarz.
* `Matrix.PosSemidef.eq_zero_of_apply_self_eq_zero_left` and
  `Matrix.PosSemidef.eq_zero_of_apply_self_eq_zero_right`: zero-diagonal vanishing.
* `Matrix.PosSemidef.norm_le_one_of_apply_self_eq_one`: the normalized scalar bound.
* `Matrix.PosSemidef.norm_le_of_norm_apply_self_le`: the diagonal bounds every entry.
* `TauCeti.sub_nonneg_of_posSemidef_hankel`: a positive-semidefinite Hankel sequence bounded above
  does not increase at the first step.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development
- B. Bounded positive-semidefinite Hankel sequences

## iv. References

* C. Berg, J. P. R. Christensen, P. Ressel, *Harmonic Analysis on Semigroups* (GTM 100, 1984),
  Chapter 3.

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.normSq_le
declarations.doc: Scalar Cauchy--Schwarz for an `RCLike`-valued positive-semidefinite matrix.

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.eq_zero_of_apply_self_eq_zero_left
declarations.doc: A zero diagonal entry forces the corresponding row entry to vanish.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_zero_of_apply_self_eq_zero_left {K : α → α → 𝕜}
    (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) {a b : α} (ha : K a a = 0) : K a b = 0

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.eq_zero_of_apply_self_eq_zero_right
declarations.doc: A zero diagonal entry forces the corresponding column entry to vanish.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_zero_of_apply_self_eq_zero_right {K : α → α → 𝕜}
    (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) {a b : α} (hb : K b b = 0) : K a b = 0

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.norm_le_one_of_apply_self_eq_one
declarations.doc:
If two diagonal entries are `1`, then the corresponding off-diagonal entry has norm at most
`1`.

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.norm_le_of_norm_apply_self_le
declarations.doc:
**The diagonal of a positive-semidefinite matrix bounds all of its entries.** Cauchy--Schwarz
turns a uniform bound on the (nonnegative real) diagonal entries into the same bound everywhere.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_le_of_norm_apply_self_le {K : α → α → 𝕜} {C : ℝ}
    (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (hdiag : ∀ i, ‖K i i‖ ≤ C) (a b : α) : ‖K a b‖ ≤ C

declarations.name: TauCeti.sub_nonneg_of_posSemidef_hankel
declarations.doc:
**A positive-semidefinite Hankel sequence bounded above does not increase at the first step.**
If `(m, n) ↦ a (m + n)` is positive semidefinite and the real parts of `a` are bounded above by `D`
— the entries are automatically real — then `a 1 ≤ a 0` in the `RCLike` order. Cauchy--Schwarz
alone gives `a n ^ 2 ≤ a 0 * a (2 n)`, and the bound rules out a ratio `a 1 / a 0` greater
than `1`.

modules.title: Extending bounded-operator convergence from dense subsets
modules.doc:
This file records two standard density arguments for uniformly bounded families of continuous linear
maps between seminormed spaces.

## i. Overview

This file records two standard density arguments for uniformly bounded families of continuous
linear maps between seminormed spaces. Pointwise convergence on a dense subset extends to
pointwise convergence everywhere, and uniform Cauchy convergence on a parameter set does likewise.
Both rest on the same estimate
`ContinuousLinearMap.norm_sub_apply_le_of_norm_le`, which moves the point at which a
difference of two uniformly bounded operators is evaluated to a nearby point of the dense subset.

## ii. Key results

This file proves the statement described in the overview.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* Standard material; the statements and proofs are original to this formalization.

declarations.name: ContinuousLinearMap.norm_sub_apply_le_of_norm_le
declarations.doc:
Comparing two continuous linear maps of norm at most `K` at `x` costs at most `2 K ‖x - y‖`
more than comparing them at `y`. This is the shared estimate of the two density arguments below:
`y` is chosen in the dense subset, close to the arbitrary vector `x`.

declarations.name: ContinuousLinearMap.tendsto_apply_of_dense
declarations.doc:
A uniformly bounded family of continuous linear maps that converges pointwise on a dense
subset converges pointwise everywhere.

declarations.name: ContinuousLinearMap.uniformCauchySeqOn_apply_of_dense
declarations.doc:
A uniformly bounded family of continuous linear maps that is uniformly Cauchy on a parameter
set at every vector in a dense subset is uniformly Cauchy there at every vector.

modules.title: Positive-definite functions on an additive commutative group
modules.doc:
On an additive commutative group `G` the classical positive-definiteness condition for `F : G → ℂ`
reads `∑_{i,j} cᵢ · conj(cⱼ) · F(aᵢ - aⱼ) ≥ 0`: the involution is negation, so the kernel is the
translation-invariant `K(a, b) = F(a - b)`.

## i. Overview

On an additive commutative group `G` the classical positive-definiteness condition for
`F : G → ℂ` reads `∑_{i,j} cᵢ · conj(cⱼ) · F(aᵢ - aⱼ) ≥ 0`: the involution is negation, so the
kernel is the translation-invariant `K(a, b) = F(a - b)`. Mathlib's `star` on a real vector space
is the identity, not negation, so the generic involutive predicate
`TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite` does *not* express this condition for the canonical instances on
`ℝ` or on a Euclidean space. This file supplies the subtraction-form predicate
`TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub` that does, and connects it to the generic theory.

The connection runs through the type synonym `TauCeti.WithNegStar G`, a copy of `G` carrying the
negation involution `star a = -a` as a genuine `StarAddMonoid` instance. Installing that
involution on `G` itself would clash with Mathlib's star conventions, so it is installed on the
synonym instead, and `TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_isPositiveDefinite` transports statements
across. The synonym is public: a generic lemma with no transfer lemma here can still be applied to
`fun a : WithNegStar G => F (WithNegStar.ofNegStar a)`.

This advances `TauCetiRoadmap/OneParameterSemigroups/README.md`, Part C, Objects, which asks for
`IsPositiveDefinite` to be defined generically and then *instantiated* on a finite-dimensional real
inner-product space with the involution `a⋆ = -a`, and the `API to develop` items (closure
properties, the value bounds at the origin, continuity at `0` implying uniform continuity, the
PD-function ↔ PD-kernel equivalence `F(a - b)`, and normalization) at that instantiation. It is
the predicate in which Bochner's theorem is stated, in
`TauCeti/Analysis/Bochner/BochnerTheorem.lean`.

## ii. Key results

* `TauCeti.WithNegStar`: the type synonym carrying the negation involution.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub`: the subtraction-form positive-definiteness predicate.
* `TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_forall_sum_nonneg`: the defining finite-family condition.
* `TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_isPositiveDefinite`: the transfer to the generic predicate.
* `TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_posSemidef`: the PD-function ↔ PD-kernel equivalence.
* `TauCeti.isPositiveDefinite_iff_isPositiveDefiniteSub`: agreement with the generic predicate on
  a group whose own involution is negation.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.map_zero_nonneg`, `map_zero_re_nonneg`, `map_zero_eq_ofReal_re`,
  `map_neg`, `conj_symm`, `normSq_le`, `norm_apply_le_map_zero_re`: values at and around the
  origin.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.add`, `const_mul`, `real_smul`, `mul`, `sum`, `prod`,
  `TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_const`: closure properties.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.comp_addMonoidHom`, `comp_smul`, `comp_neg`: pullbacks.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.of_tendsto`: pointwise limits.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.normalize`: normalization to value `1` at the origin.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.uniformContinuous_of_continuousAt_zero`: continuity at `0`
  implies uniform continuity.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development
  - A.1. The negation involution
  - A.2. The subtraction-form predicate
  - A.3. Values at and around the origin
  - A.4. Closure properties
  - A.5. Pullbacks
  - A.6. Limits
  - A.7. Normalization
  - A.8. Continuity

## iv. References

* C. Berg, J. P. R. Christensen, P. Ressel, *Harmonic Analysis on Semigroups* (GTM 100, 1984),
  Chapter 3.
* W. Rudin, *Fourier Analysis on Groups* (1962), §1.4.

sections.text: ### A.3. Values at and around the origin

declarations.name: TauCeti.WithNegStar
declarations.doc:
`WithNegStar G` is a type synonym for an additive commutative group `G`, carrying the negation
involution `star a = -a`.

Mathlib pins no negation `StarAddMonoid` instance on an additive group — on a real vector space
`star` is the identity — so the involution used by classical positive definiteness is installed on
this synonym rather than on `G` itself.
declarations.statement: def WithNegStar (G : Type*) : Type _
instance : AddCommGroup (WithNegStar G)
instance : Star (WithNegStar G)

declarations.name: TauCeti.WithNegStar.star_eq_neg
declarations.statement: lemma star_eq_neg (a : WithNegStar G) : star a = -a
instance : StarAddMonoid (WithNegStar G)

declarations.name: TauCeti.WithNegStar.toNegStar
declarations.doc: The identity additive equivalence from `G` to its negation-involution copy.
declarations.statement: def toNegStar : G ≃+ WithNegStar G

declarations.name: TauCeti.WithNegStar.ofNegStar
declarations.doc: The identity additive equivalence from the negation-involution copy of `G` back to `G`.
declarations.statement: def ofNegStar : WithNegStar G ≃+ G

declarations.name: TauCeti.WithNegStar.ofNegStar_toNegStar
declarations.statement: lemma ofNegStar_toNegStar (a : G) : ofNegStar (toNegStar a) = a

declarations.name: TauCeti.WithNegStar.toNegStar_ofNegStar
declarations.statement: lemma toNegStar_ofNegStar (a : WithNegStar G) : toNegStar (ofNegStar a) = a
instance : SeminormedAddCommGroup (WithNegStar G)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub
declarations.doc:
A function `F : G → ℂ` on an additive commutative group is **positive definite** when, for
every finite family of scalars `c : Fin n → ℂ` and points `v : Fin n → G`, the Hermitian form
`∑_{i,j} c i · conj (c j) * F (v i - v j)` is a nonnegative real number (using the order on `ℂ`
for which `0 ≤ z` means `z` is real and nonnegative).

This is the classical translation-invariant condition, the one Bochner's theorem is stated in. It
is `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite` for the negation involution; see
`TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_isPositiveDefinite`.
declarations.statement: def IsPositiveDefiniteSub (F : G → ℂ) : Prop

declarations.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_forall_sum_nonneg
declarations.doc:
The defining finite-family characterization, for building a positive-definite function
directly from the quadratic-form condition.
declarations.statement:
lemma isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_forall_sum_nonneg :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub F ↔ ∀ (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → ℂ) (v : Fin n → G),
      0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, c i * conj (c j) * F (v i - v j)

declarations.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_isPositiveDefinite
declarations.doc:
Subtraction-form positive definiteness is the generic involutive predicate for the negation
involution, read on the type synonym `TauCeti.WithNegStar`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_isPositiveDefinite :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub F ↔
      IsPositiveDefinite fun a : WithNegStar G => F (WithNegStar.ofNegStar a)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.isPositiveDefinite
declarations.doc:
The generic involutive predicate attached to a subtraction-form positive-definite function.
This is the workhorse for transporting the generic API.
declarations.statement:
lemma isPositiveDefinite (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) :
    IsPositiveDefinite fun a : WithNegStar G => F (WithNegStar.ofNegStar a)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.sum_nonneg
declarations.doc: Positive-definiteness holds for an arbitrary finite index type, not just `Fin n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (c : ι → ℂ) (v : ι → G) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, c i * conj (c j) * F (v i - v j)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.posSemidef
declarations.doc:
A subtraction-form positive-definite function gives the translation-invariant
positive-definite kernel `K(a, b) = F (a - b)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma posSemidef (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) :
    Matrix.PosSemidef fun a b : G => F (a - b)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.of_posSemidef
declarations.doc:
A function whose translation-invariant kernel `K(a, b) = F (a - b)` is positive definite is
positive definite.
declarations.statement:
lemma of_posSemidef (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef fun a b : G => F (a - b)) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub F

declarations.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_posSemidef
declarations.doc:
The PD-function ↔ PD-kernel equivalence in its classical translation-invariant form: `F` is
positive definite if and only if the kernel `K(a, b) = F (a - b)` is positive definite.
declarations.statement:
lemma isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_posSemidef :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub F ↔ Matrix.PosSemidef fun a b : G => F (a - b)

declarations.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefinite_iff_isPositiveDefiniteSub
declarations.doc:
On a group whose own involution is negation, the generic involutive predicate and the
subtraction-form predicate agree.
declarations.statement:
lemma isPositiveDefinite_iff_isPositiveDefiniteSub [StarAddMonoid G]
    (hstar : ∀ a : G, star a = -a) : IsPositiveDefinite F ↔ IsPositiveDefiniteSub F

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.map_zero_nonneg
declarations.doc: The value of a positive-definite function at `0` is real and nonnegative.
declarations.statement: lemma map_zero_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) : 0 ≤ F 0

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.map_zero_im
declarations.doc: The value of a positive-definite function at `0` has zero imaginary part.
declarations.statement: lemma map_zero_im (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) : (F 0).im = 0

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.map_zero_re_nonneg
declarations.doc: The real part of the value of a positive-definite function at `0` is nonnegative.
declarations.statement: lemma map_zero_re_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) : 0 ≤ (F 0).re

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.map_zero_eq_ofReal_re
declarations.doc:
The value at the origin of a positive-definite function is the real number `(F 0).re`, viewed
as a complex number.
declarations.statement: lemma map_zero_eq_ofReal_re (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) : F 0 = ((F 0).re : ℂ)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.map_zero_re_pos_of_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
If a positive-definite function is nonzero at the origin, then the real part of that value is
strictly positive.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_zero_re_pos_of_ne_zero (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) (h0 : F 0 ≠ 0) :
    0 < (F 0).re

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.conj_symm
declarations.doc: A positive-definite function is conjugate symmetric: `conj (F (b - a)) = F (a - b)`.
declarations.statement: lemma conj_symm (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) (a b : G) : conj (F (b - a)) = F (a - b)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.map_neg
declarations.doc: A positive-definite function satisfies `F (-a) = conj (F a)`.
declarations.statement: lemma map_neg (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) (a : G) : F (-a) = conj (F a)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.normSq_le
declarations.doc:
The Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for a positive-definite function: the squared norm of any value
is bounded by the square of the value at the origin.
declarations.statement:
lemma normSq_le (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) (a b : G) :
    Complex.normSq (F (a - b)) ≤ (F 0).re * (F 0).re

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.norm_apply_le_map_zero_re
declarations.doc: A positive-definite function is bounded by its value at the origin.
declarations.statement: lemma norm_apply_le_map_zero_re (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) (a : G) : ‖F a‖ ≤ (F 0).re

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.apply_eq_zero_of_map_zero_re_eq_zero
declarations.doc: **A positive-definite function with `(F 0).re = 0` vanishes identically.**
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_eq_zero_of_map_zero_re_eq_zero (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) (h0 : (F 0).re = 0)
    (a : G) : F a = 0

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.add
declarations.doc: Positive-definite functions are closed under addition.
declarations.statement:
lemma add (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) (hH : IsPositiveDefiniteSub H) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub fun x => F x + H x

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.const_mul
declarations.doc:
Positive-definite functions are closed under multiplication by a nonnegative complex
scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma const_mul {k : ℂ} (hk : 0 ≤ k) (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub fun x => k * F x

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.real_smul
declarations.doc: Positive-definite functions are closed under multiplication by a nonnegative real scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma real_smul {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub fun x => r • F x

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.mul
declarations.doc: Positive-definite functions are closed under pointwise multiplication (Schur product).
declarations.statement:
lemma mul (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) (hH : IsPositiveDefiniteSub H) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub fun x => F x * H x

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.sum
declarations.doc: Positive-definite functions are closed under finite sums.

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.prod
declarations.doc: Positive-definite functions are closed under finite products (Schur products).

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.comp_addMonoidHom
declarations.doc:
Positive definiteness is preserved by precomposition with an additive homomorphism; no
compatibility with an involution is needed, since an additive homomorphism automatically
commutes with negation.
declarations.statement:
lemma comp_addMonoidHom {N : Type*} [AddCommGroup N] (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F)
    (φ : N →+ G) : IsPositiveDefiniteSub fun x => F (φ x)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.comp_smul
declarations.doc: Positive definiteness is preserved by rescaling the argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma comp_smul {R : Type*} [DistribSMul R G] (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) (r : R) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub fun x => F (r • x)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.comp_neg
declarations.doc: Positive definiteness is preserved by negating the argument.
declarations.statement: lemma comp_neg (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) : IsPositiveDefiniteSub fun x => F (-x)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.of_tendsto
declarations.doc: Positive definiteness is preserved under pointwise limits along a nontrivial filter.
declarations.statement:
lemma of_tendsto {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} [NeBot l] {F : ι → G → ℂ} {H : G → ℂ}
    (hF : ∀ᶠ i in l, IsPositiveDefiniteSub (F i))
    (hlim : ∀ x : G, Tendsto (fun i => F i x) l (𝓝 (H x))) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub H

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.normalize
declarations.doc:
Multiplying a positive-definite function by the reciprocal of its real value at the origin
preserves positive definiteness.
declarations.statement:
lemma normalize (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub fun x => (((F 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F x

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.normalize_apply_zero
declarations.doc: The normalized function has value `1` at the origin.
declarations.statement:
lemma normalize_apply_zero (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) (h0 : F 0 ≠ 0) :
    (((F 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F 0 = 1

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.norm_normalize_apply_le_one
declarations.doc: A normalized positive-definite function is bounded by `1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_normalize_apply_le_one (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F) (a : G) :
    ‖(((F 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F a‖ ≤ 1

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.uniformContinuous_of_continuousAt_zero
declarations.doc:
A positive-definite function on a seminormed additive commutative group is uniformly
continuous as soon as it is continuous at the origin.
declarations.statement:
lemma uniformContinuous_of_continuousAt_zero (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F)
    (hcont : ContinuousAt F 0) : UniformContinuous F

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.continuous_of_continuousAt_zero
declarations.doc:
A positive-definite function on a seminormed additive commutative group is continuous as soon
as it is continuous at the origin.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_of_continuousAt_zero (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteSub F)
    (hcont : ContinuousAt F 0) : Continuous F

declarations.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_const
declarations.doc: A nonnegative real constant is a positive-definite function.
declarations.statement:
lemma isPositiveDefiniteSub_const {k : ℂ} (hk : 0 ≤ k) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub (fun _ : G => k)

declarations.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_zero
declarations.doc: The zero function is positive definite.
declarations.statement: lemma isPositiveDefiniteSub_zero : IsPositiveDefiniteSub (fun _ : G => (0 : ℂ))

modules.title: Pontryagin characters are positive-definite atoms
modules.doc:
A continuous character of a topological abelian group becomes a continuous function on the additive
group after transporting `G` to `Multiplicative G`.

## i. Overview

A continuous character of a topological abelian group becomes a continuous function on the
additive group after transporting `G` to `Multiplicative G`. This file proves that every such
character is a continuous subtraction-positive-definite function. The character-level fact is
an atomic input for Fourier analysis on locally compact abelian groups; it does not assert a
measure-representation or Pontryagin-duality theorem.

## ii. Key results

* `PontryaginDual.isPositiveDefiniteSub`: a continuous Pontryagin character is a
  continuous positive-definite function in the additive subtraction form.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* Standard material; the statements and proofs are original to this formalization.

declarations.name: PontryaginDual.isPositiveDefiniteSub
declarations.doc:
Precomposing a Pontryagin character with `Multiplicative.ofAdd` gives a continuous function in
subtraction-positive-definite form.
declarations.statement:
lemma isPositiveDefiniteSub
    (χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) :
    Continuous (fun g : G => (χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) : ℂ)) ∧
      IsPositiveDefiniteSub
        (fun g : G => (χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) : ℂ))

modules.title: Positive-definite functions on an involutive additive monoid
modules.doc:
A complex-valued function `F` on an additive monoid `M` equipped with an involution `star` (an
`AddMonoid` with a `StarAddMonoid` structure) is **positive definite** when, for every finite family
`(cᵢ, aᵢ)` of scalars `cᵢ : ℂ` and points `aᵢ : M`, the Hermitian form `∑_{i,j} cᵢ · conj(cⱼ) · F(aᵢ
+ aⱼ⋆)` is a nonnegative real number.

## i. Overview

A complex-valued function `F` on an additive monoid `M` equipped with an involution `star`
(an `AddMonoid` with a `StarAddMonoid` structure) is **positive definite** when, for every
finite family `(cᵢ, aᵢ)` of scalars `cᵢ : ℂ` and points `aᵢ : M`, the Hermitian form
`∑_{i,j} cᵢ · conj(cⱼ) · F(aᵢ + aⱼ⋆)` is a nonnegative real number. The involution `aⱼ⋆` inside
the argument is what makes this the right notion on an involutive semigroup (Berg–Christensen–
Ressel): on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with `a⋆ = -a` it specialises to the
classical translation-invariant positive-definiteness `∑ cᵢ conj(cⱼ) F(aᵢ - aⱼ) ≥ 0`, and on the
product monoid `ℝ≥0 × V` it produces the BCR involution `(t, a)⋆ = (t, -a)`.

This file introduces the predicate `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite` at this general level and develops
its basic algebraic API: the value at `0` is real and nonnegative, the function is conjugate
symmetric in the involution, it satisfies the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality coming from the `2 × 2`
sub-form, and the class is closed under sums and nonnegative complex scalar multiples, with the
Schur pointwise product closure and nonnegative constants as examples.

This is the `Objects` and first `API to develop` slice of Part C of the `OneParameterSemigroups`
roadmap in TauCetiRoadmap: "positive-definite functions and Bochner's theorem". Mathlib has
related APIs for positive-semidefinite matrices, bilinear and linear maps, and RKHS kernels, but
not for positive-definite functions on an involutive monoid, so the predicate and its API are built
here. The continuity theory and Bochner's representation theorem are later milestones.

## ii. Key results

* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite`: the positive-definiteness predicate for `F : M → ℂ`.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_nonneg`: nonnegativity for arbitrary finite families.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.quadForm_two_nonneg`: nonnegativity of the `2 × 2` sub-form.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.map_zero_nonneg`: `0 ≤ F 0`.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.map_zero_im`: `(F 0).im = 0`.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.map_zero_re_nonneg`: `0 ≤ (F 0).re`.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.map_zero_eq_ofReal_re`: `F 0 = ((F 0).re : ℂ)`.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.map_zero_re_pos_of_ne_zero`: if `F 0 ≠ 0`, then
  `0 < (F 0).re`.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.conj_symm`: `conj (F (b + a⋆)) = F (a + b⋆)`.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.normSq_le`: the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality
  `‖F (a + b⋆)‖² ≤ (F (a + a⋆)).re * (F (b + b⋆)).re`.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_apply_le_map_zero_re_of_add_star_eq_zero`: `‖F a‖ ≤ (F 0).re`
  when `a + star a = 0`, with the additive-group corollary
  `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_apply_le_map_zero_re_of_star_eq_neg` for `star a = -a`.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.apply_eq_zero_of_map_zero_re_eq_zero`: `(F 0).re = 0` forces
  `F` to vanish identically.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.posSemidef`: a positive-definite function gives the
  positive-definite kernel `fun a b => F (a + star b)`.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_posSemidef`: conversely, if the kernel
  `fun a b => F (a + star b)` is positive definite then `F` is positive definite.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.add`, `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum`,
  `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.const_mul`, `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.mul`,
  `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.prod`, `TauCeti.isPositiveDefinite_const`: closure properties and
  examples.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* C. Berg, J. P. R. Christensen, P. Ressel, *Harmonic Analysis on Semigroups* (GTM 100, 1984),
  Chapter 3.

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite
declarations.doc:
A function `F : M → ℂ` on an involutive additive monoid is **positive definite** when, for
every finite family of scalars `c : Fin n → ℂ` and points `v : Fin n → M`, the Hermitian form
`∑_{i,j} c i · conj (c j) · F (v i + star (v j))` is a nonnegative real number (using the order on
`ℂ` for which `0 ≤ z` means `z` is real and nonnegative).
declarations.statement: def IsPositiveDefinite (F : M → ℂ) : Prop

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_nonneg
declarations.doc:
Positive-definiteness holds for an arbitrary finite index type, not just `Fin n`: for every
finite family of scalars `c : ι → ℂ` and points `v : ι → M`, the Hermitian form
`∑_{i,j} c i · conj (c j) · F (v i + star (v j))` is a nonnegative real number.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (c : ι → ℂ) (v : ι → M) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, c i * conj (c j) * F (v i + star (v j))

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.quadForm_two_nonneg
declarations.doc:
The `2 × 2` Hermitian sub-form of a positive-definite function at the points `a, b` with
coefficients `c₀, c₁` is nonnegative.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadForm_two_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (a b : M) (c₀ c₁ : ℂ) :
    0 ≤ c₀ * conj c₀ * F (a + star a) + c₀ * conj c₁ * F (a + star b)
      + c₁ * conj c₀ * F (b + star a) + c₁ * conj c₁ * F (b + star b)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.add_star_self_nonneg
declarations.doc:
A positive-definite function takes a real, nonnegative value at every "norm point"
`a + star a`.
declarations.statement: lemma add_star_self_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (a : M) : 0 ≤ F (a + star a)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.add_star_self_im
declarations.doc:
The value of a positive-definite function at a "norm point" `a + star a` has zero imaginary
part.
declarations.statement: lemma add_star_self_im (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (a : M) : (F (a + star a)).im = 0

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.add_star_self_re_nonneg
declarations.doc:
The value of a positive-definite function at a "norm point" `a + star a` has nonnegative real
part.
declarations.statement: lemma add_star_self_re_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (a : M) : 0 ≤ (F (a + star a)).re

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.map_zero_nonneg
declarations.doc: The value of a positive-definite function at `0` is real and nonnegative.
declarations.statement: lemma map_zero_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) : 0 ≤ F 0

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.map_zero_im
declarations.doc: The value of a positive-definite function at `0` has zero imaginary part.
declarations.statement: lemma map_zero_im (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) : (F 0).im = 0

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.map_zero_re_nonneg
declarations.doc: The real part of the value of a positive-definite function at `0` is nonnegative.
declarations.statement: lemma map_zero_re_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) : 0 ≤ (F 0).re

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.map_zero_eq_ofReal_re
declarations.doc:
The value at the origin of a positive-definite function is equal to the real number
`(F 0).re`, viewed as a complex number.
declarations.statement: lemma map_zero_eq_ofReal_re (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) : F 0 = ((F 0).re : ℂ)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.map_zero_re_pos_of_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
If a positive-definite function is nonzero at the origin, then the real part of that value is
strictly positive.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_zero_re_pos_of_ne_zero (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (h0 : F 0 ≠ 0) :
    0 < (F 0).re

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.conj_symm
declarations.doc:
A positive-definite function is conjugate symmetric in the involution:
`conj (F (b + star a)) = F (a + star b)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma conj_symm (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (a b : M) :
    conj (F (b + star a)) = F (a + star b)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.posSemidef
declarations.doc:
A positive-definite function `F` induces the positive-definite kernel `K(a, b) = F(a + b⋆)`.
This is the forward half of the function ↔ kernel correspondence.
declarations.statement:
lemma posSemidef (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) :
    Matrix.PosSemidef (fun a b => F (a + star b))

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_posSemidef
declarations.doc:
If the kernel `K(a, b) = F(a + b⋆)` is positive definite, then so is the function `F`. This is
the reverse half of the function ↔ kernel correspondence.
declarations.statement:
lemma of_posSemidef
    (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef (fun a b => F (a + star b))) : IsPositiveDefinite F

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.normSq_le
declarations.doc:
The Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for a positive-definite function: the squared norm of an
off-diagonal value is bounded by the product of the two diagonal values.
declarations.statement:
lemma normSq_le (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (a b : M) :
    Complex.normSq (F (a + star b))
      ≤ (F (a + star a)).re * (F (b + star b)).re

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_apply_le_map_zero_re_of_add_star_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
If `a + star a = 0`, then a positive-definite function is bounded at `a` by its value at
zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_apply_le_map_zero_re_of_add_star_eq_zero (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    (a : M) (ha : a + star a = 0) : ‖F a‖ ≤ (F 0).re

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.apply_eq_zero_of_map_zero_re_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**A positive-definite function with `(F 0).re = 0` vanishes identically.**

No hypothesis on the point is required, and none on the ambient structure beyond an
involutive additive monoid (`AddMonoid` and `StarAddMonoid`).
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_eq_zero_of_map_zero_re_eq_zero (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    (h0 : (F 0).re = 0) (a : M) : F a = 0

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_apply_le_map_zero_re_of_star_eq_neg
declarations.doc:
If the involution negates the point `a`, then a positive-definite function is bounded at `a`
by its value at zero. In particular this applies on an additive group whose involution is
negation.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_apply_le_map_zero_re_of_star_eq_neg (hH : IsPositiveDefinite H)
    (a : N) (hstar_a : star a = -a) : ‖H a‖ ≤ (H 0).re

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.add
declarations.doc: Positive-definite functions are closed under addition.
declarations.statement:
lemma add (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (hG : IsPositiveDefinite G) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x => F x + G x)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.const_mul
declarations.doc: Positive-definite functions are closed under multiplication by a nonnegative complex scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma const_mul {k : ℂ} (hk : 0 ≤ k) (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x => k * F x)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.mul
declarations.doc: Positive-definite functions are closed under pointwise multiplication (Schur product).
declarations.statement:
lemma mul (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (hG : IsPositiveDefinite G) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x => F x * G x)

declarations.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefinite_const
declarations.doc: A nonnegative real constant is a positive-definite function.
declarations.statement:
lemma isPositiveDefinite_const {k : ℂ} (hk : 0 ≤ k) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun _ : M => k)

declarations.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefinite_zero
declarations.doc: The zero function is positive definite.
declarations.statement: lemma isPositiveDefinite_zero : IsPositiveDefinite (fun _ : M => (0 : ℂ))

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum
declarations.doc: Positive-definite functions are closed under finite sums.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum {ι : Type*} {s : Finset ι} {F : ι → M → ℂ} (hF : ∀ i ∈ s, IsPositiveDefinite (F i)) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x => ∑ i ∈ s, F i x)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.prod
declarations.doc: Positive-definite functions are closed under finite products (Schur product).
declarations.statement:
lemma prod {ι : Type*} {s : Finset ι} {F : ι → M → ℂ} (hF : ∀ i ∈ s, IsPositiveDefinite (F i)) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x => ∏ i ∈ s, F i x)

modules.title: Continuity of positive-definite functions
modules.doc:
This file records the standard continuity upgrade for positive-definite functions on a seminormed
additive group with the negation involution.

## i. Overview

This file records the standard continuity upgrade for positive-definite functions on a seminormed
additive group with the negation involution. A positive-definite function that is continuous at
the origin is uniformly continuous. The file also records the local estimates
`‖F x - F y‖² ≤ 2 F(0).re ((F 0).re - (F (x + star y)).re)` and
`‖F x - F y‖² ≤ 2 F(0).re ‖F (x + star y) - F 0‖` at points satisfying
`x + star x = 0` and `y + star y = 0`, together with their specializations to additive groups
whose involution is negation.

This advances Part C of the `OneParameterSemigroups` roadmap, whose positive-definite-function
API asks for the basic fact "continuity at `0` ⇒ uniform continuity" before Bochner's theorem.

## ii. Key results

In the namespace `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite`:

* `norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_re_sub_of_star_eq_neg`:
  the local real-part continuity estimate.
* `norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_re_sub_of_add_star_eq_zero`:
  the monoid-level local real-part continuity estimate.
* `norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_star_eq_neg`:
  the local norm-valued continuity estimate.
* `norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_add_star_eq_zero`:
  the monoid-level local norm-valued continuity estimate.
* `norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_re_sub_of_forall_star_eq_neg` and
  `norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_forall_star_eq_neg`:
  specializations to a globally negating involution.
* `uniformContinuous_of_continuousAt_zero_of_forall_star_eq_neg`:
  continuity at `0` implies uniform continuity.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* C. Berg, J. P. R. Christensen, P. Ressel, *Harmonic Analysis on Semigroups* (GTM 100, 1984),
  Chapter 3.

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_re_sub_of_add_star_eq_zero
declarations.doc: The local monoid-level real-part form of the standard positive-definite continuity estimate.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_re_sub_of_add_star_eq_zero
    (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) {x y : E} (hx : x + star x = 0) (hy : y + star y = 0) :
    ‖F x - F y‖ ^ 2
      ≤ 2 * (F 0).re * ((F 0).re - (F (x + star y)).re)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_add_star_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
The local monoid-level norm-valued form of the standard positive-definite continuity
estimate.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_add_star_eq_zero
    (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) {x y : E} (hx : x + star x = 0) (hy : y + star y = 0) :
    ‖F x - F y‖ ^ 2 ≤ 2 * (F 0).re * ‖F (x + star y) - F 0‖

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_re_sub_of_star_eq_neg
declarations.doc: The local real-part form of the standard positive-definite continuity estimate.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_re_sub_of_star_eq_neg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    {x y : E} (hx : star x = -x) (hy : star y = -y) :
    ‖F x - F y‖ ^ 2
      ≤ 2 * (F 0).re * ((F 0).re - (F (x - y)).re)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_re_sub_of_forall_star_eq_neg
declarations.doc:
The real-part form of the standard positive-definite continuity estimate under a globally
negating involution.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_re_sub_of_forall_star_eq_neg
    (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (hstar : ∀ x : E, star x = -x) (x y : E) :
    ‖F x - F y‖ ^ 2
      ≤ 2 * (F 0).re * ((F 0).re - (F (x - y)).re)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_star_eq_neg
declarations.doc: The local norm-valued form of the standard positive-definite continuity estimate.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_star_eq_neg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    {x y : E} (hx : star x = -x) (hy : star y = -y) :
    ‖F x - F y‖ ^ 2 ≤ 2 * (F 0).re * ‖F (x - y) - F 0‖

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_forall_star_eq_neg
declarations.doc:
The norm-valued form of the standard positive-definite continuity estimate under a globally
negating involution.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_forall_star_eq_neg
    (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (hstar : ∀ x : E, star x = -x) (x y : E) :
    ‖F x - F y‖ ^ 2 ≤ 2 * (F 0).re * ‖F (x - y) - F 0‖

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.uniformContinuous_of_continuousAt_zero_of_forall_star_eq_neg
declarations.doc:
A positive-definite function on a seminormed additive group with the negation involution is
uniformly continuous as soon as it is continuous at the origin.
declarations.statement:
lemma uniformContinuous_of_continuousAt_zero_of_forall_star_eq_neg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    (hstar : ∀ x : E, star x = -x) (hcont : ContinuousAt F 0) :
    UniformContinuous F

modules.title: Weighted closure for positive-definite functions
modules.doc:
This file adds the weighted finite-mixture and Schur-power API for `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite`, the
positive-definite-function predicate on an involutive additive monoid.

## i. Overview

This file adds the weighted finite-mixture and Schur-power API for
`TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite`, the positive-definite-function predicate on an involutive additive
monoid. The basic file already proves binary sums, nonnegative complex scalar multiples, pointwise
products, and unweighted finite sums/products. Here we package the forms used by examples and
finite approximations: finite nonnegative weighted sums, real-weighted variants, and powers. The
weighted sum API is available in scalar (`•`) notation.

This advances `TauCetiRoadmap/OneParameterSemigroups/README.md`, Part C, the positive-definite
functions API asking for closure under sums and products before the Bochner and BCR representation
milestones. No external formalization is vendored.

## ii. Key results

* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.real_smul`: nonnegative real scalar multiplication.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_smul`: finite nonnegative weighted sums.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_real_smul`: finite nonnegative real-weighted sums.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.pow`: Schur powers of a positive-definite function.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_smul_apply_zero_of_apply_zero_eq_one`: normalized finite
  mixtures evaluate at the origin as the sum of their weights.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* C. Berg, J. P. R. Christensen, P. Ressel, *Harmonic Analysis on Semigroups* (GTM 100, 1984),
  Chapter 3.

modules.title: The GNS translation representation of a positive-definite function
modules.doc:
A positive-definite function on an additive commutative group has a canonical Hilbert space,
obtained from its translation-invariant positive-definite kernel.

## i. Overview

A positive-definite function on an additive commutative group has a canonical Hilbert space,
obtained from its translation-invariant positive-definite kernel. Translation of the kernel
vectors extends uniquely to a unitary operator. These operators form a group representation,
and the original function is a matrix coefficient of its vector at zero.

The translation action is part of the GNS/Kolmogorov decomposition of a positive-definite
function. Its later use in LCA Bochner theory requires spectral measures and Pontryagin duality.

## ii. Key results

This file proves the statement described in the overview.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* W. Rudin, *Fourier Analysis on Groups* (1962), Chapter 1.

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsSpace
declarations.doc: The canonical Hilbert space of the translation-invariant kernel `K(a,b) = F(a-b)`.
declarations.statement: abbrev gnsSpace

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsVector
declarations.doc: The vector in the GNS space corresponding to a group element.
declarations.statement: def gnsVector (a : G) : hF.gnsSpace

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.inner_gnsVector
declarations.doc: The inner product of two GNS vectors is the original positive-definite kernel.
declarations.statement: lemma inner_gnsVector (a b : G) : ⟪hF.gnsVector a, hF.gnsVector b⟫_ℂ = F (a - b)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.norm_gnsVector_sub_sq
declarations.doc: Squared distances between GNS vectors are controlled by the real part of the function.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_gnsVector_sub_sq (a b : G) :
    ‖hF.gnsVector a - hF.gnsVector b‖ ^ 2 =
      2 * ((F 0).re - (F (a - b)).re)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsVector_dense
declarations.doc: The GNS vectors span a dense subspace.
declarations.statement:
lemma gnsVector_dense :
    (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range hF.gnsVector)).topologicalClosure = ⊤

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsTranslation
declarations.doc:
Translation by `g` is a unitary operator on the canonical GNS Hilbert space. Its action on
the dense family of kernel vectors is `v(a) ↦ v(g+a)`.
declarations.statement: def gnsTranslation (g : G) : hF.gnsSpace ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] hF.gnsSpace

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsTranslation_gnsVector
declarations.doc: Translation acts on the canonical GNS vectors by addition.
declarations.statement:
lemma gnsTranslation_gnsVector (g a : G) :
    hF.gnsTranslation g (hF.gnsVector a) = hF.gnsVector (g + a)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsTranslation_zero
declarations.doc: The translation at zero is the identity operator.
declarations.statement: lemma gnsTranslation_zero : hF.gnsTranslation 0 = LinearIsometryEquiv.refl ℂ hF.gnsSpace

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsTranslation_add
declarations.doc: GNS translations compose according to the group law.
declarations.statement:
lemma gnsTranslation_add (g k : G) :
    hF.gnsTranslation (g + k) = (hF.gnsTranslation k).trans (hF.gnsTranslation g)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsRepresentation
declarations.doc:
The GNS representation as a homomorphism from the multiplicative copy of `G` to the
unitary operators on its canonical Hilbert space.
declarations.statement: def gnsRepresentation : Multiplicative G →* (hF.gnsSpace ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] hF.gnsSpace)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsRepresentation_ofAdd
declarations.doc: The representation operator at `g` is translation by `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gnsRepresentation_ofAdd (g : G) :
    hF.gnsRepresentation (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) = hF.gnsTranslation g

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.gnsRepresentation_gnsVector
declarations.doc: The representation translates each GNS vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma gnsRepresentation_gnsVector (g a : G) :
    hF.gnsRepresentation (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) (hF.gnsVector a) =
      hF.gnsVector (g + a)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.eq_inner_gnsRepresentation
declarations.doc:
A positive-definite function is a matrix coefficient of its canonical unitary
representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_inner_gnsRepresentation (g : G) :
    F g = ⟪hF.gnsRepresentation (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) (hF.gnsVector 0),
      hF.gnsVector 0⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.continuous_gnsVector
declarations.doc:
Continuity of a positive-definite function at zero makes its canonical feature map
continuous. This is the regularity needed for a strongly continuous representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_gnsVector [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalAddGroup G]
    (hcont : ContinuousAt F 0) : Continuous hF.gnsVector

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.continuous_gnsTranslation_apply
declarations.doc:
The GNS translation representation is strongly continuous: every vector has a continuous
orbit.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_gnsTranslation_apply [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalAddGroup G]
    (hcont : ContinuousAt F 0) (x : hF.gnsSpace) :
    Continuous (fun g : G => hF.gnsTranslation g x)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub.continuous_gnsRepresentation_apply
declarations.doc: The canonical unitary representation has continuous orbits.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_gnsRepresentation_apply [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalAddGroup G]
    (hcont : ContinuousAt F 0) (x : hF.gnsSpace) :
    Continuous (fun g : Multiplicative G => hF.gnsRepresentation g x)

modules.title: The positive-definite function ↔ positive-definite kernel correspondence
modules.doc:
A positive-definite function `F : M → ℂ` on an involutive additive monoid and a positive-definite
kernel `K : M → M → ℂ` are two views of the same data, linked by the assignment `K(a, b) = F(a +
b⋆)`.

## i. Overview

A positive-definite function `F : M → ℂ` on an involutive additive monoid and a positive-definite
kernel `K : M → M → ℂ` are two views of the same data, linked by the assignment
`K(a, b) = F(a + b⋆)`. This file records the forward and reverse correspondence, packages them
as an iff, and records the translation-invariant group specialization.

Both sides express nonnegativity of finite quadratic forms; the two-variable kernel is viewed
directly as a matrix and tested with Mathlib's `Matrix.PosSemidef` predicate.

Under the negation involution `a⋆ = -a` the kernel takes the familiar translation-invariant shape
`K(a, b) = F(a - b)`, the form in which positive definiteness is usually stated on groups such as
`ℝᵈ` or a real inner-product space. We record that specialization as a corollary parameterized by
the hypothesis `star a = -a` (Mathlib pins no such `StarAddMonoid` instance, since `star` is the
identity on a real vector space, so the negation involution is supplied as a side hypothesis rather
than an instance).

This advances the `OneParameterSemigroups` roadmap, Part C ("Positive-definite functions and
Bochner's theorem", `TauCetiRoadmap/OneParameterSemigroups/README.md`): the `API to develop` bullet
"the PD-function ↔ PD-kernel equivalence (`K(a, b) = F(a + b⋆)`; `F(a − b)` for a group)".
The function-side predicate `IsPositiveDefinite` lives in Tau Ceti, while the kernel side uses
Mathlib's `Matrix.PosSemidef`; this file connects them and records the group form. No Mathlib code
is vendored.

## ii. Key results

* `TauCeti.isPositiveDefinite_iff_posSemidef`: the equivalence of the two predicates,
  packaging the two halves.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.posSemidef_sub` and
  `TauCeti.isPositiveDefinite_iff_posSemidef_sub`: the subtraction form
  `K(a, b) = F(a - b)` under the negation involution `star a = -a`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* C. Berg, J. P. R. Christensen, P. Ressel, *Harmonic Analysis on Semigroups* (GTM 100, 1984),
  Chapter 3.

declarations.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefinite_iff_posSemidef
declarations.doc:
A function `F` on an involutive additive monoid is positive definite if and only if the
two-variable kernel `K(a, b) = F(a + b⋆)` is positive definite.
declarations.statement:
lemma isPositiveDefinite_iff_posSemidef :
    IsPositiveDefinite F ↔ Matrix.PosSemidef (fun a b => F (a + star b))

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.posSemidef_sub
declarations.doc:
Under the negation involution `a⋆ = -a`, a positive-definite function `F` gives the
translation-invariant positive-definite kernel `K(a, b) = F(a - b)`. This is the form in which
positive definiteness is usually stated on groups such as `ℝᵈ` or a real inner-product space.
declarations.statement:
lemma posSemidef_sub (hstar : ∀ a : G, star a = -a) (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) :
    Matrix.PosSemidef (fun a b => F (a - b))

declarations.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefinite_iff_posSemidef_sub
declarations.doc:
Under the negation involution `a⋆ = -a`, `F` is positive definite if and only if the
translation-invariant kernel `K(a, b) = F(a - b)` is positive definite.
declarations.statement:
lemma isPositiveDefinite_iff_posSemidef_sub (hstar : ∀ a : G, star a = -a) :
    IsPositiveDefinite F ↔ Matrix.PosSemidef (fun a b => F (a - b))

modules.title: Kolmogorov decomposition of a positive-definite kernel
modules.doc:
This file constructs the canonical Hilbert-space realization of a scalar-valued positive-definite
kernel.

## i. Overview

This file constructs the canonical Hilbert-space realization of a scalar-valued
positive-definite kernel.  A kernel `K : α → α → 𝕜` is first regarded as the operator-valued
kernel whose `(a, b)` entry is multiplication by `K a b` on the one-dimensional Hilbert space
`𝕜`.  Mathlib's `RKHS.OfKernel` construction then gives a Hilbert space and kernel vectors
`Φ a` satisfying

`⟪Φ a, Φ b⟫_𝕜 = K a b`.

The span of the kernel vectors is dense, so this is the minimal Kolmogorov decomposition rather
than an arbitrary realization.  Its universal property gives a unique linear isometry into any
other realization, and a linear isometric equivalence when that realization is also minimal.

The completion and reproducing-kernel construction are Mathlib's `RKHS.OfKernel`; this file
supplies the scalar-kernel bridge and its characteristic API.

## ii. Key results

* `TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelOperator`: regard a scalar kernel as an operator-valued kernel.
* `TauCeti.posSemidef_positiveDefiniteKernelOperator`: positivity of that
  operator kernel.
* `Matrix.PosSemidef.KolmogorovSpace`: the canonical Hilbert space.
* `Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovFeature`: its canonical feature map.
* `Matrix.PosSemidef.inner_kolmogorovFeature`: the Kolmogorov identity.
* `Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovFeature_dense`: minimality of the decomposition.
* `Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovIsometry`: the universal comparison isometry.
* `Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovEquiv`: equivalence with any other minimal
  realization.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* C. Berg, J. P. R. Christensen, P. Ressel, *Harmonic Analysis on Semigroups*,
  Springer GTM 100 (1984), Chapter 3.

declarations.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelOperator
declarations.doc:
A scalar kernel regarded as an operator-valued kernel on the one-dimensional Hilbert space
`𝕜`: the entry at `(a, b)` is left multiplication by `K a b`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def positiveDefiniteKernelOperator (K : α → α → 𝕜) :
    Matrix α α (𝕜 →L[𝕜] 𝕜)

declarations.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelOperator_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma positiveDefiniteKernelOperator_apply (K : α → α → 𝕜) (a b : α) (z : 𝕜) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelOperator K a b z = K a b * z

declarations.name: TauCeti.posSemidef_positiveDefiniteKernelOperator
declarations.doc:
The operator-valued kernel obtained from a scalar positive-definite kernel is positive
semidefinite.  This is the bridge needed by Mathlib's `RKHS.OfKernel` construction.
declarations.statement:
lemma posSemidef_positiveDefiniteKernelOperator (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) :
    (positiveDefiniteKernelOperator K).PosSemidef

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.KolmogorovSpace
declarations.doc:
The canonical Hilbert space in the Kolmogorov decomposition of `K`.

This is an abbreviation because Mathlib's `RKHS.OfKernel` currently has to be an abbreviation in
order for its normed-group and inner-product instances to reduce.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev KolmogorovSpace (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K)

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovFeature
declarations.doc:
The canonical feature map into the Kolmogorov space.  It sends `a` to the reproducing-kernel
vector at `a`, evaluated on the scalar `1`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def kolmogorovFeature (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (a : α) :
    KolmogorovSpace hK

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.inner_kolmogorovFeature
declarations.doc:
**Kolmogorov identity.** Inner products of the canonical feature vectors recover the
original kernel.
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_kolmogorovFeature (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (a b : α) :
    ⟪kolmogorovFeature hK a, kolmogorovFeature hK b⟫_𝕜 = K a b

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.norm_kolmogorovFeature_sq
declarations.doc:
The squared norm of a canonical feature vector is the real part of the corresponding
diagonal kernel value.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_kolmogorovFeature_sq (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (a : α) :
    ‖kolmogorovFeature hK a‖ ^ 2 = RCLike.re (K a a)

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.norm_kolmogorovFeature_sub_sq
declarations.doc:
The squared distance between two canonical feature vectors, expressed entirely in terms of
the original kernel.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_kolmogorovFeature_sub_sq (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (a b : α) :
    ‖kolmogorovFeature hK a - kolmogorovFeature hK b‖ ^ 2 =
      RCLike.re (K a a) - 2 * RCLike.re (K a b) + RCLike.re (K b b)

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovFeature_dense
declarations.doc:
The canonical feature vectors have dense linear span in the Kolmogorov space.  Thus the
construction is minimal: it contains no orthogonal summand invisible to the kernel.
declarations.statement:
lemma kolmogorovFeature_dense (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) :
    (Submodule.span 𝕜 (Set.range (kolmogorovFeature hK))).topologicalClosure = ⊤

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovIsometry
declarations.doc:
The unique linear isometry from the canonical Kolmogorov space into any Hilbert-space
realization of `K`.  It sends each canonical feature vector to the corresponding vector in the
given realization.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def kolmogorovIsometry {E : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E] (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (φ : α → E)
    (hφ : ∀ a b, ⟪φ a, φ b⟫_𝕜 = K a b) : KolmogorovSpace hK →ₗᵢ[𝕜] E

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovIsometry_apply
declarations.doc:
The universal comparison isometry sends canonical feature vectors to the vectors of the
given realization.
declarations.statement:
lemma kolmogorovIsometry_apply {E : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E] (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (φ : α → E)
    (hφ : ∀ a b, ⟪φ a, φ b⟫_𝕜 = K a b) (a : α) :
    kolmogorovIsometry hK φ hφ (kolmogorovFeature hK a) = φ a

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovIsometry_unique
declarations.doc:
A linear isometry out of the canonical Kolmogorov space is uniquely determined by its values
on the canonical feature vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma kolmogorovIsometry_unique {E : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E] (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (φ : α → E)
    (hφ : ∀ a b, ⟪φ a, φ b⟫_𝕜 = K a b) (T : KolmogorovSpace hK →ₗᵢ[𝕜] E)
    (hT : ∀ a, T (kolmogorovFeature hK a) = φ a) : T = kolmogorovIsometry hK φ hφ

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovIsometry_surjective
declarations.doc:
If the vectors in a realization of `K` have dense linear span, the universal comparison
isometry is surjective.
declarations.statement:
lemma kolmogorovIsometry_surjective {E : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E] (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (φ : α → E)
    (hφ : ∀ a b, ⟪φ a, φ b⟫_𝕜 = K a b)
    (hφdense : (Submodule.span 𝕜 (Set.range φ)).topologicalClosure = ⊤) :
    Function.Surjective (kolmogorovIsometry hK φ hφ)

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovEquiv
declarations.doc:
The canonical Kolmogorov space is linearly isometric to every other minimal realization of
the same kernel.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def kolmogorovEquiv {E : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E] (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (φ : α → E)
    (hφ : ∀ a b, ⟪φ a, φ b⟫_𝕜 = K a b)
    (hφdense : (Submodule.span 𝕜 (Set.range φ)).topologicalClosure = ⊤) :
    KolmogorovSpace hK ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] E

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.kolmogorovEquiv_apply
declarations.doc:
The equivalence with another minimal realization sends canonical feature vectors to the
vectors of that realization.
declarations.statement:
lemma kolmogorovEquiv_apply {E : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E] (hK : Matrix.PosSemidef K) (φ : α → E)
    (hφ : ∀ a b, ⟪φ a, φ b⟫_𝕜 = K a b)
    (hφdense : (Submodule.span 𝕜 (Set.range φ)).topologicalClosure = ⊤) (a : α) :
    kolmogorovEquiv hK φ hφ hφdense (kolmogorovFeature hK a) = φ a

modules.title: Limits of positive-definite functions
modules.doc:
This file derives pointwise- and locally-uniform-limit closure for `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite`, the
positive-definite function predicate on an involutive additive monoid, from Mathlib's closedness
theorem for the cone of positive-semidefinite matrices.

## i. Overview

This file derives pointwise- and locally-uniform-limit closure for
`TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite`, the positive-definite function predicate on an involutive additive
monoid, from Mathlib's closedness theorem for the cone of positive-semidefinite matrices.

This is the limit-closure item from Part C of the `OneParameterSemigroups` roadmap. The result is
about positive-definiteness alone for pointwise limits; as the roadmap notes, continuity needs an
additional hypothesis. Mathlib's `TendstoLocallyUniformly.continuous` provides continuity of a
locally uniform limit when the approximating functions are frequently continuous, while this file
provides the positive-definiteness conclusion.

## ii. Key results

* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_tendsto`: filter-level pointwise-limit closure for
  positive-definite functions.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_forall_tendsto`: the same result when every function in the
  family is positive definite.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_seq_tendsto`: the sequential `atTop` specialization.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_tendstoLocallyUniformly`: locally uniform limits of eventually
  positive-definite functions are positive definite.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* C. Berg, J. P. R. Christensen, P. Ressel, *Harmonic Analysis on Semigroups* (GTM 100, 1984),
  Chapter 3.

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_tendsto
declarations.doc:
Positive-definiteness is preserved under pointwise limits along a nontrivial filter. The
hypothesis on positive-definiteness is eventual, so this applies equally to nets that are
eventually positive definite.
declarations.statement:
lemma of_tendsto {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} [NeBot l] {F : ι → M → ℂ} {G : M → ℂ}
    (hF : ∀ᶠ i in l, IsPositiveDefinite (F i))
    (hlim : ∀ x : M, Tendsto (fun i => F i x) l (𝓝 (G x))) :
    IsPositiveDefinite G

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_forall_tendsto
declarations.doc:
A pointwise limit of a family of positive-definite functions is positive definite. This is the
non-eventual form of `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_tendsto`.

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_seq_tendsto
declarations.doc: Sequential pointwise limits of eventually positive-definite functions are positive definite.
declarations.statement:
lemma of_seq_tendsto {F : ℕ → M → ℂ} {G : M → ℂ} (hF : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, IsPositiveDefinite (F n))
    (hlim : ∀ x : M, Tendsto (fun n => F n x) atTop (𝓝 (G x))) :
    IsPositiveDefinite G

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_tendstoLocallyUniformly
declarations.doc:
A locally uniform limit of eventually positive-definite functions is positive definite.

Unlike continuity, positive-definiteness itself only needs pointwise convergence; local uniform
convergence is converted to pointwise convergence before applying
`TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_tendsto`.

modules.title: Normalizing positive-definite functions
modules.doc:
This file records the standard normalization step for positive-definite functions: if `F : M → ℂ` is
positive definite and `F 0 ≠ 0`, then multiplying by the reciprocal of the nonnegative real number
`(F 0).re` gives a positive-definite function whose value at the origin is `1`.

## i. Overview

This file records the standard normalization step for positive-definite functions: if
`F : M → ℂ` is positive definite and `F 0 ≠ 0`, then multiplying by the reciprocal of the
nonnegative real number `(F 0).re` gives a positive-definite function whose value at the origin
is `1`.

This is part of the normalization API requested in Part C of the `OneParameterSemigroups`
roadmap ("Positive-definite functions and Bochner's theorem"). Normalized positive-definite
functions are the convenient form for characteristic functions and for the later Bochner and
GNS/Kolmogorov constructions: after normalization, the general bound `‖F a‖ ≤ (F 0).re` becomes
the familiar `‖F a‖ ≤ 1`.

The file deliberately keeps the hypotheses unbundled. It proves lemmas about the explicit
normalized function rather than introducing a new bundled predicate.

## ii. Key results

* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.normalize`: multiplying by `((F 0).re)⁻¹` preserves
  positive-definiteness.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.normalize_apply_zero`: the normalized function has value `1` at
  the origin.
* `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_add_star_eq_zero` and
  `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_star_eq_neg`: normalized functions
  are bounded by `1` on the usual group-like points.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* C. Berg, J. P. R. Christensen, P. Ressel, *Harmonic Analysis on Semigroups* (GTM 100, 1984),
  Chapter 3.

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.normalize
declarations.doc:
Multiplying a positive-definite function by the reciprocal of its real value at the origin
preserves positive-definiteness. If `F 0 = 0` this gives the zero scaling; the separate
`normalize_apply_zero` lemma below records the useful nonzero case.
declarations.statement:
lemma normalize (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x => (((F 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F x)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.normalize_apply_zero
declarations.doc: The normalized positive-definite function has value `1` at the origin.
declarations.statement:
lemma normalize_apply_zero (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (h0 : F 0 ≠ 0) :
    (((F 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F 0 = 1

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_add_star_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
At points satisfying `a + star a = 0`, the normalized positive-definite function is bounded
by `1`. When `F 0 = 0` the normalizing scalar is `0`, so the bound holds trivially.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_add_star_eq_zero (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    (a : M) (ha : a + star a = 0) :
    ‖(((F 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F a‖ ≤ 1

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_star_eq_neg
declarations.doc:
Under the negation involution, the normalized positive-definite function is bounded by `1` at
every point.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_star_eq_neg (hH : IsPositiveDefinite H)
    (a : G) (hstar_a : star a = -a) :
    ‖(((H 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * H a‖ ≤ 1

declarations.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_forall_star_eq_neg
declarations.doc:
If the involution is negation everywhere, the normalized positive-definite function is
uniformly bounded by `1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_forall_star_eq_neg (hH : IsPositiveDefinite H)
    (hstar : ∀ a : G, star a = -a) (a : G) :
    ‖(((H 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * H a‖ ≤ 1

modules.title: Positive-definite transforms of measures on a Pontryagin dual
modules.doc:
Integration of characters against a finite positive measure gives a positive-definite function on an
additive topological group.

## i. Overview

Integration of characters against a finite positive measure gives a
positive-definite function on an additive topological group. This is the positivity part
of the measure-to-function direction of Bochner representation on locally compact abelian groups.

## ii. Key results

This file proves the statement described in the overview.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Development

## iv. References

* Standard material; the statements and proofs are original to this formalization.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.isPositiveDefiniteSub_pontryaginMeasureTransform
declarations.doc: The transform of a finite positive measure on the dual is positive definite.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.isPositiveDefiniteSub_pontryaginMeasureTransform
    (μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteSub μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.norm_pontryaginMeasureTransform_le
declarations.doc: The absolute value of a measure transform is bounded by the measure's total mass.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.norm_pontryaginMeasureTransform_le
    (μ : FiniteMeasure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) (g : G) :
    ‖μ.pontryaginMeasureTransform g‖ ≤ μ.toMeasure.real Set.univ

modules.title: Intersections of submodules by dimension
modules.doc:
A dimension-counting criterion for nontrivial submodule intersection.

A dimension-counting criterion for nontrivial submodule intersection.

## ii. Key results

This file proves the statement described in the overview.

declarations.name: Submodule.inf_ne_bot_of_finrank_lt
declarations.doc:
Two subspaces whose dimensions sum to more than the dimension of the ambient
space have nontrivial intersection.
declarations.statement:
lemma inf_ne_bot_of_finrank_lt [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] {V W : Submodule 𝕜 E}
